    by `ScBanach.isScSplitting_sup_of_complementIn`; the text says "not difficult to see". (3) stays a statement in charts
    (G.7). Status: **settled**.
    (2026-11-09) `T_xX` now carries the linear structure of Definition 2.3.14, Banach through every chart and sc at
    smooth points (gap G.7 closed, Chapter 2, item 87); this statement is not restated with it.
82. **The examples `A` and `B` after Definition 2.5.19 hold** *(book 2021: p. 63)*. In `[0, ∞)² ⊕ W` for any `W`
    (`TameSubExample.examples_A_B` is `W = ℝ`): `A = {(x, y, 0)}` is a tame sub-M-polyfold with tame induced structure
    (`isTameSubMPolyfold_setA`, through `isTameSubMPolyfold_fixSet`, the fixed set of an idempotent sc-operator keeping
    the `ℝⁿ`-component); `B = {(x, x, 0)}` is a sub-M-polyfold (`isSubMPolyfold_setB`) but not a tame one
    (`not_isTameSubMPolyfold_setB`), and its induced structure is tame (`hasTameInducedStructure_setB`,
    `halfLineToB_isScDiffeoOn`). The obstruction for `B` is already in (1) and (2): near the corner, `d_X(t, 0, 0) = 1`
    for small `t > 0`, while `d_X` takes only the values `0` and `2` on `B` (`not_mem_tameSubData_setB`). Status:
    **settled**.
83. **Theorem 2.7.13 (2)–(4) and Definition 2.7.14, iterated boundaries** *(book 2021: pp. 83–84)*. `tameBoundaryPolyfold`:
    the charts `p ↦ π(φ(B p))` of centred triples (`BChartData`, `π` the face projection of Proposition 2.5.15) with
    transitions `π' ∘ (φ' ∘ φ⁻¹) ∘ ι` make `(bX, T_{bX})` a tame M-polyfold (`tameBoundaryPolyfold_isTame`); `B` is sc-smooth
    (`tameBoundaryMap_isScSmooth`); `d_X(B p) − 1 = d_{bX}(p)` (`degIndex_tameBoundaryMap_sub_one`). For centred `V`,
    `Φ_(x,V,θ)` is an sc-diffeomorphism onto `θ` (`phi_isScDiffeoOn`), and the structure is unique with this property
    (`tameBoundaryPolyfold_unique`). "The structure induced from `V`" is read as the sub-M-polyfold structure of the face
    (`isSubMPolyfold_of_isFaceIn`). Iterating needs `bX` bundled (`TameMPolyfoldBundle`): `Bᵏ` is sc-smooth, `d_X ∘ Bᵏ =
    d_{bᵏX} + k`, and its image is `{d_X ≥ k}` (`TameMPolyfoldBundle.iterMap_isScSmooth`, `degIndex_iterMap`,
    `range_iterMap`). Status: **settled**.
84. **The characterization after Theorem 2.7.13: "`Φ_(x,V,θ)` is an sc-diffeomorphism onto `θ`" does not hold as we read it

    Proposition 2.7.12 holds as printed for every pair of representatives
    (`proposition_2_7_12_scDiffeo_nonCentred`). The proof replaces the text's open sc-embeddings of faces by centred
    refinements (`TameBoundary.BTriple.exists_centred_subset`) and the sub-M-polyfold calculus (`phiInv_isScSmoothOn`). Status:
    does not hold as we read it for every representative; **repaired** with the image `θ ∩ V^x`.
    (2026-11-09) The book forms `proposition_2_7_12_book` and `theorem_2_7_13_book` carry this reading (item 89).

86. **Proposition 2.3.15 (2): `p : TX → X¹` is open (gap G.8 closed)** *(Proposition 2.3.15 (2), p. 39 (preprint 2.19,
    p. 27); proof in Appendix 2.7.3, pp. 76–77 (preprint pp. 58–60))* (2026-11-09).
    `Polyfold/Chapter2/TangentProjOpen.lean`. The local step is the openness of `π : TO → O₁`, which the text states
    without proof (p. 77): for a retract `O = r(U)` and `(o, h) ∈ TO` in an open `W`, the map `o' ↦ Tr(o', h) = (o',
    Dr(o')h)` is continuous on `U₁` since `Tr` is `sc⁰`, maps `O₁` into `TO`, and sends `o` to `(o, h)` because `Dr(o)h
    = h` on `T_oO`; so every `o'` near `o` in `O₁` is the base point of a vector of `TO ∩ W`
    (`ScRetraction.exists_isOpen_tangent_section`). The global step reads an open set of `TX` in the tangent chart of a
    representative (`MPolyfold.isOpenMap_tangentProj`), and Proposition 2.3.15 (2) holds in full
    (`proposition_2_3_15_two`). This closes gap G.8 (row V2.20) and makes the field `isOpenMap_tangentProj` of
    Chapter 7's `MPolyfold.SmoothRegular` a theorem (Chapter 7, item 153). Status: **settled**.

87. **The linear structure of `T_xX` (gap G.7 closed); `T^R_xX` and `C_xX` in `T_xX` (gap G.13 in part); strong bundle
    isomorphisms and `𝒮ℬℛ` (gap G.14 closed)** *(Definition 2.3.14, Theorem 2.3.16, Proposition 2.3.19 (3), (4), pp.
    38–44 (preprint 2.18, 2.19, 2.21, pp. 26–30); Definition 2.5.8, p. 57 (preprint 2.38, p. 42); Definition 2.6.1 and
    after Definition 2.6.3, pp. 65–67 (preprint 2.47, 2.49, pp. 48–51); items 72, 78, 79, 81)* (2026-11-09).
    `Polyfold/Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear.lean`, `TangentMapLinear.lean`, `SubMPolyfoldTangent.lean`,
    `SubMPolyfoldTangentSc.lean`, `ReducedTangentIntrinsic.lean`; `Polyfold/Chapter3/StrongBundleIsoSBR.lean`. (1)
    `T_xX` is a vector space, and for every chart `φ` around `x` the map `Tφ : T_xX → T_{φ(x)}O` is a linear isomorphism
    and a homeomorphism onto the Banach space `T_{φ(x)}O` (`MPolyfold.tangentFiberLinearEquiv`,
    `tangentFiberContinuousLinearEquiv`), with the text's formula `λ[(x, φ, h₁)] + μ[(x, φ, h₂)] = [(x, φ, λh₁ + μh₂)]`
    (`definition_2_3_14`); the chart independence that the text leaves to the reader is the linearity of the fibre
    transitions. At a smooth `x` every model `T_{φ(x)}O` is an sc-subspace of `E` with level-preserving transitions
    (`isScSubspace_tangentFiberModel`), so `T_xX` is an sc-Banach space through any chart. The tangent of an sc-smooth
    map is continuous linear on the fibres (`theorem_2_3_16_linear`). (2) Proposition 2.3.19 (3), (4) in `T_aX`:
    `T_aA` is a closed subspace with the closed complement `ker T(i⁻¹ ∘ r)`, an sc-complement at smooth points read
    through a chart, and `T_aA = Tr(a)T_aX` (`proposition_2_3_19_3_linear`, `proposition_2_3_19_3_sc`,
    `proposition_2_3_19_4`). (3) `T^R_xX` and `C_xX` are defined in `T_xX` as preimages under `Tφ(x)` and do not
    depend on the chart or on the presentation of its partial quadrant (`reducedTangentFiber_eq`,
    `partialConeFiber_eq`); in a tame chart at a smooth `x`, `d_X(x) = dim(T_xX/T^R_xX)`
    (`finrank_quotient_reducedTangentFiber_eq_degIndex`). Not formalized: that `C_xX` is a partial quadrant in `T_xX`
    with `d_{C_xX}(0_x) = d_X(x)` (in a chart, row V2.42). (4) Strong bundle isomorphisms form a groupoid
    (`IsStrongBundleIso.refl`, `symm`, `trans`), the text's wording is `exists_isStrongBundleIso_iff`, and `SBR` is a
    category with the functors `SBR.forget0`, `SBR.forget1`; these land in the sc-retracts `ScRetr`, the category `ℬℛ`
    of bundle retracts being gap G.5. Statements that use `T_xX` only in charts are not restated; their rows carry a
    dated note. Status: **settled** except `C_xX` as a partial quadrant (gap G.13); gaps G.7 and G.14 closed (rows
    V2.19, V2.21, V2.25, V2.54, V2.56, V2.94).

88. **Definition 2.5.19 with (3) in `T_yX` (gap G.77 closed; row V2.78)** *(Definitions 2.5.18, 2.5.19, pp. 62–63;
    Definition 2.3.14, p. 38; Definition 2.5.8, p. 57; items 72, 81, 82, 87)* (2026-11-09).
    `Polyfold/Chapter2/BookFormTameSub2021.lean`. With the linear structure of `T_yX` (item 87), condition (3) is
    stated in `T_yX`: `T_yY` is the image `Ti(T_yY)` of the tangent of the inclusion (`subTangentRange`), and `T_yX =
    Ti(T_yY) ⊕ A` with `A ⊆ T^R_yX` an sc-subspace, the splitting levelwise in a chart (`HasReducedScComplement`,
    `TameSubData2021`, `IsTameSubMPolyfold2021`). The step is the identification of `Ti(T_yY)` in a chart: for a chart
    `φ` of `X` and the sub-chart `σ` of `Y` built on it, `Tφ(y) ∘ Ti = Tσ(y)` (`fiberCoord_subInclusionCLM`), so
    `Tφ(y)` maps `Ti(T_yY)` onto the tangent space of `φ(W ∩ Y)` (`coe_map_range_subInclusionCLM`). Hence (3) in `T_yX`
    is equivalent to the chart form (`hasReducedScComplement_iff`, `isTameSubMPolyfold2021_iff`), it implies Definition
    2.5.18, and `Y = X` satisfies it (`definition_2_5_19_book`). "`A` is an sc-subspace and the sum is sc" is read
    through a chart, as is the sc-structure of `T_yX` at a smooth point (item 87); `T^R_yX` does not depend on the
    chart (`reducedTangentFiber_eq`). Status: **settled** (row V2.78; gap G.77 closed).

89. **The book forms of Remark 2.1.6, Proposition 2.7.12 and Theorem 2.7.13 (gaps G.76, G.78 closed)** *(Remark 2.1.6,

## Chapter 3 (sc-Fredholm theory; Lean `Polyfold/Chapter3/`)

*Numbering.* The items of this section are numbered in blocks, one block per line of work, so
that agents working at the same time do not collide; the gaps in the numbering are unused
numbers, not deleted items. 1–31: germs, the germ implicit function theorem, good position and
the quadrant theorems of the appendix (§3.3, §3.2/3.8.1, 3.8.4, 3.8.5); 40–50: sections of strong
bundles, Theorems 3.1.13 (preprint 3.12)/3.15, Proposition 3.1.10 (preprint 3.10), the filler, and the linear part of the global
implicit function theorem (Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52), Lemma 3.6.9 (preprint 3.55), Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53)); 60–79: the basic class
and local solvability (§3.4–§3.5, Lemma 3.7.4 (preprint 3.61)); 80–89: the tangent germ property (Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25),
Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27)) and the first assembly of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54); 90–99: the assembly of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) at the
centre. Blocks opened on 2026-10-25 (local session): 100–109: Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54) at the nearby zeros
in the chart at `x₀` (the kernel and the perturbation argument); 110–119: the linearization of a
section at a zero in a chart and its chart independence; 120–129: Corollary 3.4.3 (preprint 3.39) and the sharper
Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52); 130–139: good complements with a projection into the quadrant (`IsRegular` (b));
140–149: found while writing the exposition of §§3.4–3.5 and the application (Chapter3.md §5, §8);
150–159: the regularity of the solution germ away from the centre (`IsRegular` (a)), the assembly
of Theorem 3.1.22, Theorem 3.1.26, Corollary 3.1.27, Theorem 3.6.8, Theorem 3.6.10, Theorem 3.6.11 (preprint Theorems 3.19, 3.23, 3.24, 3.54, 3.56, 3.57), and the answer to "does the sc-Fredholm IFT hold
with the text's hypotheses?" (`SolutionGermRecentre.lean`, `GlobalIFTTheorems.lean`); 160–169:
Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18) (parametrized perturbations, `ParamPerturbation.lean`); 170–179: Chapter 3 polish
(statements weaker than their docstrings: the dimension of the solution set as the Fredholm index,

`∂X = ∅`, the converse in item 100; `GlobalIFTIndex.lean`); 180–189: Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54)
with the text's hypotheses (the surjectivity of `f'(y)` at the nearby zeros,
`GlobalIFTNearbyOnto*.lean`); 190–199: the tameness hypothesis repaired (`TameGerms.lean`, the
tame germ data of Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.4, 3.6.6 (preprint 3.50, 3.51, 3.53)); 200–209: non-vacuity witnesses for the §3.6
theorems (`NonVacuity.lean`); 210–219: follow-ups of the round-trip audit (`GoodPositionSc.lean`:
good position with the text's sc-complement, Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54) in the text's form; items 215–217:
Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9) with smallness on level `m`, Lemma 3.8.25's (preprint 3.81) estimate on all of `V₀`); 220–229: round-trip
audit findings recorded here only (germs versus the whole chart in §3.1, the level-`m` and
sc-Fredholm statements of Proposition 3.1.10 (preprint 3.10) and §3.6, one germ for all `k` in Theorem 3.35 (preprint; not in the 2021 edition)).

Found while formalizing §3.3 (contraction germs and the germ implicit function theorem) in
`ContractionGerm.lean` and `GermIFT.lean`. Statement numbers are the preprint's *(book 2017: see
`BookConcordance.md`)*.

1. **Theorem 3.3.3 (preprint 3.30) has no proof in the text** (p. 110 (preprint p. 86): "the following regularity result from [21],
   theorem 2.3, which is the hard part of the regularity theory"). The Lean proof
   (`Polyfold.ContractionGerm.hasFDerivWithinAt_sol`, `Polyfold.theorem_3_3_3`) is: at a parameter
   `a₀` with `(a₀, δ(a₀)) ∈ U₂` the candidate derivative `A = (1 − D₂B)⁻¹D₁B` exists on level `1`
   (Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9) on level `1` gives `‖D₂B‖ ≤ 1/2`), so `δ(a₀) + Ah` is an `E₁`-increment of size
   `O(|h|)`; the sc¹-remainder of `B` is `o(|h|)` and the `1/2`-contraction on level `0` gives
   `|δ(a₀ + h) − δ(a₀) − Ah|₀ ≤ 2·o(|h|)`. This proves that `δ` is sc¹ **on the re-indexed germ
   `V_m = N(m+1) ∩ C̃`**, not on the germ `(N m ∩ C̃)_m` on which `δ` was constructed: at points
   with `(a₀, δ(a₀)) ∈ U₁ ∖ U₂` the argument does not apply (`Ah ∉ W₁`), and whether `δ` is
   differentiable there is neither needed nor addressed. Re-indexing a germ is legitimate only
   because `C̃` is finite-dimensional (all levels of `C̃` coincide, so `(U_{m+1})_m` is again a germ
   of relatively open neighbourhoods), which the text does not remark; for a germ in an
   infinite-dimensional sc-Banach space `(U_{m+1})_m` is not a germ (`U_{m+1}` is open in `C_{m+1}`,
   not in `C_m`).
2. **The germ shrinks with `k` in Theorem 3.3.6 (preprint 3.33), Corollary 3.3.7 (preprint 3.34), Theorem 3.35 (preprint).** Each induction step
   of Theorem 3.3.6 (preprint 3.33) applies Theorem 3.3.3 (preprint 3.30) once more and so shifts the germ again: `δ` is sc^k on
   `(N(m + s_k) ∩ C̃)_m` with `s_k` growing with `k` (`Polyfold.theorem_3_3_6`). The proof gives
   `s_k = 2^k − 1` explicitly: the step `j → j + 1` uses the stage `j` twice, for `f` (shift `s`)
   and for `f⁽¹⁾` (shift `s'`), and returns `s + s' + 1` (`ContractionGerm.isSckGerm_succ_of_next`,
   `ContractionGerm.sol_isSckGerm`), so `s_0 = 0`, `s_{j+1} = 2s_j + 1`; the statement keeps
   `∃ s`. Consequently "if `f`
   is sc-smooth so is its solution germ" (Theorem 3.35 (preprint), last sentence; Corollary 3.3.7's (preprint 3.34) "in
   particular, `δ` is sc-smooth at the smooth point `0`") holds in the sense of Corollary 3.3.7 (preprint 3.34) —
   for every `k` on a neighbourhood germ `V_{·,k}` depending on `k` (`Polyfold.theorem_3_3_6_smooth`,
   `Polyfold.corollary_3_3_7`, `Polyfold.theorem_3_35_smooth_preprint`) — and **not** as "sc^k for all `k` on
   one fixed sequence `(V_m)`" (`Polyfold.IsScSmoothGerm`), which the method does not give. The
   text's germs are "up to shrinking" ("the size of the sets `U_m` does not matter", Definition 3.1.1 (preprint 3.1)),
   so there the two readings agree; with a germ as a fixed sequence of sets they do not. **The
   shrinking may not be intrinsic**: in the toy example of `Chapter3.md` §3 (the figure;
   `B(a, w) = aw + β(a)`, `β(a)_k = a e^{−k/a}`, on `[0,∞) ⊕ W` with `|w|_m² = Σ e^{2mk}|w_k|²`)
   the solution germ `δ(a) = β(a)/(1 − a)` is sc-smooth on the original germ `N(m) ∩ C̃`, while
   the proof certifies sc^k only on `N(m + 2^k − 1) ∩ C̃`. Whether some contraction germ really
   needs a shrinking germ is not decided. *(Revised in item 222: one fixed germ on which `δ` is sc^k
   for every `k` does exist, a diagonal of the `k`-dependent ones; in the project since item 250,
   `corollary_3_3_7_isScSmoothGerm`.)*
3. **Lemma 3.3.4 (preprint 3.31), "from the uniqueness we conclude that `δ⁽¹⁾ = Tδ`"** (p. 111 (preprint p. 87)). Uniqueness of the
   fixed point holds only in the contraction region, so `Tδ(v, b) = (δ(v), Dδ(v)b)` must lie in it:
   the region of `f⁽¹⁾` on level `m` has to be of the form `(N' × ℝⁿ) × (K_{m+1} × W_m)`, unbounded
   in the tangent directions `b, w` (where `B⁽¹⁾` is affine). Definition 3.3.1's (preprint 3.28) balls cannot express
   this, which is why the Lean working form `Polyfold.ContractionGerm` carries explicit regions
   `N m`, `O m ⊇ K m` and `Polyfold.ContractionGerm.next` builds those of `f⁽¹⁾` from them.
   Moreover `Dδ(v) = (1 − D₂B(v, δ(v)))⁻¹D₁B(v, δ(v))` needs the level-`1` operators, i.e.
   `(v, δ(v)) ∈ U₂`: the parameter region of `f⁽¹⁾` is `N(2+s) × ℝⁿ` (`Polyfold.ContractionGerm.next_sol`).
4. **Lemma 3.3.4 (preprint 3.31), "as one verifies by comparing the tangent map `Tf` with the map `f⁽¹⁾`"** is the
   chain rule for germs: `B⁽¹⁾ = (pr₁ ∘ TB ∘ σ, pr₂ ∘ TB ∘ Γ)` with the reshuffle
   `σ(v, b, u, w) = ((v, u), (b, w))` and `Γ(v, b, u, w) = ((v, δ(v)), (b, w))`, where
   `v ↦ δ(v) ∈ W₁` is the **shifted** solution germ (Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17), which the text states for
   relatively open sets, is needed for germs: `Polyfold.IsSckGerm.shift`). The class of `B⁽¹⁾` is
   `min(k−1, j)` as the text says (`Polyfold.ContractionGerm.lemma_3_3_4`).
5. **Lemma 3.3.5 (preprint 3.32) is reorganised.** The text iterates `f⁽¹⁾` to `f⁽ʲ⁾` and proves Theorem 3.3.6 (preprint 3.33) by
   contradiction. In Lean the induction is on `j` with the statement quantified over all contraction
   germs (the parameter space of `f⁽¹⁾` is `ℝⁿ ⊕ ℝⁿ`, its fibre `TW`): if `δ` is sc^j then `f⁽¹⁾` is
   sc^j (item 4, `k − 1 ≥ j`), so its solution germ `Tδ` is sc^j by the induction hypothesis, and
   `δ` is sc¹ by Theorem 3.3.3 (preprint 3.30), hence sc^{j+1} (`Polyfold.ContractionGerm.sol_isSckGerm`). The
   iterated germs `f⁽ʲ⁾` are not constructed.
6. **Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9) for sc¹ germs.** Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9) is stated for sc-smooth `B`, but Theorem 3.3.3 (preprint 3.30) and Lemma
   3.3.4 (preprint 3.31) use its estimate `‖D₂B(a, w)‖_m ≤ ε` for `B` merely sc¹ (Lemma 3.3.4 (preprint 3.31) for `f` of class sc^k,
   `k ≥ 1`, and `δ` of class sc^j). Its proof needs the differentiability of `B : U_{m+1} → W_m`
   (Proposition 1.2.1 (preprint 1.16), "recalling Proposition 1.17" in the text), proved for germs in
   `GermLevels.lean` (`Polyfold.IsSc1GermWith.hasFDerivWithinAt_level`); the estimate is
   `Polyfold.ContractionGerm.norm_levelDeriv_snd_le` with the constant `1/2`. The density
   argument ("it is sufficient to verify the estimate for `ζ ∈ W_{m+1}`") is as in the text.
7. **Definition 3.3.1 (preprint 3.28), "for all `(a, w), (a, w')` on level `m` sufficiently close to `(0, 0)`"**
   presupposes that these points lie in the domain `U_m` of the germ; the Lean form
   `Polyfold.IsSc0ContractionGerm` asks for `r > 0` with the estimate on `{|a| < r} × {|w|_m < r}`
   **and** these points in `U_m`. The passage from the balls to the working regions (the
   construction in the proof of Theorem 3.3.2 (preprint 3.29) — the "parametrized version of Banach fixed point
   theorem") needs radii decreasing fast enough for `K_{m+1} → K_m` and a continuity radius for
   `|B_m(a, 0)|_m` (`Polyfold.IsSc0ContractionGerm.toContractionGerm`).
8. **Corollary 3.3.7 (2) (preprint 3.34)** ("`δ : V_{m,k} → W_m` is of class `C^k`") uses Proposition 1.2.3 (preprint 1.18) for germs;
   the text cites Propositions 1.2.2 and 1.2.3 (preprint 1.17 and 1.18), stated for relatively open sets. Proved for germs
   (`Polyfold.IsSckGerm.contDiffOn_levels`, with the sets `V_{m,k} = N(m+k+s_k) ∩ C̃`). The citation
   of "Proposition 3.40" in that sentence (preprint p. 88) should be Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40) *(book 2017: unchanged,
   renumbered: "Proposition 3.11" for Theorem 3.11, before Corollary 3.3, p. 79)* *(book 2021: corrected, before Corollary 3.3.7, p. 113, cites Theorem 3.5.1)*.
9. **Theorem 3.35 (preprint)** is the same proof for any finite-dimensional partial quadrant `C̃`; in Lean the
   whole of §3.3 is proved for any convex `C̃ ∋ 0` with nonempty interior in a finite-dimensional
   `P` (`Polyfold.IsQuadrantLike (const P) C̃`), and Theorem 3.35 (preprint) is the specialisation
   (`Polyfold.theorem_3_35_preprint`, with `Polyfold.IsPartialQuadrant`).
10. Typos *(book 2017: unchanged: the first on p. 77; the second renumbered, p. 84 "Corollary 3.2" for
    Proposition 3.2, and the book's Corollary 3.2 is another statement; the statement of Theorem 3.7
    (= 3.29) is unchanged)* *(book 2021: the first unchanged, p. 110; the second corrected, §3.5, p. 117, which cites Proposition 3.1.10; Theorem 3.3.2, p. 110, unchanged)*: p. 110 (preprint p. 85), "a continuous map `δ₁ : V₁ → W₁` satisfying `δ(0) = 0`" for `δ₁(0) = 0`;
    preprint p. 94 (§3.5, first paragraph) "Corollary 3.10" for Proposition 3.1.10 (preprint 3.10); Theorem 3.3.2's (preprint 3.29) statement
    "a uniquely determined sc⁰-solution germ" leaves the uniqueness region implicit (Remark 3.3.8 (preprint 3.36)
    makes it explicit: `|w|₀ ≤ τ₀`; in Lean `O 0`, `Polyfold.theorem_3_3_2`).
11. *(Superseded by items 40–45: Definitions 3.1.3, 3.1.6, 3.1.11, 3.1.16 (preprint 3.3, 3.6, 3.11, 3.14) and Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15) are now
    formalized in `StrongBundleSections.lean`, the global Theorem 3.1.13 (preprint 3.12) and Corollary 3.1.15 (preprint 3.13) in
    `SectionCompactness.lean` (`Polyfold.theorem_3_1_13_preprint`, `corollary_3_1_15_preprint`,
    `corollary_3_1_15_section`). The item records the state when §3.3 was formalized.)*
    **Theorem 3.1.13 (preprint 3.12), Corollary 3.1.15 (preprint 3.13), Definition 3.1.16 (preprint 3.14), Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15), Lemmas 3.1.19–3.1.20 (preprint 3.16–3.17) are global
    statements** about sc-Fredholm germs and sections of tame strong bundles over M-polyfolds
    (Definitions 2.6.4–2.6.6, 3.1.3–3.1.6, 3.1.11 (preprint 2.50–2.52, 3.3–3.6, 3.11)), whose definitions are not formalized (Chapter 2 §2.6 (preprint §2.5) is
    definitions only, without strong bundle charts). What is formalized (`LocalCompactness.lean`) is
    the local content of Theorem 3.1.13 (preprint 3.12) and Corollary 3.1.15 (preprint 3.13), which is Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40) of §3.5 together with
    a compactness argument: `Polyfold.theorem_3_5_1_compactness`, `theorem_3_5_1_regularity`,
    `theorem_3_1_13_local` (for a basic germ, Definition 3.1.7 (preprint 3.7) = `Polyfold.IsBasicGerm`, plus an
    sc⁺-germ), `corollary_3_1_15_local`. Definition 3.1.16 (preprint 3.14), Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15) and Lemma 3.1.20 (preprint 3.17) are **not**
    formalized; the latter two need fillers (Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4), with the linearization condition (3)),
    the extension `s̃ = s ∘ r` of an sc⁺-section (Lemma 3.1.19 (preprint 3.16)) and the bookkeeping of
    Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) (`(g + s̃) − (s̃ + t₀) = g − t₀`), on top of strong bundle charts.
12. **Theorem 3.1.13's (preprint 3.12) compactness is not in Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40)**, of which the text says Theorem 3.1.13 (preprint 3.12) is "an
    immediate consequence": Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40) states only the regularity `cl(S ∩ O(m)) ⊆ C_m`.
    Compactness of `cl(S ∩ O(i))` in `E_i` needs, besides, that the solutions in `O(i)` lift to
    level `i + 1` with `|w|_{i+1}` bounded (so that their `W_i`-parts are precompact, by the
    compactness of `W_{i+1} → W_i`), that the solution set is closed, and that the level-`i` lift is
    continuous for the level-`0` topology (the "convergence upgrade" in the proof of Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40)).
    The sets `O(i)` are then the balls of radius `τ_{i+1}`, one level ahead of the text's `O(i)`
    (`Polyfold.IsSc0ContractionGerm.isCompact_lift_image`).
13. **The induction step of Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40) ("the induction step is now clear and the further details
    are left to the reader", p. 122 (preprint p. 98))** is not a repetition of the level-`1` step: the estimate
    `|P ∘ s(a, w)|_{m+1} ≤ τ'_{m+1}/4` needs `(a, w)` small on level `m` (`s : U_m → W_{m+1}` is
    continuous on level `m`), while `O(m+1)` controls only `|a|₀, |w|₀`. For a solution, smallness
    on level `m` follows from the continuity at `0` of the level-`m` lift
    `(a, w) ↦ (a, δ_m(a, P∘s(a, w)))` for the level-`0` topology, which is the same continuity that
    gives the convergence upgrade; so existence, bound and continuity of the lifts must be proved
    together by induction (`Polyfold.IsSc0ContractionGerm.exists_lift`). The text's `(1₃)`, with
    `|w|₀ ≤ τ₁`, is correct for `m = 1` only because `s` is sc⁺ on level `0`.
14. **Hypotheses of Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40) actually used**: of `f = h + s` only the `W`-component matters, and
    of it only that `B` is sc⁰ with the contraction estimates of Definition 3.1.7 (preprint 3.7) (not sc-smooth),
    that `s` is sc⁰ into `W¹` (the sc⁺ property level by level) with `s(0) = 0`, and that `C̃` is
    closed (true for partial quadrants; needed for the solution set to be closed in `E₀`, the text
    takes closures in `C₀`). The `ℝᴺ`-component of `f` only shrinks the solution set. The contraction
    radius on level `m + 1` must be chosen so that the level-`0` image of the level-`(m+1)` ball
    lies in the level-`0` contraction ball (the text's `τ'_1 < τ_0/c_1`), so that the level-`(m+1)`
    fixed point and the given solution agree by the level-`0` uniqueness (the text's (43)).
15. **Corollary 3.1.15 (preprint 3.13)** says "if `f(x_k) = 0` and `x_k → x` in `X₀`, then `x_k ∈ X_m` for `k` large and
    `x_k → x` in `X_m`" for the germ `(f, x₀)`; the local statement at `x₀` gives this for `x = x₀`
    (`Polyfold.corollary_3_1_15_local`, with `x_k → 0`), or for `x` in the neighbourhood `O(m)` of
    Theorem 3.1.13 (preprint 3.12) — for an arbitrary limit `x` it needs the germ property at `x` (for an sc-Fredholm
    section, Definition 3.1.16 (preprint 3.14), at every smooth point) *(book 2017: unchanged, Corollary 3.1, p. 65)* *(book 2021: corrected, Corollary 3.1.15, p. 97, takes the limit to be the centre `x₀`)*.
16. The "parametrized version of Banach's fixed point theorem" (proofs of Theorems 3.3.2 and 3.5.1 (preprint 3.29 and 3.40)):
    `Polyfold.exists_fixedPoint_continuousOn` (continuity of the fixed point in the parameter from
    the uniform contraction constant and the continuity of the map in the parameter), stated and
    proved since Mathlib has `ContractingWith.fixedPoint` without the parameter dependence.
17. **Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4) (filling), Lemmas 3.1.19–3.1.20 (preprint 3.16–3.17)** are formalized for the principal parts of the
    sections (`Polyfold.IsFillerOf`, `Polyfold.lemma_3_1_19`, `Polyfold.lemma_3_1_20` in
    `Filler.lean`): conditions (1)–(3) of Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4), with the map `y ↦ [1 − ρ(r(y))]g(y)`
    required sc¹ so that the linearization in (3) exists (the text presupposes it), and Lemma 3.1.20 (preprint 3.17)
    as "the three conditions pass from `(f, g)` to `(f + s, g + s ∘ r)`", which is what the text's
    proof checks ((1) and (2) from Lemma 3.1.19 (preprint 3.16), (3) because the two maps agree on `U`, so their
    linearizations at `0` agree by the uniqueness of derivatives on `U₁`). **Weaker than the text**:
    the regularity statements (`g` an sc-smooth section, `s̃ = s ∘ r` an sc⁺-section, Lemma 3.1.19 (preprint 3.16),
    hence `g + s̃` sc-smooth) are not included — they need the pairing and sum rules of the
    sc-calculus for maps on sets, available so far for germs only (`Polyfold.IsSckGerm.pair`).
    *Resolved at the level of Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15)*: the sum rule on sets was added
    (`Polyfold.IsScSmooth.add`, item 42), and `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScFredholmGerm.sectionAdd`
    proves `s̃ = ŝ₁ ∘ r` sc-smooth into `F¹` and `g + s̃` sc-smooth on `U` before applying
    `lemma_3_1_20`, so nothing of Lemmas 3.1.19–3.1.20 (preprint 3.16–3.17) is missing where they are used; `lemma_3_1_20`
    itself remains the statement about the three filler conditions.
    Lemma 3.1.19 (2) (preprint 3.16), `R(r(u), s̃(u)) = s(r(u))`, is "`R` fixes `K`" and uses that an sc⁺-section is
    a section (`(x, s(x)) ∈ K` on `O`), the hypothesis `hsK`. The text's "`ρ(u) : F → F` is a bounded
    linear operator" is linearity from Definition 2.6.1 (preprint 2.47) and continuity from `R` being sc⁰ on level
    `0` (`Polyfold.StrongRetr.ρCLM`).

Found while formalizing §3.2 and Appendix 3.8.1 (good position, Proposition 3.1.25 (preprint 3.22)) in
`GoodPosition.lean`.

18. **Proposition 3.1.25 (preprint 3.22) is proved without the extreme-ray lemmas.** The text's proof (Appendix
    3.8.1) rests on Lemma 3.8.1 (preprint 3.62) (Krein–Milman for closed convex cones) and Lemma 3.8.2 (preprint 3.63) (a cone with
    nonempty interior is a quadrant iff it has `dim N` extreme rays), both cited from [21] without
    proof, and on Lemmas 3.8.3, 3.8.9–3.8.11 (preprint 3.64, 3.66–3.68). The Lean proof (`Polyfold.exists_quadrantNormalForm`,
    `Polyfold.proposition_3_1_25`) keeps the text's two cases (Lemma 3.8.11 (preprint 3.68): `Ñ ∩ (ℝ^{Σᶜ} ⊕ W) = {0}`
    or `Ñ ⊆ ℝ^{Σᶜ} ⊕ W`) but needs only Lemma 3.8.8 (preprint 3.65) (`N^⊥ ⊆ ℝ^{Σᶜ} ⊕ W`, `Polyfold.lemma_3_8_8`)
    and the resulting surjectivity of `Q : N → ℝ^Σ` (`Polyfold.sigmaCoord_surjective`): in the
    first case `N ∩ C = {x ∈ N | x_i ≥ 0 for i ∈ Σ}` is shown directly by a segment argument
    (`Polyfold.mem_quadCone_of_vanIdx`: the first point of `N ∩ C` on the segment from such an `x`
    to an interior point is nonzero, hence has positive coordinates outside `Σ`, so it was not the
    first) and `N ≅ ℝ^Σ × ker Q` carries `N ∩ C` onto `[0,∞)^Σ × ker Q`; in the second case
    (`Σ = ∅`) a line argument gives `dim N = 1` (`Polyfold.quadrantNormalForm_of_vanIdx_empty`).
    The case `N ∩ C = N` (all coordinates vanish on `N`, e.g. `N ⊆ W`), not singled out by the
    text's case distinction, is treated separately (`k = 0`).
     (2026-11-12) The extreme-ray lemmas are now formalized as well, though still not used by this proof: Lemmas
     3.8.1–3.8.3 (`lemma_3_8_1` for `P ≠ {0}`, item 386; `lemma_3_8_2`, `lemma_3_8_3`) and Lemmas 3.8.9–3.8.11
     (`lemma_3_8_9_sc`, `lemma_3_8_10`, `lemma_3_8_11`) (rows V3.123–V3.125; gaps G.25, G.26 closed).
19. **Definition 3.1.24 (preprint 3.21) asks for an sc-complement; only the algebraic splitting `E₀ = N ⊕ P` is
    used.** Neither the sc-structure nor the closedness of the good complement enters
    Proposition 3.1.25 (preprint 3.22), Lemma 3.5.9 (preprint 3.45), Lemma 3.8.8 (preprint 3.65) or Proposition 3.8.12 (preprint 3.69); the Lean
    `Polyfold.IsGoodComplement` requires `IsCompl N P` only (the text's remark after Definition
    3.1.24 (preprint 3.21) already allows a "merely topological complement"). Lemma 3.8.9 (preprint 3.66) (`Ñ` in good position with
    complement `(N ∩ W) ⊕ N^⊥`) is not needed. Typo p. 102 (preprint p. 77): "finite dimensional sunspace" *(book 2017: corrected, p. 69)* *(book 2021: corrected, p. 102)*.
    *(Revised in item 210: this holds for good position as a hypothesis; as a conclusion
    (Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54)) the algebraic notion is weaker than the text's, and the sc-complement is
    now proved there, `GoodPositionSc.lean`.)*
20. **Proposition 3.8.12 (preprint 3.69)** is stated in the model `E = ℝⁿ ⊕ W`, `C = [0,∞)ⁿ ⊕ W`, as in the text;
    (2) `d_{N∩C}(x) = dim N − dim(N ∩ W)` is formalized additively
    (`Polyfold.proposition_3_8_12`), with `N ∩ W = ker(pr_{ℝⁿ} ∘ ι_N)`. The proof is read off the
    normal form: for `x ∈ N ∩ C ∖ N ∩ W` the vanishing coordinates of `e(x) ∈ ℝᵏ` are those of `x`
    (the coordinates outside `Σ` are positive), and on `N ∩ W` the `ℝᵏ`-component of `e` vanishes
    with `k = dim N − dim(N ∩ W)`. The text's proof uses the explicit basis `e^j = (a^j, b^j, w^j)`
    with `b^j_i > 0` of the complement `Ñ`; in Lean this is the right inverse `g` of `Q`.
21. **Lemma 3.5.9 (preprint 3.45)** is stated for `Tϕ(0)` with `Tϕ(0)C = C'`; it holds for any continuous linear
    isomorphism `S : E₀ → E'₀` with `S(C) = C'`, with `ε' = ε/(‖S‖‖S⁻¹‖ + 1)`
    (`Polyfold.IsGoodComplement.map`, `Polyfold.IsInGoodPosition.map`; the interior condition is
    transported along the homeomorphism `N ≅ S(N)`).

22. **Theorem 3.8.22 (1) (preprint 3.78) omits `f(k + τ(k)) = 0`, and (3) omits `k + y ∈ U`.** The first is the
    content of the theorem (the text's `τ(k) = B(k, τ(k))`), the second is needed for `f(k + y)` to
    be defined; both are included in `Polyfold.theorem_3_8_22`. The theorem is proved for a
    finite-dimensional `V` in place of `ℝⁿ`, `f` into any normed space, and `C^j` in Mathlib's sense
    (equal to Definition 3.8.14 (preprint 3.71) on relatively open subsets of partial quadrants by
    `Polyfold.isSc1_iff_contDiffOn_of_isRelOpenInQuadrant`).
23. **Theorem 3.8.22 (preprint 3.78) uses only the convexity of `C` and the nonemptiness of its interior**, not the
    partial quadrant structure (`Polyfold.ContractionData.exists_solution` is stated for a convex
    `C`); the quadrant enters only through the good position hypothesis, which is what makes
    `k + y ∈ C` for `k ∈ K ∩ C`, `|y| ≤ ε|k|` (Lemma 3.8.24 (preprint 3.80)) and gives `K ∩ C` a nonempty interior
    in `K` (needed for `Dτ(0)` to be meaningful).
24. **Lemma 3.8.26's (preprint 3.82) induction (`f ↦ f⁽¹⁾`, "on a possibly smaller neighbourhood `V` of `0`") is
    replaced by bootstrapping the derivative formula** `Dτ(k) = (1 − D₂B(k, τ k))⁻¹ D₁B(k, τ k)`:
    the right-hand side is `Φ ∘ (id, τ)` with `Φ` of class `C^{j−1}` on the region `R` of Lemma
    3.8.23 (preprint 3.79) (inversion is smooth on units), so `τ ∈ C^i` implies `τ ∈ C^{i+1}` for `i < j`
    (`Polyfold.Radii.contDiffOn_τ`), and `τ` is `C^j` on the whole `V₀ = {k ∈ K ∩ C | |k| < a}`
    without shrinking.
25. **Lemma 3.8.25's (preprint 3.81) estimate `|τ(k) − τ(k₀)| ≤ ε|k − k₀|`** uses the point `(k, τ(k₀))`, which lies
    in the domain only when `|τ(k₀)| ≤ ε|k|`, i.e. for `k` not too small relative to `k₀` (for
    `k₀ ≠ 0` and `k → 0` it fails). The Lean proof (`Polyfold.Radii.norm_τ_sub_le`) treats the case
    `|k₀| > 2|k|` through `|τ(k)| + |τ(k₀)| ≤ (ε/2)(|k| + |k₀|)` and gets the Lipschitz constant
    `1 + 2ε`. Since the fixed-point sets `X_k = B̄_Y(ε|k|)` depend on `k`, the parametrized Banach
    fixed point theorem of Theorems 3.3.2 (preprint 3.29)/3.40 (`Polyfold.exists_fixedPoint_continuousOn`, fixed
    set) does not apply and the continuity is proved by hand, as in the text.

Found while formalizing §3.1 for sections of strong bundles over M-polyfolds (Definitions 3.1.3,

40. **Tameness is not used in Definitions 3.1.3–3.1.16 (preprint 3.3–3.14) or in Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15).** The text states
    Definition 3.1.16 (preprint 3.14) and Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15) for a *tame* strong bundle (over a tame M-polyfold); nothing
    in the definitions of a filled version, of an sc-Fredholm germ or in the proof of Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15)
    uses the tameness of the retractions. `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScFredholmSection` and
    `Polyfold.theorem_3_1_18_preprint` are stated for any strong bundle (`Polyfold.StrongBundle`), hence for
    tame ones. Tameness enters only with the boundary behaviour (good position, §3.6).
41. **"A strong bundle chart" in Definitions 3.1.3, 3.1.6 and 3.1.11 (preprint 3.3, 3.6 and 3.11) must mean a chart compatible with
    the atlas, not a member of it** (`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsChart`): a chart of the atlas need
    not be centred (`φ(x₀) = 0`), and the notions must not depend on the atlas within its
    equivalence class. The price is that the local representatives of the sections have to be
    sc-smooth in every compatible chart: for an sc-smooth section this is Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14) as it
    stands (`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScSmoothSection.isScSmoothRetractMap`); for an sc⁺-section
    (sc-smooth into `Y[1]`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScPlusSection` is stated in the charts of the
    atlas) it is the change of chart `(Φ ∘ Φ'⁻¹)[1]` on `K[1]`, which is exactly the compatibility
    on `[1]` required in Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50) (`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScPlusSection.isScSmoothRetractMap_one`,
    together with the locality of sc-smoothness between retracts). This is the first place where
    the `[1]`-compatibility of Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50) is actually needed.
42. **Proof of Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15), "`f + s` is an sc-smooth section which is also regularizing".** Both
    clauses are silent in the text. Sc-smoothness is the sum rule of the sc-calculus in a chart
    (`Polyfold.IsScSmooth.add`: pairing followed by the sc-operator `F ⊕ F → F`, not stated in
    Chapter 1), applied to `z ↦ (z, f̂(z) + ŝ(z))`, which lands in `K` because `K[1] ⊆ K` and the
    fibres of `K = {(u, h) | u ∈ O, ρ(u)h = h}` are linear (`Polyfold.StrongBundleChart.add_mem_K`);
    continuity of `f + s` is read off the same representative
    (`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScSmoothSection.sectionAdd`). Regularizing: `s(x) ∈ Y_{m,m+1}` for
    `x ∈ X_m` because the representative `O → K[1]` of `s` preserves the levels
    (`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScPlusSection.snd_mem_range`), and `Y_{m,m+1}` is closed under the
    fibrewise subtraction `f(x) = (f + s)(x) − s(x)` (`Φ` is linear on the fibres;
    `Polyfold.StrongBundle.regularizing_sectionAdd`). The sum `f + s` itself needs the vector space
    structure of the fibres `P⁻¹(x)` (`Polyfold.sectionAdd`); in a chart `(f + s)^ = f̂ + ŝ`
    (`Polyfold.StrongBundleChart.principal_sectionAdd`).
43. **Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) as formalized** (`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScFredholmGerm`): the filled
    version `g` is sc-smooth on the whole `U` of the chart (the text's germ "near `0`" is recovered
    by shrinking the chart), a local sc⁺-section is a map `s : U → F₁` sc-smooth into `F¹`, and
    "`Ψ ∘ (g − s) ∘ ψ⁻¹` is a basic germ" is `(Ψ(u, g(u) − s(u)))₂ = h(ψ(u))` for `u ∈ U` near
    `0`, with `Ψ` a strong bundle isomorphism `U ◁ F → U' ◁ F'` (strong bundle maps both ways,
    `Polyfold.IsStrongBundleIso`), `ψ(0) = 0`, `U'` relatively open in `C̃ ⊕ W` (`C̃` a partial
    quadrant of a finite-dimensional space) and `h` a basic germ on a germ of neighbourhoods
    `G ⊆ U'` (`Polyfold.IsConjugateToBasicGerm`). The text's `C' = Tψ(0)C` (proof of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54))
    is not imposed. In the proof of Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15) the identity `(g + t̃) − (t̃ + t₀) = g − t₀` holds
    on `U` only (`t̃ = t ∘ r` with `ι t̃₁ = t̃` needs `r(u) ∈ O`), which is why the conjugation
    condition is stated for `u ∈ U` (`Polyfold.IsConjugateToBasicGerm.congr`); the filler
    condition (1) of Lemma 3.1.20 (preprint 3.17) likewise only involves `f̂` on `O` (`Polyfold.IsFillerOf.congr_left`).
    *(Shrinking the chart does not recover a germ whose levels shrink with `m`; the project's
    notion is stricter than the text's: items 220–221; the text's germ reading and the reduction
    to it, items 260–264.)*

44. **Theorem 3.1.13 (preprint 3.12), "an immediate consequence of Theorem 3.40".** Of the hypotheses "`f` an
    sc-smooth section of the tame strong bundle" only `P ∘ f = id` is used
    (`Polyfold.theorem_3_1_13_preprint`); the regularity enters through the filled version `g` of Definition
    3.1.11 (preprint 3.11), tameness not at all. The passage from the local statement (`theorem_3_1_13_local_subset`,
    Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40) for any subset of the solution set) to the M-polyfold needs: (i) the
    identification of the zeros of `f` near `x₀` with those of `h + t`, `t = Ψ[1]_*(s)`, through
    the chart, the filler ((1) and (2) of Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4)) and the fibre maps of `Ψ`, which are
    linear bijections (`Polyfold.IsStrongBundleIso.snd_eq_zero_iff`); (ii) `t` is an sc⁺-germ
    because `Ψ[1]` is sc-smooth (Definition 2.6.1 (preprint 2.47)) and `t(0) = 0` from `s(0) = g(0) = f̂(0) = 0`;
    (iii) the `E₀`-closure of the solution set must stay inside the chart and inside the
    neighbourhood where the filler and conjugation identities hold: the `O(i)` of Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40) are
    intersected with a small ball (the closure of a subset of the solution set stays compact);
    (iv) the closure consists of zeros of `g` in `U`, hence lies in `O` by condition (2) of the
    filler (`Polyfold.eq_of_mem_closure_of_continuousOn`); (v) the `X₀`-closure of a subset of a
    chart domain can leave the domain, so the compactness in `E₀` is used first to see that it
    does not; (vi) "a compact subset of `X_i`" needs the inverse chart `O_i → X_i` to be
    continuous for the level topology of `X_i`, i.e. the sc⁰ transition maps on level `i`
    (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.continuousOn_levelChartSymm`, the paragraph after Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14) for
    every `m`, formalized so far for `m = 1` only). The statement is formalized as
    `closure {x ∈ O(i) | f(x) = 0} = ι_i(K_i)` with `K_i ⊆ X_i` compact.
45. **Corollary 3.1.15 (preprint 3.13), "`x_k → x` in `X_m`".** For the base point `x = x₀` of the germ
    (`Polyfold.corollary_3_1_15_preprint`) and for an sc-Fredholm section with any limit `x` of zeros
    (`Polyfold.corollary_3_1_15_section`; the limit is a zero since the principal part is
    continuous, and a smooth point since `f` is regularizing — cf. item 15). The convergence in
    `X_m` is stated for lifts `y_k ∈ X_m` of the `x_k` (`k` large) converging to the lift of `x`.
    Since `X_m` is not known to be first countable (its metrizability is Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16), which the
    Lean proof does not use), the convergence is proved from the compactness of Theorem 3.1.13 (preprint 3.12) by a
    cluster-point argument (`Polyfold.tendsto_of_isCompact_of_tendsto_map`: a sequence in a
    compact set whose image under the continuous injection `X_m → X` converges, converges), not
    by extracting subsequences as in the local proof.

Found while formalizing Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9) and Proposition 3.1.10 (preprint 3.10) in `BasicGermLinearization.lean`.

46. **Proposition 3.1.10 (preprint 3.10), "`Df(0)` is an sc⁺-perturbation of the operator (32)".** The verification
    that `S = Df(0) − T₀` is an sc⁺-operator is not in the text. It needs: the `ℝᴺ`-component of
    `Df(0)` is sc⁺ because `ℝᴺ` has all levels equal; `D₁B(0)` is sc⁺ because
    `D₁B(0)δa = DB(0)(δa, 0)` with `(δa, 0)` a smooth point and `DB(0)` an sc-operator (so the
    values lie in `W_∞`), and its level maps `E_m → W_{m+1}` are continuous because they factor
    through `DB(0)_{m+1} : E_{m+1} → W_{m+1}` and `δa ↦ (δa, 0)` (no finite dimensionality of
    `ℝⁿ` is needed for this); `Ds(0)` is sc⁺ because an sc⁺-germ is sc¹ into `W¹`, so `Ds(0)`
    is an sc-operator `E → (ℝᴺ ⊕ W)¹`; and `D₂B(0) = 0` by Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9). The silent step behind
    the first two: the finite-rank terms of `Df(0)` (the `ℝᴺ`-component `(1 − P)Df(0)` and the
    term `D₁B(0)` through `ℝⁿ`) are sc⁺ because `Dh(0)` is an sc-operator at the smooth point `0`
    (the remark after Proposition 1.2.1 (preprint 1.16)); the text writes `Df(0)` as an sc⁺-perturbation of (32)
    without saying so. In Lean the operator `S`
    is built level by level (`Polyfold.proposition_3_1_10_scPlus`) and
    `Polyfold.proposition_3_1_10` is `Df(0) = T₀ + S` with Proposition 1.1.11 (preprint 1.10) and its index statement
    (`proposition_1_1_11_index`). The derivative of `h` at `0` is an sc-operator by
    `Polyfold.IsSc1GermWith.isScOperator_deriv_zero` (the remark after Proposition 1.2.1 (preprint 1.16), for
    germs, at the smooth point `0`); the identity `Df(0) = Dh(0) + ιDs(0)` and
    `pr_W Dh(0) = pr_W − DB(0)` use the uniqueness of derivatives within `U₁` and the density of
    `E₁` in `E₀`. The hypotheses are: `h` a basic germ, `s` sc¹ into `(ℝᴺ ⊕ W)¹`, and `f = h + s`
    sc¹ (the text: sc-smooth). **Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9) is proved at `(0, 0)` only**
    (`Polyfold.IsSc0ContractionGerm.deriv_zero_snd`, from the difference quotients along
    `t ↦ (0, tζ)`, `ζ ∈ W₁`, and density), which is what Proposition 3.1.10's (preprint 3.10) first statement
    needs; the second statement of Proposition 3.1.10 (preprint 3.10) (`Df(a, w)` Fredholm of index `n − N` on level
    `m` for `(a, w)` small) is **not formalized** (it needs Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9) near `(0, 0)`, available in
    `ContractionGerm.lean` for the working form of a contraction germ with `ε = 1/2`).

Found while formalizing §3.4 (Theorem 3.4.2 (preprint 3.38), weak stability of basic germs) in `BasicClass.lean`.

60. **The coordinate change of Theorem 3.4.2 (preprint 3.38) is linear.** The sc-diffeomorphism `ϕ` of the
    statement is `ψ(a, w) = ((a, (1 − P₁)w), P₁w)` and the fibre map is
    `Ψ(δa, δw) = ((δa, (1 − P₂)δw), L⁻¹P₂δw)`, both linear sc-isomorphisms built from the
    sc-splittings `W = C ⊕ X = R ⊕ Z` of `1 + A`, `A = D₂s(0)`. In Lean the strong bundle
    isomorphism is therefore not a general `IsStrongBundleIso` but the pair of sc-operators
    `Polyfold.StabilityData.split`/`glue` (base, inverse to each other) and
    `Polyfold.StabilityData.fiber`/`fiberInv` (fibre); the push-forward
    `(Φ_*(f + s))¹ = Ψ ∘ (f + s)¹ ∘ ψ⁻¹` is `Polyfold.StabilityData.pushMap`, a basic germ with
    contraction map `B̂ = L⁻¹P₂(B − S) ∘ ψ⁻¹` (`Polyfold.StabilityData.pushB`,
    `Polyfold.theorem_3_4_2`). The text's `τ : Z → C` (so that the new finite-dimensional target
    is `ℝᴺ ⊕ C`) is not applied: the new target is `(ℝᴺ ⊕ Z) ⊕ X¹`, the new source
    `(C̃ ⊕ C) ⊕ X¹`. A consequence for §3.5: since `ψ` is linear, the solution sets of `f + s`
    and of its push-forward correspond under a linear map
    (`Polyfold.StabilityData.pushMap_eq_zero_iff`), and good position is carried by Lemma 3.5.9 (preprint 3.45)
    in its linear form.
61. **"The index raise by 1" is a change of sc-structure.** The new germ is a germ on the shifted
    spaces: parameters `(a, c) ∈ C̃ ⊕ C`, fibre `X¹` with levels `X_{m+1}`
    (`Polyfold.StabilityData.E'`), and its germ of neighbourhoods is `ψ(U_{m+1})`
    (`Polyfold.StabilityData.pushGerm`). The sc-smoothness of `(f + s)¹` on the shifted germ is
    Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17) for germs (`Polyfold.IsSckGerm.shift`), and `f + s` is sc-smooth by the
    pairing and operator rules (`Polyfold.StabilityData.fsum_isScSmoothGerm`); the text says
    nothing about either.
62. **"`S` is an arbitrarily small contraction on every level `m ≥ 1`"** (preprint p. 91) needs more than
    `D₂S(0, 0) = 0`: on level `m + 1` the map `s : U_{m+1} → W_{m+1}` is `C¹` with derivative
    continuous in the operator norm (Proposition 1.2.1 (preprint 1.16) for germs, the compact-open lemma
    `Polyfold.IsSc1GermWith.continuousOn_levelDeriv_clm`), so that `‖D₂S(a, w)‖_{m+1} ≤ ε` for
    `(a, w)` small on level `m + 1`, and then the mean value inequality on a ball in `W_{m+1}`
    for fixed `a` (`Polyfold.scPlusRemainder_contraction`). The partial derivative in `a` of `S`
    does not vanish and plays no role. The operator `A = D₂s(0)` is an sc⁺-operator because its
    level maps are the level operators of Proposition 1.2.1 (preprint 1.16) at the smooth point `0`
    (`Polyfold.scPlusOfDeriv`).
63. **Hypotheses of Theorem 3.4.2 (preprint 3.38) actually used.** Of the sc⁺-section `s` only its `W`-component
    enters the contraction normal form (the `ℝᴺ`-component is carried along in the new
    finite-dimensional component); `s` must be sc-smooth into `W¹` for the push-forward to be
    sc-smooth. Of the basic germ `f` the contraction map `B` is used only through Definition 3.1.7 (preprint 3.7)
    (sc⁰ with the contraction estimates). "`1 + A` is a sc⁺-perturbation of the identity and hence
    sc-Fredholm by Proposition 1.10. Because `A` is level wise compact, the index `ind(1 + A)` is
    equal to `0`" is Proposition 1.1.11 (preprint 1.10) applied to the identity (`Polyfold.isScFredholm_id`, the
    trivial splitting) and `ind(1 + A) = ind(1) = 0` (`Polyfold.proposition_1_1_11_index`,
    `Polyfold.scIndex_id`); the equality `dim C = dim Z` (hence `n − N = n' − N'`) is
    `Polyfold.StabilityData.finrank_Cs_eq_finrank_Zs`. Corollary 3.4.3 (preprint 3.39) (composition with a given
    conjugation to a basic germ) is not formalized in `BasicClass.lean`.

Found while formalizing §3.5 (Lemma 3.5.5 (preprint 3.42), Theorem 3.5.6 (preprint 3.43), Lemmas 3.5.8, 3.5.10 (preprint 3.44, 3.46), Theorem 3.5.11 (preprint Corollary 3.47)) in
`LocalSolvability.lean`.

64. **Lemma 3.5.10 (preprint 3.46) without the intermediate complement `Y₀`.** The text (Appendix 3.8.3 (preprint 3.8.2)) picks a good
    complement `Y'` of `K' = {(α, Dδ(0)α)}` in `ℝⁿ' ⊕ W`, a complement `Y₀` of `Y' ∩ W` in `Y'`,
    and projects `Y₀` to `ℝⁿ'`. In Lean (`Polyfold.lemma_3_5_10`) one takes `Z' := pr_{ℝⁿ'}(Y')`,
    which already satisfies `ℝⁿ' = K̃ + Z'`, chooses `Z ⊆ Z'` with `ℝⁿ' = K̃ ⊕ Z` and a linear
    right inverse `ρ : Z' → Y'` of the projection; the good-complement estimate for `(K̃, Z)` with
    constant `ε' = ε/(‖ρ‖ + 1)` follows from the one for `(K', Y')` applied to `(α, Dδ(0)α)` and
    `ρ(z)`. `Z ⊕ W` is then a good complement of `K'` (`Polyfold.lemma_3_5_10_isInGoodPosition`
    records the good position of `K̃`).
65. **Lemma 3.5.5 (preprint 3.42) enters Theorem 3.5.6 (preprint 3.43) as a hypothesis.** Theorem 3.5.6 (preprint 3.43) is stated in the text for
    `g = Φ_*(f + s)`, and its proof uses Lemma 3.5.5 (preprint 3.42) ("solutions of `g = 0` near `0` on level `0`
    lie on level `1` and are small there"), whose proof is Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40) for `f + s`. In Lean
    `Polyfold.theorem_3_5_6` is stated for an abstract sc-smooth germ `g` whose index-raised germ
    `g¹` is basic (`Polyfold.ShiftedBasicData`) with this regularity as the explicit hypothesis
    `hreg` (for every `ε > 0` there is `r > 0`: a zero `x` of `g` with `|x|₀ < r` has `x₂ = ι(w₁)`
    with `|w₁|₁ < ε`). For the push-forward of Theorem 3.4.2 (preprint 3.38) the hypothesis is
    `Polyfold.StabilityData.lemma_3_5_5`, proved from the lifts of Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40)
    (`Polyfold.IsSc0ContractionGerm.exists_lift` at level `1`), their continuity at `0`, and the
    linearity of `ψ` on level `1`.
66. **A gap in the proof of Theorem 3.5.6 (3) (preprint 3.43): the `K'`-component of a solution lies in `C'`.** The
    text writes a solution `x = (a, w)` as `a = k + z` with `k ∈ K̃`, `z ∈ Z` and applies the
    uniqueness clause of Theorem 3.8.22 (preprint 3.78) to conclude `z = σ(k)`; that clause needs `k ∈ C̃`, which is
    not verified. It holds because `z` is small compared with `k`: from `H(a) = 0`, `H(0) = 0`,
    `DH(0)k = 0` one gets `|DH(0)z| = o(|a|)`, and `DH(0)` is injective on `Z`, so `|z| ≤ ε|k|`
    for `a` close to `0`, and then the good-complement property of `(K̃, Z)` gives `k ∈ C̃` from
    `k + z = a ∈ C̃` (`Polyfold.exists_proj_mem_of_eq_zero`, stated for any map differentiable
    at `0` on a partial quadrant).
67. **"The map `H` restricted to `U'_i` is of class `C^{i−1}`."** `H(a) = pr_{ℝᴺ}(g(a, δ(a)))` is
    `C^j` on a neighbourhood of `0` in `C̃` because `δ` is `C^j` into `W_{2j}` (Corollary 3.3.7 (2) (preprint 3.34)
    for the index-raised germ, whose solution germ on level `m` takes values in `W_{m+1}`) and
    `g : U_{2j} → ℝᴺ ⊕ W_j` is `C^j` (Proposition 1.2.3 (preprint 1.18) for germs,
    `Polyfold.IsSckGerm.contDiffOn_levels`); see `Polyfold.ShiftedBasicData.H_contDiffOn`. The
    text's `U'_i` is an `i`-dependent neighbourhood; in Lean a single `C¹`-neighbourhood `V₁`
    carries the kernel and the derivative (`Polyfold.ShiftedBasicData.Deriv`).
68. **Lemma 3.5.8 (preprint 3.44), "recalling from Lemma 3.9 that `D₂B(0) = 0`".** Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9) gives `D₂B(0) = 0` for
    the basic germ `g¹`, i.e. on level `1` (`Polyfold.IsSc0ContractionGerm.deriv_zero_snd`); the
    kernel of `Dg(0)` is computed on level `0`. The identity `pr_W Dg(0)(0, ζ) = ζ` for all
    `ζ ∈ W₀` follows from the one for `ζ ∈ W₁` by the density of `W₁` in `W₀`
    (`Polyfold.ShiftedBasicData.Deriv.snd_Dg_inr`), after which
    `ker Dg(0) = {(α, Dδ(0)α) | α ∈ ker DH(0)}` is the chain rule for `a ↦ g(a, δ(a))`
    (`Polyfold.ShiftedBasicData.Deriv.ker_Dg_eq`).
69. **Theorem 3.5.11 (preprint Corollary 3.47) does not need Theorem 3.8.15 (preprint 3.72) and Lemma 3.8.13 (preprint 3.70).** The text transports the solution
    set of `g = Φ_*(f + s)` back to `f + s` with the sc-diffeomorphism `ϕ` and justifies the good
    position of `ker D(f + s)(0)` and the form of the zero set with the degeneracy index
    (Lemma 3.8.13 (preprint 3.70), Theorem 3.8.15 (preprint 3.72)). Since `ϕ` is linear (Finding 60), `ker D(f + s)(0) = ψ⁻¹(K')`,
    its good complement is `ψ⁻¹(Y')` (Lemma 3.5.9 (preprint 3.45) in its linear form,
    `Polyfold.IsGoodComplement.map`), `V = ψ⁻¹(V')` and `σ = ψ⁻¹ ∘ τ ∘ ψ` on the kernels; the
    derivative `Dg(0)` is `Ψ ∘ D(f + s)(0) ∘ ψ⁻¹` (`Polyfold.StabilityData.scDerivGerm_pushMap₀`),
    so surjectivity and the kernels correspond (`Polyfold.theorem_3_5_11`). The finite
    dimensionality of `ker D(f + s)(0)`, needed to transport good position
    (`Polyfold.IsInGoodPosition.map`), comes from Lemma 3.5.8 (preprint 3.44).
70. **Theorem 3.5.6 (1) (preprint 3.43), "`τ` is sc-smooth"** (`Polyfold.ShiftedBasicData.Sol.exists_contDiffOn_level`,
    the last clause of `Polyfold.theorem_3_5_6_sc_smooth` and of `Polyfold.theorem_3_5_11_sc_smooth`;
    `Polyfold.theorem_3_5_6`, `Polyfold.theorem_3_5_11` are the statements without it): for every `k ≥ 1`
    there are a relatively open neighbourhood `V_k ⊆ V` of `0` in `K' ∩ C'` and a `C^k`-map
    `τ_k : V_k → E_k = ℝⁿ' ⊕ W_k` with `ι_k ∘ τ_k = τ` on `V_k`. The text's "`τ` is sc-smooth"
    is read in this level-wise sense (Corollary 3.3.7 (2) (preprint 3.34), Proposition 1.2.4 (preprint 1.19) for maps from
    finite-dimensional spaces). The proof applies Theorem 3.8.22 (preprint 3.78) to the `C^k`-map `H` on `U'_k ∩ V₁`
    (Finding 67) and identifies the `C^k` solution `σ_k` with `σ` near `0` through the uniqueness
    clause (3) of Theorem 3.8.22 (preprint 3.78) (this needs `σ` continuous at `0` with `σ(0) = 0`, so that
    `|σ(y)| ≤ σ_k` and `y + σ(y) ∈ U'_k` for `y` small); the `W`-component `ι(δ(a)) − L(πy)`,
    `a = πy + σ(πy)`, lifts to `W_k` through the `C^k` lift `δ' : U'_k → W_{2k}` of `δ` and
    `L = ι_{2k} ∘ Dδ'(0)`, which follows from the uniqueness of the derivative of `ι ∘ δ` at `0`.
    The text says nothing about why the solutions produced by Theorem 3.8.22 (preprint 3.78) for the different
    `k` coincide.
71. **Corollary 3.5.3 (preprint 3.41) as formalized** (`Polyfold.StabilityData.corollary_3_5_3`, in
    `SolutionLinearization.lean`), with three simplifications of the text's proof. (a) The
    hypothesis "`f(a, w) = 0`" is used only to bring the point to level `1`: the Fredholm property
    with index `n − N` (`Polyfold.StabilityData.exists_isFredholm_Dfs'`) and the triviality of
    `ker Df(x) ∩ N` for a closed complement `N` of `ker Df(0)`
    (`Polyfold.StabilityData.exists_ker_Dfs'_inf_eq_bot`) hold for *every* `x ∈ U₁` small on
    level `1`, so `Df(x)` is a surjective Fredholm operator of index `n − N` for all such `x`;
    for zeros `x` small on level `0` the level-`1` lift is small by the continuity at `0` of the
    lifts of Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40) (`Polyfold.IsSc0ContractionGerm.exists_lift`), and the text's detour
    through "bounded on level `2`, hence convergent on level `1` by the compact embedding
    `W₂ → W₁`" is not needed. (b) "`‖D₂B(a, w)‖ ≤ ε` if `(a, w)` is sufficiently small in `E₀`"
    (Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9)) is used for `(a, w) ∈ E₁` small on level `1`
    (`Polyfold.IsSc0ContractionGerm.exists_norm_deriv_snd_le`): `B` is differentiable only as a
    map `U₁ → W₀`, so the difference quotient along `t ↦ (a, w + tζ)` needs the curve in `U₁`;
    the contraction estimate itself is the level-`0` one of Definition 3.3.1 (preprint 3.28). (c) The Fredholm
    property and the index of `Df(x)` are obtained directly, without restricting to `N`:
    `Df(x) = Df(0) + S(x) + K(x)` with `S(x)(α, ζ) = (0, −D₂B(x)ζ)` of norm `≤ ε` and `K(x)`
    compact (the finite-rank parts through `ℝⁿ` and `ℝᴺ`, and `ι(Ds(x) − Ds(0))` through the
    compact inclusion `W₁ → W₀`; `Polyfold.StabilityData.Kop_isCompactOperator`), so
    `Df(0) + S(x)` is Fredholm of the same index by the Neumann series
    (`Polyfold.isFredholm_add_of_norm_lt`, the quasi-inverse `(1 + vS)⁻¹v`) and then `K(x)` does
    not change the index (Kato IV.5.26, `Polyfold.fredholmIndex_add_isCompactOperator`);
    surjectivity follows from `dim ker Df(x) ≤ dim ker Df(0) = n − N = ind Df(x)`
    (`Polyfold.HasFiniteIndex.surjective_of_finrank_ker_le`) instead of "`Df(x)|N` has index
    `0` and is injective". In the compactness argument the Neumann series
    `ζ_k = Σ (D₂B(x_k))ˡ z_k` is replaced by `|ζ_k − z_k| = |D₂B(x_k)ζ_k| ≤ ε_k → 0`. `Df(0)` is
    Fredholm of index `n − N` by Proposition 3.1.10 (preprint 3.10) for the basic germ `h`
    (`Polyfold.proposition_3_1_10_basic_level_zero`) plus the compact `ι ∘ Ds(0)`, which avoids
    the sc⁺-operator form of `Ds(0)`.

72. **Lemma 3.7.4 (preprint 3.61), the proof** (`Polyfold.lemma_3_7_4`, for germs: `V` is a germ of relatively open
    neighbourhoods of `0` in the partial quadrant `C̃ ⊆ G` and `V ⊕ E` the product germ
    `Polyfold.ScNbhdGerm.prodFull`). Hypothesis (i) is built into the data `L : G → ScIso E F`,
    (ii) is `IsScSmoothGerm (V ⊕ E) Φ`, `Φ(v, h) = L(v)h`, and (iii) is the uniform lower bound on
    `V₀`. The sc⁰ part is the estimate
    `|L(v)⁻¹k − L(v₀)⁻¹k₀|_m ≤ c_m⁻¹(|k − k₀|_m + |(L(v₀) − L(v))h₀|_m)`, `h₀ = L(v₀)⁻¹k₀`
    (`Polyfold.famInv_isSc0Germ`). The sc¹ part needs an argument not visible in the statement:
    with `Λ(v, k) = L(v)⁻¹k`, `h = Λ(v, k)` and `w = DΛ(v, k)(δv, δk) = L(v)⁻¹(δk − D₁Φ(v, h)δv)`,
    `Λ(v', k') − Λ(v, k) − w = L(v')⁻¹[(L(v) − L(v'))w] − L(v')⁻¹r` with
    `r = Φ(v', h) − Φ(v, h) − D₁Φ(v, h)δv = o(|δv|)` (the remainder of `Φ` along the direction
    `(δv, 0)`, with the base point `h` fixed, so that only the finite-dimensional variable moves);
    the term `(L(v) − L(v'))w` is `o(|(δv, δk)|₁)` **because the increment is measured on level
    `1`**: `w/|(δv, δk)|₁` lies in the compact set `DΛ(v, k)(ι(B₁))`, `ι : F₁ → F₀` being compact,
    and `(L(v) − L(v'))u → 0` uniformly for `u` in a compact set by the joint continuity of `Φ`
    (`Polyfold.exists_forall_norm_le_of_isCompact`, `Polyfold.famInv_hasFDerivWithinAt`). The
    operator-norm continuity of `v ↦ L(v)`, which is not assumed, is thus replaced by strong
    continuity plus the compactness of the inclusion `F₁ → F₀`; the differentiability of `Λ` as a
    map `(V ⊕ F)₀ → E₀` would need the norm continuity and is not claimed. The tangent map is
    `TΛ((v, k), (δv, δk)) = (Λ(v, k), Λ(v, δk − (TΦ((v, Λ(v, k)), (δv, 0)))₂))`, a composition of
    `Λ`, `TΦ` and sc-operators, which gives sc⁰ of `TΛ` (`Polyfold.famInv_tangent_isSc0`) and the
    induction `Φ` sc^{k+1} ⇒ `Λ` sc^{k+1} from `Λ` sc^k and `TΦ` sc^k
    (`Polyfold.famInv_isSckGerm`); the sc¹ part uses no quadrant hypothesis, the induction uses
    the composition rules for germs on quadrant-like sets (`C̃` a partial quadrant).
73. **Lemmas 3.7.2 and 3.7.3 (preprint 3.59 and 3.60) in abstract form; what remains of Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58).** The two lemmas are
    sequence arguments about the family `L(b) = P ∘ Df(b)|X`, and all they use of the
    compactness property (2) of Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58) is: if `b_j → b`, `(h_j)` is bounded in `X_m` and
    `L(b_j)h_j → 0` in `Y_m`, then `(h_j)` has a convergent subsequence in `X_m`
    (`Polyfold.FamilyCompactness`; for `L = P ∘ Df|X` this follows from (2) because
    `Df(b_j)h_j − L(b_j)h_j = (1 − P)Df(b_j)h_j` lies in the finite-dimensional smooth space `A`
    and is bounded on every level). With this property, the joint continuity of `(b, h) ↦ L(b)h`
    on each level (the sc-smoothness of `(b, x) ↦ P ∘ Df(b)x`) and the injectivity of `L(0)`,
    `Polyfold.lemma_3_7_2` gives the injectivity of `L(b)` for `b` near `0` and
    `Polyfold.lemma_3_7_3` the uniform lower bounds on a compact set of parameters where the
    `L(b)_m` are injective. The text's intermediate step "`P ∘ Df(b)|X` is an injective
    sc-Fredholm operator of index `0`, hence an sc-isomorphism" (from hypothesis (1) and the
    Fredholm property of `P`) is not needed for Lemma 3.7.3 (preprint 3.60) as formalized, only for turning the
    lower bounds into the sc-isomorphisms required by Lemma 3.7.4 (preprint 3.61). Not formalized: the setup of
    Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58) (the sc-splitting `E = B ⊕ X` as coordinates `ℝⁿ ⊕ X`, the finite-dimensional
    sc-complement `A` of `Y = Df(0)X`, the index computation `ind(P ∘ Df(b)|X) = 0`), the strong
    bundle map `Φ((b, x), (c, y)) = ((b, x), (c, L(b)⁻¹y))` (Lemma 3.7.4 (preprint 3.61) gives its
    sc-smoothness), and the contraction estimate for `H(b, x) = x − L(b)⁻¹P h(b, x)` from
    condition (3), which needs the integral form of the mean value inequality
    `h(b, x) − h(b, x') = ∫₀¹ D₂f(b, tx + (1 − t)x')(x − x') dt` in `F_m` for `x, x' ∈ X_{m+1}`
    (the derivative bound (3) is in the level-`m` norm of `x − x'`, so the usual mean value
    inequality on level `m + 1` does not give the estimate) and the density of `X_{m+1}` in `X_m`.
74. **Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58) as formalized** (`Polyfold.theorem_3_7_1` in `BasicGermCriterionIndex.lean`, on
    top of `Polyfold.theorem_3_7_1_of_family` in `BasicGermCriterionProof.lean`; this completes the
    list of Finding 73). The theorem is stated in the coordinates of the text's proof
    ("we may assume that `B = ℝⁿ`, `E = ℝⁿ ⊕ X`, `C = [0,∞)ᵏ ⊕ ℝⁿ⁻ᵏ ⊕ X`, `A = ℝᴺ`"): `U` is a
    relatively open neighbourhood of `0` in the partial quadrant `C̃ ⊕ X` of `ℝⁿ ⊕ X`,
    `f : U → ℝᴺ ⊕ Y` is sc-smooth, and the hypotheses are (1) `Df(b, 0)` sc-Fredholm with index
    independent of `b` at the smooth points `(b, 0) ∈ U`, `b ∈ C̃` (the text asks this at every
    smooth point of `U`; only these points are used), (2) `P ∘ Df(0)|X : X → Y` bijective (the
    coordinate form of "`B` contains `ker Df(0)`" and "`Y = Df(0)X`") and the compactness property
    `Polyfold.CompactnessCondition`, read with the smallness of `b` uniform in the level `m`
    (`∃ r > 0, ∀ m, …`, the order of the quantifiers in the text; Lemma 3.7.3 (preprint 3.60) needs the property on
    every level on one fixed neighbourhood), (3) `Polyfold.DerivCondition`, the estimate of the
    text with both `(b, 0)` and `(b, x)` in `U` and `|x|_m < r`. The conclusion is explicit: an
    open neighbourhood `Vo` of `0` in `ℝⁿ` and the family `L(b) = P ∘ D₂f(b, 0)|X` of
    sc-isomorphisms such that `k = Φ_*(f − f(0))` is a basic germ on `O(U ∩ (Vo ⊕ X), 0)` with
    contraction map `H(b, x) = x − L(b)⁻¹Ph(b, x)`, the fibre map
    `Φ((b, x), (c, y)) = ((b, x), (c, L(b)⁻¹y))` is a strong bundle isomorphism covering the
    identity (`IsStrongBundleIso`), and `f − f(0)` is conjugated near `0` to a basic germ
    (`IsConjugateToBasicGerm`, with the neighbourhood `U ∩ (Vo ⊕ X)` as its domain: "replacing
    `U` by a smaller one"). Four points of the proof are not in the text. (a) The mean value
    inequality `|P[D₂f(b, 0)(x − x') − h(b, x) + h(b, x')]|_m ≤ ε|x − x'|_m` for `x, x' ∈ X_{m+1}`
    small on level `m`: the text writes the integral `∫₀¹ P[D₂f(b, 0) − D₂f(b, tx + (1 − t)x')](x − x') dt`
    in `F_m`; here the one-dimensional mean value inequality for
    `t ↦ h(b, x' + t(x − x')) − L(b)(x' + t(x − x'))` on `[0, 1]`, whose derivative is bounded by
    `ε|x − x'|_m` by (3) (`Polyfold.norm_sub_sub_le_of_hasFDerivWithinAt_segment`; the usual
    mean value inequality for `h(b, ·) : X_{m+1} → F_m` would give the bound in the norm of
    `X_{m+1}`). The extension to `x, x' ∈ X_m` is a sequence argument with the continuity of
    `H_m` on `U'_m` ("the map `H` is sc-smooth, therefore using the density of `X_{m+1}` in
    `X_m`"). (b) The strong bundle map `Φ` must be sc-smooth on `U' ◁ (ℝᴺ ⊕ Y)` and on
    `(U' ◁ (ℝᴺ ⊕ Y))[1]` (Definition 2.6.1 (preprint 2.47)); the second is Lemma 3.7.4 (preprint 3.61) for the shifted family
    `L(b) : X¹ → Y¹`, whose sc-smoothness hypothesis is Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17) for
    `(b, h) ↦ L(b)h` — the text's "if we raise the index by one, then the map ... is also
    sc-smooth by Proposition 1.17" — and the lift of `(c, L(b)⁻¹ιy₁)` to `F'₁` is `(c, L(b)⁻¹y₁)`

    germ `ofSet (O ⊕ Y)`, which needs the converse of `IsSck.isSckGerm`
    (`Polyfold.IsSckGerm.isSck_ofSet`: a germ on `ofSet U` is an sc^k map on `U`), not previously
    available. (c) "`P ∘ Df(b)|X` is an injective sc-Fredholm operator of index `0`, hence an
    sc-isomorphism" (from (1) and the sc-Fredholm property of `P`) is here, on every level `m`,
    the block computation `ind Df(b, 0) = n + ind L(b)_m − N` (`Polyfold.fredholmIndex_block`:
    `Df(b, 0)_m` differs from `inr ∘ L(b)_m ∘ pr_X` by the finite-rank operator
    `(p, x) ↦ Df(b, 0)(p, 0) + (pr_{ℝᴺ}Df(b, 0)(0, x), 0)`, which does not change the index, Kato
