     (item 123). In the displayed formula for `dω` (p. 197) the second sum carries `(−1)^{ℓ+k}`, where the classical formula
     has `(−1)^{ℓ+j}`, and the first sum is indexed by `i` with terms in `j`: possible misprints.
159. **Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3): the 2021 example (gap G.31 changed)** *(book 2021: p. 176)*. The 2021 text recalls the
     space `X = {(s, 0)} ∪ {(s, t) : s > 0} ⊂ ℝ²` of its Subsection 1.4.4, made an M-polyfold with `X_∞ = X`; if `1₀¹` were
     sc-smooth, Theorem 4.1.2 (preprint 4.2) would make the connected `X` a manifold of constant local dimension, which it
     is not. As we read it the argument holds (with `C = E`, condition (3) of Theorem 4.1.2 follows from the sc⁺ property,
     Lemma 4.1.7 (preprint 4.7)); it is not formalized. The formalized example (`remark_4_1_3_example`, items 140–146) is a
     different one, and shows moreover that `X` and `X¹` can carry different topologies. Status: G.31 stays **formalized**;
     the text now gives an example.

**160–164: the Springer 2021 additions on M-polyfolds (2026-11-08).** (`Chapter4/VectorFieldsGlobal.lean`, on
`Chapter2/TangentLift.lean`; item 164: `Chapter2/TangentLiftAll.lean`; comparison items V4.74–V4.79; gap G.38 closed, G.92 new.)

160. **Lemma 4.4.4 on an M-polyfold, `i = 1`** *(book 2021: p. 196; new in the 2021 edition)*. `lemma_4_4_4`: for an
     sc-smooth vector field `A`, `raiseIndex hA = Φ⁻¹ ∘ A₁ : X² → T(X¹)`, with `A₁ : X² → (TX)¹` the level-`1` map
     (`vectorFieldLevelOne`) and `Φ = tangentShiftEquiv : T(X¹) ≃ (TX)¹` the sc-diffeomorphism of Proposition 2.3.17
     (`proposition_2_3_17`), is an sc-smooth vector field on `X¹`, and `Φ(A^(1)(x)) = A(x)`. The text's "natural
     identification" is `Φ` (gap G.6, closed). Every `i` follows by iterating, `A^(1)` being again an sc-smooth vector
     field; the statement for every `i` is item 164. Status: **settled**.
161. **Proposition 4.4.5 (preprint 4.26) on an M-polyfold is formalized (gap G.38 closed)** *(book 2021: p. 196; proof
     §§4.5.1–4.5.2, pp. 200–202)*. `MPolyfold.lieBracket`: at `x ∈ X²` the tangent vector represented by
     `[A_φ, B_φ](φ(x))` in a chosen chart `φ`, `A_φ` the principal part (`principalPart`, a vector field on the model by
     `isRetractVectorField_principalPart`); `tangentChartMap_lieBracket`: in every chart `ψ` around `x`,
     `Tψ([A, B](x)) = (ψ(x), [A_ψ, B_ψ](ψ(x)))`, so the bracket depends neither on the chart nor on the retraction chosen
     for its model (`chartLieBracket_change`, Lemma 4.5.1 for transition maps); `proposition_4_4_5`: `[A, B]` is
     sc-smooth `X² → TX` and `p([A, B](x)) = x`. Reading: "an sc-smooth section of `TX|X² → X²`" is an sc-smooth map
     `X² → TX` over the inclusion `X² → X¹`; the pull-back bundle itself is not built (item 163). The earlier statement,
     a vector field on `X¹` (a section of `T(X¹) → X²`), would through `Φ` put `[A, B](x)` on level `1` of the fibre, in
     `E₁`, for `x ∈ X₂`; the example of item 156 excludes this, so that statement does not hold as we read it, and the 2021
     statement is the one that holds (an argument from item 156, not a separate theorem). Status: **settled**; G.38
     **closed**.
162. **Lemma 4.5.1 (new in 2021; proof left to the reader) is formalized, more general in the map** *(book 2021: p. 201;
     §4.5.2, pp. 201–202)*. In a local model, `retractLieBracket_natural`, by the computation of §4.5.2: the relations
     differentiated at `x ∈ O₂` (`IsRetractVectorField.diff_related`) and taken on level `1`
     (`IsRetractVectorField.related_shift`), subtracted, with the symmetry `scSecondDeriv_symm`; on an open part `O ∩ W`,
     the shape of a transition map, `retractLieBracket_natural_inter` (with `retractLieBracket_restrict`); on M-polyfolds,
     `lemma_4_5_1`: for every sc-smooth `f : X → Y` and vector fields with `Tf ∘ A = A' ∘ f₁`, `Tf ∘ B = B' ∘ f₁` on
     `X¹`, `Tf ∘ [A, B] = [A', B'] ∘ f₂` on `X²`. Readings: (a) the text relates the fields at points of `X₂`, but the
     computation differentiates the relations, which needs them on an open set of level `1`; they are assumed on `X¹`
     (a hidden hypothesis); (b) the text has a local sc-diffeomorphism `φ : X → X` and one pair of fields; the formal
     statement takes any sc-smooth `f` between two M-polyfolds and a pair on each side; (c) "Proposition 4.5.1" at the end
     of §4.5.2 (item 157). With these readings the computation holds as we read it. Status: **settled**, except the
     open-subset form (item 163).
163. **What remains of the vector fields of §4.4 (gap G.92 new)** *(book 2021: pp. 196, 201)*. Not formalized: Lemma
     4.5.1 for a local sc-diffeomorphism between open subsets of `X` (open subsets of an M-polyfold are not built as
     M-polyfolds; such a map is covered only when it is the restriction of an sc-smooth map `X → Y`); the pull-back bundle
     `TX|X² → X²` as a bundle object (Lemma 4.4.4 for every `i` is item 164). The hypotheses of the section
     are satisfiable: `MPolyfold.isScVectorField_zero`. The forms of §4.4 remain gap G.80 (item 158).
     (2026-11-12) **Resolved.** Lemma 4.5.1 between open subsets uses Part I's open sub-M-polyfolds (`restrictOpen`),
     the restricted vector fields and the locality of the bracket (`lemma_4_5_1_open`, `lieBracket_restrictOpen`,
     `GapP1_Lemma451.lean`). The pull-back bundle `TX|X²` is a sub-M-polyfold of `X² × TX`
     (`isSubMPolyfold_tangentPullback`), with `[A, B]` an sc-smooth section (`proposition_4_4_5_section`) and Lemma
     4.5.1 on sections (`lemma_4_5_1_section`, `GapP1_Lemma451Bundle.lean`). Rows V4.76, V4.77; gap G.92 closed.
164. **Lemma 4.4.4 for every `i` (new in 2021)** *(book 2021: p. 196, with the diagram before the lemma)*.
     `lemma_4_4_4_all` (`Chapter2/TangentLiftAll.lean`): with the lifts bundled with their spaces (`BundledMPolyfold`,
     `BundledMPolyfold.lift`), `A^(0) = A` and `A^(i+1) = (A^(i))^(1)` (`raiseIndexAll`), for every `i` `A^(i)` is an
     sc-smooth vector field on `X^i`; its image under `T(X^i) → TX` at `x ∈ X^{i+1}` is `A(x)`; and through the
     sc-diffeomorphisms `Φ_i : T(X^i) → (TX)^i`, `J_i : (X¹)^i → (X^i)¹` of Proposition 2.3.17 for every `i`
     (`proposition_2_3_17_all`, Chapter 2), `Φ_i ∘ A^(i) ∘ J_i` is the `i`-th index raise of `A`, the diagram printed
     before the lemma. Readings: "the natural identification" is `Φ_i`, `J_i`; "`A^(i)` is `A`" is read through the
     inclusions into `TX` and the diagram. Witness: `BundledMPolyfold.lemma_4_4_4_all_zero` (the zero field). Status:
     **settled**.

165. **Remark 4.2.2: the local form near `{d_X = 0}`; the 2021 wording with `d_A` (gap G.33 in part)** *(Remark 4.2.2,
     p. 184 (preprint 4.14, p. 157); Theorem 4.2.7, p. 188 (preprint 4.18); item 61)* (2026-11-09).
     `Polyfold/Chapter4/RemarkLocalForm.lean`; `Polyfold/Chapter9/MathlibManifoldBridge.lean`. For a smooth
     finite-dimensional submanifold `A`, the open piece `A ∩ {d_X = 0}` is a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold whose
     induced structure has a corner structure (`remark_4_2_2_interior`), and every `a` with `d_X(a) = 0` has an open `U
     ∋ a` with `A ∩ U` such a submanifold (`remark_4_2_2_near`); no tameness of `X` is used. With a dimension `n` the
     piece is `IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞` (`IsSubmanifoldOfDim.isManifold_of_degIndex_eq_zero`), and Theorem 4.2.7 gives
     `IsManifold (modelWithCornersEuclideanQuadrant n) ∞` (`theorem_4_2_7_isManifold`). The 2021 Remark 4.2.2 speaks of
     the points with `d_A(a) = 0`, more points since `d_A ≤ d_X`, and adds that near `d_A(a) = 1` the set `A` is a
     manifold with boundary; neither is formalized. Status: **settled** for the preprint wording and (2026-11-12, item 176) for the 2021 wording (gap G.33 closed; rows V4.32, V4.41).

166. **Proposition 4.4.5 in the book's form (rows V4.72, V4.76)** *(Proposition 4.4.5 (preprint 4.26), p. 196; Lemma
     4.5.1, proof §§4.5.1–4.5.2, pp. 200–202; items 155, 161–163)* (2026-11-09).
     `Polyfold/Chapter4/BookFormLieBracket2021.lean`. `proposition_4_4_5_book`: for sc-smooth vector fields `A`, `B`
     the bracket `[A, B] : X² → TX` (`lieBracket`) is given in every chart `ψ` by the usual formula `Tψ([A, B](x)) =
     (ψ(x), [A_ψ, B_ψ](ψ(x)))`, is sc-smooth, and covers the inclusion `X² → X¹`. "An sc-smooth section of `TX|X² →
     X²`" is read as such a map, as in row V4.76, since the pull-back bundle is not built (gap G.92, item 163). Status:
     **settled** (rows V4.72, V4.76).

**167–172: sc-differential forms, the exterior derivative, integration and Stokes (2026-11-09).**
(`Chapter4/ScForms2021.lean`, `ScExteriorDerivative2021.lean`, `ScFormsNatural2021.lean` – `ScFormsLower2021.lean`;
`Chapter4/EuclideanForms2021.lean`, `EuclideanStokes2021.lean`, `ManifoldForms2021.lean` – `ManifoldBoundary2021.lean`;
comparison items V4.80–V4.88; gap G.37 closed, G.39, G.40, G.80 in part.)

167. **The sign in the formula for `dω` (p. 197) does not hold as we read it, with the text's bracket** *(book 2021:
     p. 197; the bracket: §4.5.1, p. 200; refines item 158)*. The 2021 text defines the bracket as `[A, B] = DA·B −
     DB·A` (p. 200), the negative of the classical `DB·A − DA·B`, and prints the second sum of the formula for `dω` with
     the sign `(−1)^{ℓ+k}`. Take `k = 1`, `ω = dy` on `ℝ²`, `A₀ = (1, 0)` and `A₁(p) = (0, p₁)`: then `[A₀, A₁] = (0,
     −1)`, the right side at `0` is `1 − 0 + 1 = 2`, and `dω = 0`. The classical sign `(−1)^{ℓ+j}`, which item 158
     proposed, also gives `2`. With `A₁' = 0`, which agrees with `A₁` at `0`, the printed right side is `0`, so the
     printed expression is not tensorial. With this bracket the sign must be `(−1)^{ℓ+j+1}`: the formula is then
     Mathlib's exterior derivative (`extDeriv_eq_invariantFormula`, from Mathlib's `extDeriv_apply_vectorField`). Lean:
     `invariantFormula_printedSign_counterexample`. The preprint (p. 167) and the 2017 text print `(−1)^{i+j}` and give
     the bracket only as "the usual formula"; with the classical bracket that sign is the classical one. So the 2021
     sign is possibly a misprint, or the text intends another bracket convention. The index `i` of the first sum is read
     as `j`. The formal `d` on M-polyfolds (item 169) is defined by the local formula, so this sign does not enter it.
     Status: **settled** (row V4.83, narrower).
168. **Definitions 4.4.1–4.4.2: the forms are read in the charts of the Whitney sum (gap G.37 closed)** *(book 2021:
     p. 195; preprint Definition 4.25, p. 167)*. `MPolyfold.IsScForm`: a form is a family of alternating `k`-linear maps
     `ω(x)` on the linear spaces `T_xX`, `x ∈ X¹` (row V2.19), whose representative `ω_φ` on `⊕ₖ TO` (`chartForm`) is
     sc-smooth for every chart `φ` of the maximal atlas. Reading: "sc-smooth on `⊕ₖ TX`" is read in the charts `⊕ₖ Tφ`,
     the charts the Whitney sum would have as an M-polyfold. The "easy exercise" of p. 195 is done in the local models:
     `⊕ₖ TO` is an sc-retract, the image of `⊕ₖ Tr` (`IsScRetract.whitney`), and `⊕ₖ Tf` is sc-smooth
     (`IsScSmoothRetractMap.whitney`), so the transitions `⊕ₖ T(ψ ∘ φ⁻¹)` are sc-smooth; the Whitney sum itself is not
     assembled into an M-polyfold bundle. A covering family of charts suffices (`isScForm_of_cover`), so the condition
     over all charts is satisfiable; witnesses are `0` and the constant `0`-forms (`constForm_mem_scForms`). The
     pull-back along `X¹ → X` (`formLower_mem_scForms`) gives the directed system (4.4) on the bundled lifts
     (`BundledMPolyfold.formsMap`), with direct limit `formsInfty` (Mathlib's `Module.DirectLimit`) and sum
     `formsInftyGraded`; the preprint's double use of `Ω*_∞` (item 124) is resolved by two names, as in the 2021 text.
     Status: **settled** (rows V4.80–V4.82).
169. **The exterior derivative: the direction of item 120, and the local formula** *(book 2021: pp. 196–197; items
     120, 158)*. The 2021 text runs `d : Ωᵏ(Xⁱ) → Ωᵏ⁺¹(Xⁱ⁺¹)`, the direction item 120 proposed for the preprint, and
     the formal `d` has it: `MPolyfold.extD` maps `Ωᵏ(X)` to `Ωᵏ⁺¹(X¹)` (`extD_mem_scForms`), and
     `BundledMPolyfold.formsD` maps `Ωᵏ(Xⁱ)` to `Ωᵏ⁺¹(Xⁱ⁺¹)`. Reading: the text defines `d` through vector fields and
     their brackets (p. 197); the formal `d` is, in charts, the local formula `dΩ(y, h₀, …, h_k) = Σⱼ (−1)ʲ DΩ(y, h₀,
     …, ĥⱼ, …, h_k)(hⱼ, 0)` (`ambientD`, `chartD`), which on normed spaces is the invariant formula with the sign of
     item 167 (`extDeriv_eq_invariantFormula`). It depends neither on the retraction nor on the chart
     (`retractD_eq_of_subset`, `chartD_transition`, `extD_apply`), by the naturality `d(f^*Ω) = f^*dΩ` in the local
     models (`retractD_comp_retractWhitneyMap`), whose proof uses the symmetry of the second derivative as the bracket
     does in §4.5.2. The vector-field formula itself is not proved in the sc setting. Status: **settled** (rows V4.84,
     V4.85; gap G.39 in part).
170. **`d ∘ d = 0`, `d` on `Ω*_∞(X)` and Definition 4.4.6 now have proofs behind them (item 121)** *(book 2021:
     pp. 197–198; Definition 4.4.6, p. 198)*. Item 121 noted that `d ∘ d = 0` and `d j* = j* d` are asserted without
     proof. Now `extD_extD` gives `d(dω) = 0` in `Ωᵏ⁺²(X²)` (locally `ambientD_ambientD`, from the symmetry of the
     second derivative and `sum_removeNth_symm_eq_zero`); `extD_formLower`, that `d` commutes with `X¹ → X` (the square
     of p. 197); `formsInftyD` and `formsInftyGradedD`, the map `d` on `Ωᵏ_∞(X)` and on `Ω*_∞(X)`, with `d² = 0`
     (`formsInftyGradedD_comp_self`); and `BundledMPolyfold.scDeRham`, Definition 4.4.6 read degree by degree, with
     `scDeRhamMk_eq_iff`. Not formalized: the wedge product (the text calls `(Ω*_∞(X), d)` a graded differential
     algebra); `f^*` along sc-smooth maps of M-polyfolds and `f^* d_Y = d_X f^*` (p. 198; its local form is
     `retractD_comp_retractWhitneyMap`); forms on `∂X` (item 122), hence `d j* = j* d` and the relative complex with its
     `d ∘ d = 0`; the Poincaré Lemma 4.4.8 and Lemma 4.5.2. Status: **settled** for `d² = 0` and Definition 4.4.6 (rows
     V4.86–V4.88); **open** for the relative complex (gap G.39) and the rest of gap G.80.
171. **Theorem 4.4.7: the induced orientation of the faces is read as outward vector first** *(book 2021: p. 199;
     Definitions 9.3.8, 9.3.10, pp. 427–428)*. §4.4 says "equipped with the induced orientation" and fixes no
     convention. We read it as Definition 9.3.8's: a frame of a face is positive when the outward vector followed by
     the frame is positive. On the quadrant `{xᵢ ≥ 0, i ∈ S}` the outward vector at the face `{xᵢ = 0}` is `−eᵢ`
     (`add_smul_neg_stdFrame_not_mem_quadrant`), so the face frame `(e_j)_{j ≠ i}` has the sign `(−1)^{i+1}`
     (`faceSign`, `det_cons_neg_stdFrame_faceFrame`). With this convention and Mathlib's `d`, Stokes' theorem carries
     the sign `+`: `∫_Q dω = Σ_{i ∈ S} ∫_{Fᵢ} ω` (`stokes_quadrant`), and on manifolds `∫_M dω = ∫_{∂M} ω`
     (`stokes_of_compactSpace`). The convention is that of the project's boundary frames (`MPolyfold.boundaryFrames`,
     `Chapter9/OrientationBoundary.lean`), and the induced orientation is the same in every chart at the boundary
     points of degeneracy index `1` (`orientation_face_chartChange`). Status: **settled** (a reading; gap G.40).
172. **Theorem 4.4.7 (Stokes): `∫_N` in the 2021 text, and what is formalized** *(book 2021: p. 199; preprint Theorem
     4.28, p. 168; item 123)*. The preprint and 2017 formulas write `∫_M dω`; the 2021 text writes `∫_N dω` (item 123),
     still without proof. Formalized for classical forms: on a compact Hausdorff Mathlib manifold `M` modelled on
     `[0,∞)ⁿ⁺¹` with a continuous tangent orientation, `∫_M dω = ∫_{∂M} ω` for every `C¹` `n`-form `ω`
     (`ManifoldForm.stokes_of_compactSpace`); the oriented solution sets of Theorem 6.6.18 are such manifolds
     (`theorem_6_6_18_oriented`). `∫_M` is built from signed charts and a smooth partition of unity, and does not depend
     on these choices (`IntegrationData.integral_eq`). Reading: the charts carry a sign because with the quadrant model
     every chart of `[0, 1]` at `1` reverses the orientation, so `[0, 1]` has no oriented atlas (as
     `Chapter6/ManifoldOrientation.lean` notes); `∫_{−o} = −∫_o` (`integral_neg_orientation`). `∫_{∂M}` is the sum,
     over the charts of a partition of unity, of the face integrals in each chart, and the corners are a null set
     (`chartBoundaryIntegral_eq_sum_openQuadrant`). The forms need only be `C¹`. Not formalized: the restriction of an
     sc-form to `N` ("clearly" a classical form, p. 199), which needs the derivative of `N → X` in charts and that
     sc-smooth functions restrict to `C^∞` functions on `N`; the faces of `N` as manifolds and the text's `Σ_F ∫_F`;
     forms and integrals given only on `∂N`; `d ∘ d = 0` for `ManifoldForm`. Status: **open** (gap G.40 in part).

**173–174: forms on `∂X`, the pull-back, the relative complex and Stokes for sc-forms (2026-11-10).**
(`Chapter4/ScFormsPullback2021.lean`, `BoundaryForms2021.lean`, `ManifoldFaceForms2021.lean`;
`Chapter9/MathlibFormsBridge2021.lean`; comparison items V4.89–V4.92; gap G.39 closed, G.40, G.80 in part.)

173. **Forms on `∂X` are read through the tame boundary `bX`, with agreement over `B` (reading R-a; gap G.39
     closed)** *(book 2021: pp. 198–199; preprint p. 168; items 121, 122)*. The text notes that local faces and
     their intersections are tame M-polyfolds, so that forms on `∂X` make sense, and gives no definition (item
     122). We read a `k`-form on `∂X^i` as an sc-form `τ` on the tame boundary `bX^i` (Theorem 2.7.13,
     `tameBoundaryPolyfold`) that agrees over `B : bX → X`: `τ_p(v) = τ_{p'}(v')` whenever `Bp = Bp'` and `TB v_j =
     TB v'_j` (`IsAgreeingOver`, `IsFaceCompatible`). Some agreement is needed for the invariant of Theorem 6.7.1:
     on `[0, 1]²` with functions given face by face, `∫_{∂S} dβ` is the sum of the jumps at the corners, which is not
     `0` unless the face values agree there (a remark, not formalized). `bForms` asks in addition that `dτ` agree
     over `B^{i+1}`; then `d` maps `Ωᵏ(∂X^i)` to `Ωᵏ⁺¹(∂X^{i+1})` (`extD_mem_bForms`), and `bForms` is the largest
     `d`-stable family of agreeing forms (`le_bForms`). Caveat (step A3 of the plan): that the agreement of `τ`
     implies that of `dτ` is not proved; it needs the corner strata of tame retracts as sub-M-polyfolds. If it
     holds, `bForms` is the set of agreeing forms, the text's reading; if not, it is the largest complex inside that
     set. Every `j^*ω` lies in `bForms`: `j^* = B^*` (`jStar`, `formsPullback_mem_bForms`), and `dj^* = j^*d`
     (`jStar_comp_D`), asserted without proof (item 121), is proved. The relative complex `Ωᵏ_∞(X) × Ωᵏ⁻¹_∞(∂X)`,
     `d(ω, τ) = (dω, j^*ω − dτ)`, has `d ∘ d = 0` (`relD_comp_relD`; "one easily verifies" in the text) and the
     cohomology `relDeRham`, read degree by degree; for `∂X = ∅` it is `Hᵏ_sc(X)` (`relDeRhamEquivOfNoBoundary`).
     The pull-back `f^*` along an sc-smooth map (p. 198; `formPullback`, `formsInftyPullback`) and `f^* d_Y = d_X
     f^*`, left to the reader in the 2021 text, hold as we read them and are proved (`extD_formPullback`,
     `formsInftyD_comp_formsInftyPullback`). Not formalized: the wedge product (gap G.80). Status: **settled** under reading R-a (rows V4.89–V4.91; gap G.39 closed); step A3 is **settled** too (2026-11-12, below).
     (2026-11-12) **Step A3 holds as we read it**: the agreement of `τ` over `B` implies that of `dτ`
     (`isFaceCompatible_extD`), so `bForms` is the set of agreeing forms (`bForms_eq_agreeForms`;
     `A3BoundaryForms2021.lean`, `A3BoundaryForms2021b.lean`), the text's reading. The proof goes through
     `r ∘ P_i ∘ P_j`, lifts `G`, `G'` with `B ∘ G = B ∘ G'`, and `CornerChart.exists_tangent` (row V4.90, now "same").
174. **Theorem 4.4.7 for sc-forms on a finite-dimensional submanifold (refines item 172; gap G.40 in part)** *(book
     2021: Theorem 4.4.7, p. 199; preprint Theorem 4.28, p. 168)*. Item 172 left the restriction of an sc-form to `N`
     ("clearly" a classical form, p. 199) open. It is the pull-back along `S → X^i`, read on the corner frames of
     `T_xS` (`scFormRestrict`, `formsInftyRestrict`); in a chart of `X` it is `ω_φ ∘ modelDeriv`
     (`scFormRestrict_apply_modelDeriv`), it is `C^∞` (`contMDiffForm_formsInftyRestrict`) and it commutes with `d`
     (`extDeriv_formsInftyRestrict`). With it, `∫_S (dω)|_S = ∫_{∂S} ω|_S` for `ω ∈ Ωⁿ_∞(X)` and a compact
     sub-M-polyfold `S` with a corner structure of dimension `n + 1` and a continuous tangent orientation
     (`stokes_formsInftyRestrict`); every submanifold in good position of a tame `X` has such a corner structure
     (`exists_hasCornerStructureOfDim_of_tame`), in particular the solution sets of Theorem 6.6.18
     (`exists_hasCornerStructureOfDim_solutionSet`). The face sum `Σ_F ∫_F ω` is read as the boundary integral of
     the Mathlib manifold `S`, the faces oriented outward vector first (item 171). Forms given only on the faces of a
     Mathlib manifold with corners (`ChartFaceForm`: `C^∞` on the faces of the charts, compatible under chart changes,
     agreeing at the corners) are formalized for the second integral of Theorem 6.7.1: a compactly supported one is
     `j^*β` for a compactly supported form `β` on `M` (`exists_extension`), `∫_{∂M}` is defined through any extension
     (`faceIntegral_eq`), and `∫_{∂M} dτ = 0` (`ChartFaceForm.integral_d_eq_zero`). `d ∘ d = 0` for `ManifoldForm`,
     open in item 172, is `ManifoldForm.extDeriv_extDeriv`. Not formalized: the faces `F` of `N` as tame
     M-polyfolds and integrals over them (gap G.40). Status: **settled** (2026-11-12; row V4.92; gap G.40 closed; item 177 (c)).
     (2026-11-12) The faces in their own right are formalized for face-structured `N`, and the face sum equals
     `∫_{∂S}` (item 177 (c); gap G.40 closed).

175. **In a tame M-polyfold the good position hypothesis of Theorem 4.1.2 (2) is automatic** *(Theorem 4.1.2, p. 176
     (preprint 4.2, p. 148); Lemma 4.2.8)* (2026-11-12). `Polyfold/Chapter4/GapP1_Remark422.lean`. In a tame chart
     centred at a smooth point, `T₀O` is in good position to `C`, with a complement inside `T₀O` of the `lemma_4_2_8`
     form (`ScRetraction.isInGoodPosition_rangeS_of_isTameWith`,
     `ScRetraction.interior_rangeS_scDeriv_zero_nonempty`). So a tame M-polyfold with `X = X_∞` and `1₀¹` sc-smooth
     has a corner structure (`hasCornerStructure_of_isTame`), and so does the tame induced structure of a submanifold
     (`IsSmoothSubmanifold.hasCornerStructure_of_isTame`). Without tameness `d_X ≤ 1` suffices
     (`hasCornerStructure_of_degIndex_le_one`, `GapP1_Remark422One.lean`); the case where the boundary coordinate
     vanishes on `T₀O` is excluded by the graph argument of Lemma 9.2.13 (`degIndex_eq_zero_of_isReducedTangentAt`).
     The statement of Theorem 4.1.2 holds as we read it; the hypothesis is redundant in the tame case. Status:
     **settled** (row V4.5; item 176).

176. **Remark 4.2.2 in the 2021 wording (gap G.33 closed; settles the open part of item 165)** *(Remark 4.2.2, p. 184
     (preprint 4.14, p. 157))* (2026-11-12). `Polyfold/Chapter4/GapP1_Remark422.lean`, `GapP1_Remark422One.lean`. The
     2021 text replaces `d_X` by `d_A`, which covers more points, since `d_A ≤ d_X`: for the parabola `{(y², y)}` in
     `[0, ∞) × ℝ`, `d_A ≡ 0` while `d_X(0, 0) = 1`. Both 2021 sentences hold as we read them, without tameness: the
     open piece `{d_A = 0}` of `A` is a smooth submanifold without boundary (`remark_4_2_2_dA_zero`,
     `remark_4_2_2_dA_zero_near`), and the open piece `{d_A ≤ 1}` is a manifold with boundary, a corner structure with
     `d ≤ 1` (`remark_4_2_2_dA_one`, `remark_4_2_2_dA_one_near`). For the second, take a chart realizing `d_A(a) = 1`,
     re-centred at `a`, with boundary coordinate `λ`: if `λ|_{T_aA} ≠ 0`, `T_aA` is in good position
     (`isInGoodPosition_halfSpace`); if `λ|_{T_aA} = 0`, `A` is near `a` a graph over `T_aA` and `d_A(a) = 0` (the
     argument of Lemma 9.2.13), a contradiction; then Theorem 4.1.2 applies. The earlier version for a tame induced
     structure (`remark_4_2_2_dA_one_of_isTame`) is no longer needed. Status: **settled** (rows V4.32, now "same",
     V4.41).

177. **Reading points of §4.4 and Appendix 4.5: the wedge product, the Poincaré lemmas, the faces in Stokes** *(pp.
     198–204)* (2026-11-12). None is a counterexample; each statement holds as we read it. (a) *The wedge product.*
     The text uses ∧ without defining it ("graded differential algebra", p. 198). We take the classical normalisation
     `(a ∧ b)(v) = (k! l!)⁻¹ Σ_σ sign σ · a(v_{σ(1..k)}) b(v_{σ(k+1..k+l)})` (`formWedge`, `formsInftyWedge`,
     `ScFormsWedge2021.lean`, `ScFormsWedge2021b.lean`); with it the Leibniz rule holds with the sign `(−1)ᵏ`
     (`extD_formWedge`, `formsInftyD_formsInftyWedge`), ∧ is associative, graded commutative and unital, `⊕ₖ Ωᵏ_∞(X)`
     is a graded ℝ-algebra (`formsInftyGAlgebra`) with `d` a derivation of degree +1, and `f^*` is a morphism of
     graded algebras. Not formalized: the wedge product on `Ω*_∞(X, ∂X)`, which the text also calls a differential
     algebra (gap G.80). (b) *Lemma 4.5.2 about a smooth centre.* In the proof of Lemma 4.4.8, Lemma 4.5.2 is applied
     to `B_δ(φ(x)) ∩ C`, which need not contain `0` when `φ(x)` is off the corner, and the remark after Lemma 4.5.2 (a
     centre `(0, w₀)`) does not cover it. The homotopy about any smooth centre `c` works with the same proof,
     `τ(y)(v) = ∫₀¹ tᵏ ω(c + t(y − c))(y − c, v) dt` (`homotopyForm`, `hasPoincare_relOpen`); the centre must be
     smooth for the homotopy to be sc-smooth on every level. Lemma 4.4.8 is proved this way (`lemma_4_4_8`, from
     `lemma_4_4_8_of_local` and `localPoincare`); the printed case `c = 0` is `hasPoincare_relOpen_of_zero_mem`.
     "`dτ = ω` on `U¹`" is read as `dτ = ι^*ω`, and the degrees `k, k − 1` as `k + 1, k`; the sc-smoothness of
     `x ↦ ∫₀¹ g(t, x) dt` is `isScSmooth_intervalIntegral` (`Poincare2021.lean`). (c) *"Whose boundary ∂N is a union
     of smooth faces"* (Theorem 4.4.7) is read as `N` face-structured (Definition 2.5.10). With it the faces of `N`
     have corner structures of dimension `n` (`hasCornerStructureOfDim_face`) and induced orientations, outward vector
     first, unique and continuous (`inducedOrientation`, `isContinuous_faceOrientation`), and
     `Σ_F ∫_F ω|_F = ∫_{∂N} ω` (`sum_integral_restrictForm_eq_boundaryIntegral`); so Theorem 4.4.7 holds with the sum
     over the faces, as printed (`MPolyfold.theorem_4_4_7_hyp`). The reading is satisfiable: it holds without boundary
     (`isFaceStructured_of_forall_degIndex_eq_zero`) and for the quadrants (`isFaceStructured_quadrant`); whether it
     can be dropped is not examined. A compact tame M-polyfold has finitely many faces (`finite_setOf_isFace`).
     Status: **settled** (rows V4.87, V4.92, V4.95, V4.96; gap G.40 closed, gap G.80 in part).
     (2026-11-13) The wedge product on `Ω*_∞(X, ∂X)` of (a) is formalized with the product of the mapping cone of
     `j^*` (item 178; gap G.80 closed).

178. **The product on `Ω*_∞(X, ∂X)`: the mapping cone of `j^*` (our choice; gap G.80 closed)** *(§4.4, p. 199)*
     (2026-11-13). `Polyfold/Chapter4/GapP3_K4_BoundaryWedge.lean`, `GapP3_K4_RelWedge.lean`. The text calls
     `Ω*_∞(X, ∂X) = Ω*_∞(X) ⊕ Ω*⁻¹_∞(∂X)` a differential algebra and gives no product. We take the product of the
     mapping cone of `j^*`: `(ω, τ)(ω′, τ′) = (ω∧ω′, (−1)ᵏ j^*ω∧τ′)` for `(ω, τ)` of degree `k` (`relWedge`). With it
     `d(ω, τ) = (dω, j^*ω − dτ)` is a derivation of degree +1 (`relD_relWedge`, `relGradedD_of_mul_of`), the product
     is associative (`relWedge_assoc`, `relGraded_mul_assoc`), `⊕ₖ Ωᵏ_∞(X, ∂X)` is an associative non-unital ring
     (`relGradedNonUnitalRing`), and the projection to `Ω*_∞(X)` is multiplicative (`relFst_relWedge`). `(1, 0)` is a
     unit on the left only: `x·(1, 0) = (ω, 0)` (`relWedge_relOne`), and the product is not graded commutative;
     relative cohomology has no unit in general either, so this is a property of the construction, not a reading of a
     printed claim. For it, the wedge product of agreeing forms on `∂X` is agreeing and makes `Ω*_∞(∂X)` an
     associative unital algebra with the Leibniz rule, and `j^*` is multiplicative (`agreeDFormsInftyWedge`,
     `agreeDFormsInftyD_agreeDFormsInftyWedge`, `agreeDFormsInftyWedge_assoc`, `jStar_formsInftyWedge`). On the
     pull-back of forms on `∂X`: the 2021 text of §4.4 (pp. 198–199) defines `f^*` for sc-smooth maps of M-polyfolds
     and, on `∂X`, only `j^*`; Parts I–II pull forms on `∂X` back along a map only in the proof of Theorem 6.7.1 (p.
     279), along `p₁` on the faces of the solution set `S_F`, and that is formalized (`faceAlongData`; Chapter 6, item
     136). The pull-back along a general sc-smooth map of tame M-polyfolds is not formalized (estimate 600–1,500
     lines); no statement of Parts I–II depends on it. No counterexample; nothing is found not to hold as we read it.
     Status: **settled** (row V4.91; gap G.80 closed; completes item 177 (a)).

Found while formalizing §5.1 in `Chapter5/AuxNorm.lean` (2026-10-26).

1. **The fibres of `Y_{0,1}` carry no linear or normed structure in the text, and "complete norm"
   is read as "the fibre with `N` is complete"** *(book 2017: Definition 5.1)*. Definition 5.1.1 (1) (preprint 5.1)
   presupposes that the fibres `(Y_{0,1})_x` are vector spaces on which `N` can be a norm; §5.1
   only says "the fibers `Y_x` have the structure of Banach spaces". The formalization defines
   `(Y_{0,1})_x` as the subspace of `P⁻¹(x)` of the points in `Y_{0,1}` (`StrongBundle.oneFiber`; a
   subspace because the strong bundle charts are linear on the fibres and `F₁ ⊆ F` is a subspace),
   and reads (1) as: `N` is a norm on it and every `N`-Cauchy sequence converges
   (`StrongBundle.IsCompleteFiberNorm`). The text's `|h|₁` is the `F₁`-norm of the fibre component
   of `Φ[1](w)` (`StrongBundle.liftOneFiber`, an injective linear map `(Y_{0,1})_x → F₁`); it
   depends on the chart, but the norms of two charts are equivalent on each fibre, and even locally
   uniformly in the base point (`StrongBundle.exists_norm_liftOne_le_mul`). The fibre is complete
   for `|·|₁` because its image in `F₁` is the slice `{h | (φ(x), h) ∈ K[1]}`, the fixed point set
   of the continuous map `h ↦ R[1](φ(x), h)` (`isClosed_slice`, `complete_liftOneFiber`); the text
   takes this for granted.
2. **Lemma 5.1.2 (preprint 5.2) needs the charts `Φ[1]` of `Y[1]` for every strong bundle chart, and "(ii) ⇒ (i) is
   obvious" needs that they are homeomorphisms** *(book 2017: Lemma 5.1)*. (ii) quantifies over
   "a strong bundle isomorphism `Φ : Y|V → K`", i.e. over all strong bundle charts compatible with
   the atlas, while `StrongBundleOne.lean` gave the charts `Φ[1] : P⁻¹(V)[1] → K[1]` of `Y[1]` only
   for the charts of the atlas. `StrongBundle.oneChartOf` builds them for every compatible chart,
   with `isChart_oneChartOf` (they are charts of the M-polyfold `Y[1]`: the transition maps are the
   `[1]`-transitions of Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50)) and `mem_oneSet_iff_of_isChart`. In "(ii) ⇒ (i)" the
   bounds give `Φ[1](w_k) → (φ(x), 0)`, and `w_k → 0_x` in `Y_{0,1}` follows from the continuity
   of `Φ[1]⁻¹` on `K[1]`; in "(i) ⇒ (ii)" the set "`|p − q|₀ + |h|₁ < ε`" is a neighbourhood of
   `0_x` in `Y_{0,1}` by the continuity of `Φ[1]`.
3. **Lemma 5.1.2 (preprint 5.2): the bounds hold only near `x`, and the contradiction argument needs no
   metrizability.** (ii) asks for `c·N(w) ≤ |h|₁ ≤ C·N(w)` for all `w ∈ P⁻¹(V)`, `V` the domain of
   `Φ`; the proof gives them "for `P(w)` close to `x`". The formalization (`Polyfold.lemma_5_1_2`)
   takes `V` to be a neighbourhood of `x` inside the domain on which the bounds hold, and
   `w ∈ P⁻¹(V) ∩ Y_{0,1}` (`N` and `|h|₁` are defined only there). The upper bound
   `N(w) ≤ (2/ε)|h|₁` is `StrongBundle.exists_le_mul_norm_liftOne` (for any `g` continuous at `0_x`
   and positively homogeneous on the fibres); the lower bound, by contradiction with sequences
   `|h_k|₁ = 1`, `N(w_k) → 0`, is `IsAuxNorm.exists_norm_liftOne_le`, with the neighbourhoods
   `φ⁻¹(B(φ(x), 1/(k + 1)))`, whose points converge to `x` because `φ⁻¹` is continuous on `O`.
   "(i) ⇒ (ii)" holds in every strong bundle chart around `x` (`IsAuxNorm.exists_bounds`), which
   the comparison of Proposition 5.1.3 (preprint 5.3) uses (two auxiliary norms compared in the same chart). The
   constants `0 < c < C` can always be arranged (`c` can be decreased).
4. **Proposition 5.1.3 (preprint 5.3), existence: the "partition of unity argument"** *(book 2017: Proposition 5.1)*.
   `Polyfold.proposition_5_1_3_exists`: `N(w) = Σᵢ ρᵢ(P(w))·|Φᵢ[1](w)|₁` over the charts of the
   atlas, `(ρᵢ)` a partition of unity of `X` subordinate to their domains (`X` paracompact and
   Hausdorff, hence normal; `PartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate`). The steps the text omits:
   `N` is continuous on `Y[1]` (each term vanishes off the closed set `P⁻¹(supp ρᵢ)`, contained in
   the open domain of `Φᵢ[1]`, and the sum is locally finite: `continuous_gluedNorm`); `N` is a norm
   on each fibre and the fibre is complete (`isCompleteFiberNorm_gluedNorm`: near `x` only
   finitely many `ρᵢ` are non-zero, all with `x` in the domain of `Φᵢ`, and their norms are
   uniformly comparable with the norm of one chart around `x`, `exists_uniform_comparison`); the
   bounds of Lemma 5.1.2 (ii) (preprint 5.2) (`gluedNorm_bounds`), after which Lemma 5.1.2 (preprint 5.2) gives condition (2).
5. **Proposition 5.1.3 (preprint 5.3), comparison: "the local compatibility implies the existence of `f`".**
   `Polyfold.proposition_5_1_3_compare`: Lemma 5.1.2 (preprint 5.2) "(i) ⇒ (ii)" for `N₀` and `N₁` in one chart
   around `y` gives `r_y > 0` with `r_y N₀ ≤ N₁` and `r_y N₁ ≤ N₀` on the fibres over a
   neighbourhood of `y`; for each point the admissible `r` form a convex set, so the local
   constants glue to a continuous `f : X → (0, ∞)` with values in these sets (a partition of unity
   argument, `exists_continuous_forall_mem_convex_of_local_const`); then `f N₀ ≤ N₁ ≤ f⁻¹ N₀`. In
   the statement, `N₀(h)` and `N₁(h)` stand for `N₀(w)` and `N₁(w)`.
6. **Tameness is not used in §5.1.** The section places the strong bundle over a tame M-polyfold,
   but Lemma 5.1.2 (preprint 5.2) is stated without tameness, and none of Definition 5.1.1 (preprint 5.1), Lemma 5.1.2 (preprint 5.2), Proposition 5.1.3 (preprint 5.3)
   uses it. The comparison with the auxiliary norms of [21] ("our definition is more general than
   the earlier one") is not formalized.

Found while formalizing §5.2 and §5.2 (preprint Appendix 5.4.1) in `Chapter5/Compactness.lean` (2026-10-26).

20. **Theorem 5.2.4 (preprint 5.7) uses Corollary 3.1.15 (preprint 3.13) at an arbitrary limit, not Theorem 5.2.3 (preprint 5.6); `X_∞` has no
    topology in the text** *(book 2017: Theorems 5.2, 5.3)*. The step "`x_k → x` in `X₀`, hence
    `x_k → x` on every level, by Theorem 5.6" needs the convergence of a given sequence of zeros at
    its limit, which is Corollary 3.1.15 (preprint 3.13) at the point `x`; Corollary 3.1.15 (preprint 3.13) is stated for a germ `(f, x₀)`
    and the limit `x₀` of the germ (Chapter 3, item 15), so it applies once one knows that the limit
    of zeros is a zero (continuity of the principal part) and a smooth point (regularizing), where
    `(f, x)` is an sc-Fredholm germ (`corollary_3_1_15_section`). "`X_∞` is a metric space" presupposes
    a topology on `X_∞`, which the text never defines; the formalization uses the initial topology
    of the inclusions `X_∞ → X_m` (`MPolyfold.smoothLevel_topology_eq`, metrizable by Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16)),
    for which convergence is convergence on every level (`MPolyfold.tendsto_smoothLevel_iff`).
    Theorem 5.2.4 (preprint 5.7) (`Polyfold.theorem_5_2_4`) and the compact solution set on every level
    (`Polyfold.isCompact_solutionSet_level`) then follow by sequences. Theorem 5.2.3 (preprint 5.6)
    (`Polyfold.theorem_5_2_3`) is `theorem_3_1_13_preprint` at a zero. Tameness is not used in Theorems 5.2.2–5.2.4 (preprint 5.5–5.7).
21. **Corollary 5.2.5 (preprint 5.8): "it is a priori clear that `f^i` is sc-Fredholm" is not clear, and the bundle
    `P^i : Y^i → X^i` is not defined** *(book 2017: unchanged, Corollary 5.1, p. 158; "tame" dropped;
    only `Y[i]`, `i = 0, 1`, defined, p. 47)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Corollary 5.2.5, p. 213; only `Y[i]`, `i = 0, 1`, defined, p. 68)*. The text defines `Y[i]` for
    `i = 0, 1` (after Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51)), not `Y^i`; the natural `Y¹` is `Y_{1,1} = (Y[0])¹` over
    `X¹ = X₁`, with the fibrewise linear structure on `P⁻¹(x) ∩ Y_{1,1}` and the charts `Φ¹`. This
    shifted strong bundle is not built in the project. What is formalized (`Polyfold.corollary_5_2_5_chart`):
    the compact solution set in `X₁` (indeed in every `X_i`), and, at every smooth point, the data of
    Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) for `f` with `(g − s)¹ : U¹ → F¹` conjugated to the basic germ `h¹` by the index
    raise `Ψ¹` (`IsConjugateToBasicGerm.shift`) and `s¹` an sc⁺-section of `U¹ ◁ F¹`. The shift of a
    basic germ is a basic germ (`IsBasicGerm.shift`), with `C̃` a partial quadrant (needed for
    Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17) for germs; it is part of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11)). For `i ≥ 2` the iteration needs the
    level sets of `X¹` to be those of `X` shifted by one (gap G.6; closed since, Chapter 2, item 77). (Round-trip items V5.13, V5.14:
    the compactness half follows from the project, `RoundTrip/Items/V5_13.lean`,
    `A_gives_B_compact`; "`f^i` is sc-Fredholm" for every `i` is missing mathematics, including
    condition (3) on level `i` (item 22) — the sc-level gap of Chapter 3 item 224.)
    *(2026-11-02: superseded. The shifted strong bundle `P¹ : Y¹ → X¹` is built
    (`StrongBundle.shift`) and Corollary 5.2.5 (preprint 5.8) is proved for `i = 1` (`Polyfold.corollary_5_2_5`), for
    `i = 2` (`corollary_5_2_5_two`) and by iteration for every fixed `i`, with the text's hypotheses
    and without tameness; see items 140–146.)*
22. **The filler condition (3) on level `1` does not follow from condition (3) on level `0`.**
    For `f¹` to have the filled version `g¹`, the map `L = (1 − ρ(0))Dg(0)` must be a topological
    isomorphism `ker Dr(0) ∩ E₁ → ker ρ(0) ∩ F₁`, while Definition 3.1.4 (3) (preprint 3.4) only gives it on level
    `0`. An sc-operator can be bijective on level `0` and not onto on level `1`: on
    `E_m = {x : |x|_m² = Σ_k e^{2mk} x_k² < ∞}` the right shift `T` has `|T|_m = e^m`, `1 − T/2` is
    invertible on `E₀`, and `(1 − T/2)⁻¹e₀ = Σ_n 2^{−n}e_n ∉ E₁` (since `e²/4 > 1`). For an
    sc-Fredholm germ the level-`1` condition holds, by an argument the text does not give: (a) by
    Lemma 3.1.20 (preprint 3.17), subtracting the sc⁺-section `y ↦ R(y, f̂(0))` (`f̂(0) ∈ F_∞` at a smooth point)
    reduces to `g(0) = 0` without changing `L`; (b) `Dg(0)` is regularizing (`Dg(0)ξ ∈ F₁ ⇒ ξ ∈ E₁`):
    `Dg(0) − Ds(0)` is conjugated to `Dh(0)` by `Γ(0)` and `Dψ(0)` (because `(g − s)(0) = 0`), `Ds(0)`
    maps into `F₁`, and `Dh(0)(a, w)_W = w − D_aB(0)a` with `D_aB(0)a ∈ W_∞` and `D_wB(0) = 0` (the
    contraction estimate holds with every `ε`); (c) for `k ∈ ker ρ(0) ∩ F₁` and `κ = L⁻¹k`, the
    linearization `A = ρ(0)Dg(0)|_{T₀O}` is Fredholm, so `im A + ρ(0)F₁ = ρ(0)F₀` and there is
    `t ∈ T₀O` with `Dg(0)(t + κ) ∈ F₁`; then `t + κ ∈ E₁` and `κ = (1 − Dr(0))(t + κ) ∈ E₁`. This
    argument is not formalized. *(2026-11-02: formalized in the form of item 144 —
    `IsFillingGerm.mem_range_toBase_of_fillDefect`, `IsFillingGerm.germ_shift` — where the reduction
    to a zero subtracts `Γ(z, −g(0))` composed with `r`, so that the fill defect, and with it `L`,
    does not change; see items 140–146.)*
23. **Theorem 5.2.2 (preprint 5.5) uses the uniform `(0, 1)` fibre bound of the conjugating isomorphism silently**
    *(book 2017: Theorem 5.1)*. "Without loss of generality ... `f = h + t`" replaces the bound
    `N(f(x)) ≤ 1` on `X` by a bound `|(h + t)(a, w)|₁ ≤ c` in the coordinates of the basic germ. This
    needs: Lemma 5.1.2 (preprint 5.2) in the chart of the germ (`|Φ[1](w)₂|₁ ≤ A·N(w)` near the point,
    `StrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.exists_norm_liftOne_le` of `AuxNorm.lean`, which holds in every
    compatible chart), and a bound `|Ψ[1](u, k)₂|₁ ≤ M|k|₁` for `u` near `0`
    (`IsStrongBundleMap.exists_fiber_bound_one`, from the continuity of `Ψ[1]` at `(0, 0)` and the
    linearity of the fibre maps). Subtracting the sc⁺-section `s` before the conjugation
    (`|g(u) − s(u)|₁ ≤ A + |s(0)|₁ + 1` near `0`) makes the text's `t = Ψ_*s` and its estimates (83)
    and (85) unnecessary, and gives a neighbourhood independent of the bound `c`
    (`IsSc0ContractionGerm.exists_isCompact_bdd`, `IsBasicGerm.exists_isCompact_bdd`); `C̃` must be
    closed, as in Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40).
24. **Theorem 5.2.2 (preprint 5.5): the way back from local coordinates and the covering are left implicit.** The set
    `{(a, w) ∈ U | |(h + t)(a, w)|₁ ≤ c}` of the appendix lives in the domain `U` of the filled
    version, which contains points that are not in the retract `O ≅ V ⊆ X`; for its closure to say
    anything about `cl_X{x | N(f(x)) ≤ 1}`, the closure of the image of `{x ∈ V | N(f(x)) ≤ 1}`
    must lie in `O`. It does, since `O` is the fixed point set of the retraction `r` in `U`, after
    cutting the compact set on the side of the basic germ down to a closed ball inside `U'`
    (`exists_nbhd_isCompact_closure_bdd`). The last sentence ("since the solution set of `f` is
    compact, the proof ... is complete") stands for: finitely many such neighbourhoods cover
    `f⁻¹(0)`, and the closure of a finite union is the union of the closures (`Polyfold.theorem_5_2_2_preprint`).
    The local statement holds at every smooth point where `(f, x)` is an sc-Fredholm germ, not only
    at zeros.
25. **Slips in the proof of Theorem 5.2.2 (preprint 5.5)** (§5.2 (preprint Appendix 5.4.1), lines 7769–7891): "`z' = h(a, w)`" for
    `(h + t)(a, w)`; "`ℝⁿ ⊕ Y₁`" for `ℝᴺ ⊕ W₁`; "in view of (2) and (3)" for (84) and (86); in `Σ`,
    "`a ∈ ℝⁿ`" for `a ∈ C̃` (`B` is defined on `C̃ ⊕ W` only); the dangling clause after (86); "the
    closed ball in `Y₀`" for `W₀`; in (89), `z = z' − ((1 − P)h + t)(a, w)` mixes the `ℝᴺ`- and
    `W`-components (it is `P z' − P t(a, w)`; then (85) is not needed). In the extracted text (90)
    reads `τ/4` for `τ'/4` (possibly a displaced prime). The theorem is stated for a tame `X` in
    §5.2 and for any `X` in the appendix; tameness is not used.
26. **Definition 5.2.1 (preprint 5.4): the conventions made explicit** *(book 2017: Definition 5.5)*. "`N(f(x)) = ∞`
    if `f(x)` does not have biregularity `(0, 1)`" is `StrongBundle.AuxLe`; the support of `s` is
    the closure of `{s ≠ 0}`. "Obviously proper implies weakly proper" uses that `{f = s}` is closed
    (`f`, `s` continuous, `Y` Hausdorff) and that a solution of `f(x) = s(x)` outside `U` is a zero
    of `f` (`s = 0` there), hence lies in `U` after all; then `N(f(x)) = N(s(x)) ≤ 1`
    (`StrongBundle.IsProper.isWeaklyProper`, for a continuous `f`). With Theorem 5.2.2 (preprint 5.5),
    `Polyfold.theorem_5_2_2_iff`.
27. **Remark 5.3.4 (preprint 5.12): the completion is not constructed, and closedness is not discussed**
    *(book 2017: Remark 5.3)*. Of a section `s` in the completion of `Γ^{+,1}_U` the argument only
    uses that `s = 0` outside `U` and `N(s(x)) ≤ 1` (both survive uniform limits for
    `ρ(s, s') = sup N(s(x) − s'(x))`); then the solutions of `f + s = 0` lie in
    `{x ∈ U | N(f(x)) ≤ 1}` (`N(f(x)) = N(−s(x))`), whose closure is compact (`Polyfold.remark_5_3_4`,
    no sc⁺ property used). The solution set itself is compact only if it is closed, i.e. essentially
    if the limit section is continuous, which the remark does not address. The clause "adapted to
    `N`, in the sense that `N(f(x)) ≤ 1` for `x ∈ U`, has the properties stipulated in the
    properness result" is garbled; it is read as "`cl{x ∈ U | N(f(x)) ≤ 1}` is compact".

Found while formalizing the start of §5.3 and §5.5 (preprint Appendix 5.4.2) in `Chapter5/BumpFunctions.lean`
(2026-10-26).

40. **Sc-smooth functions need `ℝ` as an M-polyfold.** "Sc-smooth map `f : X → ℝ`" (Definitions
    5.3.1, 5.5.2, 5.5.6 (preprint 5.9, 5.29, 5.33)) is Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14) with target the M-polyfold `ℝ` (constant sc-structure,
    identity chart), which the project did not have: `Polyfold.realPolyfold`. Sc-smoothness of a
    map between M-polyfolds can be checked in one pair of charts around each point, continuity
    included (`MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_of_local`); this is what makes "extend by `0`" work in
    Theorem 5.5.7 (preprint 5.34) and Lemma 5.3.3 (preprint 5.11).
41. **Definition 5.3.1 (preprint 5.9) "`f ≠ 0`" against Definition 5.5.2 (preprint 5.29) "not identically zero"** *(book 2017:
    unchanged, Definitions 5.7, 5.13, pp. 161, 174)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Definitions 5.3.1, 5.5.2, pp. 216, 229)*. The two definitions of "admits sc-smooth bump functions" differ:
    Definition 5.5.2 (preprint 5.29) asks for an `f` that is not identically zero with support in `U(x)`;
    Proposition 5.5.3's (preprint 5.30) proof starts from "a sc-smooth bump function `g` having support in `U(x)` and
    satisfying `g(0) = 1`", i.e. it needs `g(x) ≠ 0` at the given point. On an M-polyfold there are
    no translations, and even on an sc-Banach space the translation by a vector that is not smooth
    does not preserve the levels, so a bump that is non-zero somewhere in `U(x)` cannot be moved to
    `x`. The formalization reads Definition 5.3.1 (preprint 5.9) (and Definition 5.5.6 (preprint 5.33)) as `f(x) ≠ 0`
    (`MPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctions`, `LocalModel.HasBumpProperty`), keeps Definition 5.5.2 (preprint 5.29) as
    written (`MPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak`, implied by the first:
    `AdmitsBumpFunctions.weak`), and assumes the first in Proposition 5.5.3 (preprint 5.30), Theorem 5.5.7 (preprint 5.34) and Lemma
    5.3.3 (preprint 5.11). Whether the weak reading implies the strong one is not settled here. (Round-trip items
    V5.16, V5.17, V5.20, V5.44, V5.51: both project notions are the text's literal and pointwise
    ones (`Iff.rfl`), and this one word is the only obstacle to deriving the text's Proposition
    5.5.3 (preprint 5.30), Lemmas 5.3.3, 5.3.17 (preprint 5.11, 5.24) and, with the text's misprints corrected (e.g. item 62), Theorems 5.3.5, 5.3.10, 5.3.12, 5.5.7 (preprint 5.13, 5.18, 5.19, 5.34) and Theorem 5.25 (preprint) from the project's; with the pointwise reading they follow, e.g.
    `RoundTrip/Items/V5_44.lean`, `A_to_BStrong`.) *(2026-11-02: the weak reading gives the
    pointwise one at the smooth points of an sc-Banach space, both hold on Hilbert models, and the
    question is open only at non-smooth points; items 160–163.)*
42. **Proposition 5.5.3 (preprint 5.30): the function `σ` is misprinted** *(book 2017: unchanged, Proposition 5.5,
    p. 174)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Proposition 5.5.3, p. 230)*. "`σ(s) = 0`
    for `s ≤ 1` and `σ(s) = 1` for `s ≥ 1`" is not a function, and `f = σ ∘ g` needs `g(x) = 1`.
    The formalization (`Polyfold.proposition_5_5_3`, `proposition_5_3_2`) takes `f = τ(3g/g(x) − 1)`,
    `τ` the smooth transition (`0` on `(−∞, 0]`, `1` on `[1, ∞)`): `f(x) = 1`, `f ≡ 1` where
    `g/g(x) > 2/3` (a neighbourhood of `x`), `0 ≤ f ≤ 1`, and `f ≠ 0` only where `g ≠ 0`. The
    composition of an sc-smooth function with a `C^∞` function `ℝ → ℝ` is sc-smooth
    (`MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.comp_contDiff`).
43. **Theorem 5.5.7 (preprint 5.34) ("Clearly"): the extension of a local bump need not be continuous** *(book
    2017: unchanged, Theorem 5.11, p. 175)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Theorem 5.5.7, p. 231)*. For "⇐", a bump `f₀` of a chart `φ : V → O` with `supp_O(f₀) ⊆ U(x)` and
    `cl_E(U(x)) ⊆ O` gives `f = f₀ ∘ φ` on `V`, extended by `0`; but `cl_X({f ≠ 0})` may leave `V`:
    for `X = E` with `E₀` a Hilbert space, `V` the open unit ball and the chart
    `φ(u) = u/(1 − |u|₀²)` onto `O = E`, `U(x) = O` satisfies `cl_E(U(x)) ⊆ O` and `f₀ ≡ 1` is
    admissible, while `f` is `1` on `V` and `0` outside. The repair (`Polyfold.theorem_5_5_7`):
    choose `U₁ ∋ x` with `cl_X(U₁) ⊆ U ∩ V` (`X` is regular) and the local bump in a small ball
    `B(φ(x), r/2)` with `B(φ(x), r) ∩ O ⊆ φ(U₁)`; then `supp(f) ⊆ cl_X(U₁) ⊆ U`, and `f` is
    sc-smooth (it vanishes on the open set `X ∖ supp(f)`). The small ball is admissible in
    Definition 5.5.6 (preprint 5.33) because a retract is closed near each of its points
    (`closure_inter_ball_subset`: `O ∩ cl(B(z, r/2))` lies in the fixed point set of the retraction,
    which is continuous on its domain `C ∩ W' ⊇ C ∩ B(z, r)`, and `C` is closed). The text's "atlas"
    is read as a family of charts of `X` covering `X`; "⇒" holds for every chart.
44. **Proposition 5.5.8 (preprint 5.35): "Hilbert space", and why the translation is allowed** *(book 2017:
    Proposition 5.6)*. "`E₀` is a Hilbert space" is formalized as: the norm of `E₀` comes from a
    continuous bilinear form, `‖v‖² = b(v, v)` (`Polyfold.proposition_5_5_8`); an
    `InnerProductSpace` instance on `E₀` would be a second normed structure on the type, not
    definitionally equal to the one of the sc-scale, so Mathlib's `ContDiffBump` for inner product
    spaces is not used. The proof needs only a continuous quadratic form dominating `κ‖v‖²`
    (`LocalModel.hasBumpProperty_of_quadratic`, which covers spaces isomorphic to a Hilbert space):
    `f(v) = τ(1 − b(v − x, v − x)/ρ)`. "Translating" is legitimate because `f` is `C^∞` on `E₀`
    itself, hence sc-smooth by Corollary 1.2.5 (preprint 1.20) from the base level
    (`IsScSmooth.of_contDiffOn_finiteDimensional`); for a merely sc-smooth function the translation
    by a non-smooth `x ∈ O` is not covered by the chain rule (it is not an sc-smooth map). Composing
    with any retraction onto `O` gives an sc-smooth function on `O`. The remark before Definition
    5.3.1 (preprint 5.9) ("this is the case if `X` is built on sc-Hilbert spaces") is
    `MPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert`.
45. **The product of an sc-smooth function and an sc⁺-section, and sums of sc⁺-sections, are used
    but not stated.** Lemma 5.3.3's (preprint 5.11) "`s(y) = β(y)t(y)` is a sc⁺-section" and the finite
    combinations `Σ λᵢsᵢ` of Theorems 5.3.5 and 5.3.10 (preprint 5.13 and 5.18) need: `f·s ∈ Γ⁺(P)` for `f` sc-smooth and
    `s ∈ Γ⁺(P)` (`StrongBundle.IsScPlusSection.smul_left`: in a chart `(f·s)^ = (f ∘ φ⁻¹)·ŝ`, by the
    product rule `IsScSmooth.smul`), `s₁ + s₂ ∈ Γ⁺(P)` (`IsScPlusSection.add`), finite sums
    (`isScPlusSection_sectionSum`) and the zero section (`isScPlusSection_fiberZero`).
46. **Lemma 5.3.3 (preprint 5.11): the bound holds at every point, and neither tameness nor a centred chart is
    needed** *(book 2017: Lemma 5.3)*. (a) The statement's "`N(s(x)) < N(e) + ε`" is trivial at `x`
    (`s(x) = e`); what §5.3 needs (for `Γ^{+,1}_U`) and the proof gives is `N(s(y)) < N(e) + ε` for
    all `y` (`Polyfold.lemma_5_3_3`). In the proof `ε` is reused for the radius (`β` is supported in
    "`O' ∩ {|y|₀ < ε}`", where `δ` is meant), and "`W|Q`" stands for `Y|Q`. (b) The proof's
    `t(y) = R(y, ẽ)` is an sc⁺-section of `K → O` because `ẽ ∈ F_∞` (`e` is smooth): the constant
    `ẽ₁ ∈ (F¹)_∞` is sc-smooth into `F¹`, and `R[1]` is sc-smooth. (c) "`s = β·t` has the required
    properties" needs the product rule (item 45) and the extension by `0` of a section defined on
    the chart domain: `StrongBundle.isScPlusSection_cutoffSection` (sc⁺ through `Φ[1]` on the chart
    domain, the zero section off `supp(β)`, and these two open sets cover `X`). (d) The bound: `β`
    is chosen with support in `U` and in the open set `{N(t(y)) < N(e) + ε}` (continuity of `N` on
    `Y[1]` and of `t` into `Y[1]`), and `N(β(y)t(y)) = β(y)N(t(y)) ≤ N(t(y))` because `0 ≤ β ≤ 1`
    and `N` is a norm on the fibres. (e) Not needed: tameness of `P` and `X`, the normality of `X`
    ("Since `X` is metrizable, it is a normal space"; the support condition comes from Proposition
    5.5.3 (preprint 5.30)), and a chart centred at `x` (any chart of the atlas around `x` works; centring only turns
    `|φ(y) − φ(x)|₀` into `|y|₀`). The hypothesis "`x` smooth" is kept as in the text; it follows
    from `e` smooth. The bump function hypothesis is Definition 5.3.1 (preprint 5.9), read as in item 41.
47. **`Γ^{+,1}_U(P)` and its metric.** `StrongBundle.allowableSections`: the `s ∈ Γ⁺(P)` with
    `supp(s) ⊆ U` and `N(s(x)) ≤ 1` for all `x`; the condition is meaningful at every point because
    sc⁺-sections take values in `Y_{0,1}` (`IsScPlusSection.mem_oneSet`). The uniform distance
    `ρ(s, s') = sup N(s(x) − s'(x))` and the remark that `(Γ^{+,1}_U(P), ρ)` is not complete *(book 2017: unchanged,
    p. 162)* *(book 2021: unchanged, p. 217)* are not formalized. (Round-trip item V5.21: `allowableSections` is the text's set (`allowable_eq`), and
    `ρ` is a metric on it for every auxiliary norm, proved from the fibre-norm axioms in
    `RoundTrip/Items/V5_21.lean`, `B2_holds`; not moved into the project. The non-completeness is
    not proved: it needs a concrete bundle and a `ρ`-Cauchy sequence of sc⁺-sections whose limit is
    not sc⁺.) *(2026-11-02: the metric is in the project (`StrongBundle.allowableMetric`), the
    non-completeness is proved for the trivial bundle `ℝ × ℝ → ℝ`, and "not complete" turns out to
    need a hypothesis; items 150–153.)*
48. **Not formalized in WP 5.3**: Definition 5.5.4 (preprint 5.31) and Theorem 5.5.5 (preprint 5.32) (Bonic–Frampton, the smoothness
    of the `Lᵖ`-norm, cited from [9]), the remark on `W^{1,4}` and `W^{1,3/2}` (Sobolev spaces,
    gap G.1), and the open question whether sc-smooth bump functions give sc-smooth partitions of
    unity.

60. **Theorem 5.3.5 (preprint 5.13) as formalized** *(book 2017: unchanged, Theorem 5.5, p. 162)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Theorem 5.3.5, pp. 217–218)*. `Polyfold.theorem_5_3_5_generic`
    (the generic form) and `Polyfold.theorem_5_3_5_preprint` (the text's dense-set form). Hypotheses: `X`
    without boundary (`d_X ≡ 0`, `IsWithoutBoundary`), `X` admits sc-smooth bump functions
    (Definition 5.3.1 (preprint 5.9) read as `f(x) ≠ 0`, item 41), `f` sc-Fredholm with compact solution set, `N`
    an auxiliary norm, and the tameness hypotheses of item 61. Conclusion: an open `U ⊇ S_f` such
    that (1) for every allowable `s ∈ Γ^{+,1}_U(P)` (`StrongBundle.allowableSections`, item 47)
    `S_{f+s}` is compact, and (2) *generic form*: for every sc⁺-section `s₀` with `supp(s₀) ⊆ U`
    and `N(s₀(x)) ≤ 1 − ε` there are finitely many allowable sc⁺-sections `t₁, …, t_m`, a
    `δ > 0` and a Lebesgue null set `CV ⊆ ℝᵐ` such that for every `λ` with `|λ| < δ`
    (maximum norm) and `λ ∉ CV`: `s_λ = s₀ + Σ λᵢ tᵢ` is allowable, `f + s_λ` is transversal to
    the zero section (Definition 5.3.7 (preprint 5.15)), `S_{f+s_λ}` is compact and, if non-empty, a
    sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame, that of a manifold without boundary of
    locally constant dimension, with regular tangent germ data at every zero of dimension the
    Fredholm index of `(f + s_λ)'(y)` (`StrongBundle.SolutionSetIsManifold`, the conclusion of
    `theorem_3_6_10_of_surjective`); *dense form*: for every allowable `s'` and `ε > 0` an allowable
    `s` with `N(s(x) − s'(x)) ≤ ε` for all `x` (`StrongBundle.sectionDistAt`, the pointwise form
    of the text's `ρ`) and the same properties. "Generic" is thus made precise as "for every `λ`
    outside a null set of the ball", and the text's "dense subset `O`" as the pointwise density.
    The metric space `(Γ^{+,1}_U(P), ρ)` is not built; `Remark 5.14` and `Remark 5.16` are not
    formalized.
61. **The tameness hypotheses** *(book 2017: Theorem 5.5)* *(book 2021: unchanged, §5.3, p. 216; Theorem 5.3.5, p. 217)*. Theorem 5.3.5 (preprint 5.13) does not assume
    tameness, but §5.3 opens with "`P : Y → X` a tame strong M-polyfold bundle", and the proof
    uses Theorems 3.1.21, 3.1.22 and 3.6.8 (preprint 3.18, 3.19 and 3.54), which the project proves for strong bundles whose
    compatible charts have tame base retractions (`htame`, Chapter 3 items 86, 173). The
    formalization takes `htame` for `P` and, since the implicit function theorem is applied to the
    parametrized section `F` of Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18) on `ℝᵏ × X`, also for the pull-back bundles
    `π*P → ℝᵏ × X` for every `k` (`StrongBundle.PullbacksHaveTameCharts`), a hypothesis the text
    does not state (tameness of `π*P` is not discussed; `ℝᵏ × X` is tame when `X` is,
    `prod_rn_isTame`, but the base retraction of an arbitrary compatible chart of `π*P` is not
    constrained by that). **The hypothesis `htame` over all compatible charts is very strong**: a
    strong bundle chart `(φ, U, R, Φ)` can be re-equipped with another sc-smooth retraction `r'`
    of `U` onto the same `O` (`R'(u, h) = R(r'(u), h)`, same `K`, same `Φ`), which is again a
    compatible strong bundle chart, and `r'` need not satisfy condition (1) of Definition 2.5.2 (preprint 2.34)
    (`d_C(r'(u)) = d_C(u)` on `U`). For instance, for `X = ℝ` and the trivial bundle, the chart
    `x ↦ (1, x)` with model `O' = {1} × ℝ ⊆ C' = [0, ∞) × ℝ`, `U' = C'`, `r'(a, x) = (1, x)` is
    compatible with the chart `id` and `d_{C'}(r'(0, 5)) = 0 ≠ 1 = d_{C'}(0, 5)`. So `htame` (and
    `PullbacksHaveTameCharts`) can fail for any strong bundle; the natural weaker reading, that the
    chart of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) at each point can be chosen with a tame base retraction (or that the
    charts of a tame strong bundle atlas are tame), would require restating the §3.6 theorems,
    which is not done here (not verified in Lean).

    and the text never shows it** (plan risk 15). "Hence we can apply Theorem 4.23" needs
    `S̃ ⊆ ℝᵐ × X` with local sc⁺-retractions; the implicit function theorem gives only the tangent

    `exists_isScPlusRetractionOn`, `MPolyfold.isSmoothSubmanifold_of_isRegular`,
    `StrongBundle.isSmoothSubmanifold_solutionSet_inter`): for regular data (`IsRegular`, which

    sc⁺-retraction: `π ∘ r` is sc-smooth into the finite-dimensional `N`, and an sc-smooth map on a
    finite-dimensional space with the constant structure is sc⁺ (`isScPlus_of_isScSmooth_const`:
    all levels of the domain coincide). So the zeros of a section in an open set where they are all
    in good position form a smooth submanifold in the sense of Definition 4.2.1 (preprint 4.13).

    (i)–(ii) (linear algebra), and they hold at the nearby `(0, y)` by item 83.

87. **Theorem 5.3.12 (preprint 5.19) as formalized** *(book 2017: unchanged, Theorem 5.7, p. 167)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Theorem 5.3.12, p. 222)* (`Polyfold.theorem_5_3_12_param`, generic
    form): bump functions, `f` with tame germ data and compact solution set, `(f, x)` in good
    position at the zeros on `∂X`. Conclusion: `U` as before, finitely many allowable `tᵢ` with
    `supp(tᵢ) ∩ ∂X = ∅`, `δ > 0`, a null set `CV`, such that for `|λ| < δ`, `λ ∉ CV`,

88. **Theorem 5.3.12 (preprint 5.19): the parametrized section is in general not in good position at the boundary
    zeros, so "as before" does not apply** (not verified in Lean). At a zero `(0, x)`, `x ∈ ∂X`,
    where all `tᵢ` vanish, `ker F'(0, x) = ℝᵐ × ker f'(x)`. If `ℝᵐ × K` had a good complement `Y`
    in `ℝᵐ × T_xX` for the cone `ℝᵐ × C_x` (Definition 3.1.24 (preprint 3.21) with constant `ε`), then for `(a, 0)`
    with `|a|` large and any `y ∈ Y` with `‖y‖ ≤ ε|a|`, `(a, y₂) ∈ ℝᵐ × C_x`; so the second
    components of `Y` lie in `C_x ∩ −C_x = E_x` and `K + E_x ⊇ T_xX` — a general position condition
    which good position does not imply (e.g. `K = ℝ(1, 1)` in the corner `[0, ∞)²` is in good but not
    in general position). So Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) cannot be applied to `F` at these points. The proof here
    avoids it: the sections are supported off `∂X ∪ cl V₁` (`V₁` a neighbourhood of `S_f ∩ ∂X` on
    whose closure the zeros of `f` are in good position, `theorem_3_6_8_one'`); on `V₁`,
    `f + s_λ = f` and the good position is that of `f` (`IsGoodPositionGermTame.congr_nhds`: good
    position depends only on the germ of the section); off `V₁` the zeros are interior points
    (`d = 0`), where good position is surjectivity and the implicit function theorem and the Sard
    step of Theorem 5.3.5 (preprint 5.13) apply to `F`.
    (2026-11-09) Machine-checked: `ℝ(1, 1)` is in good position to `[0, ∞)²`, also with an sc-complement, but `ℝ × ℝ(1,
    1)` is not in good position to `ℝ × [0, ∞)²`, not even with an algebraic complement
    (`Counterexamples2021.theorem_5_3_12_goodPosition_not_stable`, `Polyfold/Chapter3/Counterexamples2021.lean`).
    Gap G.46 is closed as a step that does not hold as we read it (row V5.40).

100. **Definition 5.3.13 (preprint 5.20) as formalized** *(book 2017: Definition 5.10)*
    (`StrongBundle.IsGenCompactHomotopy`). "Tame strong bundle" is read as `X` tame with `f` having
    tame germ data (`IsScFredholmSectionTame`, Definition 3.6.4 (preprint 3.51), as in Chapter 3 items 190–199);
    "`t : X → [0, 1]` sc-smooth surjective" as an sc-smooth `t : X → ℝ` with `t(X) = [0, 1]`;
    "`X_t` is a tame M-polyfold" as "`t⁻¹(τ)` is a sub-M-polyfold (Definition 2.19) whose induced
    structure (Proposition 2.21) is tame"; "`f_t = f|X_t` is an sc-Fredholm section of `Y|X_t`" as:
    the section `a ↦ (a, f(a))` (`restrictSection`) of the pull-back `ι*Y` along the inclusion
    `ι : X_t → X` (Proposition 2.6.8 (preprint 2.54), `StrongBundle.pullback`; `ι` sc-smooth by Proposition 2.3.19 (preprint 2.21))
    has tame germ data. The text does not say what `Y|X_t` is; the pull-back is the only strong
    bundle structure available. "`(f|Xᵢ, P|Yᵢ) = (fᵢ, Pᵢ)`" is an identification of given problems
    with the restrictions, which in type theory needs an isomorphism of strong bundles (Remark 5.3.14 (preprint 5.21)
    says so); the formalization takes the restrictions to `X₀ = t⁻¹(0)` and `X₁ = t⁻¹(1)` as the end
    problems, and Remark 5.3.14 (preprint 5.21) is not formalized. The text's hypothesis that the end problems have
    compact solution sets is a consequence
    (`IsGenCompactHomotopy.isCompact_solutionSet_restrict`: `S_{f|X_t} = S_f ∩ X_t`, closed in
    the compact `S_f`). (Round-trip item V5.41: the project's notion is the text's for a bundle with
    an equivalent strong bundle atlas whose base retractions are tame, `RoundTrip/Items/V5_41.lean`,
    `B_of_project`, `B_iff_tame`; that every strong bundle over a tame `X` has one is believed true,
    by rebuilding the charts over tame base retractions, but not constructed.)
     (2026-11-12) Remark 5.3.14 is formalized as `StrongBundle.IsGenCompactHomotopyBetween` (V5.74, gap G.47 closed).
101. **Lemma 5.3.16 (preprint 5.23) and the hidden hypothesis of Theorem 5.3.15 (preprint 5.22)** *(book 2017: unchanged, Lemma 5.4,
     Theorem 5.8, pp. 168–169)* *(book 2021: corrected, Definition 5.3.13 (3), p. 223, now asks `dt(x)` onto at every smooth `x`, which gives the `Z` of the proof of Theorem 5.3.15, p. 224)*
    (`lemma_5_3_16_preprint`, `ne_zero_of_isCompl_ker`, `exists_isCompl_ker_of_ne_zero`). The proof of
    Theorem 5.3.15 (preprint 5.22) says: "since `x` is a smooth point, we find a one-dimensional smooth linear
    sc-subspace `Z ⊂ T_xX` such that `T_xX = Z ⊕ ker(dt(x))`". Such a `Z` exists if and only if
    `dt(x) ≠ 0` on `T_xX`: for `dt(x) = 0`, `ker dt(x) = T_xX` and the only complement is `0`
    (`ne_zero_of_isCompl_ker`), and then `b_τ` with `dt(x) ∘ b_τ = τ` exists only for `τ = 0`. The
    theorem does not assume that `t` is a submersion at the critical points of `t|S` (nor at all),
    so this is a **hidden hypothesis** of Theorem 5.3.15 (preprint 5.22) (plan risk 17). With `dt(x) ≠ 0`, `Z` can
    be spanned by a vector of any spanning set (`exists_isCompl_ker_of_ne_zero`, e.g. the dense
    smooth vectors), and Lemma 5.3.16 (preprint 5.23) is linear algebra (`lemma_5_3_16_preprint`, under `ℓ ≠ 0`); "sc-operator"
    is automatic since `T_xS` is finite-dimensional and `Z` smooth. (Machine-checked in the
    round-trip audit: `RoundTrip/Items/V5_42.lean`, `not_BLiteral`: without `dt(x) ≠ 0` the first
    sentence fails for the trivial bundle `ℝ¹ × ℝ⁰ → ℝ¹`, the zero section and `t = 0`. The same
    file corrects the example above: `exists_isCompl_ker_of_ne_zero` needs `D` to span `T`
    algebraically, which the dense smooth vectors do not in infinite dimensions; the smooth `Z`
    comes instead from continuity and density, `exists_splits`.)
102. **Lemma 5.3.17 (preprint 5.24) as formalized; the graph is not needed** *(book 2017: Lemma 5.5)*
    (`exists_scPlusSection_linAt`, `lemma_5_3_17`, with `scDeriv_smul_apply`,
    `scDeriv_clm_sub_apply`, `chartLinCutoff`, `isScSmoothMap_chartLinCutoff`,
    `principal_sectionSmul`, `sectionSupport_sectionSmul_subset`). The linearization `s'(x)` is read
    in a strong bundle chart (`linAt`), `T_xS` as a finite-dimensional subspace `K ⊆ T_zO` (the
    text's `T_xS = ker f'(x)`, finite-dimensional by Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52)), `b_τ` as a linear
    `b : K → T_zO`, and "the operator `f'(x) ∘ b_τ` has a one-dimensional image spanned by some
    smooth point `e ∈ Y_x`" is a hypothesis (`Lin_f(z)(b v) ∈ ℝ·Φ(e)₂` for a smooth point `e` of
    the fibre; the text's justification "the image of any vector in `T_xS` belongs to `Y_∞`" is not
    formalized). The text's construction uses the local graph `q ↦ q + δ(q)` of `S` over `T_xS` and
    a complement `V`; it is not needed: with `Lin_f(z)(b v) = λ(v)·Φ(e)₂`, a continuous linear
    functional `ℓ` on the model space extending `−λ` (Hahn–Banach on the finite-dimensional `K`)
    and the section `s = g·sₑ`, `sₑ` the sc⁺-section through `e` of Lemma 5.3.3 (preprint 5.11) and

    `Lin_s(z)v = ℓ(v)·Φ(e)₂` on `T_zO` (product rule; `Dr(z) = 1` on `T_zO`). The text's case
    distinction ("if this operator is the zero operator we can take `s = 0`") is not needed, and

    section has `supp(s) ⊆ U` for any prescribed open `U ∋ x` ("sufficiently small support").
103. **Theorem 5.3.15 (preprint 5.22) (Morse-type structure) is not formalized** *(book 2017: Theorem 5.8)* *(book 2021: partly corrected, Theorem 5.3.15, pp. 223–228: (5.12) now has `T*_yS_λ`; the other slips listed unchanged; the hidden hypothesis of item 101 is now in Definition 5.3.13 (3))*. It
