Found while formalizing the rest of §5.5 (preprint Appendix 5.4.2) in `Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity.lean`
(2026-10-26).

110. **Definitions 5.5.1 and 5.5.9 (preprint 5.28 and 5.36): the readings** *(book 2017: Definitions 5.12, 5.16)*. A partition
     of unity is Mathlib's `PartitionOfUnity ι X` (continuous `ρᵢ ≥ 0`, locally finite supports,
     `Σᵢ ρᵢ = 1`), subordinate to `(Uᵢ)` when `cl{ρᵢ ≠ 0} ⊆ Uᵢ`, with sc-smooth `ρᵢ`
     (`MPolyfold.IsScSmoothPartitionOfUnity`); "for every open covering" quantifies over index
     types in the universe of `X` (`MPolyfold.AdmitsScPartitionsOfUnity`). In Definition 5.5.9 (preprint 5.36)
     (`LocalModel.HasApproxProperty`) the open `V ⊆ O` is `O ∩ W` with `W` open in `E₀`,
     `cl_C(V)` is the closure in `E₀` (`C` is closed), and the supports of `f` and `g` are taken
     in `O` (the closure of `{f ≠ 0}` in `O`).
111. **Theorem 5.5.10 (preprint 5.37) "(i) ⇒ (ii)": `cl_X(W) ⊆ U` does not follow from `cl_C(V) ⊆ O`, and `f ∘ φ` is
     only continuous** *(book 2017: unchanged, Theorem 5.12, p. 176)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Theorem 5.5.10, p. 232)*. The proof calls `f ∘ φ` "sc-smooth" (`f` is
     the continuous function of Definition 5.5.9 (preprint 5.36)) and asserts `cl_X(φ⁻¹(V)) ⊆ U`. Counterexample:
     `X = E` with `E₀` a Hilbert space, `U` the open unit ball, the sc-diffeomorphism
     `φ(u) = u/(1 − |u|₀²)` onto `O = E` (inverse `v ↦ 2v/(1 + (1 + 4|v|₀²)^{1/2})`; both are a
     `C^∞` function of `|·|₀²` times the identity, hence sc-smooth), `V = O`, `f ≡ 1`: then
     `cl_C(V) ⊆ O`, `W = U`, `cl_X(W) ⊄ U`, the extension `g` of `f ∘ φ` by `0` is the indicator
     of the open ball (not continuous) and `U₀ = {g < ε/2}` is not open. Repair
     (`Polyfold.hasApproxProperty_restrict`, `Polyfold.theorem_5_5_10`): since (ii) asks only for
     *an* atlas, take the charts restricted to open `s` with `cl_X(s) ⊆ dom φ`; then for closed
     `A ⊆ φ(s)` the set `φ⁻¹(A)` is closed in `X` (`MChart.isClosed_inter_preimage`), so `g`
     vanishes off the closed set `φ⁻¹(cl V) ⊆ s` and is continuous. Whether under (i) *every*
     chart has the approximation property is not settled here: it needs approximations on the
     open set `dom φ`, for instance from partitions of unity on open subsets of `X` (an exhaustion
     of `dom φ` by closed shells, using metrizability, Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16)), which the text does not
     provide. Simplifications: the set `W̃ = {g > ε/4}` is not needed (the sets `U_x`, `x ∈ φ⁻¹(V)`,
     need only lie in `φ⁻¹(V)`, since subordinate means `supp β_x ⊆ U_x`), and the estimate gives
     `|g − ĝ| ≤ ε/2` (`PartitionOfUnity.abs_sub_finsum_mul_le`). (Machine-checked in the round-trip
     audit: read literally, "the sc-smooth function `f ∘ φ`" fails on the one-chart M-polyfold `ℝ`,
     which admits sc-smooth partitions of unity, with `f = min(|x|, 1)`;
     `RoundTrip/Items/V5_55.lean`, `not_B`.)
     (2026-11-12) **Settled**: under (i) every chart has the approximation property (`hasApproxProperty_of_isChart`,
     `theorem_5_5_10_every_chart`), by shells of the chart domain; the step `cl_X(W) ⊆ U` is not needed (item 184; row
     V5.55, now restated).
112. **Theorem 5.5.10 (preprint 5.37) "(ii) ⇒ (i)": the refinement, the closure in `O`, and the extension by `0`.**
     (a) "A refinement `(W_λ)_{λ ∈ Λ}` with the same index set, `W_λ ⊆ V_λ` and
     `cl_X(W_λ) ⊆ U_{τ(λ)}`" does not exist in general (the cover `{X}`, `X` not inside one chart
     domain). (b) Hypothesis (ii) is applied to `(f'_λ, φ(W_λ), 1/2)` without ensuring
     `cl_C(φ(W_λ)) ⊆ O`, which `cl_X(W_λ) ⊆ U` does not give (the inverse of the chart of item 111).
     (c) The extension of `g_λ ∘ φ` by `0` is continuous only because `cl_X(W_λ) ⊆ dom φ` (as in
     item 111). The formalization (`Polyfold.exists_isScSmoothMap_urysohn`,
     `Polyfold.admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_approx`): small neighbourhoods `N` with
     `cl_X(N) ⊆ dom φ` and `φ(N)` inside half a ball contained in the domain of a retraction onto
     `O` (`MChart.exists_small_nhds`, with `closure_inter_ball_subset` of `BumpFunctions.lean`),
     the approximation property transported to `X` (`LocalModel.HasApproxProperty.exists_approx`),
     and the text's estimate `ĝ_x ≥ 1/2` where `f_x = 1`, give **sc-smooth Urysohn functions**
     `F = τ(4 Σ ĝ_x − 1)` for disjoint closed sets; then Mathlib's
     `BumpCovering.exists_isSubordinate_of_prop` produces a bump covering indexed by `Λ` with
     sc-smooth functions, and `BumpCovering.toPartitionOfUnity` (`ρᵢ = fᵢ ∏_{j < i}(1 − f_j)`,
     locally a finite product) replaces the quotient `ĝ_λ / Σ ĝ`. Needed and not stated: locally
     finite sums and finite products of sc-smooth functions are sc-smooth
     (`isScSmoothMap_real_finsum`, `isScSmoothMap_real_finsetProd`), and a function supported in a
     chart domain and sc-smooth in the chart is sc-smooth (`isScSmoothMap_real_of_chart`).
     Metrizability, used twice in the text, is not needed (paracompact Hausdorff spaces are
     normal).
113. **Proposition 5.5.11 (preprint 5.38) is not "an immediate consequence of Theorem 5.37"** *(book 2017:
     Proposition 5.7)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Proposition 5.5.11, p. 234)*. Theorem 5.5.10 (preprint 5.37) produces some atlas with the property, not the given local
     model, and applying "(i) ⇒ (ii)" to the M-polyfold `O` needs sc-smooth partitions of unity on
     `O`, i.e. on the domain of a retraction, a relatively open subset of `C` (partitions of unity
     on open subsets). The formalization (`Polyfold.proposition_5_5_11`) reads "the sc-Banach space
     admits smooth partitions of unity" as "`E₀` admits `C^∞` partitions of unity"
     (`AdmitsContDiffPartitionsOfUnity`) and repeats the argument of "(i) ⇒ (ii)" in `E₀`:
     `A = {x ∈ O | f(x) ≥ ε/2}` is closed in `E₀` because `cl(V) ⊆ O`, so `E₀ ∖ A` and balls
     `B(x, r_x) ⊆ W` (`x ∈ V`, `f` varying by `< ε/2` on `O ∩ B`) cover `E₀`; `g = Σ β_x f(x)` is
     `C^∞` on `E₀`, hence sc-smooth (Corollary 1.2.5 (preprint 1.20)), and composed with any retraction.
114. **Definitions 5.5.4, 5.5.12, 5.5.14 (preprint 5.31, 5.39, 5.41): the readings** *(book 2017: Definitions 5.14, 5.17, 5.18)*.
     `HasContDiffBump V k`: a `C^k` `f ≠ 0` with bounded support. `c₀(Γ)` (`Polyfold.cZero`) is
     the subspace of `ℓ^∞(Γ)` of functions tending to `0` along the cofinite filter, equivalent to
     the text's "`{γ | |f(γ)| > ε}` finite for every `ε > 0`" (`mem_cZero_iff`); the norm is the
     supremum (`norm_cZero`; the text's "max" is attained for `f ≠ 0`). "Homeomorphic embedding" is
     `Topology.IsEmbedding` (`IsCoordinatewiseContDiffEmbedding`). WCG (`IsWCG`): a set `K`
     compact in `WeakSpace ℝ V` with `cl(span K) = V`. "Reflexive", used in Proposition 5.5.15 (preprint 5.42) but
     not defined in the text, is the surjectivity of `V → V''` (`IsReflexive`).
115. **Proposition 5.5.15 (preprint 5.42): both cases are formalized; Kakutani's theorem is in Mathlib in another
     form** *(book 2017: Proposition 5.8)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Proposition 5.5.15, p. 235)*. (i) The weak compactness of the unit ball of a reflexive
     space is `NormedSpace.isCompact_closure_of_isBounded` (Banach–Alaoglu in `V''` and the
     embedding of `V` with its weak topology into `V''` with its weak-* topology): the weak closure
     of the ball is weakly compact, and its span is `V` (the text's "Clearly `E = span(B)`", here
     `span_closedBall_eq_top`) (`Polyfold.proposition_5_5_15_reflexive`). (ii) The text's `{0} ∪
     {xₙ/n}` for a dense sequence of the unit ball (index range missing, "`(xₙ)_{n≥}`") is replaced by
     a dense sequence `(yₙ)` of `V` scaled by `1/((n + 1)(|yₙ| + 1))`: a null sequence with its
     limit is compact, hence weakly compact, and its span contains every `yₙ`
     (`Polyfold.proposition_5_5_15_separable`).
116. **Corollary 5.5.17 (preprint 5.44): the proof's two references are off, and "Hilbert ⇒ reflexive" is proved**
     *(book 2017: Corollary 5.2)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Corollary 5.5.17, p. 235)*. (a) Theorem 5.5.16 (preprint 5.43) enters as the explicit hypothesis
     `GodefroyTroyanskiWhitfieldZizlerStatement (E₀) ∞` (`Polyfold.corollary_5_5_17`). (b) "Hilbert"
     is `‖v‖² = b(v, v)` for a continuous bilinear `b`, as in Proposition 5.5.8 (preprint 5.35) (item 44); "a
     Hilbert space is reflexive" is proved (`isReflexive_of_hilbert`: the parallelogram law gives an
     inner product with the same norm, `InnerProductSpace.ofNorm`, and every `φ ∈ V''` is `J(y)` for
     the Riesz representative `y` of `x ↦ φ(⟨x, ·⟩)`), then Proposition 5.5.15 (i) (preprint 5.42). (c) What Theorem
     5.5.16 (preprint 5.43) needs is a classical `C^∞`-bump on `E₀` (`τ(1 − |v|²)`, `hasContDiffBump_of_hilbert`),
     not the sc-smooth bump functions the text recalls. (d) "it admits sc-smooth partition of
     unity" should be "`E₀` admits `C^∞` partitions of unity", and "in view of Theorem 5.37" should
     be "in view of Proposition 5.38" (item 113). With Theorem 5.5.10 (preprint 5.37): an M-polyfold built on
     sc-Hilbert spaces admits sc-smooth partitions of unity under the same hypothesis in the charts
     (`MPolyfold.admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_hilbert`).
     (2026-11-12) The hypothesis is dropped: `corollary_5_5_17_unconditional`, since `E₀` is separable and the
     separable case of Theorem 5.5.16 is proved (item 184; row V5.63, now restated).
117. **Cited theorems not formalized: 5.32, 5.40, 5.43** *(book 2017: Theorems 5.10, 5.13, 5.14)*.
     Theorem 5.5.5 (preprint 5.32) (Bonic–Frampton: smoothness of the `p`-th power of the `Lᵖ`-norm, [9] Theorem 1),
     Theorem 5.5.13 (preprint 5.40) (Toruńczyk: `C^k` partitions of unity iff a coordinate-wise `C^k` homeomorphic
     embedding into some `c₀(Γ)`, [9] Theorem 30) and Theorem 5.5.16 (preprint 5.43) (Godefroy–Troyanski–Whitfield–
     Zizler [12]: a WCG space with a `C^k`-bump function admits `C^k` partitions of unity, [9]
     Theorem 31) are deep Banach space geometry, and nothing on the main line uses partitions of
     unity (the transversality theorems use bump functions, whose Hilbert case, Proposition 5.5.8 (preprint 5.35),
     is elementary). Theorem 5.5.13 (preprint 5.40) is recorded as the statement `TorunczykStatement V k` (not used),
     Theorem 5.5.16 (preprint 5.43) as `GodefroyTroyanskiWhitfieldZizlerStatement V k`, the explicit hypothesis of
     Corollary 5.5.17 (preprint 5.44); Theorem 5.5.5 (preprint 5.32) is used only in the remarks of item 118 and is not stated.
     (2026-11-12) **All three are now proved**: Theorem 5.5.5 is `BonicFrampton.theorem_5_5_5` (all three cases, real
     `Lᵖ(μ)` of any measure space; V5.75, gap G.50), Theorem 5.5.13 is `theorem_5_5_13` (V5.59, gap G.52), Theorem
     5.5.16 is `theorem_5_5_16` (V5.62, gap G.53) (item 184).
118. **The `Lᵖ` and Sobolev remarks are not formalized** (lines 7962–7979): "we deduce immediately
     for the Sobolev spaces `W^{k,p}(Ω)` that the usual norms have the same differentiability as
     `|·|_{Lᵖ}`", the bump function `β(|x|ᵖ)` of `Lᵖ`, and the remark that `W^{1,4}(Ω)` with
     `E_m = W^{1+m,4}(Ω)` admits sc-smooth bump functions while for `W^{1,3/2}(Ω)` the
     straightforward one is only sc¹ (with the open question whether an sc-smooth bump exists). They
     need Sobolev spaces and their sc-structures (gap G.1) and Theorem 5.5.5 (preprint 5.32). In the extracted text
     "`E_m = (W^{1+m,4}(Ω)`" has an unbalanced parenthesis.
     (2026-11-12) **Now formalized** (`GapP1_SobolevRemark1–3`, `GapP1_SobolevCube1–5`; row V5.76, narrower; gap G.51;
     item 185). `W^{k,p}(Ω)` is modelled by tuples of weak derivatives in the `ℓ^p`-product of `L^p(Ω)`, so the usual
     norm satisfies `‖u‖^p = Σ‖D^α u‖^p` by definition of the product norm, and the differentiability follows from
     Theorem 5.5.5 by composition with the continuous linear maps `D^α`. The sc-consequences use only `E₀`: a `C^∞`
     bump on `E₀`, rescaled and translated, gives the bump property of every local model on `E` (a generalization of
     the proof of Proposition 5.5.8). The sc-structure `E_m = W^{1+m,p}(Ω)` is constructed for the unit interval
     `(0,1)¹` and every `p > 1` (`SobolevCube.cubeSc`: every `u ∈ W^{k+1,p}` has `D^ju = c + ∫_0^x D^{j+1}u`, the
     Volterra operator is compact on `L^p(0,1)` by the Hölder estimate, and density comes from approximating the top
     derivative by a polynomial); for other bounded domains, including cubes in `ℝⁿ`, `n ≥ 2`, it remains a hypothesis
     of `sobolevSc`. "Non-vanishing `β`" is read as `β(0) ≠ 0`.
119. **Partitions of unity give bump functions** (the easy direction of the open problem stated
     after Definition 5.5.2 (preprint 5.29)): `MPolyfold.AdmitsScPartitionsOfUnity.admitsBumpFunctions` (for
     `x ∈ U`, the function attached to `U` of a partition of unity subordinate to `{U, X ∖ {x}}` is
     `1` at `x`), with bump functions in the sense of Definition 5.3.1 (preprint 5.9) read as `f(x) ≠ 0` (item 41).
     The converse, open in the text, is not addressed.
120. **Slips in §5.5 (preprint Appendix 5.4.2) after Proposition 5.5.8 (preprint 5.35)** (lines 7890–8197): "Fry and McManusi" (and
     "Epostiones" in [9]), "Godefry" in [12] (Godefroy); Theorem 5.5.5 (preprint 5.32) "(1) If is an even integer"
     (`p` missing, also in (2)); in the proof of Theorem 5.5.10 (preprint 5.37) the final estimate writes `β₀(x)g(y)`
     for `β₀(y)g(y)` and `β_{x_i}(z)` for `β_{x_i}(y)`, "for all `y ∈ U`" for all `y ∈ X`, and
     "`f|Q_λ ≡ 1`" for `f_λ|Q_λ ≡ 1`; hypothesis (ii) is used with "`< 1/2`" while Definition 5.5.9 (preprint 5.36)
     gives "`≤ ε`" (enough: `ĝ_λ ≥ 1/2 > 0` on `Q_λ`); Proposition 5.5.15 (preprint 5.42): "compact. in the weak
     topology"; Corollary 5.5.17 (preprint 5.44): "has the smooth approximation property" for the sc-smooth one.

Follow-ups of the round-trip audit (`RoundTrip/`, item V5.22): Remark 5.3.4 (preprint 5.12) as stated
(`Chapter5/SolutionSetClosed.lean`, 2026-11-01).

130. **Remark 5.3.4 (preprint 5.12) as stated is now proved: for every `s` in the completion of `Γ^{+,1}_U(P)`
     the solution set of `f + s = 0` is closed, hence compact (revises item 27).** Item 27: the
     remark's argument gives `S_{f+s} ⊆ {x ∈ U | N(f(x)) ≤ 1}` and so a compact closure
     (`Polyfold.remark_5_3_4`), but the closedness of `S_{f+s}` is not discussed in the text and was
     left open in the project. The points of the completion are now represented by sections:
     `StrongBundle.IsInAllowableCompletion N U s` says that `s` is a section with values in
     `Y_{0,1}` and that for every `ε > 0` some allowable `s' ∈ StrongBundle.allowableSections N U`
     has `N(s(x) − s'(x)) ≤ ε` for all `x` (the difference taken in the fibre `(Y_{0,1})_x`,
     `StrongBundle.sectionOneVec`). The allowable sections satisfy it
     (`StrongBundle.isInAllowableCompletion_of_mem`). Proved: such an `s` vanishes off `U` and has
     `N(s) ≤ 1` (`IsInAllowableCompletion.isZeroAt_of_not_mem`, `.auxLe_one`), the hypotheses of
     `remark_5_3_4`; for a continuous section `f`, the solution set of `f + s` is closed
     (`IsInAllowableCompletion.isClosed_solutionSet_sectionAdd`); hence the remark as stated,
     `Polyfold.remark_5_3_4_completion` (`U ⊇ f⁻¹(0)` with `cl{x ∈ U | N(f(x)) ≤ 1}` compact) and
     `Polyfold.remark_5_3_4_of_isScFredholmSection` (`f` sc-Fredholm with compact solution set,
     `U` the neighbourhood of Theorem 5.2.2 (preprint 5.5)). The closedness is a chart argument. Near a limit
     point `x` of `S_{f+s}`, in a strong bundle chart `Φ` of the atlas, Lemma 5.1.2's (preprint 5.2) bound
     `|Φ[1](w)₂|₁ ≤ A·N(w)` turns `ρ(s, s') ≤ ε` into `|Φ(s(y))₂ − Φ(s'(y))₂|₀ ≤ ‖ι‖Aε` near `x`.
     The map `y ↦ Φ(f(y))₂ + Φ(s'(y))₂` is continuous (`s'` is sc⁺) and is `≤ ‖ι‖Aε` at the zeros
     of `f + s` near `x`, hence at `x`; so `|Φ(f(x))₂ + Φ(s(x))₂|₀ ≤ 2‖ι‖Aε` for every `ε`, and
     `f(x) + s(x) = 0`. Only the continuity of `f` is used. This is the round-trip auditor's proof
     (item V5.22, `RoundTrip/Items/V5_22.lean`, `isClosed_solSet`) moved into the project; the
     docstrings of `remark_5_3_4` and of `Compactness.lean` now point to it.
131. **Choices, and what is not done.** (a) "The completion" is read through its representation
     by sections (uniform `N`-limits of allowable sections). That every `ρ`-Cauchy sequence of
     allowable sections has such a limit (by the completeness of the fibres, Definition 5.1.1 (1) (preprint 5.1))
     is not formalized, and neither is the metric space `(Γ^{+,1}_U(P), ρ)` itself (item 89).
     (b) `remark_5_3_4` keeps its statement (any section vanishing off `U` with `N(s) ≤ 1`, compact
     closure): Theorems 5.3.5, 5.3.10, 5.3.12 (preprint 5.13, 5.18, 5.19) use it in that form for sc⁺-sections, whose solution sets
     are closed by `isClosed_solutionSet` (item 69). The new theorems are corollaries, so the
     change is local to the new file. (c) The proof shows in effect that near each point the
     principal part of `s` in a chart is a uniform limit in `F₀` of continuous maps; the
     continuity of `s` is not stated as a separate lemma.

**140–149: Corollary 5.2.5 (preprint 5.8) on the shifted strong bundle (2026-11-02).** (`Chapter5/StrongBundleShift.lean`,
`Chapter5/Corollary58.lean`; round-trip item V5.14, HANDOFF item 9; revises items 21, 22.)

140. **The shifted strong bundle `P¹ : Y¹ → X¹` is constructed (revises item 21).** The text uses
     `P^i : Y^i → X^i` in Corollary 5.2.5 (preprint 5.8) without defining it. `Polyfold.StrongBundle.shift` is a
     strong bundle over the M-polyfold `X¹` (`MPolyfold.shift`) in the sense of Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51):
     total space `StrongBundle.ShiftSpace` = `Y_{1,1}` = the level `Y[0]_1` of the M-polyfold `Y[0]`
     with its level topology (Hausdorff and paracompact by Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) for `Y[0]`), projection
     `StrongBundle.shiftProj` (`P¹ = P|_{Y_{1,1}}`, continuous and surjective), fibres
     `P⁻¹(x) ∩ Y_{1,1}` (`shiftFiberSubmodule`, a linear subspace: in a chart it is the preimage of
     `F₁` under the linear fibre map), and the atlas of the **index raises of the strong bundle
     charts** `StrongBundleChart.shift`: base chart the level chart `φ¹ : V₁ → O₁`, fibre model `F¹`,
     retraction `R¹ = strongShift R` on `U¹ ◁ F¹` (`IsStrongBundleRetraction.shift`, with
     `R¹(U¹ ◁ F¹) = K_{1,1}` and `r¹(U¹) = O¹`), bundle chart the level chart of `Φ` in `Y[0]`.
     `StrongBundleChart.Compatible.shift`: compatible charts have compatible index raises — on `[0]`
     by `levelChart_compatible`, on `[1]` because `(Φ'¹ ∘ (Φ¹)⁻¹)[1]` is the level-`1` map of
     `(Φ' ∘ Φ⁻¹)[1]` (Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17) for retracts), and the `F₁`-condition of Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50)
     because `[1]` of the transition is sc⁰ (it maps `E₁ ⊕ F₂` into `E'₁ ⊕ F'₂`). The Banachable
     fibres come from a general fact proved here, `StrongBundleChart.isBanachable_fiber`: through a
     chart, `P⁻¹(x) ≅ K_{φ(x)} = {h | Γ(φ(x), h) = h}`, a closed subspace of `F₀`
     (`StrongBundleChart.fiberCLE`). Checks: `StrongBundle.mem_shift_doubleLevel_iff`
     (`(Y¹)_{m,k} = Y_{m+1,k+1}`), `StrongBundle.isChart_shift_toMPolyfold0_iff` (the M-polyfold
     `Y¹[0]` is `Y[0]¹`), `StrongBundle.isChart_shift` (the index raise of every chart of `P` is a
     chart of `P¹`).
141. **The reading of `Y^1`.** `Y¹ = Y_{1,1}` with `(Y¹)_{m,k} = Y_{m+1,k+1}`, the convention of
     `E¹` and of `(U ◁ F)¹ = U¹ ◁ F¹`; not `Y_{0,1} = Y[1]` and not `Y_{1,2}`. It is forced by
     "`f^i` is the section obtained by raising the index": an sc-smooth section maps `X₁` into
     `Y_{1,1}` (and in general not into `Y_{1,2}`), so `f¹ = f|_{X₁}` is a section of `Y_{1,1} → X₁`.
     The fibre `P¹⁻¹(x)` carries the topology of `F₁` (from `Y¹`), not the subspace topology of
     `P⁻¹(x)`.
142. **Raising the index of sc-smooth maps, and the levels of `X¹` (part of gap G.6; G.6 is closed since, Chapter 2, item 77).**
     `MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.levelOne`: an sc-smooth map `f : X → Z` between M-polyfolds induces an
     sc-smooth `f₁ : X¹ → Z¹` (continuity and the chart condition from the level-`1` maps of the
     local representatives, Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17) for retracts). `MPolyfold.mem_shift_levelSet_iff`,
     `mem_shift_smoothSet_iff`: `(X¹)_m = X_{m+1}`, `(X¹)_∞ = X_∞` as sets (the topologies of

143. **Corollary 5.2.5 (preprint 5.8) for `i = 1` is proved: `f¹` is an sc-Fredholm section of `P¹ : Y¹ → X¹` with
     compact solution set (revises items 21, 22; gap G.41).** `Polyfold.corollary_5_2_5`: for an
     sc-Fredholm `f` (Definition 3.1.16 (preprint 3.14), the text's germ reading of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11)) with compact
     solution set, `B.shift.IsScFredholmSection (B.sectionShift f)` and the solution set of `f¹` is

144. **Condition (3) of the filling on level `1` (the content of "it is a priori clear"): proved

     `K → O`, so by Lemma 3.1.20 (preprint 3.17) (`IsFillingGerm.add_section`) `g' = g + ŝ ∘ r` fills `f̂ + ŝ` with the
     **same** fill defect, and `g'(0) = g(0) − Γ(0, g(0)) = 0`; with the sc⁺-germ
     `s' = s + Γ¹(r(·), −s(0))`, `g' − s' = g − s` on `U`, so Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52) in sc form

**150–159: the allowable sections are not complete (2026-11-02).** (`Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric.lean`;
comparison item V5.21, gap G.42; revises items 47, 89, 131 (a).)

150. **`(Γ^{+,1}_U(P), ρ)` is a metric space.** `StrongBundle.allowableDist B N U s s'` is
     `ρ(s, s') = sup_x N(s(x) − s'(x))`, the supremum of the existing pointwise distance
     `StrongBundle.sectionDistAt`. For an auxiliary norm `N`: the supremum is finite,
     `ρ ≤ 2` (`allowableDist_le_two`, from `N(s(x) − s'(x)) ≤ N(s(x)) + N(s'(x))` and
     `N(s(x)) ≤ 1`); `ρ(s, s) = 0`, symmetry and the triangle inequality come from the fibre
     norms (Definition 5.1.1 (1) (preprint 5.1): `N(−v) = N(v)`, subadditivity), and `ρ(s, s') = 0 ⇒ s = s'` from
     "`N` vanishes only at `0_x`" (`allowableDist_self`, `allowableDist_comm`,
     `allowableDist_triangle`, `eq_of_allowableDist_eq_zero`). `StrongBundle.allowableMetric U hN`
     is the `MetricSpace` structure; `StrongBundle.AllowableSpace U hN` is `Γ^{+,1}_U(P)` as a type
     carrying it (a type synonym: `X → Y` carries the product topology). The project's density
     statements (`N(s(x) − s'(x)) ≤ ε` for all `x`, items 60, 89) are `ρ(s, s') ≤ ε`
     (`allowableDist_le_iff`). The round-trip proof of the metric axioms (item 47,
     `RoundTrip/Items/V5_21.lean`) is now in the project in this form. Only the continuity-free
     axioms of `N` are used (Definition 5.1.1 (1) (preprint 5.1)); (2) and the continuity of `N` are not needed.
151. **"Not complete" is proved for the trivial bundle `ℝ × ℝ → ℝ`.** With
     `TrivialBundle.bundle 1 1` (the bundle of `Chapter3/NonVacuity.lean`), the fibre norm
     `N(x, v) = |v|` (`TrivialBundle.fibNorm`, an auxiliary norm: `isAuxNorm_fibNorm`, including
     the condition on `Y[1]`'s generated topology) and `U = ℝ`:
     `TrivialBundle.not_completeSpace_allowableSections`. The sections
     `s_j(x) = (x, √(x² + 1/(j+1)²)/(2√(1 + x²)))` are allowable (graphs of `C^∞` maps are sc⁺,
     `isScPlusSection_graphSection`; `N ≤ 1/2`) and `ρ(s_i, s_j) ≤ (ε_i + ε_j)/2`; a `ρ`-limit `s`
     would have fibre part `|x|/(2√(1 + x²))` (pointwise limits), which is not differentiable at
     `0`, but the fibre part of any sc⁺-section of the trivial bundle is `C¹`
     (`differentiable_snd_of_isScPlusSection`, from Proposition 1.2.3 (preprint 1.18) in the chart `Φ = id`).
152. **The text's "not complete" is false without a hypothesis.** `(Γ^{+,1}_U(P), ρ)` is complete
     when `U = ∅` (it is `{0}`: `StrongBundle.completeSpace_allowableSections_empty`, any bundle,
     any auxiliary norm) and over a point with finite-dimensional fibre
     (`TrivialBundle.completeSpace_allowableSections_point`: `X = ℝ⁰`, fibre `ℝᵏ`, any `U`;
     `Γ^{+,1}_U(P)` is the closed unit ball of `ℝᵏ`, or `{0}` if `U = ∅`). In the text's setting
     (`U` a neighbourhood of the solution set of an sc-Fredholm section, in an M-polyfold that
     admits sc-smooth bump functions) one expects non-completeness as soon as `U` contains a
     non-isolated point over which `Y_{0,1}` is nonzero, by the same mechanism (bump functions
     times a non-smooth uniform limit); this general statement is **not formalized**. Suggested
     reading: "not complete in general".
153. **Not done.** The general sufficient condition of item 152; the identification of the
     metric completion of `(Γ^{+,1}_U(P), ρ)` with the section representation used in Remark 5.3.4 (preprint 5.12)
     (item 131 (a): that every `ρ`-Cauchy sequence has a uniform `N`-limit section is still not
     formalized).

**160–169: weak versus pointwise bump functions (2026-11-02).** (`Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise.lean`;
comparison items V5.16, V5.17, V5.51; sharpens item 41.)

160. **Bump points.** `MPolyfold.HasBumpAt PX x`: for every open `U ∋ x` there is an sc-smooth
     `f : X → ℝ` with `f(x) ≠ 0` and `supp(f) ⊆ U`. The pointwise reading of Definition 5.3.1 (preprint 5.9)
     (`AdmitsBumpFunctions`, item 41) is "every point is a bump point"
     (`admitsBumpFunctions_iff_forall_hasBumpAt`, `Iff.rfl`); the weak reading (Definition 5.5.2 (preprint 5.29) as
     written, `AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak`) follows from "the bump points are dense"
     (`admitsBumpFunctionsWeak_of_dense`: a bump at a bump point `y ∈ U` is not identically zero
     and has support in `U`). The converse — weak ⟹ the bump points are dense — holds by a
     nested-neighbourhoods argument: in a chart `φ`, open sets `V₀ ⊇ cl V₁ ⊇ V₁ ⊇ …` inside `U`
     with `f_n` supported in `V_n` and non-zero on `V_{n+1}`, `diam φ(V_n) → 0`, and Cantor's
     theorem in `E₀` (a retract is closed near its points, `closure_inter_ball_subset`) gives a
     point of `⋂ V_n`, which is a bump point; **not formalized**. So the two readings are:
     pointwise = every point is a bump point, weak = the bump points are dense. The set of bump
     points is invariant under sc-diffeomorphisms of `X`.
161. **On an sc-Banach space the weak reading gives all smooth points**
     (`MPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak.hasBumpAt_of_mem_smooth`,
     `…exists_bump_of_mem_smooth`), for `E` as the M-polyfold `scPolyfold E` with the identity
     chart `scChart E` (model `(E, E, E)`; `isScSmoothMap_scPolyfold_iff`: the sc-smooth functions
     of the M-polyfold `E` are the sc-smooth maps `E → ℝ` on `univ`). Given `x ∈ E_∞` and
     `B(x, ε) ⊆ U`: a bump `f ≢ 0` with support in `B(x, ε/2)` is non-zero on a non-empty open set,
     which contains a smooth point `y` (`E_∞` is dense); `a = y − x` is smooth, so `v ↦ f(v + a)`
     is sc-smooth (`isScSmooth_add_const`, `Chapter4/Recentre.lean`), non-zero at `x`, with support
     in `B(x, ε/2) − a ⊆ B(x, ε) ⊆ U`. Point (b) of item 41 by machine: translation by `a ∉ E_m`
     is not even sc⁰ (`not_isSc0_add_const`, `not_isScSmooth_add_const`: it sends `0 ∈ E_m`
     outside `E_m`), so the argument stops at `E_∞`. For charts whose models are open subsets of
     `E` without boundary the same argument works locally; for a general retract `O` there is no
     translation, and nothing beyond item 160 is proved.
162. **Hilbert models: both readings hold at every point** (already in the project:
     `MPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert`, Proposition 5.5.8 (preprint 5.35) in the charts and Theorem 5.5.7 (preprint 5.34);
     the weak form by `AdmitsBumpFunctions.weak`). The bump `v ↦ τ(1 − b(v − x, v − x)/ρ)` is `C^∞`
     on `E₀`, hence sc-smooth, at every `x`, smooth or not. For M-polyfolds built on sc-Hilbert
     spaces the question of item 41 does not arise — the text's own remark before Definition 5.3.1 (preprint 5.9).
163. **The open question, precisely.** Is there an sc-Banach space `E` (or an M-polyfold `X`) and
     a point `x ∉ E_∞` (necessarily non-smooth, by item 161) such that every sc-smooth
     `f : E → ℝ` with support in some neighbourhood of `x` vanishes at `x`, while the bump points
     are dense (for instance all of `E_∞`)? Equivalently: can the set of bump points be dense
     without being everything? What is known: an sc-smooth `f` is `C^k` on `E_{m+k}` but only
     continuous on `E₀`; for `X = E` the bump points form an `E_∞`-translation-invariant set, so
     they contain `E_∞` as soon as they meet it (item 161); a candidate must have `E₀` without
     `C¹` bump functions (otherwise `β(‖v − x‖²)`-type bumps exist at every point, item 162 and
     `LocalModel.hasBumpProperty_of_quadratic`), e.g. an `ℓ¹`-type scale, but the required `f` is
     only `C¹` on `E_1` on the `E_1`-unbounded set `E_1 ∩ B_0(x, ε)`, so the classical obstructions
     to `C¹` bumps do not apply directly. Neither a counterexample nor a proof is known here. The
     formalization keeps the pointwise reading as the hypothesis of Propositions 5.3.2 (preprint 5.10)/5.30, Lemma
     5.3.3 (preprint 5.11) and Theorem 5.5.7 (preprint 5.34) (item 41), now knowing that it is automatic at the smooth points of a
     linear model and everywhere on Hilbert models. (2026-11-09: settled for sc-Banach spaces, item 180: the bump points of an sc-Banach space are all points or none.)
164. **Bookkeeping.** New file `Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise.lean` (imports `BumpFunctions`,
     `Chapter4/Recentre`), registered after `AllowableSectionsMetric` in `Polyfold.lean`, with a
     `Test.lean` section; every `#print axioms` is standard. Comparison: V5.16 keeps "restated",
     with the chips "weak ⇐ bump points dense" and "weak ⇒ pointwise at smooth points (sc-Banach
     space)", and the diff "Whether the weak reading suffices is open at non-smooth points: on an
     sc-Banach space the weak reading gives a bump at every smooth point
     (`AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak.hasBumpAt_of_mem_smooth`), on Hilbert models both readings hold
     everywhere (`admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert`), and the weak reading is the density of the bump
     points (`HasBumpAt`; one direction formalized) (Findings, Chapter 5, items 160–163)". V5.17
     and V5.51 unchanged. No gap entry changes.

and G.50 changed.)

180. **Bump points of an sc-Banach space: all points or none (item 163 settled for sc-Banach spaces)** *(Definition
     5.5.2 and Proposition 5.5.3, pp. 229–230 (preprint 5.29, 5.30); items 160–163)*.
     `Polyfold/Chapter5/BumpPointsResearch.lean`. Item 161 translates a bump at `x` by `y − x`, which needs `x − y`
     smooth. Instead, an sc-smooth `f` with `f(y) ≠ 0` is continuous on `E₀`, so `f ≠ 0` on a ball `B(y, δ)`; `E_∞` is
     dense, so some smooth `a` has `‖a − (y − x)‖ < δ`, and `v ↦ f(v + a)` is sc-smooth, non-zero at `x`, with support
     in `supp f − a` (`exists_smooth_translate_ne_zero`, `exists_bump_translate`). Hence the bump points of an
     sc-Banach space are empty or everything (`MPolyfold.hasBumpAt_scPolyfold_all_or_nothing`,
     `MPolyfold.HasBumpAt.scPolyfold_all`); dense bump points are all points
     (`MPolyfold.hasBumpAt_scPolyfold_of_dense`), which answers item 163 negatively for sc-Banach spaces; and the weak
     and pointwise readings of bump functions agree there at every point
     (`MPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctionsWeak_iff_admitsBumpFunctions_scPolyfold`; item 161 had the smooth points). Through
     Theorem 5.5.7, an M-polyfold admits bump functions in the pointwise reading when every point has a chart whose
     model sc-Banach space has one bump point (`MPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctions_of_model_hasBumpAt`,
     `MPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctions_of_model_weak`). Open: item 163 for a general M-polyfold (bumps on a retract need
     not come from bumps of `E`), and whether some sc-Banach space has no bump point. Status: **settled** for
     sc-Banach spaces.
181. **Index raises of tame charts are tame (item 145 settled)** *(Corollary 5.2.5, p. 213 (preprint 5.8); Definition
     2.5.2, p. 53; item 145)*. `Polyfold/Chapter5/ShiftTameResearch.lean`. By the presentation independence of
     tameness (`ScRetraction.IsTameWith.isTame`) one presentation of `C¹` suffices, the index raise `T¹` of a
     presentation `T` of `C` (`ScIso.shiftPres`): there `d_{C¹} = d_C` (`degIndex_shift`), `E_y(T¹) = E_y ∩ E₁`
     (`mem_minimalSubspaceWith_shift`), `Dr¹ = Dr|E₁` has range `T_yO ∩ E₁` (Proposition 1.2.2), and `A ∩ E₁` is an
     sc-complement (`ScBanach.IsScSplitting.levelSub_one`). So the index raise of a tame sc-retraction is tame
     (`ScRetraction.IsTame.shift`, `IsTameRetract.shift`, `MPolyfold.IsTame.shift`, a Part I proof of Chapter 7's
     `MPolyfold.IsTame.levelOne`), the base retraction of a shifted strong bundle chart is tame
     (`IsStrongBundleRetraction.baseRetraction_shift_isTame`), and the index raise of a tame strong bundle chart is a
     tame chart of `P¹` (`StrongBundle.IsTameChart.shift`). The germ data of `isScFredholmGerm_sectionShift` thus lie
     in a tame chart (`isScFredholmGermTame_sectionShift`), and Corollary 5.2.5 holds with tame germ data and compact
     solution set (`corollary_5_2_5_tame`, `corollary_5_2_5_isScFredholmSectionTame`; `i = 2` by iteration,
     `corollary_5_2_5_tame_two`). Status: **settled**.

182. **Theorems 5.3.10 and 5.3.12 with the book's quantifiers** *(Theorem 5.3.10, p. 220 (preprint 5.18, p. 177);
     Theorem 5.3.12, p. 222 (preprint 5.19, p. 180); items 80, 85, 87–89)* (2026-11-09).

183. **Theorem 5.3.15: remarks on the proof, settled in Lean** *(Theorem 5.3.15, p. 223 (preprint 5.22, p. 181); proof
     pp. 223–228; items 101, 102, 178; rows V5.71, V5.72)* (2026-11-12). `Polyfold/Chapter5/Theorem5315_*.lean`;
     `theorem_5_3_15` is the printed statement with both conclusions and no added hypothesis (gap G.48 closed). (a)
     *General position at the boundary.* The proof uses the ends only through the general position of `(f, x)` at the
     zeros `x ∈ ∂X`. It follows from the surjectivity of `f_i'(x)` on `T_xX_i` and `T_xX_i ⊆ T^R_xX`, which holds
     because `X_i` has no boundary (the reduced tangent space is chart independent and `T^R_xX_i = T_xX_i`); the
     kernel complement in `X_i` is not needed (`isGeneralPositionGerm_of_restrict`). (b) *No critical points near
     `∂S`.* At `x ∈ ∂X ∩ S` this follows from `0 ≤ t ≤ 1`, `t(x) ∈ {0, 1}`, `dt(x) ≠ 0` and general position: a
     function with an extremum has derivative zero on the reduced tangent space, because reduced directions are
     two-sided (`scDeriv_eq_zero_of_extremum`), so `dt(x) ≠ 0` on `ker f'(x)`, at every degeneracy index of `x` and
     without the ends (`isRegularPointOn_of_extremum`). (c) *The sections at a critical point.* The value
     `−f'(x)b(eᵢ)` of the section must be a smooth point of the fibre (Lemma 5.3.3); it is when the tangent vector is
     smooth, since `f'(x)` is an sc-operator at the smooth point `x`, and smooth tangent vectors with `dt(x)w ≠ 0`
     exist by density (`exists_hasRegularFamilyParam`). This discharges, for the use in Theorem 5.3.15, the "image in
     a smooth line" point of V5.44 (item 102). (d) *"By construction" on p. 227.* That the union of the families keeps
     a surjective linearization at every critical point `(0, y)` uses that the transversality obtained at `x_i`
     persists near `x_i` and in the larger family; with sections vanishing at `x_i` only, the second point needs an
     argument, here the constant function `a₀ = 1` and the coordinates `aᵢ = arctan(qᵢ)/2`
     (`exists_spanning_of_group`). (e) The trivialization `Φ_λ` is replaced by Lagrange multipliers on level sets of
     the solution manifold of `f + Σ μ_j σ_j`; "Morse-type" is read through smooth parametrizations and does not
     depend on the parametrization (`IsMorseOrRegularPoint.morseClause`); the comparison with the Mathlib charts of
     the solution set is not formalized. No statement of the text was found not to hold as we read it. Status:
     **settled**.

184. **The `0`-level of an sc-Banach space is separable; Corollary 5.5.17 needs only the separable case of Theorem
     5.5.16** *(Corollary 5.5.17, p. 235 (preprint 5.44); Theorems 5.5.10, 5.5.13, 5.5.16; items 111, 116, 117; rows
     V5.55, V5.59, V5.62, V5.63)* (2026-11-12). `ScBanach.separableSpace_zero`: `E₁ → E₀` is a compact operator with
     dense range, and the range of a compact operator is separable, so `E₀` is separable. Theorem 5.5.16 for separable
     spaces is the Bonic–Frampton construction (`admitsContDiffPartitionsOfUnity_of_separable`), and Corollary 5.5.17
     holds as stated, with no hypothesis (`corollary_5_5_17_unconditional`,
     `MPolyfold.admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_hilbert_unconditional`). The cited theorems are proved as well: Theorem
     5.5.13 (Toruńczyk) for every real Banach space and every `k` (`theorem_5_5_13`), and Theorem 5.5.16 for every WCG
     Banach space (`theorem_5_5_16`; the recorded statement `GodefroyTroyanskiWhitfieldZizlerStatement` leaves
     completeness out, the theorem assumes it, the text's "Banach"), by the Amir–Lindenstrauss projectional resolution
     built from Lindenstrauss pairs. Under (i) of Theorem 5.5.10 every chart has the approximation property
     (`hasApproxProperty_of_isChart`): shells `{1/(n+2) ≤ d ≤ 1/(n+1)}` of the chart domain avoid the step
     `cl_X(W) ⊆ U` of item 111. Status: **settled**.

185. **The Sobolev remark after Theorem 5.5.5: what it uses, and the sc-structure on `(0,1)`** *(pp. 230–231 (preprint
     pp. 193–194); items 118, 120; row V5.76)* (2026-11-12). The deduction "`W^{1,4}(Ω)` admits sc-smooth bump
     functions" uses only the `0`-level: it holds for every sc-structure on `W^{1,4}(Ω)` and every `Ω`
     (`remark_5_5_5_W14`, through `LocalModel.hasBumpProperty_of_hasContDiffBump`); boundedness and the regularity of
     the boundary matter only for the existence of the sc-structure `E_m = W^{1+m,4}(Ω)`. That structure is built for
     the unit interval `(0,1) ⊂ ℝ¹` and every `p > 1` (`SobolevCube.cubeSc`), where the claim holds on the text's
     sc-structure (`remark_5_5_5_W14_cube`, `remark_5_5_5_W14_instance`). For other bounded domains, including cubes
     in `ℝⁿ`, `n ≥ 2`, the structure is the hypothesis of `sobolevSc` (as we read it, "bounded domain" carries the
     boundary regularity that Rellich's theorem needs). Status: **in part** (one domain).

186. **Preprint Theorem 5.27 in its good-position form, a reading note** *(preprint Theorem 5.27, p. 188; not in the
     2017 or 2021 text; items 88, 104; gap G.49)* (2026-11-12). The general-position analogue is formalized
     (`exists_cobordism`, `exists_homotopy_cobordism`, `remark_5_3_8_arc`). For good position of `f + s` at the corner
     points `{i} × ∂X`, the kernel `ℝ × ker(f + s_i)'(x)` would have to be in good position to `[0,∞) × C_x`, which
     good position of `ker(f + s_i)'(x)` to `C_x` does not imply (`not_isInGoodPosition_prod_diag`, gap G.46). No
     counterexample to the theorem is built, and the 2021 edition drops it.

Found in Part III wave 1 (2026-11-13; files `Chapter5/P3R_*`, `P3B_*`): the reflexive auxiliary norms of §§5.1–5.2 and

187. **Definition 5.1.4: "an (equivalent) atlas of reflexive charts"** *(Definition 5.1.4, p. 207 (2017: Definition
     5.2); not in the preprint)* (2026-11-13). `Chapter5/P3R_Reflexive2021.lean`. Read as: the compatible strong bundle
     charts with reflexive `F₁` cover `X` (`StrongBundle.HasReflexiveFibers`); an atlas all of whose charts have
     reflexive `F₁` gives it (`hasReflexiveFibers_of_atlas`). Reflexivity is the project's §5.5 notion `IsReflexive`

     (`TrivialBundle.hasReflexiveFibers_bundle`). Lemma 5.1.5 is proved in a strong form that identifies the two weak
     limits as one point of `Y₀,₁` (`lemma_5_1_5_limit`), which the proof uses; Proposition 5.1.8, whose proof is left

     5.4.1, Theorem 5.4.2, p. 228 (2017: Definition 5.11, Theorem 5.9))* (2026-11-13).

## Chapter 6 (Linearizations, orientations and invariants; Lean `Polyfold/Chapter6/`)

*Numbering.* The items of this section are numbered in blocks, one block per phase of the work, so
that agents working at the same time do not collide; the gaps in the numbering are unused numbers,
not deleted items. 1–19: §§6.3–6.4 (preprint §§6.2–6.3) and Appendix 6.8 (preprint 6.7), determinant lines, exact sequences, good
left-projections and stabilization (Definitions 6.3.1, 6.4.1–6.4.3, 6.4.16 (preprint 6.3, 6.7–6.9, 6.16), Propositions 6.3.2, 6.3.5, 6.4.11,
6.4.15 (preprint 6.4, 6.6, 6.12,
6.15), Lemma 6.3.3, Proposition 6.4.10, Lemma 6.4.14 (preprint Lemmas 6.5, 6.11, 6.14) and Lemma 6.10 (preprint; not in the 2021 edition), Corollary 6.4.12 (preprint 6.13); `Chapter6/DetLine.lean` to
`Chapter6/DirectSumDet.lean`); 20–39: §6.5 (preprint §6.4) and Proposition 6.6.1 (preprint 6.26), the determinant bundle

Definition 6.6.2 (preprint 6.27) to Definition 6.6.12 (preprint 6.36), the local propagation (`LinSet` to `ContinuousOrientation`);

items 340–369). Statement numbers and pages are the preprint's *(book 2017: see
`BookConcordance.md`)*.

1. **Lemma 6.3.3 (preprint 6.5) is read as "(91) holds for every choice", and the step "if and only if
   `det(τ) = det(ε)`" of §6.8.1 (preprint §6.7.1) as homogeneity** *(book 2017: Lemma 6.1, p. 187; §6.7.1, pp.
   218–219)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Lemma 6.3.3, p. 244; Appendix 6.8.1, pp. 280–281, the same wording)*. "The definition of `Φ_E` does not depend on the choices" is formalized as: the
   linear map `FourTermExact.phi`, defined by (91) for one choice (`canonicalChoice`), satisfies
   (91) for every choice (`lemma_6_3_3`). This is the form every later computation uses: each
   evaluation of `γ^P_T` in §§6.4 and §6.8.2 (preprint §6.3 and §6.7.2) makes its own choices. The proof follows §6.8.1 (preprint §6.7.1)
   (`Choice.exists_smul_source_value`). In §6.8.1 (preprint §6.7.1) the bases of `A` are changed by a map named `σ`
   and the factor is then written `det(τ)` (possible misprint, `τ` for `σ`); "the vector … is
   independent of the choices of the basis if and only if `det(τ) = det(ε)`" states a condition
   where what is needed is that both sides of (91) scale by the same factor `det(σ)/det(ε)`, and
   the proof goes through with that. In the last step the corrections are chosen in "`β(C)`",
   which is read as `β(B)` (possible misprint), and they are combinations of the `β`-images, not
   of the `γ`-preimages: the names of the two blocks of the wedge in `C` are exchanged there with
   respect to the first part of the proof (possible misprint). The 2017 text has the same wording.
2. **Proposition 6.3.5 (preprint 6.6) exchanges the names of the two blocks of the wedge in `C`** *(book 2017:
   Proposition 6.3, p. 188)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Proposition 6.3.5, p. 246)*. The statement writes the basis of `C` with the `β`-images first and
   the `γ`-preimages second, under the names that (91) gives the other way round; the order meant
   is (91)'s, `γ`-preimages first (possible misprint). `proposition_6_3_5` is stated in the order of
   (91). The 2017 text has the same wording.
3. **`Π_T` is not empty, which the text uses without stating it** *(book 2017: Definition 6.5, p.
   189)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Definition 6.4.3, p. 247)*. From Proposition 6.4.10 (preprint Lemma 6.11) on, constructions start with "`P ∈ Π_T`". For `T` Fredholm the
   projection onto `R(T)` along a finite-dimensional complement is good
   (`exists_isGoodLeftProj`). The remarks after Definition 6.4.3 (preprint 6.9) (`P` Fredholm of index `0`, `P T`
   Fredholm of index `ind T`, `R(P) ∩ R(P')` of finite codimension) are formalized as stated
   (`IsGoodLeftProj.isFredholm`, `IsGoodLeftProj.fredholmIndex_comp`,
   `IsGoodLeftProj.finiteDimensional_quotient_inf`).
4. **Lemma 6.10 (preprint): the projection of the text's proof is not below `P` and `P'` as we read it; the
   lemma holds by another construction, without `T` Fredholm; the 2017 remark that a common lower
   bound need not exist does not hold as we read it** *(book 2017: dropped; the remark on p. 190
   before Remark 6.3, and the new Lemmas 6.3–6.5, Definition 6.6, Proposition 6.6)* *(book 2021: unchanged, the remark before Remark 6.4.6, p. 248; Lemma 6.10 absent, as in 2017)*. The text's
   `P''` projects onto `R(P) ∩ R(P')` along a complement `Z ⊕ X ⊕ X'`, and `P'' = P''P` needs
   `ker P ⊆ ker P''`. On `ℝ²` with `T = 1`, `P` the projection onto the `x`-axis along the
   `y`-axis and `P'` the one along the diagonal, `R(P) ∩ R(P')` is the `x`-axis and a projection
   onto it below both would equal both (`lemma_6_10_text_reading_preprint`). The lemma holds with a
   smaller range: for `K = ker P + ker P'` (finite-dimensional), a closed finite-codimensional `N`
   with `N ∩ K = 0` (Hahn–Banach), `R'' = R(P) ∩ R(P') ∩ N` and a closed complement `C ⊇ K` of
   `R''`, the projection onto `R''` along `C` lies in `Π_T` and below `P` and `P'`; `T` need not
   be Fredholm (`lemma_6_10_preprint`). The 2017 version replaces the lemma by the remark that for `P, Q ∈
   Π_T` there need not be `L ∈ Π_T` with `L ≤ P`, `L ≤ Q`, and rebuilds §§6.4–6.5 (preprint §§6.3–6.4) around the
   projections `P_H` onto a fixed range; with the order `P ≤ Q` iff `P = PQ = QP` of both versions
   such an `L` always exists, as we read it. The preprint's route to Lemma 6.5.9 (preprint 6.25) (a common lower
   bound, Corollary 6.4.12 (preprint 6.13), Lemma 6.5.5 (preprint 6.21)) is therefore sound and is the one formalized.

Found while formalizing §6.5 (preprint §6.4) and Proposition 6.6.1 (preprint 6.26) (2026-11-06).

20. **Lemma 6.5.1 (preprint 6.17) does not use that `T` is Fredholm** *(book 2017: Lemma 6.7, p. 201)*. For a
    bounded `T`, `P ∈ Π_T` and a topological complement `Y` of `ker(PT)` (an algebraic complement
    with a continuous projection, `Submodule.IsTopCompl`), `P ∈ Π_S` and `PS|_Y` is an isomorphism
    onto `R(P)` for `S` near `T` (`lemma_6_5_1`); the Fredholm hypothesis is not needed.

    bundle" is formalized as: `(S, k) ↦ (S, k + y(k, S))` is continuous, maps `ker(PT)` onto
    `ker(PS)`, and is inverted by the continuous projection onto `ker(PT)` along `Y`
    (`LocalDetChart.lemma_6_5_2`).

    frames** *(book 2017: Lemma 6.9, Proposition 6.8, p. 202)*. Mathlib has no exterior powers or
    tensor products of vector bundles, and the general Lemma 6.5.3 (preprint 6.19) is not formalized (gap G.59).
    The bundles it is applied to are trivial; `DET(T, P, ε)` is given the frame
    `ω(S) = (k₁(S) ∧ … ∧ kₙ(S)) ⊗ (e₁ ∧ … ∧ e_l)*` (`LocalDetChart.frame`), and "in a natural way"
    is read as: the frames of two charts with the same `P` differ by a continuous nowhere-zero
    factor (`proposition_6_5_4`).
    (2026-11-09) Lemma 6.5.3 is formalized in general (`lemma_6_5_3`, item 125; gap G.59 closed).

    Lemma 6.10, p. 202)*. Lemma 6.5.9 (preprint 6.25) compares charts with different centres and radii, so
    `lemma_6_5_5` is stated on the common ball of any two charts. The text's "this is trivial and
    follows from an inspection" is carried out by extending the kernel sections of `PS` to

    Propositions 6.9, 6.10, Lemma 6.11, p. 204)*. The charts `γ_(T,P,ε)`, read in their frames, are

    collection `𝓑` is a basis of that topology (`detBasis`, `proposition_6_5_7`); Proposition 6.5.8 (preprint 6.24)

    Proposition 6.11, p. 205)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Proposition 6.6.1, p. 263)*. "Consequently has two possible orientations since the base space
    is contractible" needs that a line bundle over such a base is orientable. The proof formalized
    is the standard one: the rays of the fibres form a two-sheeted covering (`OrCover`,
    `isCoveringMap_orCover`), an orientation is a continuous section of it, and the lifting
    criterion applies over a simply connected, locally path-connected base
    (`exists_lineOrientation_apply_eq`, `exists_two_lineOrientation`); a nonempty convex set of
    Fredholm operators is such a base. `proposition_6_6_1` is stated for every nonempty convex set.

Found while formalizing Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1) and §6.6 (preprint §6.5), Definitions 6.6.2–6.6.12 (preprint 6.27–6.36) (2026-11-07).

    exists under `HasScPlusSectionsThrough` (`ChartPoint.linSet_nonempty`), which bump functions
    give (`MPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctions.hasScPlusSectionsThrough`). The members are shown Fredholm

    determinant lines use; that they are sc-Fredholm on every level is not stated (gap G.64).

    (`ChartPoint.definition_6_2_1_linSet_isScFredholm`, `Polyfold/Chapter6/LinSetFredholm.lean`; gap G.64 closed).
    `T_xX` now carries the linear structure of Definition 2.3.14, Banach through every chart and sc at smooth points
    (gap G.7 closed, Chapter 2, item 87); this statement is not restated with it.

    6.9, p. 205)*. `Or_x^f` is the type of orientations of `DET(f, x)` at a chart point
    (`ChartPoint.Or`), with exactly two elements (`ChartPoint.exists_two_or`); on the tensor
    products no negation is set up, so `{o_x, −o_x}` is stated as "exactly two". The morphisms are
    bijections; between two two-element types there are exactly two, each determined by one value
    (`nonempty_equiv_of_two`, `equiv_eq_of_apply_eq_of_two`).
45. **Proposition 6.6.3 (1) (preprint 6.28) is not established for `U` as we read it; (1′) is proved instead**
    *(book 2017: Proposition 6.12, p. 205, with a `U′ ⊂ U` and (1) "`U′ ⊂ U` is sc-smoothly

    `O = r(V)` for a convex `V`; for `U = r(V')` it needs `r(V') ⊆ V'`, which is not stated, and a
    convex domain of the retraction is not available in general. What the proof of Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35)
    uses is (1′): two sc-smooth paths in `U` with the same end points are sc-smoothly homotopic,
    with the end points fixed, in a larger region `W` where (3) holds. `proposition_6_6_3` proves
    (1′) with `W = O ∩ B_δ`, `U = O ∩ B_δ'` and `r(B_δ') ⊆ B_δ`, by
    `Φ(τ, t) = r((1 − ρ(τ)) φ(γ₀(σ(t))) + ρ(τ) φ(γ₁(σ(t))))` in the chart, with `σ` the identity
    near `[0, 1]` and taking values where both paths lie in `U` (the paths lie in `U` only on
    `[0, 1]`; `exists_contDiff_eq_id_near_Icc_mapsTo`) (gap G.61).
    (2026-11-13) This item reads the preprint's (1). The 2021 text, as the 2017 one, prints (1) as "`U′ ⊂ U` is
    sc-smoothly contractible in `U` to the point `x`", and that form is proved (`proposition_6_6_3_one`, item 137; gap
    G.61 closed).
46. **Proposition 6.6.3 (preprint 6.28): the sections are global, (3) is stated for families, and the smoothness of
    `x` is not used** *(book 2017: Proposition 6.12, p. 205)*. The sections of (3) and (4) are
    global sc⁺-sections of `ℝⁿ × X → Y`, made with bump functions, in place of sections over

    `Φ(q)` (`exists_isScPlusSection_pullback_of_family`). The construction does not use that `x` is
    smooth, nor that `X` is tame.
47. **Lemma 6.6.4 (preprint 6.29) has no proof in the text; the general position of `F` is proved, the slice form of

48. **Lemma 6.6.5 (preprint 6.30) is formalized as a continuous family of kernels** *(book 2017: Lemma 6.13, p.
    207)*. Near a zero in good position the kernel is the tangent space of the solution set
    (Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54)), the range of the derivative of an sc-retraction, so the kernels along a
    continuous family of zeros form a continuous family of subspaces of the model space
    (`exists_subspaceFamily_linKer`). The manifold statements (the solution set as a manifold with
    boundary with corners near `(t, φ(t), 0)`, the map `π`, `L` as a smooth bundle) are not
    formalized (gap G.62); the continuation of orientations does not need them.
    (2026-11-09) Near a zero in good position the solution set is a submanifold of dimension the index and a Mathlib
    manifold with corners (`theorem_3_6_8_isSubmanifoldOfDim`, `theorem_3_1_26_isManifold`, Chapter 3, item 380); the
    map `π` and `L` as a smooth bundle are still not formalized (gap G.62 in part).
    (2026-11-09) Near the family the solution set is a manifold, and `π` a submersion at the points of the family (item
    126); `π` off the family and `L` remain open (gap G.62 in part).
     (2026-11-12) The rest is formalized as well: the fibres `S_q` (`lemma_6_6_5_fibre_isManifold`), `π` as a
     submersion near the family (`lemma_6_6_5_submersion_nhds`), `L` as a `C^∞` vector bundle over a neighbourhood of
     `[0, 1]ⁿ`, read in one chart, the text's "X = U" (`lemma_6_6_5_smoothBundle`), and the cube forms
     (`lemma_6_6_5_fibre_isManifold_cube`, `lemma_6_6_5_submersion_cube`). The continuation of orientations still uses

49. **Lemma 6.6.6 (preprint 6.31): `ker F_t'` is read as the kernel of `F'` cut by `σ = 0`, and `c` is onto by the
    general position of `F`** *(book 2017: Lemma 6.14, p. 209)*. In the product chart the
    linearization of the slice is `(v, λ) ↦ T v + φ λ`, and `ker F'(0, (q, z)) ∩ {σ = 0}` is the
    image of `ker(T ⊕ φ)` (`linKer_inf_ker_sliceProj_eq_map`). The text has `c` onto by (P); here
    `F'` is onto by `lemma_6_6_4`, and the `ℝⁿ`-directions are absorbed because the derivative of the
    curve of zeros lies in `ker F'` (`fderiv_mem_linKer`, `surjective_coprod_of_isLinSurjAt`).
    With this, (96) is the stabilization sequence of `T` and `φ` (`lemma_6_6_6`).
50. **Formula (94): `Φ_E` does not vary continuously where `dim coker T` changes parity, as we read
    it; the propagation uses `(−1)^{dim coker T} Φ_E`** *(book 2017: Proposition 6.7, p. 199, and
    §6.5)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Proposition 6.4.15, p. 257, and §6.6)*. In a local determinant chart with projection `P`, the coordinate of `ι_ψ(x)` in
    `det(S ⊕ ψ)` is `(−1)^{k · dim F/R(P) + dim coker S} D(S, ψ)` times that of `x`, with `D`
    continuous and nowhere zero (`coord_stabIota`); the first exponent is constant on a chart, the
    second is not. So along a norm-continuous family `T_q` with continuous stabilizations, the rays
    `Φ_E(o(T_q))` of `λ(ker(T_q ⊕ φ_q))` carried from a continuous orientation `o` need not form an
    orientation: `not_isLineOrientation_stabRay_uncorrected` is an instance with `E = F = ℝ`,
    `k = 1`, `T_q = q/(1 + |q|)`, `φ(r) = r₀`. Lemmas 6.6.8, 6.6.10 (preprint 6.33, 6.34) and the homotopy argument before
    Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35) use that these orientations vary continuously with the parameter. With
    `α(T) = (−1)^{dim coker T}` (`stabSign`) the rays `α(T_q) Φ_E(o(T_q))` do form an orientation
    (`isLineOrientation_stabRay`), and the push-forward uses `α Φ_E` at both end points
    (`IsStabKernels.push`). On each operator `α(T) Φ_E` carries the text's orientation or its
    opposite; for given end-point operators the two push-forwards differ by `α(T_a) α(T_b)`.
51. **Lemma 6.6.8 (preprint 6.33): the homotopy of the text's proof is not needed** *(book 2017: Lemma 6.15, p.
    209)*. "One verifies by a simple computation" is `detEquiv_stabIota_append`: with the appended
    sections last (`appendStab`), the stabilization isomorphism of `(φ, ψ)` is that of `φ` followed
    by `w ↦ (w, 0) ∧ ℓ₁ ∧ … ∧ ℓ_d`, exactly, with no sign. The comparison is made directly between
    `T ⊕ φ` and `T ⊕ (φ, ψ)`, at the end points by Proposition 6.4.15 (preprint 6.15) and along the family by
    `isLineOrientation_wedgeExt` (`propagate_append`, `IsStabKernels.push_append`).
52. **Proposition 6.6.7 (preprint 6.32): Lemmas 6.6.8 and 6.6.10 (preprint 6.33 and 6.34) are combined over one square** *(book 2017:
    Proposition 6.13, Lemmas 6.15, 6.16, pp. 209–211)*. For two data along the same path,
    `S^τ = (1 − τ) S⁰ + τ S¹` with the sections `(1 − τ) ŝ⁰ⱼ + τ ŝ¹ⱼ` (`ŝⁱⱼ = sⁱⱼ` for `j < kⁱ`, `0`
    otherwise), followed by the sections of Lemma 6.6.4 (preprint 6.29) on the square. At `τ = 0` the sections `s⁰`
    are the first `k⁰` of the family and at `τ = 1` the sections `s¹` are the first `k¹`, so Lemma
    6.6.8 (preprint 6.33) applies on both edges without reordering (`IsStabKernels.push_eq_of_prefix`); along the
    edges `t = 0, 1` the operators are affine in `τ` (`linAt_principal_combo`), hence continuous.
53. **Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35) does not introduce `f`; contractibility is replaced by (1′), and the proof needs a

    (2026-11-13) In 2021 Theorem 6.6.11 (p. 272) asks for an open neighbourhood, without "contractible"; Proposition
    6.6.3 (1) holds in its 2021 form (item 137).
54. **Definition 6.6.12 (preprint 6.36) is read over a pair `V ⊆ U`** *(book 2017: Definition 6.10, p. 212, "open path

    Proposition 6.6.3 (preprint 6.28) gives (1′), an orientable neighbourhood is `U` with the local propagation

Found while formalizing Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37) and Definitions 6.6.14–6.6.16 (preprint 6.38–6.40) (2026-11-07).

70. **`Or_x^f` is chart-free in the text; it is made in a chart point and identified between
    charts, and the local propagation is shown to be independent of the chart** *(book 2017: §6.5,
    p. 205, and Theorem 6.2, p. 213)*. The proof of Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37) carries an orientation along
    orientable neighbourhoods of different points of a path, which may lie in different charts; the
    text takes `T_xX`, `Y_x`, `Lin(f, x)` and `Or_x^f` to be the same whichever chart is used. Here
    two chart points at `x` are related by the derivative `A` of the base transition and the fibre
    part `Γ` of the strong bundle transition (`ChartPoint.transferT`, `ChartPoint.transferK`, with
    the cocycle rules), `L ↦ Γ L A⁻¹` maps `Lin_p(f, x)` onto `Lin_{p'}(f, x)`
    (`ChartPoint.mem_linSet_transfer_iff`), and `ChartPoint.orTransfer` identifies the two sets
    `Or_x^f`. The push-forward then agrees in the two charts (`IsPush.transfer`,
    `HasLocalPropagation.push_compat`), by the naturality of the stabilization isomorphism
    (`stabRayEquiv_conjDet`) and of continuation (`SubspaceFamily.cont_map`). `Or_x^f` itself is
    read in a chosen chart (`Orx`, `toChartOr`).
71. **Homotopy classes: the edge conditions hold only on `[0, 1]`, so transitivity needs a
    reparametrization; the identities are the constant paths** *(book 2017: before Theorem 6.2,
    pp. 212–213)*. Paths are maps `ℝ → X` and homotopies maps `ℝ² → X` whose edge conditions are imposed
    for parameters in `[0, 1]` (decision D2). Two homotopies glued in `τ` need not agree off
    `[0, 1]`, so `ScHomotopic.trans` first reparametrizes all paths and homotopies by `κ` in `t`.
    The text does not name the identities of `PX`; they are the classes of the constant paths. The
    reversed paths give inverses, so `PX` is a groupoid (`PathCat.groupoid`).
    (2026-11-09) Paths on the M-polyfold `[0, 1]` are now available (`IsPropagationContinuousI`, `orTransportI`, item
    122); the path category with the text's concatenation is still read on `ℝ`.
     (2026-11-12) The path category is also built on `[0, 1]` as printed, with homotopies on the M-polyfold `[0, 1]²`
     and the text's `β` (`PathCatI`), and it is equivalent to `PathCat` (`PathCatI.toPathCat_isEquivalence`; V6.52).
72. **Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37): the covering argument is a dyadic subdivision, (∗) is asked on every open set
    with the local propagation property, and uniqueness uses only composition and (∗)** *(book
    2017: Theorem 6.2, p. 213)*. The transport along a path is the composite of the push-forwards
    along its `2ᴺ` dyadic pieces for any `N` at which every piece lies in a good set (Lebesgue
    number lemma); homotopy invariance is the same on the square (`LocalTransport`,
    `transport_eq_of_isScHomotopyRel`). (∗) is formalized for every chart, every open `U` with the
    local propagation property in it and every push-forward along a path in `U`
    (`IsStarProperty`); the sc-smooth contractibility of `U` is not asked (gap G.61), and the
    uniqueness needs (∗) only on a family of such sets covering `X_∞`
    (`orFunctorMap_unique_of_cover`). "Uniquely determined functor" is read for the maps on
    morphisms (on objects there is no choice), and `𝒪_f` as types and bijections (`orFunctor`).
    The theorem uses the standing hypotheses of Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35) and sc⁺-sections through every smooth
    fibre point (so that every `Or_x^f` has two elements), which bump functions give.
    (2026-11-09) The clean `theorem_6_6_13` takes only `X` tame, bump functions and tame germ data: the sc⁺-sections
    come from the bump functions and the paracompactness instances are proved (item 122).
73. **Definitions 6.6.14 and 6.6.15 (preprint 6.38 and 6.39) are called equivalent without proof; the equivalence is proved, with
    "the same path component" read as "joined by an sc-smooth path"** *(book 2017: Definitions
    6.11, 6.12, p. 213)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Definitions 6.6.14, 6.6.15, p. 274)*. For points not joined by an sc-smooth path there is nothing to check in
    Definition 6.6.14 (preprint 6.38) (`IsOrientableSection`). Both definitions are shown equivalent to the existence
    of `y ↦ o_y` with `Γ_f([φ]) o_x = o_y` for all `[φ]` (`isOrientableSection_iff_exists`,
    `isOrientableSection'_iff_exists`), hence to each other (`isOrientableSection_iff`). From 6.39
    to 6.38 the transport along a path is computed on dyadic pieces inside orientable
    neighbourhoods (`LocalTransport.transport_apply_eq_of_local`); from 6.38 to 6.39 a base point is
    chosen in each class of points joined by sc-smooth paths.
74. **Definition 6.6.15 (preprint 6.39) writes "`y ∈ U_∞`" before any `U` is introduced** *(book 2017: corrected
    to `y ∈ X_∞`, Definition 6.12, p. 213)* *(book 2021: corrected as in 2017, Definition 6.6.15, p. 274)*. It is read as `y ∈ X_∞` (possible misprint).
75. **Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40): orientations are the families preserved by `Γ_f`** *(book 2017: Definition
    6.13, p. 214)*. With the orientable neighbourhoods of item 54, an orientation of `f` is a map
    `y ↦ o_y` with `Γ_f([φ]) o_x = o_y` for all `[φ]` (`isSectionOrientation_iff`); `f` has one iff
    it is orientable (`exists_isSectionOrientation_iff`), two that agree at a point agree on the
    points joined to it by sc-smooth paths, and there are exactly two on each such class
    (`IsSectionOrientation.apply_eq_iff`, `IsSectionOrientation.exists_two`).

Found while formalizing Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41) and Remark 6.6.19 (preprint 6.42) (2026-11-07).

90. **Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41): the first assertion comes from Chapters 4 and 5; "proper" is used only through
    the compactness of `S`** *(book 2017: Theorem 6.3, p. 214)*. "We already know from the
    transversality discussion" is `theorem_6_6_18_solutionSet`: for `X` tame and `f` with tame germ
    data in general position (Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17)) at every zero, `S` is compact, a smooth submanifold
    in general position with the induced structure of a tame manifold with boundary with corners
    (the conclusions of Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18)), using Lemma 4.2.8 (preprint 4.19) for good position
    (`MPolyfold.IsGeneralPositionAt.isGoodPositionAt`). Of "proper" (`StrongBundle.IsProper`)
    only the compactness of the solution set is used; for sc-Fredholm sections the two are
    equivalent (Chapter 5, comparison item V5.10), so nothing of the hypothesis is lost.
91. **"`T_xS` is oriented by `o_f(x)`" and "the local prolongation … is the Fredholm one" are read
    in a chart, along the paths of zeros** *(book 2017: Theorem 6.3, p. 214)*. At a zero, `f'(x)`
    (the linearization of `f + s` with `s = 0`) lies in `Lin(f, x)` and is onto, and
    `det f'(x) ≅ λ(ker f'(x))`, with `ker f'(x) = T_xS` in the chart
    (`tangentSpace_solutionSet_eq_linKer`); `ChartPoint.tangentOr` is the resulting orientation of
    `λ(T_xS)`. The second sentence is read as: along every sc-smooth path of zeros in an orientable
    neighbourhood, the kernels form a continuous family `Λ` (Lemma 6.6.5 (preprint 6.30), `tangentFamily`) and the
    tangent orientations of an orientation of `f` form an orientation of `λ(Λ)`
    (`isLineOrientation_tangentOr`). The Fredholm side is the push-forward for the datum `S = 0`,
    `k = 0`, which along a path of zeros is continuation between tangent orientations
    (`isStabKernels_zero`, `IsStabKernels.orRay_eq_tangentOr`); intermediate points are reached by
    the paths `s ↦ γ(t κ(s))`, which stay in `γ([0, t])` for all `s ∈ ℝ`.
92. **Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41): the orientation of `S` as a manifold and its chart independence are not
    formalized** *(book 2017: Theorem 6.3, p. 214)*. "A natural orientation" is formalized as the
    tangent orientations with their continuity along paths of zeros in a chart (`theorem_6_6_18_hyp`);
    an orientation of `S` as an abstract finite-dimensional manifold, of its tangent bundle in the
    charts of the induced structure (gap G.67), and the compatibility of the tangent orientations
    read in two charts at the same zero (gap G.68) are not formalized.
    (2026-11-09) The chart compatibility of the tangent orientations is proved (`tangentOrAt_toChartOr`; gap G.68
    closed), and `S` is a compact Mathlib manifold with corners (`theorem_6_6_18_isManifold`); the orientation of `S` as
    a manifold is still open (gap G.67; item 123).
    (2026-11-09) The orientation of `S` as a manifold is formalized as a continuous tangent orientation of the Mathlib
    manifold `S` (`theorem_6_6_18_oriented`; gap G.67 closed; item 127).
93. **The paragraph after Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41) is not formalized** *(book 2017: after Theorem 6.3, p.
    214)*. For `f` not generic, a small sc⁺-perturbation `s` supported near the zero set, the
    orientation of `S_{f+s}` coming from `o_f`, and the identification of `det((f + s)'(x))` with a

    `S_{f+s}` for the perturbations of Theorem 5.3.10 (`theorem_6_6_18_perturbation`; gap G.69 closed; item 123).
95. **Remark 6.6.19 (preprint 6.42): the map `h ↦ h̃` is not continuous in `L` where the parity of `dim coker L`
    changes, as we read it; the sign `(−1)^{dim coker L}` is used** *(book 2017: Remark 6.4, p.
    214)* *(book 2021: corrected, as we read it: Remark 6.6.19, p. 276, wedges `e` first, so `h ↦ h̃` is `w ↦ e ∧ w` in local charts and no parity sign arises)*. For `L̃ = L ⊕ 0 : E × ℝ → F`, `h ↦ h̃ = (a₁ ∧ … ∧ aₙ ∧ e) ⊗ (b₁ ∧ … ∧ b_l)*` is an
    isomorphism `det(L) ≅ det(L̃)` (`extDet`, `extDet_wedge_tmul`), and in local determinant charts
    its coordinate is `(−1)^{dim F/R(P) + dim coker L}` times a continuous nowhere-zero function
    (`coord_extDet`). Over the convex set `Lin(f, x)`, where `dim coker L` can change parity, the
    orientation of `DET(f̂, (x, t))` defined by `h̃` at one `L` could therefore differ from the one
    defined at another. With `extDetN = (−1)^{dim coker L} · extDet` (the sign `stabSign` of item 50)
    the coordinate is continuous up to a sign constant on a chart (`coord_extDetN`), continuous
    orientations pull back (`LineOrientation.extPull`), and an orientation `o` of `DET(f, x)` gives
    exactly one orientation `ô` of `DET(f̂, (t, x))` with `ô(L̂)` the image of `o(L)` for every
    `L ∈ Lin(f, x)` (`ChartPoint.existsUnique_prodOr`, `ChartPoint.prodOr`). The two maps agree when
    `L` is onto (`extDetN_eq_of_surjective`). This is the same kind of sign as formula (94), item 50.
    (2026-11-09) The 2021 Remark 6.6.19 puts `e` first, `h̃ = (e ∧ a₁ ∧ … ∧ a_n) ⊗ d*`; that map differs from the
    continuous sign-normalized one by `(−1)^{ind L}`, which is locally constant, so it is continuous in `L` and is used
    as printed (`extDetFirst`, `ChartPoint.existsUnique_prodOrFirst`,
    `Polyfold/Chapter6/OrientationConvention2021.lean`; item 122). The discontinuity above concerns the preprint's map,
    with `e` last.
96. **Remark 6.6.19 (preprint 6.42): readings** *(book 2017: Remark 6.4, p. 214)*. `X × [0, 1]` is read as `ℝ¹ × X`
    (decision D2), with the parameter first; `s` is an sc⁺-section `S` of the pull-back `π*P`, and
    `f̂ = f̃ + S` with `f̃(t, x) = f(x)`. `Lin(f̂, (t, x))` is read in the product chart point
    `ChartPoint.prodPt`, where `T_{(t,z)} = ℝ¹ × T_zO` and the fibre is `K_z`; the text's

110. **Lemma 6.4.4 (2017: 6.3): the index equalities, new in the 2021 edition, are formalized** *(book 2017: Lemma 6.3, p. 189;
     book 2021: Lemma 6.4.4, p. 247; no preprint counterpart)*. `lemma_6_4_4`: near `(T₀, P₀)`, `T` is Fredholm, `P ∈ Π_T`
     and `ind(P ∘ T) = ind(T) = ind(T₀) = ind(P₀ ∘ T₀)`. The proof is not the text's map `Φ_(P,T)(x, h) = PTx + (I − P)h`: the
     intertwiner `J(P) = PP₀ + (1 − P)(1 − P₀)` (`projIntertwiner`, `projIntertwiner_self`, `projIntertwiner_mul`:
     `J(P)P₀ = PJ(P)`, `continuous_projIntertwiner`) is a unit near `P₀`, so `P = JP₀J⁻¹`, `R(P) = JR(P₀)` has finite
     codimension, and `lemma_6_5_1` for `J⁻¹T` near `T₀` gives `R(PT) = JR(P₀J⁻¹T) = JR(P₀) = R(P)`. The indices come from
     `isFredholm_add_of_norm_lt`, `fredholmIndex_add_of_norm_lt` and `IsGoodLeftProj.fredholmIndex_comp`. Status: **settled**.
111. **Lemma 6.4.4: readings** *(book 2021: p. 247)*. `ind(P ∘ T)` is the index of `P ∘ T : E → F`, as in
     `IsGoodLeftProj.fredholmIndex_comp` (and as the proof of Proposition 6.4.13 uses it, with `R(PT) = H`); as a map onto
     `R(P)` its index would be `dim ker(PT) = ind(T) + codim R(P)`, which exceeds `ind(T)` when `coker T ≠ 0`. `E` and `F` are
     taken in the universe `Type`, that of `isFredholm_add_of_norm_lt`.
112. **Proposition 6.4.13 (2017: 6.6): the algebraic part is formalized** *(book 2017: Proposition 6.6, p. 195; book 2021:
     Proposition 6.4.13, p. 253, proof pp. 253–255; no preprint counterpart)*. `proposition_6_4_13`: for `T` Fredholm and
     `P, Q ∈ Π_T` with `R(P) = R(Q) = H` (the 2021 text makes `Π_T ∩ 𝒫_H ≠ ∅` a hypothesis), the text's `A_T(e) = e − x(e)` and
     `B_T(f + H) = f̃ + H` are linear isomorphisms with `A_T ∘ j_P = j_Q`, `Φ_Q ∘ A_T = B_T ∘ Φ_P`, `π_Q ∘ B_T = π_P`
     (`projSeqJ`, `projSeqPhi`, `projSeqPi`). The text takes "a closed linear subspace `X`" complementing both kernels without
     argument; the formalization uses an algebraic one (`exists_isCompl_isCompl_of_finrank_eq`: two finite-dimensional
     subspaces of the same dimension have a common complement, by induction on `dim(K₁ + K₂) − dim K₁`, adding `a + b` with
     `a ∈ K₂ ∖ K₁`, `b ∈ K₁ ∖ K₂`). A closed one exists as we read it (a common complement inside `K₁ + K₂` plus a closed
     complement of the finite-dimensional `K₁ + K₂`); formalized since (item 116). `B_T` is shown injective and then bijective by
     dimension, in place of the text's five lemma. Status: **settled** for the algebraic part.

     bundle) and a closed `X`; the text's argument keeps `X` and notes that the equation for `x(e)` stays uniquely solvable.

116. **A common closed complement of the two kernels** *(book 2021: proof of Proposition 6.4.13, p. 253; 2017 p. 195)*.
     `exists_isClosed_isTopCompl_isTopCompl_of_finrank_eq`: two finite-dimensional subspaces `K₁`, `K₂` of the same dimension

     closed, a closed subspace plus a finite-dimensional one. The text's "closed linear subspace" exists as we read it, without
     argument in the text. Status: **settled**.

     `proposition_6_4_13_continuity`: with the closed `X` of item 116 for `ker(PT)` and `ker(QT)` there is `ε > 0` such
     that on `‖S − T‖ < ε`: `P, Q ∈ Π_S` (from `lemma_6_5_1`), and `QS|_X : X → R(Q)` is an isomorphism; `ξ_S = (QS|_X)⁻¹ ∘ Q`
     (`solveOp`, `projCod`), `A_S = 1 − ξ_S ∘ S` (`kerTransition`) and `B_S = (1 − P) − Sξ_S(1 − P)` (`cokerTransition`) are
     continuous in `S` in the operator norm, and jointly with the vector (`continuousAt_solveOp`: inversion is continuous at
     isomorphisms, `X` being complete); `ker(PS) ⊕ X = ker(QS) ⊕ X = E` topologically (`disjoint_ker_comp_of_projRestrict_eq`,
     `isTopCompl_ker_comp_of_projRestrict_eq`); (6.15)–(6.16) and (6.18)–(6.19) hold (`kerTransition_apply`,
     `cokerTransition_apply`, `solveOp_mem`, `apply_solveOp_of_projRestrict_eq`); and `A_S`, `B_S` induce isomorphisms
     `ker(PS) → ker(QS)` and `F/R(P) → F/R(Q)` filling the diagram of `E(S, P)`, `E(S, Q)` (`diagram_of_solveOp`). The
     reading (item 113): `A_S` acts between kernels that move with `S`, so "depend continuously" is read as the continuity of

118. **Theorem 6.6.17: the orientation space, its topology, and the readings** *(book 2021: pp. 274–275, Theorem 6.6.17,
     p. 275, new in the 2021 edition)*. `OrSpace` is `O_f`, a sigma type over `MPolyfold.SmoothLevel` (`X_∞` with the topology
     of Theorem 2.3.10, `theorem_2_3_10`), and `orProj` is `π_f`; `Or_x^f` is read in the chosen chart (V6.55). Readings: the
     sc-smooth paths `φ : [0, 1] → X` are sc-smooth maps `ℝ → X` restricted to `[0, 1]` (decision D2, gap G.65); their values
     are smooth (`mem_smoothSet_of_isScSmoothMap`), so `φ*O_f` is the subspace `{(t, p) : φ(t) = π_f(p)}` of `[0, 1] × O_f`
     (`OrPullback`). A continuous section of `O_f|(U ∩ X_∞)` is a continuous `σ : U_∞ → O_f` with `π_f ∘ σ = id`
     (`IsContSectionOver`). "`o_t` is the local propagation of `o_{t₀}`" is read as: for `t` near `t₀` the push-forward
     `orPush` along the segment `φ|[t₀, t]` (`segPath`), in an open set with the local propagation property in some chart
     (`IsPropagationNbhd`), maps `o_{t₀}` to `o_t`; it does not depend on the set (`orPush_compat`) (`IsPropagationContinuous`).
     "A uniquely defined Hausdorff topology characterized by (1), (2), (3)" is read as exactly one Hausdorff topology with
     (1)–(3) (`IsOrientationTopology`). The text leaves the proof to the reader, citing Proposition 6.6.3 and Theorem 6.6.11. The
     topology formalized is `orTopology L` for local transport data `L`: `W` is open iff `{y ∈ U_∞ : (y, o_y) ∈ W}` is open for
     every continuous orientation `o` over an open `U` (`IsContOrOn`: `o` is carried along by `L` along every sc-smooth path in
     `U`). For every `L` the sheets `{(y, o_y)}` are open (`IsContOrOn.eventually_iff`, `isOpen_orBasic`), every point lies on
     one (`exists_isContOrOn`), and `π_f` maps each sheet homeomorphically onto `U_∞` (`orChartHomeo`); hence (1)
     (`isLocalHomeomorph_orProj`), and the topology is Hausdorff (`t2Space_orTopology`, with
     `MPolyfold.metrizableSpace_smoothLevel`). The set `O_f` appears without a topology in the preprint (after Definition 6.27,
     p. 219) and in the 2017 text (after Definition 6.9, p. 205). Status: **settled**.
119. **Theorem 6.6.17: uniqueness from (1) and (3) alone** *(book 2021: p. 275)*. `eq_orTopology_of`: every topology on `O_f`
     with (1) and (3) is `orTopology` for the transport data of `Γ_f` (`orLocalTransport`). Neither Hausdorffness nor (2) is
     used, so the uniqueness is stronger than stated. The core is `eventually_eq_orSec_of_continuousOn`: a continuous local
     section that agrees with a continuous orientation at `y₀` agrees with it near `y₀`, by (3) along short paths and the
     connectedness of `[0, 1]`. It uses two facts on `X_∞` that the text does not state. An sc-smooth `ℝⁿ → X` is continuous
     into `X_∞` (`continuous_smoothMk_comp`, through `continuousOn_levelLift_comp`), and smooth points near `x` in `X_∞` are
     joined to `x` by sc-smooth paths staying in a given `X_∞`-neighbourhood of `x` (`eventually_exists_scPath_smoothLevel`,
     the retracted chart segment `chartSegPath`). Existence: `orTopology` has (3) (`isPropagationContinuous_orTopology`).
     `existsUnique_orientationTopology`: there is exactly one Hausdorff topology with (1) and (3), with no hypothesis
     beyond those of `theorem_6_6_13_hyp` (V6.57): `X` tame with bump functions, tame germ data for `f`, sc⁺-sections through the
     smooth fibre points, and the paracompactness instances. Status: **settled**.
120. **Theorem 6.6.17 (2): proved under connected smooth neighbourhoods only (gap G.90)** *(book 2021: p. 275)*.
     `hasTwoContSections_orTopology`: if every `Or_y^f` has two elements (`exists_two_orx`) and `X` has connected smooth
     neighbourhoods (`MPolyfold.HasConnectedSmoothNbhds`: inside every open `W ∋ x`, `x` smooth, an open `U ∋ x` with
     `U ∩ X_∞` preconnected in `X_∞`), the continuous sections over such a `U ∩ X_∞` are exactly `y ↦ (y, ±o_y)`
     (`eq_orSec_or_eq_orSec`). A continuous section is locally one of the two sheets, so over a `U` whose smooth part is not
     connected there are more than two; (2) needs small `U` with connected smooth part. Part I does not state that they exist.
     The paths of `exists_nhds_scPath` join the smooth points of a small `V` only inside a larger `U`, which does not make
     `V ∩ X_∞` connected. The proofs of §7.4 use that `U ∩ X_∞` is connected for connected open `U`
     (`MPolyfold.SmoothConnected`, Chapter 7, item 134, gap G.85); as we read it, that fact gives the hypothesis, M-polyfolds
     being locally path connected (2021 Proposition 2.3.7, `MPolyfold.locallyPathConnectedSpace`); not formalized. Witnesses:
     `rnPolyfold_hasConnectedSmoothNbhds` (`ℝⁿ`: the smooth part of a ball is the image of a convex set under the continuous
     map of `continuous_smoothMk_comp`) and `MPolyfold.hasConnectedSmoothNbhds_of_subsingleton`. `theorem_6_6_17_hyp` is the
     theorem with (1)–(3) under this hypothesis. Status: **open** (gap G.90).
     (2026-11-09) The hypothesis holds for every M-polyfold (`MPolyfold.hasConnectedSmoothNbhds`,
     `Polyfold/Chapter6/OrientationMainClean.lean`): inside an open `W ∋ x` the connected component of `x` is open
     (Proposition 2.3.7), and its smooth part is path connected in `X_∞` (`isPathConnected_smoothVal_preimage`,
     `Polyfold/Chapter2/SmoothPaths.lean`). So `theorem_6_6_17_hyp PX.hasConnectedSmoothNbhds` gives (1)–(3) under the
     hypotheses under which `Γ_f` is built. Status: **settled**; gap G.90 closed (Chapter 7, item 153).
     (2026-11-09) The clean `theorem_6_6_17` no longer takes `HasConnectedSmoothNbhds`, which is proved in the same file
     (item 122).
121. **The remarks after Theorem 6.6.17: not formalized (gap G.91)** *(book 2021: p. 275)*. That `π_f`, with this topology, is
