     Definition 6.6.16 (`SectionOrientation`), `S` is a compact manifold with boundary with corners in general position
     with the natural orientation given by `o` (`IsNaturalSolutionOrientation`): at every zero `o_x` orients `T_xS = ker
     f'(x)`, the orientations read in two charts correspond under the tangent map of the transition
     (`tangentOrAt_toChartOr`; gap G.68), and along every sc-smooth path of zeros they form an orientation of the kernel
     line bundle. The paragraph after the theorem: `Lin(f + s, x) = Lin(f, x)` for an sc⁺-section `s`, so an orientation
     of `f` is one of `f + s` (`isSectionOrientation_sectionAdd`) and orients `S_{f+s}` (`theorem_6_6_18_sectionAdd`),
     for the dense set of perturbations of Theorem 5.3.10 (`theorem_6_6_18_perturbation`; gap G.69). In Mathlib's
     language `S` is a compact `IsManifold (modelWithCornersEuclideanQuadrant d) ∞` of dimension the index
     (`theorem_6_6_18_isManifold`). Not formalized: an orientation of `S` as a manifold, of its tangent bundle in the
     charts of the induced structure or of the Mathlib manifold (gap G.67). Status: **settled** except the orientation
     of `S` as a manifold (row V6.61). (2026-11-09) That orientation is item 127 (gap G.67 closed).

124. **The facts on paths recalled before Proposition 6.2.2 (gap G.56 closed)** *(before Proposition 6.2.2, p. 240
     (preprint p. 201; 2017: before Proposition 6.1, p. 183); Definitions 6.6.2, 6.6.14; items 42, 122)* (2026-11-09).
     `Polyfold/Chapter6/SmoothPathComponents2021.lean`. `paths_before_proposition_6_2_2`: an M-polyfold is locally path
     connected (`MPolyfold.locallyPathConnectedSpace`), and two smooth points of one connected component are joined by
     an sc-smooth path `φ : [0, 1] → X` in that component, which lifts to an sc-smooth path into `X¹`
     (`IsScSmoothMap.exists_scPlus_lift`, through the sc-smoothness of `1₀¹ : [0, 1] → [0, 1]¹`). The local step joins
     the smooth points of a small open set by sc-smooth paths without a strong bundle chart (`exists_nhds_scJoinedIn`);
     the global step uses the connectedness of an open set (`scJoinedIn_of_isConnected`). The 2021 text speaks of
     connected components, the preprint of path components: for smooth points both agree with "joined by an sc-smooth
     path" (`mem_connectedComponent_iff_exists_scPath`, `mem_pathComponent_iff_exists_scPath`), which justifies the
     reading of Definitions 6.6.2 and 6.6.14 in item 42. With Proposition 6.2.2 on `[0, 1]` (item 122), two smooth
     points of one connected component have the same index (`proposition_6_2_2_connectedComponent_2021def`). Status:
     **settled** (rows V6.49, V6.58; gap G.56 closed).

125. **Lemma 6.5.3 for general vector bundles (gap G.59 closed)** *(Lemma 6.5.3 (preprint 6.19) and Proposition 6.5.4
     (preprint 6.20), p. 260 (preprint p. 216); item 22)* (2026-11-09). `Polyfold/Chapter6/DetVectorBundles2021.lean`.
     For Mathlib topological vector bundles `E`, `F` with finite-dimensional fibres over a topological space, `λ(E)`
     (fibres `Λ^max E_b`), `λ*(E)`, `E ⊕ F` (Mathlib's `E ×ᵇ F`) and `E ⊗ F` are Mathlib topological vector bundles
     (`lemma_6_5_3`), built as vector prebundles whose trivializations are induced by those of `E` and `F`
     (`lamPrebundle`, `lamDualPrebundle`, `tenPrebundle`); this is the reading of "in a natural way". The coordinate
     changes of `λ(E)` are the determinants of those of `E` (`coord_wedgeAt_eq_det`), and those of `E ⊗ F` the tensor
     products (`tenMap_tenInv_eq`). The model fibre of `E ⊗ F` is `F₁ⁿ`, `n = dim F₀`, since Mathlib puts no norm on
     `F₀ ⊗ F₁`; this does not change the bundle. Proposition 6.5.4 is still proved with the explicit frames of item 22.
     Status: **settled** (row V6.22; gap G.59 closed).

126. **Lemma 6.6.5: near the family the solution set is a manifold and `π` a submersion at the family (gap G.62 in
     part)** *(Lemma 6.6.5 (preprint 6.30), p. 265 (preprint p. 222); item 48)* (2026-11-09).
     `Polyfold/Chapter6/SolutionManifoldFamily2021.lean`. For `F = f + S + Σ λᵢsᵢ` near `(0, (q, Φ(q)))`, `q` near `[0,
     1]ⁿ` (decision D2), in the setting of Lemma 6.6.4, the solution set is a Mathlib manifold with boundary and
     corners (`lemma_6_6_5_isManifold`, from `theorem_3_1_26_isManifold`) and a submanifold of dimension the index
     (`lemma_6_6_5_isSubmanifoldOfDim`); at the points of the family its tangent space is `ker F'` in the product
     chart, and `dπ` maps it onto `ℝⁿ` (`lemma_6_6_5_submersion`, `exists_mem_linKer_sliceProj_eq`). Not formalized:
     `π` as a submersion off the family, which would need a curve of zeros through every point of the solution set, the
     fibres `S_t` (property (P) for the slices, gap G.63), and `L` as a smooth vector bundle; the continuation of
     orientations uses only the continuous family of kernels (item 48). Status: **settled** (2026-11-12; item 48; rows V6.34, V6.42 restated; gap G.62 closed).

127. **Theorem 6.6.18: the orientation of `S` as a manifold (gap G.67 closed)** *(Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41),
     p. 274; items 92, 123)* (2026-11-09). `Polyfold/Chapter6/ManifoldOrientation.lean`,
     `Polyfold/Chapter6/SolutionSetOrientation.lean`. Mathlib has no orientations of manifolds; the first file gives
     them for a Mathlib manifold with corners: a tangent orientation (an orientation of every `TangentSpace I x`), its
     continuity read in the charts of the maximal atlas (`TangentOrientation.IsContinuous`), oriented atlases (charts
     whose changes have positive Jacobian determinant, `IsOrientedAtlas`) and the passage between them
     (`isOrientedAtlas_positiveCharts`, `IsOrientedAtlas.tangentOrientation`). `theorem_6_6_18_oriented`: under the
     hypotheses of `theorem_6_6_18`, with the sc-smooth bump functions that §6.6 assumes, the compact Mathlib manifold
     `S` of `theorem_6_6_18_isManifold` carries a continuous tangent orientation which at every zero `x`, in every chart
     of `X` at `x`, is `o_x` transported along the tangent map of `S ↪ X`, an isomorphism `T_xS ≅ ker f'(x)`
     (`solKerEquiv`, `solOr_spec`); it is built in corner charts (`solOr`, chart independent by
     `solReadOr_chartChange`) and is continuous through the kernel line bundle (`isLineOrientation_solKer`,
     `isContinuous_solOr`). "A natural orientation" of the manifold is read as a continuous tangent orientation, not as
     an oriented atlas: for the quadrant model the two differ, since in dimension 1 `[0, 1]` has no atlas of quadrant
     charts with positive chart changes (a chart at `0` increases, one at `1` decreases), and in dimension 0 every atlas
     is oriented while a tangent orientation is a sign at every point; an oriented atlas follows whenever the positive
     charts cover `S`. Not formalized: the same for `S_{f+s}` in the paragraph after the theorem (a short corollary).
     Status: **settled** (row V6.61; gap G.67 closed).

**128–134: Theorem 6.7.1 and the case `∂X = ∅` (2026-11-10).** (`Chapter5/CylinderPerturbation2021.lean`;

128. **The neighbourhood `U` of (1): read with a margin, for every auxiliary norm (reading R-b; refines item 101)**
     *(book 2021: §6.7, p. 276; Theorem 6.7.1 (1), p. 277; Theorem 5.3.10)*. The text takes `U` from Theorem 5.3.10, which gives, for an
     auxiliary norm `N`, an open `U ⊇ S_f` such that the sections supported in `U` with `N(s) ≤ 1` have compact
     solution sets. We read this as the existential of Theorem 5.3.10, so (1) is stated for every `N` with some `U`.
     The `U` carries a margin: `cl{x ∈ U | N(f(x)) ≤ C}` is compact for every `C > 0` (`exists_adapted_margin`), and
     then `S_{f+s}` is compact for every allowable `s` (`isCompact_solutionSet_sectionAdd_of_margin`). Admissible
     means `s ∈ allowableSections N U` with `(f + s, x)` in general position at every zero (`StrongBundle.IsAdmissible`,
     p. 276). The text defines `Ψ` from one `N`; the formal `Ψ` is `psiAt` for one chosen admissible section, and (1)
     holds for every `N`, every `U` with the margin and every admissible `s` (`psiInvariant_eq_psiAt`). Two pairs
     `(N₀, U₀)`, `(N₁, U₁)` are compared through a section admissible for both (`exists_admissible_two`, with
     `IsAuxNorm.max`); `psiAt` depends on `s` only (`psiAt_congr_admissible`). Status: **settled** (a reading; row
     V6.76; gap G.55 closed).

129. **"Zero if the dimensions do not agree": degree `k` is paired with the index-`k` part `S_k` (reading R-c)**
     *(book 2021: Theorem 6.7.1 (1), p. 277; p. 279)*. The theorem has no hypothesis on the index, which need not be
     constant. We read the clause as: in degree `k` both integrals are taken over `S_k`, the points of `S_{f+s}` at
     which the index of `f` is `k` (`solPart`). `S_k` is closed and open in `S_{f+s}`, since the index is locally
     constant (`isClosed_solPart`, `isOpen_solIndexNbhd`), `S_{f+s}` is the union of the `S_k`
     (`solutionSet_eq_iUnion_solPart`), and each `S_k` is a compact Mathlib manifold of dimension `k` oriented by `o`
     (`solPartIsOrientedManifold`). In degree `0` the invariant is a signed count of the points of `S_0`
     (`psiAt_mk_zero_eq_sum`). The case of p. 279, a constant index `n`, is a lemma: `S_{f+s} = S_n` and `S_k = ∅` for
     `k ≠ n` (`solPart_eq_solutionSet`, `solPart_eq_empty_of_ne`), so `Φ = 0` off degree `n`
     (`psiInvariantNoBoundary_of_ne`). Status: **settled** (a reading; rows V6.76, V6.77).

130. **The proper oriented homotopy of (2) is read through Remark 6.6.19, over `ℝ¹ × X` (reading R-d)** *(book 2021:
     Theorem 6.7.1 (2), p. 277; Remark 6.6.19, p. 275; Remark 5.3.8; decision D2)*. The text does not define a proper
     oriented homotopy. The only oriented homotopy in it is that of Remark 6.6.19: `f̂ = f̃₀ + S` with `S` an
     sc⁺-section over `[0, 1] × X`, oriented by `e ∧ o`. We read `[0, 1] × X` as `ℝ¹ × X` (decision D2) and the
     homotopy as an sc⁺-section `S` over `ℝ¹ × X` with `S(0, ·) = 0`, `f₁ = f₀ + S(1, ·)` and `o₁` the orientation `o₀`
     transported to `f₁` (an orientation of `f` is one of `f + s`), with compact zeros over `t ∈ [0, 1]` and the second
     clause of properness (Definition 5.2.1 (3)) on that slab (`IsProperOrientedHomotopy`,
     `IsProperOrientedHomotopyBetween`); `f₀` and `f₁` are then proper (`IsProperOrientedHomotopy.isProper_zero`,
     `isProper_one`). Arcs of sc-Fredholm sections in general (Remark 5.3.8) carry no orientation in the text and are
     not covered. Status: **settled** (a reading; row V6.76).

131. **The degree of the form `ω̄ = p₁^*ω ∧ p₂^*dt` of the proof (reading R-e; settles item 103)** *(book 2021: proof
     of Theorem 6.7.1, p. 278)*. For a closed relative form `(ω, τ)` of degree `k`, the proof extends `ω` to `X × [0,
     1]` by `ω̄ = p₁^*ω ∧ p₂^*dt` and applies Stokes' theorem to it on the `(k + 1)`-dimensional `S_F`. As we read it
     (item 103), `ω̄` has degree `k + 1`, one more than the dimension `k` of `∂S_F`, so its integrals over `S₀`, `S₁`
     and `S̃` are `0`, while the comparison needs `∫_{S₀} ω` and `∫_{S₁} ω`. The argument goes through with `p₁^*ω`
     (degree `k`) in place of `ω̄` and `p₁^*τ` in place of `τ̄`: `dp₁^*ω = 0`, and `p₁^*ω` reads as `ω` on the ends of
     `S_F` (`isEndPullback_formsInftyRestrict_snd`). The formal proof uses `p₁^*ω` (item 133). Status: **settled** (a
     reading; row V6.76).

132. **The signs on `∂S_F`: outward vector first; the piece `I × ∂N` carries `−(e ∧ o_{∂N})` (reading R-f)** *(book
     2021: proof of Theorem 6.7.1, pp. 278–279; Definitions 9.3.8, 9.3.10; Chapter 4, item 171)*. The proof orients
     `S_F` from `o` and the standard orientation of `[0, 1]` and writes the pieces `S₀`, `S₁`, `S̃` of `∂S_F` with signs
     obtained "taking the orientations into account", without a convention. We read the boundary orientation as outward
     vector first (Definition 9.3.8, as in Chapter 4, item 171), which gives Stokes' theorem with the sign `+`, as the
     text uses it. On a product end `(a, b) × N` of a manifold `M` oriented by `e ∧ o_N` (time first), the piece `(a, b)
     × ∂N` of `∂M` then carries `−(e ∧ o_{∂N})`: for `β` reading as `h(t) dt ∧ β_N`, `∫_{∂M} β = −(∫ₐᵇ h) ∫_{∂N} β_N`
     (`ProductEnd.boundaryIntegral_end_sign`, `ProductEnd.faceIntegral_end_sign`, from `d(h dt ∧ η) = −h dt ∧ dη`).
     The final route does not use these signs, since it avoids the decomposition of `∂S_F` (item 133). Status:
     **settled** (a reading; row V6.76).

133. **The decomposition of `∂S_F` replaced by a cut-off in time, and the support of the cut-off** *(book 2021: proof
     of Theorem 6.7.1, p. 278; Remark 5.3.8)*. In place of `∂S_F = S₀ ∪ S₁ ∪ S̃`, which needs integrals of forms on
     the faces of `S_F` over `S̃ ⊂ ∂X × (0, 1)` and a Fubini theorem for face forms, the formal proof uses a cut-off
     `g(t)` and Stokes' theorem on the index-`(k + 1)` part of `S_F` (`integral_eq_of_cutCobordism`): for the closed
     form `A` on `S_F` with vanishing face restriction (item 134), `∫_{S_F} d(gA) = ∫_{∂S_F} gA = 0`
     (`boundaryIntegral_congr_face`), while on the ends `∫_{S_F} d(g_iA) = ∫_{S_i} a_i` (`ProductEnd.integral_end_fubini`),
     with `a_i = ω|_{S_i} + dγ_i` and `γ_i` an extension of `−τ|_{∂S_i}` (`IsPsiIntegrand`, `IsPsiIntegrand.psiAt_eq`).
     The cobordism data (`IsCobordismData`, `exists_isCobordismData`) make `S_F` a product only near the ends: over `t ≤
     1/8` it is an interval times `S₀`, over `t ≥ 7/8` an interval times `S₁` (`solutionSet_left_eq_prod`). The plan
     placed the support of `g′` in `[0.1, 0.2]` and `[0.8, 0.9]`, which leaves these ends; `g′` must be supported in
     `(0, 1/8)` and `(7/8, 1)`, and the formal cut-off is `cutRise 0 (1/8)` and `cutRise (7/8) 1` (`cutRise`,
     `cobPart_end_left`, `cobPart_end_right`). This concerns the formal plan, not the text. Status: **settled** (row
     V6.76).

134. **Theorem 6.7.1 and the case `∂X = ∅` as formalized: two steps of the proof as hypotheses (refines item 100;
     gaps G.54, G.66 in part)** *(book 2021: Theorem 6.7.1, p. 277; proof pp. 277–279; p. 279)*. `theorem_6_7_1_hyp` proves the theorem,
     with (1) and (2) in readings R-b, R-c, R-d (items 128–130), from two hypotheses that are steps of the text's
     proof, not hypotheses of the text. `CobordismOrientationHyp`: the orientation of `S_F` induced from `o` and the
     standard orientation of `[0, 1]`, stated as an orientation of product form `e ∧ o_{S_i}` on the two ends (Remark
     6.6.19, gap G.66), for the cobordisms of (1), with `o₁ = o₀`, and for those of (2), along a proper oriented
     homotopy. `CobordismRelativeFormsHyp`: a closed form on `S_F` with vanishing face restriction that reads as
     `ω|_{S_i} + dγ_i` on the ends; it needs the pull-back of forms on `∂X` to `∂(ℝ¹ × X)` along `p₁` (gap G.54).
     Neither quantifies over all orientations. From them, (A) `PsiIndepAdmissible` and (B) `PsiIndepHomotopy` follow by
     the cobordism identity `psiAt_eq_of_cobordism` (`psiAt_eq_of_admissible_hyp`, `psiAt_eq_of_homotopy_hyp`, in
     `Chapter6/Theorem671Assembly2021.lean`), and the theorem follows from (A) and (B) with no other hypothesis
     (`theorem_6_7_1_of_indep`). The case `∂X = ∅` of p. 279 is `theorem_6_7_1_noBoundary_hyp`, with `Hⁿ_dR(X)` read
     as `Hⁿ_sc(X)` (Chapter 4, item 173). No Lean witness of the two hypotheses is given; on the point `ℝ⁰` with `f =
     0`, `Ψ([1]) = ±1` (`theorem_6_7_1_witness`). Left: the orientation of `S_F` (gap G.66, items 1–4, 6, 7 of the
     plan) and the face-form part of the relative form (gap G.54). Status: **settled** (2026-11-12, below; rows V6.76, V6.77 restated; gaps G.54, G.66 closed).
     (2026-11-12) One hypothesis is left: `theorem_6_7_1_of_orientation` needs only `CobordismOrientationHyp`; the
     relative form is built on the inner ends (`cobordismRelativeFormsInner`, item 136); the orientation `cobOr` of
     `S_F` exists and is continuous (`isContinuous_cobOr`), and `cobordismOrientation_of_ends` reduces the hypothesis
     to the value `e ∧ o_{S_i}` of `cobOr` on the two ends. This value is then proved: `cobordismOrientationHyp`
     (`Chapter6/CobordismOrientationEnds2021d.lean`, through `isEndProductOrientation_cobOr`) shows that `cobOr` is
     `e ∧ o_{S_i}` on the ends, the time vector first and with no sign (as item 132 reads it), and `theorem_6_7_1`,
     `theorem_6_7_1_noBoundary` (`Chapter6/Theorem671Final2021.lean`) prove the theorem with the hypotheses of the
     text only (`X` tame, sc-smooth bump functions).

135. **The remark that `DET(E, F)` is not orientable does not hold as we read it for finite-dimensional `E`, `F`; it
     holds for every infinite-dimensional Hilbert space (refines item 26; gap G.60 closed)** *(book 2021: end of §6.5,
     p. 262; preprint p. 218)* (2026-11-12). `Polyfold/Chapter6/GapP1_DetNonOrientable.lean`,
     `GapP1_DetNonOrientableEll2.lean`, `GapP1_DetNonOrientableTransport.lean`. The text gives the remark without
     hypotheses on `E`, `F` and without proof or reference. Non-orientable is read as
     `IsEmpty (LineOrientation (DetFiber (E := E) (F := F)))`: no orientation in the sense of Proposition 6.6.1. For
     finite-dimensional `E`, `F` every operator is Fredholm, the base `L(E, F)` is convex, and `DET(E, F)` has exactly
     two orientations (`exists_two_lineOrientation_det_of_finiteDimensional`), so the remark does not hold as we read
     it there. It holds when `E` and `F` carry bounded `J` with `J² = −1` and there is a surjective `T : E → F` with
     kernel of odd finite dimension (`isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_complexStructure`): along `A_θ = R'_θ T R_{−θ}`,
     `θ ∈ [0, π]`, `R_θ = cos θ + sin θ J`, all operators are surjective, a basis of the kernels is a continuous
     section of `DET` in the chart with `P = 1`, and it returns to its negative
     (`isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_kernel_loop`). Hence `DET(H, H)` has no orientation for every
     infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space `H` (`isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_hilbert`), nor `DET(E, F)` for `E`, `F`
     isomorphic to such an `H` or to `H × H` with `H ≅ ℝ × H` (`isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_equiv_hilbert`,
     `isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_equiv_prod`); orientability depends only on the isomorphism classes of `E` and
     `F` (`nonempty_lineOrientation_det_iff_of_equiv`). Not claimed: infinite-dimensional Banach spaces without such
     structures. For the notes to the authors (one line): the remark presumably intends infinite-dimensional `E`, `F`
     of the kind in the applications. Status: **settled** (rows V6.80, V6.81; gap G.60 closed).

136. **Theorem 6.7.1: the relative form on `S_F`, two readings (refines items 131, 134)** *(book 2021: proof of
     Theorem 6.7.1, p. 278)* (2026-11-12). `Polyfold/Chapter4/BoundaryFormsPullback2021.lean`,
     `Polyfold/Chapter6/CobordismRelativeForms2021.lean`, `CobordismRelativeForms2021b.lean`. (1) The text integrates
     `p₁^*τ` over `∂S_F` without saying why `p₁` maps the faces of `S_F` to faces of `X`. It follows from
     `d_{S_F} = d_{ℝ¹ × X}` (Theorem 4.2.11) and `d_{ℝ¹ × X}(t, x) = d_X(x)` (`CornerCoords.zero_coord_face_along`,
     `degIndex_cobPart`); the face form of `τ` along `p₁` is `faceAlongData`. (2) The form `β` on `S_F` with
     `j^*β = p₁^*τ` and `β = p₁^*β_i` near the ends is built by cut-offs in `t` between `p₁^*γ_i` and an extension,
     which needs room in `t` on both sides of the cut-off region. The text's `[0, 1] × X` has collars by construction
     of the homotopy; the formal cobordism data fix the slices only for `t ≤ 1/8` and `t ≥ 7/8`, so the form is built
     on the inner ends `(0, 1/16) × S₀`, `(15/16, 1) × S₁` (`cobordismRelativeFormsInner`), and the cobordism identity
     is run there (`psiAt_eq_of_cobordism_of_orientation`). The statement on the full ends
     (`CobordismRelativeFormsHyp`) would need a smooth extension across `t = 1/8` and is no longer used. No
     counterexample; nothing is found not to hold as we read it. Status: **settled** (rows V6.76, V6.77; gap G.54
     closed).

137. **Proposition 6.6.3 (1): the 2021 wording, `U′ ⊂ U` contractible in `U`, holds (gap G.61 closed; a reading point
     on item 45)** *(book 2021: Proposition 6.6.3 (1), p. 263; 2017: Proposition 6.12, p. 205; preprint 6.28, p. 220)*
     (2026-11-13). `Polyfold/Chapter6/GapP3_K4_Contractible.lean`, `GapP3_K4_IntervalHomotopy.lean`. The 2021 text, as
     the 2017 one, prints (1) with a second neighbourhood: "`U′ ⊂ U` is sc-smoothly contractible in `U` to the point
     `x`". The reading of gap G.61 and item 45, (1) for `U` itself, is the preprint's wording; it is a reading point
     on the preprint, not an item that does not hold. The 2021 form is proved for every smooth `x` and every open
     `U ∋ x`: in a chart `φ` with retraction `r`, `H(t, y) = φ⁻¹ r(φ(x) + t(φ(y) − φ(x)))` on `U′ = φ⁻¹(B_ε(φ(x)))`,
     with `ε` so small that `B_ε ∩ C` lies in the domain of `r` and `φ⁻¹ r(B_ε ∩ C) ⊆ U`; `H` is sc-smooth on the
     product M-polyfold `[0, 1] × U′`, with `H(0, ·) = x`, `H(1, ·) = id` and `H(t, x) = x` (`IsScContraction`,
     `exists_isScContraction`; with parameter ℝ, `exists_isScContractionRn`). The text's `r̂(t, y) = r(ty)` is this
     map for `x = 0`. The smoothness of `x` is used: `φ(x)` must be a smooth point for the constant to be sc-smooth.
     `proposition_6_6_3_one` states Proposition 6.6.3 as printed in 2021, with (1), (1′), (2), (3), (4) in one chart.
     The preprint's "`U` contractible", which needs `r(V′) ⊆ V′`, is not formalized; nothing here shows that it fails.
     In 2021, Theorem 6.6.11 (p. 272) asks only for an open neighbourhood and Definition 6.6.12 (p. 273) for an open
     path-connected one (items 53, 54). No counterexample. Status: **settled** (row V6.32, now restated; gap G.61
     closed).

138. **Paths on `[0, 1]`: (1′) with homotopies on `[0, 1]²`, and `L` over `[0, 1]` (gap G.65 in part)** *(book 2021:
     Proposition 6.6.3 and Lemma 6.6.5, pp. 263–265)* (2026-11-13).
     `Polyfold/Chapter6/GapP3_K4_IntervalHomotopy.lean`, `GapP3_K4_SmoothLInterval.lean`. Two sc-smooth paths
     `γ₀, γ₁ : [0, 1] → U` with the same end points are joined by the segment homotopy
     `H(τ, t) = φ⁻¹ r(φγ₀(t) + τ(φγ₁(t) − φγ₀(t)))`, sc-smooth on the M-polyfold `[0, 1]²` (`unitSquarePolyfold`,
     `exists_isScHomotopyI`). The parameter must stay in `[0, 1]`: outside it the segment leaves the partial quadrant
     `C`; in the charts `t` and `1 − t` of `[0, 1]` the representative is `(v, a, b) ↦ r(a + s(v)(b − a))`
     (`isScSmoothOn_chartSegment`). No reparametrization is needed: the edge conditions hold exactly, which is the
     hypothesis of `orTransportI_eq_of_homotopy`. With (1) in its 2021 form this gives `proposition_6_6_3_interval`.
     For a path (`n = 1`) the bundle `L` of Lemma 6.6.5 is a smooth vector bundle over Mathlib's manifold with
     boundary `[0, 1]` itself, the pull-back along the `C^∞` inclusion (`lemma_6_6_5_smoothBundle_interval`,
     `SmoothSubspaceFamily.comp`). Still read on ℝ (decision D2): `L` over `[0, 1]ⁿ` for `n ≥ 2` (Mathlib has no
     manifold-with-corners structure on the cube; estimate 300–600 lines), the stabilized kernels for families with
     sections over `[0, 1]ⁿ × X` (400–700 lines), and Remark 6.6.19 over `[0, 1] × X` (1,500–2,500 lines). Status:
     **open** in part (rows V6.32, V6.34; gap G.65 in part; items 71, 102, 122, 124).

Found while formalizing §7.1 up to Proposition 7.1.12 (2017: 7.4) (2026-11-07).

1. **Definition 7.1.1 (2017: 7.1) is read as a structure of maps; the composition is total** *(Definition 7.1.1 (2017: 7.1),
   pp. 287–288 (2017 pp. 225–226))*. A groupoid is `GroupoidStr Obj Mor`: maps `src`, `tgt`, `comp`, `unit`, `inv`
   with the laws of (1)–(4) required on composable pairs only; `comp φ ψ` of a non-composable
   pair is a junk value, never used. `mor(x, y)`, the relation `x ∼ y` (`Isomorphic`,
   `orbitSetoid`), `|X|` (`OrbitSpace`) and `π` are as in the text; the saturation `π⁻¹(π(A))`
   used from Definition 7.1.21 (2017: 7.10) on is `saturation`, with `isSaturated_iff`. Not in the text: the
   bridge `GroupoidStr.Ob` to Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Groupoid` and `GroupoidFunctor.toFunctor`,
   so that "full" and "faithful" (2017 p. 232, Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6)) are Mathlib's `Functor.Full`,
   `Functor.Faithful`.
2. **The isotropy group has the text's multiplication** *(Definition 7.1.2 (2017: 7.2), p. 288 (2017 p. 226))*. `Isotropy x`
   is the group of `φ : x → x` with `g * h = g ∘ h`, which is the text's. Mathlib's vertex group
   `x ⟶ x` multiplies in the other order: `isotropyEquivVertexGroup` identifies `G_x` with its
   opposite group, and `isotropyEquivAut` with `Aut x`.
3. **Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3) is read existentially, with Mathlib's proper maps** *(Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3),
   2017 p. 227)*. "Every point `x` possesses an open neighbourhood `V(x)` such that
   `t : s⁻¹(cl_X(V(x))) → X` is proper" is `exists_isProperMap`: for each `x` there is such a `V`,
   and "proper" is `IsProperMap` of the restriction (`domRestrict`). The text's proofs use the
   sequential form ("after perhaps taking a subsequence"; Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3), Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1),
   Propositions 7.1.22, 7.3.9, 7.5.9 (2017: 7.7, 7.11, 7.13), Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8)); it is equivalent here (`isProperMap_iff_exists_tendsto_subseq`, `isProperMap_domRestrict_iff`,
   `MPolyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_iff_isCompact_preimage`), since M-polyfolds are metrizable
   (Theorem 2.3.10 (2017: 2.2)). Two facts the text uses without comment are proved: properness passes to every
   smaller open `V' ⊆ V(x)` (`isProperMap_domRestrict_closure_mono`, `HasPropernessProperty.mono`),
   and it cannot be asked of every neighbourhood (item 103).
4. **Definition 7.1.3 (4) (2017: 7.3): the fibred product, and the citation "Lemma 2.8 in [38]"** *(Definition
   7.1.3 (4) (2017: 7.3), 2017 p. 227)*. The text makes `𝐗 ₛ×ₜ 𝐗` an M-polyfold "in view of Lemma 2.8 in [38]", the
   paper *A General Fredholm Theory III* (bibliography, entry [38]); this is an external citation,
   not a misprint. Its statement in the book is Part I's Proposition 2.5.20 (2017: 2.15), which the formalization
   uses (`MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_fibredProduct`, `MPolyfold.subPolyfold`): (4) is `IsScSmoothComp`,
   sc-smoothness of `m` on that sub-M-polyfold of `𝐗 × 𝐗`. The proofs use the equivalent sheet form
   `IsScSmoothCompSheet` (for every sheet `σ` of `s`, `ψ ↦ m(σ(t ψ), ψ)` is sc-smooth), proved
   equivalent in `isScSmoothComp_iff_sheet`.
5. **`φ̂` and Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4); `Tφ` is only defined** *(p. 289 (2017 p. 227), Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4))* *(book 2021: before Definition 7.1.4, p. 289: the `∘` for `:` corrected; `T_{t(φ)}` without `X` unchanged, checked on the printed page)*. The open sets
   `𝐔(φ)`, `U(x)`, `U(y)` on which `s` and `t` are sc-diffeomorphisms are `Sheet` (`exists_sheet`,
   `sheetAt`), and `φ̂ = t ∘ (s|𝐔(φ))⁻¹ : U(x) → U(y)` is `hat`, an sc-diffeomorphism
   (`isScDiffeoOn_hat`) with `φ̂(x) = y` (`hat_src`). `Tφ := Tφ̂(x)` is `tangentMor`, a definition
   only: that it is well defined (`Ts` injective on `T_φ𝐗`), equal to `Tφ̂(s(φ))`, bijective, a
   bounded linear isomorphism on level `0` for `φ ∈ 𝐗₁`, and an sc-operator for smooth `φ` is not
   formalized; the linearity needs the linear structure of `T_xX` (gap G.7) and is deferred to
   Chapter 8 (gap G.70). In the extracted text the display reads "`φ̂ = t ∘ (s|𝐔(φ))⁻¹ ∘ U(x) →
   U(y)`", `∘` for `:` (possible misprint; the same slip as in Definition 7.1.20 (2017: 7.9), item 28), and
   "`Tφ : T_{s(φ)}X → T_{t(φ)}`" lacks the `X` (possible misprint or extraction artefact; check
   against the printed page).
   (2026-11-09) For `φ ∈ 𝐗₁`, `Tφ = Tφ̂(s(φ))` (`tangentMor_eq_tangentMapOn_hat`), and `Tφ` is a bijection `T_{s(φ)}X →
   T_{t(φ)}X` with inverse `T(φ⁻¹)` and, in charts, a bounded linear isomorphism of the tangent spaces of the retracts
   (item 110).
   (2026-11-09) `Tφ` is a bounded linear isomorphism of `T_{s(φ)}X` onto `T_{t(φ)}X` for `φ ∈ 𝐗₁`, and an sc-isomorphism
   for smooth `φ` (item 154; gap G.70 closed).
6. **Levels, the degeneracy index, and the filtration of `|X|`** *(pp. 289 ff. (2017 pp. 227–228), Definition 7.1.5 (2017: 7.5))*.
   `s` and `t` preserve the levels (`mem_levelSet_src_iff`, `mem_levelSet_tgt_iff`), so
   `ml(x) = ml(φ) = ml(y)` (`MPolyfold.maxLevel`, `MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.maxLevel_eq`), and
   `d_X(s φ) = d_𝐗(φ) = d_X(t φ)` by Part I's Proposition 2.4.4 (2017: 2.7) (`MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.degIndex_eq`,
   `degIndex_src`, `degIndex_tgt`); `d_|X|` of Definition 7.1.5 (2017: 7.5) is `degIndexOrbit`, well defined by
   `degIndexOrbit_π`. The sets `|X_k| = π(X_k)` are `orbitLevel k`; the set `|X_∞|` and the identity
   `|X_∞| = ⋂_k |X_k|` (immediate, as `ml` is constant on classes) are not stated (gap G.72). The
   density of `X_∞` in every `X_k` (2017 p. 227) is item 116 (gap G.73).
   (2026-11-09) The density of `X_∞` in every `X_k` and the set `|X_∞| = ⋂_k |X_k|` are proved (items 112, 116).
7. **Definition 7.1.6 (2017: 7.6) and the tameness of `𝐗`** *(Definition 7.1.6 (2017: 7.6) and the paragraph after it, p.
   228)*. "`X` is a tame M-polyfold" is `MPolyfold.IsTame`, the existence of an equivalent tame
   atlas (Definition 2.5.7 (2017: 2.19)). The claim that `𝐗` is then tame is proved by transporting tame charts
   along the local sc-diffeomorphism `s` (`MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.exists_tame_chart`,
   `MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isTame`; the converse for surjective maps is
   `MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isTame_iff_of_surjective`). Read as "every chart is modelled on a
   tame retract" the definition would be unsatisfiable (item 106, point 1).
8. **Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7): the category `EP`** *(Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7), p. 290 (2017 p. 228))*. Morphisms are `EpFunctor`s:
   `GroupoidFunctor`s (maps on objects and morphisms commuting with `s`, `t`, `m`, `u`) that are
   sc-smooth on both spaces. That a functor commutes with `ι` is derived (`GroupoidFunctor.mor_inv`);
   identities and composites (`EpFunctor.id`, `EpFunctor.comp`) make `EP` a category, and functors
   induce continuous maps of orbit spaces (`GroupoidFunctor.orbitMap`).
9. **The remark after Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7) does not hold as we read it; it holds for functors continuous
   on morphisms** *(pp. 290–292 (2017 pp. 228–229))* *(book 2021: corrected, the remark after Definition 7.1.7, p. 291, now asks continuity on morphisms)*. The text says that sc-smoothness of `f` on objects suffices,
   because `f(γ) = (s|𝐔(ψ))⁻¹(f(s(γ)))` on `𝐔(φ)`, given neighbourhoods with
   `f(𝐔(φ)) ⊆ 𝐔(ψ)`. Such neighbourhoods need `f` to be continuous on morphisms, and without that
   the claim fails: on the ep-groupoid of `ℤ/3` acting trivially on `ℝ`, the functor that is the
   identity on objects and sends `(g, y)` to `(g, y)` for `y ≤ 0` and to `(g², y)` for `y > 0` is a
   functor, sc-smooth on objects, not continuous on morphisms
   (`Examples.remark_definition_7_1_7_counterexample`, item 104). With continuity the argument goes
   through, and needs only a sheet `𝐔(ψ)` of `s` at `ψ = f(φ)` and `𝐔(φ) = f⁻¹(𝐔(ψ))`
   (`isScSmoothMap_mor_of_continuous`, `isScSmoothMap_mor_iff_continuous`, `EpFunctor.ofContinuous`;
   the formula is `mor_eq_srcInv_obj_src`).
    (2026-11-12) The 2021 text (p. 291) asks continuity on level 0 between the morphism spaces, the hypothesis of
    `isScSmoothMap_mor_of_continuous`, so the 2021 remark holds as we read it (row V7.10, now same); the
    counterexample concerns the 2017 sentence. Status: **settled**.
10. **Propositions 7.1.8 and 7.1.9 (2017: 7.1 and 7.2): the proofs** *(2017 p. 229)*. Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1) is proved through the
    saturation: `π⁻¹(π(U)) = t(s⁻¹(U))` is open since `t` is an open map
    (`proposition_7_1_8`; also `proposition_7_1_8_isOpenQuotientMap`, `proposition_7_1_8_map_nhds`); the
    text argues point by point with the same sheets. Proposition 7.1.9 (2017: 7.2) uses the metrizability of `X`
    (Theorem 2.3.10 (2017: 2.2), `MPolyfold.metrizableSpace`): balls of radius `1/(k + 1)` give a monotone
    countable basis, read as Mathlib's `HasAntitoneBasis` (`proposition_7_1_9_of_hasAntitoneBasis`,
    `proposition_7_1_9`, `proposition_7_1_9_firstCountableTopology`).
11. **Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3) is proved without sequences, for every `A ⊆ cl U`** *(Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3), pp.
    229–230)*. For `U` with the properness property, `π(cl A) = cl π(A)` holds for every
    `A ⊆ cl_X(U)` (`proposition_7_1_10_of_isProperMap`), from the closedness of the proper map
    `t : s⁻¹(cl U) → X` (`isClosed_image_preimage_of_isProperMap_domRestrict`); the statement for
    `A ⊆ U` is `proposition_7_1_10`. The text's sequence argument is the same fact.
12. **Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1): the proof works with the inverses; misprints** *(Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1), p. 292 (2017 p. 230))* *(book 2021: Lemma 7.1.11, p. 292: the exchange of `s` and `t` and "`V(y)`" unchanged; "`s(ψ) ∈ s⁻¹(…)`" corrected to `s(ψ) ∈ cl_X(U(x′))`)*. The
    statement counts the `ψ` with `s(ψ) = x`, `t(ψ) ∈ U(x₀)` (`lemma_7_1_11`); the proof takes
    `ψ_n : s(ψ_n) → x` with `s(ψ_n) ∈ U(x₀)`, the inverses of those, with `s` and `t` exchanged
    (possible misprint; both forms are proved, the proof's as `lemma_7_1_11_swap`, and they are
    equivalent by `ι`). In the proof, "`t : V(ψ) → V(y)`" is meant for `V(x)`, and the limit
    satisfies "`s(ψ) ∈ s⁻¹(cl_X(U(x₀)))`" where `ψ ∈ s⁻¹(cl_X(U(x₀)))`, i.e. `s(ψ) ∈ cl_X(U(x₀))`,
    is meant (possible misprints; for the parentheses see item 96). The openness of `U(x₀)` and
    `x₀ ∈ U(x₀)` are not used (`_hU`, `_hx₀`). The finiteness is proved without sequences: the
    fibre over `x` of the proper map is compact and discrete, as `t` is a local homeomorphism
    (`finite_setOf_mem_of_isProperMap_domRestrict`,
    `IsProperMap.finite_preimage_singleton_of_isLocallyInjective`).
13. **Proposition 7.1.12 (2017: 7.4) and the conjugation `G_x → G_y`** *(Proposition 7.1.12 (2017: 7.4) and the paragraph after
    it, 2017 p. 230)*. `G_x` is finite by Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1) with `x₀ = x` (`proposition_7_1_12`, an instance; the
    abstract form is `MPolyfold.finite_isotropy_of_isLocalScDiffeo`). The isomorphism
    `g ↦ φ ∘ g ∘ φ⁻¹` is `conjIsotropy` (`nonempty_isotropy_mulEquiv`, `nat_card_isotropy_eq`);
    "there is no canonical identification" is made precise: two choices of `φ` give isomorphisms
    that differ by an inner automorphism of `G_y` (`isotropyConj_eq_isotropyConj_conj`).

Found while formalizing the natural representations and local uniformizers (2026-11-07).

20. **Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1) is read as the datum `NaturalRep`, with `U` connected** *(Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1), p. 293 (2017 p. 231))*.
    `NaturalRep x` holds `U` open, connected, containing `x`, `Φ` and `Γ` with (1)–(3); the theorem
    is `theorem_7_1_13`: for every open `V ∋ x` there is one with `U ⊆ V`. The statement does not say
    "connected", but the text chooses "the connected open neighborhood `U(x)`" two paragraphs later
    (p. 293 (2017 p. 231)), and connectedness is what makes `Φ` a homomorphism with `Φ(1) = id`: two sections of
    `s` through the same morphism agree on a connected set (`eqOn_sections_of_isPreconnected`).
    `Φ(g) ∈ Diff_sc(U)` is read as an sc-diffeomorphism of `U` with inverse `Φ(g⁻¹)`
    (`isScDiffeoOn_Φ`, `Φ_mul`), and "`Γ : G × U → 𝐗` sc-smooth" per sheet, `y ↦ Γ(g, y)`
    sc-smooth for each `g` (`isScSmoothOn_Γ`), which is sc-smoothness on `G × U` (item 23). (3) is
    `existsUnique_Γ`, with the bijection `NaturalRep.bijOn_Γ`.
21. **Local path connectedness of M-polyfolds is proved** *(used on 2017 p. 231, in Lemma 7.6.3 (2017: 7.9) and in
    Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2))*. The text takes connected neighbourhoods `U(x)`, `U₂` and open connected
    components for granted. An sc-retract `O = r(U)` is locally path connected: a point `p ∈ O`
    near `o` is joined to `o` inside `O ∩ W` by the path `τ ↦ r(o + τ(p − o))`
    (`ScRetraction.exists_ball_joinedIn`, `IsScRetract.locallyPathConnectedSpace`); hence so is
    every M-polyfold
    (`MPolyfold.locallyPathConnectedSpace`, `MPolyfold.locallyConnectedSpace`,
    `MPolyfold.hasBasis_isOpen_isConnected`, `MPolyfold.isOpen_connectedComponent`) and every
    quotient of one (`MPolyfold.locallyPathConnectedSpace_quotient`). This is the first of the two
    facts of gap G.56 (item 114).
22. **The discussion on pp. 293–297 (2017 pp. 231–233) is formalized** *(pp. 293–297 (2017 pp. 231–233))* *(book 2021: the composability condition with `Φ(h)(y)` unchanged, after Theorem 7.1.13, p. 294)*. The splitting
    `𝐔(x) = ⊔_g 𝐔(g)` into the connected open sets `𝐔(g) = Γ(g, U)` with `s, t : 𝐔(g) → U`
    sc-diffeomorphisms (`NaturalRep.pairwise_disjoint_image_Γ`, `NaturalRep.iUnion_image_Γ`,
    `NaturalRep.connectedComponentIn_morOn`, `NaturalRep.isScDiffeoOn_src_image`,
    `NaturalRep.isScDiffeoOn_tgt_image`); "`𝐔(x)` fits into an arbitrarily small open neighbourhood
    of `G_x`" is Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8) with any open `N_g ∋ g` followed by Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1) with `V = U₁`
    (`lemma_7_6_2`, `theorem_7_1_13`). The translation groupoid `G_x ⋉ U(x)` is an ep-groupoid built from
    the data `(Φ, Γ)` alone (`NaturalRep.translationEpGroupoid`), with the properness for every `V`
    (`NaturalRep.translation_isProperMap`), "using the proof of Theorem 7.1" not being needed. The
    functor `Γ` is a functor because `U` is connected (`NaturalRep.Γ_mul`, `NaturalRep.Γ_one`,
    `NaturalRep.Γ_inv`), full and faithful by (3) (`NaturalRep.full`, `NaturalRep.faithful`), an
    `EpFunctor` (`NaturalRep.epFunctor`), with image the full subcategory on `U`. `Φ̂` is defined by
    the text's formula (`NaturalRep.Φhat`, `NaturalRep.Φhat_Γ`); it is a homomorphism of
    sc-diffeomorphisms of `𝐔(x)` with the two commutative diagrams (`NaturalRep.Φhat_mul`,
    `NaturalRep.Φhat_one`, `NaturalRep.src_Φhat`, `NaturalRep.tgt_Φhat`, `NaturalRep.image_Φhat`,
    `NaturalRep.isScDiffeoOn_Φhat`). One possible misprint (2017 p. 232, added 2026-11-07 from the
    comparison): the composability condition reads "`y = s(g, y) = t(h, z) = Φ(h)(y)`", where
    `Φ(h)(z)` is meant.
23. **`G × U` as an M-polyfold** *(p. 294 (2017 p. 232))*. "The finite disjoint union of copies of the
    M-polyfold `U`" is the product of `U` with the discrete M-polyfold on `G`
    (`discretePolyfold`, `discreteChart`); a map on `G × U` is sc-smooth iff it is on every slice
    (`isScSmoothOn_univ_prod_discrete_iff`, `isScSmoothMap_prod_discrete_iff`). The source and target
    of `G ⋉ U` are local sc-diffeomorphisms, `t` through the shear `(g, y) ↦ (g, Φ(g)(y))`
    (`NaturalRep.shearHomeomorph`).
24. **Uniqueness and restriction of natural representations** *(used on pp. 307–311 (2017 pp. 239–241): "`U(x)` can be
    chosen arbitrarily small", "adapting restrictions" in Lemma 7.2.3 (2017: 7.3))*. Two natural representations
    at `x` agree on the connected component of `x` in `U ∩ U'` (`NaturalRep.Γ_eqOn`,
    `NaturalRep.Φ_eqOn`), and a natural representation restricts to every `G_x`-invariant connected
    open neighbourhood (`NaturalRep.restrict`, `NaturalRep.restrictInter`,
    `exists_naturalRep_restrict`, `exists_naturalRep_shrink`). The text uses both without
    statement.
25. **Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5) is proved by a star construction, without induction or shrinking**
    *(Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5), pp. 297–304 (2017 pp. 233–236))*. The functor `f` with its properties is the datum
    `NaturalRepFinite Y V` (Definition 7.1.18 (2017: 7.8)). Instead of the text's induction on `k`, which shrinks
    the neighbourhoods at each step, the formalization fixes a natural representation at one object
    `x` (which need not lie in `Y`), chooses morphisms `x → y` for `y ∈ Y` and transports it along
    them (`NatRepFinite.transportRep`, `NatRepFinite.Star`, `NatRepFinite.exists_star`); (1) holds
    with the transported natural representations. `V` is read as a neighbourhood of the set `Y`
    (`proposition_7_1_15_of_mem_nhdsSet`; the open form `proposition_7_1_15_2017`), and `Y = ∅` is allowed
    (`NatRepFinite.emptyNaturalRepFinite`).
26. **Possible misprints in the proof of Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5)** *(pp. 297–305 (2017 pp. 234–236))* *(book 2021: proof of Proposition 7.1.15, pp. 297–300: the four slips of p. 234, `Ψ_g` and "k = 1" corrected; the other six unchanged)*. 2017 p. 234: "unique

    `k ≥ 2`; "as in the case `k = 1`" where the two-object case `k = 2` is meant;

27. **Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6): the openness of `σ` is not needed** *(Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6), pp. 304 ff. (2017 pp. 236–237))*. The
    proof follows the text (injectivity by Theorem 7.1.13 (3) (2017: 7.1), openness of `|U(x)|` by Proposition
    7.1.8 (2017: 7.1)). The image of an open `Q ⊆ G_x\U(x)` is `π(σ⁻¹(Q))` with `σ⁻¹(Q)` open in `U(x)`, so `τ`
    into `|X|` is a continuous injective open map, an open embedding onto `π(U(x))`
    (`NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_orbitQuotientMap`, `proposition_7_1_19`); the second form is
    `proposition_7_1_19_fullyFaithful` and `proposition_7_1_19_orbitMap`.
28. **Definition 7.1.20 (2017: 7.9) and the claims after it** *(Definition 7.1.20 (2017: 7.9), p. 305 (2017 p. 237))* *(book 2021: both corrected, Definition 7.1.20, p. 305)*. "`Ψx ◦ Gx ⋉ U(x) → X`"
    is read as `Ψ_x : G_x ⋉ U(x) → X` (possible misprint), and "a a local uniformizer" doubles the
    article (possible misprint). `LocalUniformizer` has `Ψ_x` the inclusion on objects, full and
    faithful, inducing a homeomorphism onto `π(U(x))`; "embedding" is not a separate field: the
    injectivity on objects and morphisms that the text notes afterwards follows
    (`LocalUniformizer.injective_obj`, `LocalUniformizer.injective_mor`), and for the uniformizers
    built from natural representations `Ψ_x` is an open embedding on both spaces
    (`NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_functor_obj`, `NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_functor_mor`). Existence
    is proved inside every open `V ∋ x` (`exists_localUniformizer`).
29. **The proof of Theorem 7.6.1 (2017: 7.5) (= Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1))** *(Theorem 7.6.1 (2017: 7.5), pp. 344–346 (2017 pp. 253–254))* *(book 2021: "`G_x`" for `G_{x₀}` unchanged, Theorem 7.6.1, p. 344)*. `theorem_7_6_1` is
    `theorem_7_1_13` (the text restates Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1) in Appendix 7.6.1 (2017 7.5.1)), proved along the text with
    Lemmas 7.6.2 and 7.6.3 (2017: 7.8 and 7.9) (`NatRepConstruction.exists_sheets`, `NatRepConstruction.Sheets.mkRep`).
    Readings: the neighbourhood is started at `U₀ := V ∩ ⋂_g s(N_g)`, so that `U ⊆ V`, which the
    text's proof does not address; only `s_g` has to be an sc-diffeomorphism onto `U₀`; the
    disjointness of the `N_g` is used only for the uniqueness in (3); "contractible" `N^t_g`, `N^s_g`
    is not needed. In the statement, "`Φ : G_x → Diff_sc(U)`" in the sentence after the bullets is
    meant for `G_{x₀}` (possible misprint).
30. **Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8)** *(Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8), pp. 345 ff. (2017 pp. 253–254))* *(book 2021: corrected, Lemma 7.6.2, p. 345)*. The indirect argument is run along a countable basis
    of `x₀`; properness applies once `s(h_k)`, `t(h_k)` lie in a neighbourhood with the properness
    property, i.e. for large `k`. The lemma holds for any open `N_g ∋ g` and any neighbourhood `U₀`
    (`lemma_7_6_2`). "By the properness assumption of ep-polyfolds" is meant for ep-groupoids
    (possible misprint).
31. **Lemma 7.6.3 (2017: 7.9): `U₂` connected** *(Lemma 7.6.3 (2017: 7.9), p. 345 (2017 p. 254))*. `U₂` is chosen connected, by item 21
    (the text does not say so); then `U = ⋃_g t_g s_g⁻¹(U₂)` is connected as each piece contains
    `x₀` (`NatRepConstruction.Sheets.isConnected_unionHat`), which the homomorphism property needs.
    The invariance and `U ⊆ U₁` are `lemma_7_6_3`; the continuity of the composition used for
    `Φ(gh) = Φ(g)Φ(h)` comes from (4) in sheet form (`NatRepConstruction.Sheets.eqOn_σ_mul`,
    `NatRepConstruction.Sheets.hat_mul`, `NatRepConstruction.Sheets.hat_one`).

Found while formalizing the ep-subgroupoids (2026-11-07).

40. **Definition 7.1.21 (2017: 7.10) and the facts (1)–(4) of a sub-M-polyfold** *(Definition 7.1.21 (2017: 7.10) and pp.
    237–238)*. Definition 7.1.21 (2017: 7.10) is `IsEpSubgroupoid` (sub-M-polyfold and saturated). The four facts
    recalled from Part I's Proposition 2.3.19 (2017: 2.6) are used in their forms (1) and (2) (`subObjPolyfold`,
    `isScSmoothMap_val_subObj`, `isScSmoothOn_retractInto_subObj`); the tangent facts (3) and (4) are
    not restated, as `T_aA` and `T_aX` carry no linear structure here (gap G.7); in a chart they are
    Part I's `proposition_2_3_19_three`, `proposition_2_3_19_four`.
    (2026-11-09) (3) and (4) are now stated with the linear structure of `T_aX` (`EpGroupoid.fact_3_subObj`,
    `fact_3_subObj_sc`, `fact_4_subObj`, item 154).
41. **The morphisms `𝐀` and the retraction `𝐫`** *(2017 p. 238)* *(book 2021: the claim `t(𝐫(ψ)) ∈ U(a)` unchanged, before Proposition 7.1.22, p. 306)*. For saturated `A`, `𝐀 = s⁻¹(A) =
    t⁻¹(A)` (`morOn_eq_preimage_src`, `morOn_eq_preimage_tgt`, `src_mem_of_tgt_mem_of_isSaturated`),
    the preimage of a sub-M-polyfold under a local sc-diffeomorphism, hence a sub-M-polyfold
    (`isSubMPolyfold_preimage_src`, `isSubMPolyfold_morOn`); the text's `𝐫 = (s|𝐔(φ))⁻¹ ∘ r ∘ s` is
    that construction. The extracted text has "`s(𝐫(ψ)) = r(s(ψ)) ∈ A` and `t(𝐫(ψ)) ∈ U(a)`, so that
    `𝐫(ψ) ∈ 𝐔(a)`": the second claim need not hold (`t(𝐫(ψ))` lies near `t(φ)`, not near `a`) and is
    not used, since `𝐫(ψ) ∈ 𝐀` follows from `s(𝐫(ψ)) ∈ A` and saturation (possible misprint or
    extraction artefact; check against the printed page).
42. **Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7): steps the text leaves out** *(Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7), pp. 307 ff. (2017 pp. 238–239))*. (i) A map that
    is sc-smooth into `X` and takes values in the sub-M-polyfold `A` is sc-smooth into `A` (a private
    lemma of `SubGroupoid.lean`); this is what "restrictions of sc-smooth maps" needs. (ii) The
    fibred product of `𝐀` includes sc-smoothly into that of `𝐗`, which (4) for `A` needs
    (`isScSmoothComp_fullSub`). (iii)
    `A` and `𝐀` must be paracompact for the project's M-polyfolds; the text does not address it
    (`instParacompactSpaceMorOn`, scoped). (iv) The properness: any `V(a)` with the properness
    property works, the `G_a`-invariance of `U(a)` is not used, and the subsequence is taken by the
    sequential criterion (`exists_isProperMap_fullSub`). Not in the text: the inclusion is a fully
    faithful functor (`subEpFunctor`, `subEpFunctor_full`, `subEpFunctor_faithful`). The conclusion is
    `proposition_7_1_22`, with `subEpGroupoid`.

Found while formalizing §7.2 (2026-11-07).

50. **Definition 7.2.1 (2017: 7.11) and the regular objects** *(Definition 7.2.1 (2017: 7.11) and the sentence after it, p.
    239)*. `IsEffective` is the text's condition (every open neighbourhood of `g ≠ 1_x` contains `ψ`
    with `s(ψ) ≠ t(ψ)`); regular objects are `GroupoidStr.IsRegular`, `X_reg` is `regularSet`. The
    sentence "if `s(φ)` is regular, so is `t(φ)`" is `isRegular_tgt_of_isRegular_src`, by the
    conjugation of item 13; `X_reg` is saturated (`isSaturated_regularSet`).
51. **Lemma 7.2.2 (2017: 7.2) uses `Γ(1, a) = 1_a`** *(Lemma 7.2.2 (2017: 7.2), p. 307 (2017 p. 239))*. For `a ∈ U(x)` the morphisms
    `a → a` are `Γ(g, a)` with `Φ(g)(a) = a`; that `G_x = {1}` gives `G_a = {1_a}` needs
    `Γ(1, a) = 1_a`, which holds because `U` is connected (item 20). The lemma holds for every
    natural representation (`NaturalRep.subset_regularSet`, `lemma_7_2_2`).
52. **Lemma 7.2.3 (2017: 7.3): "adapting restrictions" through uniqueness** *(Lemma 7.2.3 (2017: 7.3), pp. 308–309 (2017 pp. 239–240))*. (2) is
    read with "injective" as "trivial kernel" (`NaturalRep.injective_Φ_iff`,
    `NaturalRep.kerΦ_eq_bot_iff`). (1) ⇒ (2) holds for every natural representation and is proved
    without sequences (`IsEffective.eq_one`, `isEffective_iff_forall_naturalRep`). (2) ⇒ (1): the
    text's "adapting restrictions" is read through the uniqueness of item 24, applied once with
    `V = {y ∈ U₀ | Γ₀(g, y) ∈ 𝐔(g)}`. The equivalence is `lemma_7_2_3`.
53. **Proposition 7.2.4 (2017: 7.8): the minimum is taken over the open set itself; the converse holds**
    *(Proposition 7.2.4 (2017: 7.8), pp. 309 ff. (2017 pp. 240–241))*. The text minimizes `#G_x` over `U(x₀)`; the formalization
    minimizes over the given open set, so `U(x₀)` is not needed, and identifies `G_a` with the
    stabilizer of `a` in `G_x` (`NaturalRep.stabilizerEquivIsotropy`, the text's `H`). The converse,
    not in the text, also holds: `X` is effective iff `X_reg` is dense
    (`isEffective_of_dense_regularSet`, `isEffective_iff_dense_regularSet`).
54. **The subgroup `T_x`** *(2017 p. 241)* *(book 2021: the parenthesis corrected, p. 309; `T_x` is now Definition 7.2.5, and `φ T_x φ⁻¹ = T_y` is Lemma 7.2.6, p. 310)*. "`g` acts trivially" is `ActsTrivially` (there is a natural
    representation with `Φ(g) = id`), `T_x` is `trivialSet` and `trivialSubgroup`. The kernel of `Φ`
    depends on `U(x)` (sc-smooth maps are not analytic); the text's "we can choose `U(x)` so small
    that the kernel is `T_x`" is proved in the form: there is a neighbourhood `N` of `x` such that
    `ker Φ = T_x` for every natural representation inside `N` (`exists_mem_nhds_trivialSet_iff`,
    `exists_naturalRep_kerΦ_eq`). Not in the text: the intrinsic form `g ∈ T_x` iff `s = t` near `g`
    in `𝐗` (`mem_trivialSet_iff_eventually`); `T_x` is a normal subgroup (`trivialSubgroup_normal`),
    trivial for all `x` iff `X` is effective (`isEffective_iff_trivialSubgroup_eq_bot`). Needed for
    Definition 7.2.7 (2017: 7.12) and not stated: `φ T_x φ⁻¹ = T_y` for `φ : x → y`
    (`isotropyConj_mem_trivialSet`, `map_isotropyConj_trivialSubgroup`). "`Diff_sc(U(x)`" lacks a
    parenthesis (possible misprint or extraction artefact; check against the printed page).
55. **Definition 7.2.7 (2017: 7.12): `∼` is an equivalence relation; "the subset `𝐗^R`"** *(Definition 7.2.7 (2017: 7.12), p.
    241)* *(book 2021: corrected, Definition 7.2.7, p. 310)*. `∼` is an equivalence relation because `T_x` is a subgroup (`reducedSetoid`). Equivalent
    forms: `φ = φ' ∘ k` with `k ∈ 𝐗^T`, and `𝐗^T` is the interior of `{s = t}`
    (`nonEffectivePart_eq_interior`); the left form `k ∘ φ` (`reducedRel_comp_left`). `𝐗^R` is called
    "the subset of reduced morphisms"; it is a quotient of `𝐗`, as the next sentence says
    ("the collection of all equivalence classes") (possible misprint). `𝐗^R` is `ReducedMor`.
56. **Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) takes `𝐗^R` Hausdorff and paracompact as hypotheses** *(Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9), pp.
    242–243)* *(book 2021: corrected, Theorem 7.2.14, p. 318, assumes `T_R` Hausdorff; paracompactness is Proposition 7.2.12, p. 317)*. An M-polyfold is a paracompact Hausdorff space (Definition 2.3.4 (2017: 2.8)). The proof gives the
    quotient topology, the openness of the projection (`isOpenMap_reducedπ`), the charts
    `Ψ_φ = ψ ∘ σ ∘ s` on `π(dom ψ)` (`reducedChart`) and their sc-smooth transitions
    `ψ₂ ∘ σ₂ ∘ s ∘ ψ₁⁻¹` (`reducedChart_compatible`), all without hypotheses; but, as we read it,
    neither Hausdorffness nor paracompactness, and `𝐗^R` need not be Hausdorff (item 107: `ℤ/2`
    acting on the dimension-jumping retract of Part I's Remark 4.2.2 (2017: 4.3)). So `reducedPolyfold`, and
    `proposition_7_2_10`, take `[T2Space X.ReducedMor] [ParacompactSpace X.ReducedMor]` (gap G.71).
    Small sheets are not needed. The hypotheses are satisfiable (item 60).
    (2026-11-12) For the 2021 statements only `T_R` Hausdorff remains: Proposition 7.2.10 is the charts and their
    transitions, with no hypothesis (`proposition_7_2_10_natural_charts`), and paracompactness is an instance
    (`paracompactSpace_reducedMor`, Proposition 7.2.12) (rows V7.39, V7.40, now same).
57. **Possible misprints in the proof of Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9)** *(2017 pp. 242–243)* *(book 2021: rewritten as Lemma 7.2.9, Proposition 7.2.10 and the proof of Theorem 7.2.14, pp. 311–318; the first three now print the intended symbols, the garbled sentence is gone)*. "`ψ' = (s|𝐔(ψ))⁻¹(s(ψ))`"
    for `(s|𝐔(ψ))⁻¹(s(ψ'))` (a displaced prime is possible, an extraction artefact);
    "`𝐔(φ) ⊂ Ψ_{φ₀}(𝐔([φ₀]) ∩ 𝐔([ψ₀]))`" for `Ψ_{φ₀}⁻¹(…)` (a lost superscript is possible, an
    extraction artefact); "such that `T_x` agrees with the kernel of the `G_{s(φ)}`-action" for
    `T_{s(φ)}`; the garbled sentence "which show that the source and target maps are smoothness of
    the natural maps can be reduced" (2017 p. 243).
58. **Proposition 7.10 (2017; rewritten in 2021 as Theorem 7.2.14): the conditions of Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3) for `X_R`** *(2017 p. 243, Proposition 7.10 (2017), p.
    244)* *(book 2021: rewritten, proof of Theorem 7.2.14, pp. 318–319, for `T_R` Hausdorff: properness proved, (4) left to the reader; effectiveness is Proposition 7.2.16, p. 319)*. `X_R` is `reducedEpGroupoid`, with `reductionFunctor : X → X_R`. (1): on a sheet,
    `s, t` of `𝐗^R` are `s_X ∘ (π|𝐔)⁻¹`, `t_X ∘ (π|𝐔)⁻¹`. (3), "proved similarly": `t ∘ π = t_X` with
    `π` a continuous surjection (Mathlib's `isProperMap_of_comp_of_surj`, `exists_isProperMap_reduced`).
    (4), "reduced by our local charts", in the sheet form, with `κ = σ₂ ∘ s ∘ σ'` the inverse of `s` on
    an open set of `𝐗`, a step the text leaves implicit (`isScSmoothCompSheet_reduced`). The text
    obtains the continuity of `δ` from (4) applied to inverses; the formalization uses the left form
    `Γ(g, t ψ') ∘ ψ'` (`NaturalRep.isScSmoothOn_comp_Γ_tgt`). Effectiveness is proved from the
    intrinsic `T_x` of item 54 instead of a point with `Φ(g)(a) ≠ a` (`isEffective_reducedEpGroupoid`).
    The conclusion is `proposition_7_10_2017`.
59. **The isotropy of `X_R` and Definition 7.2.15 (2017: 7.13)** *(p. 319 (2017 p. 244), Definition 7.2.15 (2017: 7.13))* *(book 2021: "For and object" corrected, Definition 7.2.15, p. 319)*. `[1_x] = T_x` is
    `ker_reducedIsotropyHom`, and the isotropy of `X_R` at `x` is `G_x/T_x`
    (`surjective_reducedIsotropyHom`, `quotientTrivialSubgroupEquiv`). `G_x^eff` is `EffIsotropy`, the
    quotient by the normal closure of `T_x`, which is `T_x` (`normalClosure_trivialSet`,
    `effIsotropyEquiv`, `effIsotropyEquivReduced`). "For and object" (Definition 7.2.15 (2017: 7.13)) (possible
    misprint).
60. **The hypotheses on `𝐗^R` are satisfiable; for non-effective `X` they are not shown to hold**
    *(not in the text)* *(book 2021: Proposition 7.2.17 and Theorem 7.2.22, pp. 320–323: `T_R` Hausdorff iff `𝐗^T` closed iff (LUC); by it item 102 has `T_R` Hausdorff, item 107 not)*. For effective `X` the projection `𝐗 → 𝐗^R` is a homeomorphism
    (`reducedHomeomorph`), so `𝐗^R` is Hausdorff, paracompact and regular
    (`t2Space_reducedMor_of_isEffective`, `paracompactSpace_reducedMor_of_isEffective`,
    `t3Space_reducedMor_of_isEffective`) and `X_R ≅ X` (`reductionIso`); this covers the trivial
    ep-groupoid of every M-polyfold (`t2Space_reducedMor_trivial`,
    `paracompactSpace_reducedMor_trivial`). Paracompactness follows from regularity of `𝐗^R` when `𝐗`
    is second countable (`paracompactSpace_reducedMor_of_t3`). No non-effective witness is given:
    for the trivial `ℤ/3`-action (item 102) Hausdorffness of `𝐗^R` is not proved, and Hausdorff with
    `𝐗` second countable is not shown to suffice (a locally metrizable, second countable Hausdorff
    space need not be regular, the `K`-topology on `ℝ`). For the non-effective `ℤ/2 ⋉ O` of item
    107, `𝐗^R` is not Hausdorff (added 2026-11-07, after the round-trip audit).

Found while formalizing §7.3 up to Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2) (2026-11-07).

70. **Theorem 7.3.1 (2017: 7.2)** *(Theorem 7.3.1 (2017: 7.2), p. 324 (2017 p. 244))*. "Locally metrizable" is read as: every point has an
    open neighbourhood that is metrizable in the subspace topology (`theorem_7_3_1`). The metrizability
    of a paracompact `|X|` is proved by Smirnov's theorem in the form of Part I
    (`metrizableSpace_of_locally`, `theorem_7_3_1_metrizable`), as the text indicates.
71. **Lemma 7.3.2 (2017: 7.4): the metric `ρ̂`** *(Lemma 7.3.2 (2017: 7.4), pp. 324 ff. (2017 pp. 244–245))*. The text's invariant metric
    `ρ(y, y') = max_g d(g ∗ y, g ∗ y')` and the quotient metric are used; `ρ̂([y], [y'])` is computed
    as `min_h ρ(y, h ∗ y')`, equal to the text's expression by invariance, and the topology is
    checked through Mathlib's `MetricSpace.ofDistTopology` (`metrizableSpace_orbitRel_quotient_naturalRep`,
    `lemma_7_3_2_naturalRep`, `lemma_7_3_2`). With Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6) this gives the metrizability of
    `|U(x)|`, the text's "in fact one can take `|U(x)|`".
72. **Lemmas 7.3.3–7.3.5 (2017: 7.5–7.7): the order of proof** *(pp. 324–326 (2017 pp. 245–246))*. Lemma 7.3.3 (2017: 7.5) is Proposition 7.1.9 (2017: 7.2)
    (`lemma_7_3_3`; the text derives it from Lemma 7.3.2 (2017: 7.4)). Lemma 7.3.5 (2017: 7.7) is proved with a closed
    neighbourhood basis and Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3) (`lemma_7_3_5`), and Lemma 7.3.4 (2017: 7.6) from Lemma 7.3.5 (2017: 7.7) and the
    closedness of points (`t1Space_orbitSpace`, Proposition 7.5.10 (1) (2017: 7.14) for `{x}`; `lemma_7_3_4`); the text
    proves Lemma 7.3.4 (2017: 7.6) directly.
73. **Corollary 7.3.6 (2017: 7.1) and subsets of `|X|`** *(Corollary 7.3.6 (2017: 7.1) and the sentence before Definition 7.3.7 (2017: 7.14), p. 326 (2017 p. 247))*. Corollary 7.3.6 (2017: 7.1) is
    Urysohn's theorem (`corollary_7_3_6`). The sentence before Definition 7.3.7 (2017: 7.14), that a subset of `|X|`
    is again locally metrizable, regular and Hausdorff, is `exists_metrizable_nhds_subtype` and
    Mathlib's instances; a paracompact subset is metrizable
    (`metrizableSpace_of_paracompactSpace_subtype`).
74. **Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2): from compact pieces to a component compact `K`; `U` names two sets**
    *(Definition 7.3.7 (2017: 7.14), Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2), p. 326 (2017 p. 247))* *(book 2021: absent, proof of Corollary 7.3.8, pp. 326–327: the printed page writes `Ū` for the union of closures, a bar the extraction drops, so the 2017 reading was probably an extraction artefact)*. Definition 7.3.7 (2017: 7.14) is `IsComponentCompact`. "We work in a
    connected component of `K` and may assume … `K` compact" needs that the components of `|X|` are
    open (local connectedness of `|X|`, `locallyPathConnectedSpace_orbitSpace`, from item 21) and a
    step the text does not give: the neighbourhoods found in the components form a locally finite
    family of closed paracompact sets, whose union is paracompact (`paracompactSpace_iUnion`). The
    finite union of closed paracompact sets is paracompact by Michael's theorem (item 75), which the
    text does not cite (`paracompactSpace_biUnion_of_finite`). The compact case is
    `corollary_7_3_8_of_isCompact` (with `cl U` inside a given open `W ⊇ K`), the general one
    `corollary_7_3_8`. In the proof `U` denotes both `⋃ cl_|X|(U(z_i))` and `⋃ U(z_i)` (possible
    misprint). No other possible misprint was found on pp. 319–327 (2017 pp. 244–247).
75. **Michael's theorem and the paracompact unions** *(Part I, Lemma 2.7.3 (2017: 2.7) and Proposition 2.7.4 (2017: 2.17), used
    for Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2) and on the text's route to Proposition 7.5.3 (2017: 7.12))*. Part I left Lemma 2.7.3 (2017: 2.7) (Michael)
    and Proposition 2.7.4 (2017: 2.17) unformalized, as not needed (gap G.15). They are now proved
    (`lemma_2_7_3`, `proposition_2_7_4`, `michael_tfae`, `paracompactSpace_of_closed_refinement`,
    `exists_closed_precise_refinement`), with the unions used here (`paracompactSpace_iUnion`,
    `paracompactSpace_iUnion_of_finite`, `paracompactSpace_union`,
    `paracompactSpace_of_isClosed_subset`). Both are proved for regular spaces; the Hausdorff
    property, which the 2017 text assumes, is not used.

Found while formalizing the index lifts and paracompact orbit spaces (2026-11-07).

80. **Proposition 7.3.9 (2017: 7.11): "(1), (2) and (4) trivially"** *(Proposition 7.3.9 (2017: 7.11), pp. 327–328 (2017 pp. 247–248))* *(book 2021: unchanged, Proposition 7.3.9, p. 327)*. `X¹` is
    `liftOne`. The structure maps of `X¹` are the restrictions to level `1`; that `m(φ, ψ)` lies on
    level `1` uses `ml(t(φ ∘ ψ)) = ml(φ)` (item 6, `comp_mem_levelSet`); `liftComp` of a
    non-composable pair is a junk value. (1) is the level-`1` lift of a local sc-diffeomorphism
    (`MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.levelOne`), (2) Part I's `MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.levelOne`. For (4)
    the "trivially" uses, as we read it, `(𝐗 ₛ×ₜ 𝐗)¹ = 𝐗¹ ₛ×ₜ 𝐗¹` as M-polyfolds, which is not proved;
    it is avoided through the sheet form (`isScSmoothCompSheet_lift`, `isScSmoothComp_lift`). (3)
    follows the text, with "`(t(φ_k))` belongs to a compact subset of `X₁`" replaced by "`t(φ_k)`
    converges in `X₁`" and without the text's step (b) (`exists_isProperMap_lift`). The conclusion is
    `proposition_7_3_9`.
81. **Proposition 7.3.9 (2017: 7.11): the tameness of `X¹` is proved** *(Proposition 7.3.9 (2017: 7.11), p. 327 (2017 p. 247), "If `X` is tame
    so is `X¹`")* *(book 2021: unchanged, Proposition 7.3.9, pp. 327–328, which now calls it trivial without an argument)*. The text gives no argument. As we read it, the claim needs that the index lift of
    a tame retraction is tame, which Part I left open (Chapter 5, item 145). It is proved
    (`MPolyfold.IsTame.levelOne`, `isTame_liftOne`): for a presentation `T : E ≅ ℝⁿ ⊕ W` of `C`, the
    shifted presentation of `C¹` has the same `ℝⁿ`-coordinates, so `d_{C¹} = d_C` on `C¹` and
    `E_x` for it is `E_x ∩ E₁`; `Dr¹(x) = Dr(x)|E₁` has range `T_xO ∩ E₁`; an sc-complement `A` of
    `T_xO` gives the sc-complement `A ∩ E₁` of `T_xO¹`. Part I's presentation independence
    (`ScRetraction.IsTameWith.isTame`) then gives tameness for every presentation of `C¹`, and the
    level charts of tame charts form a tame atlas of `X¹`.
82. **Definition 7.5.1 (2017: 7.15), the sentence before Remark 7.5.2 (2017: 7.1), and Remark 7.5.2 (2017: 7.1)** *(2017 p. 249)*. Definition 7.5.1 (2017: 7.15)
    is `HasParacompactOrbitSpace`, Mathlib's `ParacompactSpace` without Hausdorff, as the text
    stipulates. "In case `X` has a second countable topology we have already seen that (1)–(4) imply
    (5)" is read with `X` the object space: `|X|` is then second countable (`π` is open), metrizable
    by Corollary 7.3.6 (2017: 7.1), hence paracompact (`remark_7_5_2`); also for `|X|` second countable
    (`hasParacompactOrbitSpace_of_secondCountableTopology`). "It is presently not known whether the
    property (5) is a consequence of the properties (1)–(4)" is an open question, recorded without a
    gap (item 113). Remark 7.5.2 (2017: 7.1) itself, on the requirement of [38], has no formal content. (2026-11-09: the open question is settled negatively, item 152.)
83. **Proposition 7.5.3 (2017: 7.12) by metrizability; `|X¹| → |X|`** *(Proposition 7.5.3 (2017: 7.12), pp. 340 ff. (2017 pp. 249–250))*. The text
    writes `|X₁|` for the orbit space of `X¹` and treats it as the subset `π(X₁)` of `|X|`. Here `|X¹|`
    keeps its quotient topology, and `orbitIncl : |X¹| → |X|` is a continuous injection onto
    `π(X₁)` (`continuous_orbitIncl`, `orbitIncl_injective`, `range_orbitIncl`). The text's route
    (Lemma 2.7.3 (2017: 2.7), a locally finite closed refinement, Michael's union of closed paracompact sets) is
    replaced by Smirnov's theorem pulled back along `orbitIncl` (`metrizableSpace_of_pullback`): every
    point of `|X|` has the neighbourhood `π(U(x))` whose preimage is metrizable
    (`NaturalRep.metrizableSpace_preimage_orbitIncl`), so `|X¹|` is metrizable
    (`metrizableSpace_liftOne_orbitSpace`), hence paracompact (`proposition_7_5_3`), a stronger
    conclusion. "`U(x)₁` has the natural `G_x`-action" is read as the restricted action only
    (`NaturalRep.liftMulAction`): `U(x)₁` need not be connected in `X¹`, so it is not a natural
    representation of `X¹`. The regularity of `|X¹|` is not needed on this route.

Found while formalizing §7.5 (2017 §7.4) and Appendix 7.6.2 (2017 7.5.2) (2026-11-07).

93. **Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10): the cover of `X`, and a stronger statement** *(Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10), p. 346 (2017 p. 255))*. "`V(x)` admits
    the natural `G_x`-action" is a natural representation with `V(x) = R.U`. The partition of unity

94. **The proof of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4)** *(pp. 346–347 (2017 pp. 255–256))* *(book 2021: both points unchanged, Lemma 7.6.5 and the proof of Theorem 7.5.7, pp. 346–347)*. Properties (1)–(3) are
    `exists_invariant_nhds_of_isOpen`; (4) follows from (1) and is not a further choice

95. **Theorem 7.6.4 (2017: 7.6) (= Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4)) and Corollary 7.6.6 (2017: 7.3)** *(2017 p. 255; Corollary 7.6.6 (2017: 7.3), p. 347 (2017 p. 256))*.
