    artefact of the text extraction).

Found while formalizing Theorem 8.1.15 (2017: 8.4) (2026-11-07).

20. **Theorem 8.1.15 (2017: 8.4) by metrizability; the conclusion is stronger** *(Theorem 8.1.15 (2017: 8.4) and its proof, p.
    268)*. The text covers `|X¹|` by the sets `|U(x_z)¹|`, takes a subordinate locally finite closed
    refinement (Part I's Lemma 2.7.3 (2017: 2.7)), shows that the preimages `Ã_z ⊆ |TX|` are closed and
    paracompact, and concludes with the regularity of `|TX|` and Part I's Proposition 2.7.4 (2017: 2.17). The
    proof here follows that of Proposition 7.5.3 (2017: 7.12) (Chapter 7, item 83): `|X¹|` is metrizable, every
    point of it has the open neighbourhood `|U(x)₁|`, whose preimage under `|p| : |TX| → |X¹|`
    (`tangentOrbitProj`, `continuous_tangentOrbitProj`) is `|TU(x)|`
    (`NaturalRep.image_tangentU_eq_preimage`) and is metrizable
    (`NaturalRep.metrizableSpace_image_tangentU`); Part I's `metrizableSpace_of_pullback` (Smirnov's
    theorem) then makes `|TX|` metrizable (`metrizableSpace_tangent_orbitSpace`), hence paracompact
    (`theorem_8_1_15`). The step shared with the text is the metrizability of `|TU(x_z)|`; neither the
    regularity of `|TX|` nor Proposition 2.7.4 (2017: 2.17) is used.

21. **`TU(x)`, the action of `G_x`, and the open embedding** *(proof of Theorem 8.1.15 (2017: 8.4), p. 368 (2017 p. 268))* *(book 2021: proof of Theorem 8.1.15, pp. 368–369, unchanged; "parcompact" corrected in the statement, p. 368)*.
    `TU(x)` is read as `p⁻¹(U(x)) ⊆ TX` (`NaturalRep.tangentU`), and the bundle action of `G_x` as
    `g ↦ TΦ(g)`, the tangent maps of the natural action (`NaturalRep.tΦ`,
    `NaturalRep.isScDiffeoOn_tΦ`, `NaturalRep.tangentMulAction`), with `TΓ` (`NaturalRep.tΓ`). The
    sc-isomorphism of `TU(x)` with a local bundle model `TO → O¹` is not used: `TU(x)` is metrizable
    as a subspace of `TX` (Part I's Proposition 2.3.15 (3) (2017: 2.5)), and `G_x\TU(x)` by the metric `ρ̂` of
    Lemma 7.3.2 (2017: 7.4), repeated privately in `TangentOrbit.lean` for a finite group acting by homeomorphisms
    on a metrizable space, since Chapter 7's versions are private. The linearity of the action on
    the fibres is not formalized (gap G.7). That `G_x\TU(x) → |TX|` is an open embedding onto
    `|TU(x)|` is left implicit in the text and is proved (`NaturalRep.tangent_π_eq_iff`,
    `NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_tangentOrbitQuotientMap`,
    `NaturalRep.range_tangentOrbitQuotientMap`): a morphism `k : v → w` of `TX` between vectors over
    `U(x)` lies over `p(k) = Γ(g, s(p k))` (Theorem 7.1.13 (3) (2017: 7.1)), and `k = TΓ(g)(v)` by fibre
    injectivity (item 4). `|TU(x)| = |p|⁻¹(|U(x)₁|)` uses the surjectivity of `Ts` on the fibres
    (`exists_tSrc_eq`). The statement writes "parcompact" for "paracompact" (possible misprint).
    (2026-11-09) `T_xX` now carries the linear structure of Definition 2.3.14, Banach through every chart and sc at
    smooth points (gap G.7 closed, Chapter 2, item 87); this statement is not restated with it. Every `Tφ`, `φ ∈ 𝐗₁`, is
    linear on the tangent spaces (Chapter 7, item 154).

Found while formalizing §8.3 (2026-11-07).

30. **Strong bundle maps between strong bundles over M-polyfolds are a reading** *(used in
    Definitions 8.3.1–8.3.3, 8.5.9 (2017: 8.4–8.6, 8.10), pp. 373–396 (2017 pp. 270–285); Part I's Definitions 2.6.1, 2.6.4 (2017: 2.22, 2.25))*. Part I defines strong
    bundle maps only between local models (Definition 2.6.1 (2017: 2.22)) and treats the transition maps of a
    strong bundle atlas in Definition 2.6.4 (2017: 2.25). The global notion used throughout §8.3 is
    `StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleMap B B' f Φ`: `P' ∘ Φ = f ∘ P`; `Φ` linear on the fibres
    (`fiberRestrict`); `Φ : Y[0] → Y'[0]` sc-smooth; `Φ(Y_{0,1}) ⊆ Y'_{0,1}` with `Y[1] → Y'[1]`
    sc-smooth. In the charts the last two conditions say that the local representatives `K[i] →
    K'[i]` are sc-smooth, as Definition 2.6.4 (2017: 2.25) asks of transition maps. The preservation of the double
    filtration, part of Definition 2.6.1 (2017: 2.22), is not assumed but follows
    (`IsStrongBundleMap.mapsTo_doubleLevel`), and so do the boundedness of the fibre maps
    (`IsStrongBundleMap.fiberMap`) and the sc-smoothness of the base map, `f = P' ∘ Φ ∘ 0`
    (`IsStrongBundleMap.isScSmoothMap_base`). A strong bundle isomorphism is a pair of inverse
    strong bundle maps (`StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleIso`). Strong bundle maps defined over open
    subsets of the base are not formalized (item 113).

31. **The pull-back along `s`** *(2017 p. 270; Part I's Proposition 2.6.8 (2017: 2.16))*. `𝐗 ₛ×_P W` is Part I's
    pull-back `pullbackSpace P X.src` with its strong bundle structure (`StrongBundle.pullback`);
    its paracompactness, which Part I's definition of a strong bundle requires, is an instance
    argument, supplied by `StrongBundle.paracompactSpace_pullback`. Added here: the atlas of the
    pull-back (`StrongBundle.pullback_atlas`), its universal property on `[0]`
    (`StrongBundle.isScSmoothOn_to_pullback_iff`, `StrongBundle.isScSmoothMap_pullbackPair`) and on
    `[1]` (`StrongBundle.pullbackProj'One`, `StrongBundle.isScSmoothMap_to_pullback_one`), and the
    fact that over a sheet of the local sc-diffeomorphism `s` the projection to `W` is an
    sc-diffeomorphism (`StrongBundle.isScDiffeoOn_pullbackProj'`,
    `StrongBundle.isLocalScDiffeo_pullbackProj'`); its inverse `w ↦ (σ(P w), w)` takes a junk value
    off `P⁻¹(V)`.

32. **Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4) and the fibre maps `μ(ψ, ·)`** *(Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4) and 2017 p. 271)*. `EpStrongBundle X
    B`: a structure map `μ` on Part I's pull-back, a strong bundle map covering `t` in the sense of
    item 30 (which contains `P ∘ μ = t ∘ π₁` and the fibrewise linearity), a surjective local
    sc-diffeomorphism of the `[0]`-M-polyfolds, with (2) and (3); the conditions `s(ψ) = P(w)` are
    carried by the points of the pull-back. The surjectivity in (1) follows from (2), `μ(1_x, w) =
    w`, and is kept as in the text. The claim after the definition that `μ(ψ, ·) : W_x → W_y` is a
    linear isomorphism is proved in the stronger form of a topological linear isomorphism with
    inverse `μ(ψ⁻¹, ·)` (`EpStrongBundle.fiberMorEquiv`, `μ_inv_μ`, `μ_μ_inv`); `μ` is continuous
    (`continuous_μ`).

33. **The functorial picture: "we can define the ep-groupoid"** *(pp. 375–377 (2017 pp. 271–272))* *(book 2021: unchanged, after Definition 8.3.1, p. 376)*. Asserted without
    proof; Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3) is proved for `(W, 𝐖)`, `𝐖 = 𝐗 ₛ×_P W` (`EpStrongBundle.toEpGroupoid`):
    (1) `s_𝐖` is the pull-back projection along the local sc-diffeomorphism `s` (item 31), and `t_𝐖
    = μ` is one by Definition 8.3.1 (1) (2017: 8.4); (2) the units and inverses are sc-smooth by the universal
    property of the pull-back; (3) holds with `V = P⁻¹(V(P w))`, by sequences, from the properness
    of `X`, the continuity of `μ` and `w = μ(ψ⁻¹, μ(ψ, w))` (`exists_isProperMap_tgt`); (4) is
    proved in the sheet form, through a sheet of `s` and condition (4) for `X`
    (`isScSmoothCompSheet_toGroupoidStr`). The groupoid laws use Definition 8.3.1 (2), (3) (2017: 8.4); the
    composition is total, with the junk value `(γ, w)` off composable pairs (`morComp`). `s_𝐖`,
    `t_𝐖` are strong bundle maps covering `s`, `t` (`isStrongBundleMap_src`,
    `isStrongBundleMap_tgt`), `(P, π₁)` is an sc-smooth functor (`projFunctor`), and `|P|` is
    continuous and surjective (`continuous_orbitMap_projFunctor`,
    `surjective_orbitMap_projFunctor`). From here on `W` lives in the universe of the objects and
    morphisms of `X` (item 2).

34. **Definitions 8.3.2, 8.3.3 (2017: 8.5, 8.6) and "these are identical notions"** *(pp. 377–379 (2017 pp. 273–274))*. Definition 8.3.2 (2017: 8.5) is
    `EpStrongBundle.IsMap`. In Definition 8.3.3 (2017: 8.6), "linear on the fibers", "covers `ϕ`" and "induces
    strong bundle maps `W → W'` and `𝐖 → 𝐖'`" are read together as two conditions
    `IsStrongBundleMap` (`IsStrongBundleFunctor`): on objects, for `P`, `P'`, covering `ϕ` on
    objects, which contains `P' ∘ Φ = ϕ ∘ P`; and on morphisms, for the pull-backs `𝐖 → 𝐗`, `𝐖' →
    𝐗'`, covering `ϕ` on morphisms. The text's claim that the two notions are identical, and that
    the functor is recovered from the strong bundle map, is proved: `isMap_iff_strongBundleFunctor`,
    with the unique functor `Φ(γ, w) = (ϕ(γ), Φ(w))` (`IsMap.liftFunctor`,
    `IsStrongBundleFunctor.eq_liftFunctor`). The `[1]`-smoothness of the lifted morphism map needs
    the universal property of the pull-back on level `[1]` (item 31) and the fibrewise linearity of
    maps of pull-backs (`isLinearMap_fiberRestrict_pullbackMap`).

35. **Definition 8.3.4 (2017: 8.7): "the vector space `Γ(P, μ)`"** *(Definition 8.3.4 (2017: 8.7), pp. 379 ff. (2017 pp. 274–275))*. The section
    functors are `IsScSmoothSectionFunctor`, `IsScPlusSectionFunctor`, `IsScFredholmSectionFunctor`,
    with the sets `sectionFunctors`, `plusSectionFunctors`, `fredholmSectionFunctors`; (3) uses Part
    I's Definition 3.1.16 (2017: 3.8) in its germ reading. "Vector space" and "subspace" are read as closure under
    Part I's fibrewise zero section, sums and constant multiples (`fiberZero_mem_sectionFunctors`,
    `sectionAdd_mem_sectionFunctors`, `sectionSmul_mem_sectionFunctors`, and the same for `Γ⁺`, with
    `plusSectionFunctors_subset`); no `Module` structure is built. The sum of two sc-smooth sections
    and the constant multiples of one, which Part I does not state, are proved in the charts
    (`StrongBundle.IsScSmoothSection.sectionAdd_of_isScSmoothSection`,
    `StrongBundle.IsScSmoothSection.sectionSmul_const`).

Found while formalizing §8.5 (2017 §8.4) up to Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6) (2026-11-07).

50. **Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8)** *(2017 p. 275)*. `EpFunctor.IsProperCovering`: (1) `F` is surjective and a local
    sc-diffeomorphism on objects; (2) every fibre `F⁻¹(x)` is finite, and an open `U(x) ∋ x` has
    `F⁻¹(U(x))` the union of mutually disjoint `U(y) ∋ y`, `y ∈ F⁻¹(x)`, with `F : U(y) → U(x)`
    sc-diffeomorphisms whose inverses `σ(y)` are part of the data; (3) `L_F = (F, s) : 𝐘 → 𝐗 ₛ×_F Y`
    (`fibredMap`) is an sc-diffeomorphism onto Part I's fibred-product sub-M-polyfold of `𝐗 × Y`
    (`MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_fibredProduct`, Part I's Proposition 2.5.20 (2017: 2.15)), as in Definition 7.1.3 (4) (2017: 7.3).

51. **The degeneracy remark after Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8) needs tameness** *(pp. 379–385 (2017 pp. 275–276))* *(book 2021: unchanged, after Definition 8.5.1, p. 384)*. The text computes
    `d_{𝐗 ₛ×_F Y}(F(φ), s(φ)) = ½ d_{𝐗 × Y}(F(φ), s(φ))` through `d_{𝐗 × Y} = d_𝐗 + d_Y`. The first
    equality, `d_𝐘(φ) = d_{𝐗 ₛ×_F Y}(L_F(φ))` (`IsProperCovering.degIndex_fibredMap`), and
    `d_𝐗(F(φ)) = d_𝐘(φ)` (`IsProperCovering.degIndex_mor`) hold in general, by Part I's Proposition
    2.4.4 (2017: 2.7) (`proposition_2_4_4`). The product formula is available in Part I's formalization for tame
    factors (`MPolyfold.isTame_prod`) and in general only as `d_{X × Y} ≤ d_X + d_Y`
    (`MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_le`; section "From the Lean proofs of Chapter 2, §2.5–§2.6 and Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint §2.4–§2.5 and Theorem
    2.16)" above, items 15, 16), and Part I's Proposition 2.5.20 (2017: 2.15) states its formula `d = ½ d_{X × Y}`
    for tame `X`, `Y`. So `d_{𝐗 × Y}(F(φ), s(φ)) = 2 d_𝐘(φ)` and `d_{𝐗 ₛ×_F Y} = ½ d_{𝐗 × Y}` along
    the image of `L_F` are stated for tame `X` and `Y` (`IsProperCovering.degIndex_prod_fibredMap`;
    `𝐗` is then tame, `s` being a local sc-diffeomorphism), and in general as `≤`
    (`IsProperCovering.degIndex_prod_fibredMap_le`). As we read it, the remark needs `X` and `Y`
    tame, which the text does not state; whether the equality holds without tameness is not settled
    here.

52. **Proposition 8.5.2 (2017: 8.2)** *(pp. 384–386 (2017 pp. 276–277))* *(book 2021: corrected, proof of Proposition 8.5.2, p. 385)*. `IsProperCovering.proposition_8_5_2`. Condition (2), "follows
    easily", is proved by shrinking `U(x)` of `F` to a `U₀` with `(F|U(y))⁻¹(U₀) ⊆ U'(y)` for the
    evenly covered neighbourhoods `U'(y)` of `H`, `y ∈ F⁻¹(x)`, a finite intersection
    (`IsProperCovering.evenlyCovered_comp`). Condition (3) goes through the text's `K̃`, `L̃`
    (`IsProperCovering.isScDiffeo_fibredMap_comp`); their sc-smoothness, as maps between
    sub-M-polyfolds of products, uses Part I's Proposition 2.3.19 (2) (2017: 2.6) (a map into a sub-M-polyfold is
    sc-smooth as soon as it is sc-smooth into the ambient M-polyfold), proved again privately in
    `ProperCovering.lean`, as in Chapter 7's `SubGroupoid.lean`. "fo" for "for" in the proof (p.
    276; possible misprint).

53. **Theorem 8.5.3 (2017: 8.5): the chart and "sufficiently small"** *(Theorem 8.5.3 (2017: 8.5), p. 385 (2017 p. 277))*. The data of the
    theorem form a `ProperCoveringChart`: a natural representation `R : X.NaturalRep x` (Chapter 7's
    structure: `U(x)` open and connected, with the natural `G_x`-action), sets `U(y)` for `y ∈
    F⁻¹(x)` and `𝐔(ψ₀)` for the morphisms `ψ₀` between points of `F⁻¹(x)` (`Y.morOn (F⁻¹(x))`), and
    (0)–(5) as fields. "Disjoint union of connected open neighbourhoods" means: each set open,
    connected and containing its centre, the sets pairwise disjoint, with the given union; that they
    are then the connected components is `ProperCoveringChart.connectedComponentIn_U`,
    `ProperCoveringChart.connectedComponentIn_sheet`. `𝐔(φ)` for `φ ∈ 𝐔(x)` is read as the connected
    component of `𝐔(x)` containing `φ`; by Remark 8.5.4 (2017: 8.2) (a) `F(ψ₀) ∈ 𝐔(x)`, and (1) is Chapter 7's
    description of `𝐔(x)` by the sheets `Γ(g, U(x))`. "`s : 𝐔(ψ₀) → U(y)` is an sc-diffeomorphism"
    is Part I's `IsScDiffeoOn`, with an inverse. "Sufficiently small" is proved in two forms: charts
    with `U(x)` inside every open `V ∋ x` (`theorem_8_5_3`), and one open `W ∋ x` that works for every
    natural representation on a connected `U(x) ⊆ W` (`theorem_8_5_3_of_naturalRep`); the proof uses
    only `U(x) ⊆ U'(x)` for `U'(x)` as in Definition 8.5.1 (2) (2017: 8.8).

54. **Theorem 8.5.3 (5) (2017: 8.5) does not hold as printed, as we read it** *(Theorem 8.5.3 (5) (2017: 8.5), p. 385 (2017 p. 277))* *(book 2021: unchanged, Theorem 8.5.3 (5), p. 386)*. As
    printed, the left vertical arrow of the square is `s : 𝐔(ψ₀) → U(s(ψ₀))`, the bottom arrow `F`,
    the right vertical arrow `t` and its lower right corner `U(t(F(ψ₀)))`. With `t` the square says
    `F(s(ψ)) = t(F(ψ))` for `ψ ∈ 𝐔(ψ₀)`. A functor gives `F(s(ψ)) = s(F(ψ))`, and `F(ψ) = Γ(g, F(s
    ψ))` with `g = F(ψ₀)` has `t(F(ψ)) = Φ(g)(F(s ψ))`, which differs from `F(s ψ)` wherever `Φ(g)`
    does not fix `F(s ψ)`. Example (checked in Lean, `CoveringExamples.theorem_8_5_3_five_as_printed`,
    for every chart of Theorem 8.5.3 (2017: 8.5) at `0`; charts exist by
    `theorem_8_5_3_five_as_printed_nonvacuous`): the identity functor of `ℤ/2 ⋉ ℝ`, `ℤ/2` acting by `z
    ↦ ±z`, is a proper covering functor (`EpFunctor.isProperCovering_id`); at `x = 0`, with
    `ψ₀ = (−1, 0)` and `ψ = (−1, z) ∈ 𝐔(ψ₀)`, `F(s(ψ)) = z` and `t(F(ψ)) = −z`. The square is
    formalized with `s` on both vertical arrows (`ProperCoveringChart.comm_src`; the corner
    `U(s(F(ψ₀))) = U(x)` is the same set, since `s(F(ψ₀)) = t(F(ψ₀)) = x`), together with the
    companion square with `t` on both (`ProperCoveringChart.comm_tgt`: `F(t(ψ)) = t(F(ψ))` over `F :
    U(t ψ₀) → U(x)`). The right arrow `t` is therefore a possible misprint for `s`. "Of
    sc-diffeomorphisms": the left arrows are (3), the top arrow (4), the bottom arrows (0), and the
    right arrows `s, t : 𝐔(F(ψ₀)) → U(x)` are `ProperCoveringChart.isScDiffeoOn_src_sheetF`,
    `ProperCoveringChart.isScDiffeoOn_tgt_sheetF`.

55. **Theorem 8.5.3 (2017: 8.5): the route of the proof, and possible misprints** *(proof, pp. 386–388 (2017 pp. 278–279))* *(book 2021: proof of Theorem 8.5.3, pp. 386–387: `g ∈ G_y` unchanged; `G_y`-invariant, `s(F(φ))`, "admitting admitting" and, in the statement, "morphismsm" (p. 385) corrected)*. The text
    decomposes the morphisms of `𝐘` near `F⁻¹(x)` by sheets and natural representations of the
    groups `G_y` in `Y`, and does not invoke Definition 8.5.1 (3) (2017: 8.8). Here (3) does that work: `L_F` is a
    bijection with continuous inverse; for `ψ₀ : y → y'` with `g = F(ψ₀)`, `τ(z) = L_F⁻¹(Γ(g, F(z)),
    z)` on `U(y) = U'(y) ∩ F⁻¹(U(x))`, and `𝐔(ψ₀) = τ(U(y))` (`ProperCoveringLocal.Data`,
    `ProperCoveringLocal.exists_data`, `Data.toChart`). `τ` is a continuous section of `s`, hence
    sc-smooth (`ProperCoveringLocal.isScSmoothOn_of_section`); `t ∘ τ` maps `U(y)` into `U(y')`
    because `U(y)` is connected and `F⁻¹(U(x))` is the disjoint union of the open `U(y'')`
    (`Data.tgt_τ_mem`, the counterpart of the text's claim that `ψ̂` maps `U(y)` onto `U(y')`); and
    `F = Γ(g, ·) ∘ F ∘ s` on `𝐔(ψ₀)` is the text's formula for (4). The finiteness of `F⁻¹(x)` and
    Definition 8.5.1 (1) (2017: 8.8) are not needed. Possible misprints in the proof (2017 p. 278): "there exists `g ∈
    G_y` for which `F(φ) = Γ(g, F(z))`" for `g ∈ G_x`, `Γ` being the natural representation of
    `G_x`; "`U(x)` is a `G_y`-invariant subset" for `G_x`-invariant; "`F(z') = s(F(φ))`" for
    `t(F(φ))`, with `φ : z → z'`; "admitting admitting". In the statement, (2) has "morphismsm" (p.
    277).

56. **Remark 8.5.4 (2017: 8.2)** *(pp. 385–387 (2017 pp. 277–278))*. (a) is `remark_8_5_4_a`: a morphism between points of `F⁻¹(x)` is
    mapped into `G_x` (`isotropyMor`). (b), "everything is determined by `U(x)`", is read as: two
    charts with the same `U(x)` have the same `Φ` and `Γ` on `U(x)` (on a connected `U(x)`, `Γ(g,
    ·)` is the continuous section of `s` through `g`, Chapter 7's `NaturalRep.Γ_eqOn`), the same
    `U(y)` and the same `𝐔(ψ₀)` (`remark_8_5_4_b`). Its remarks on the naturality of Theorem 7.1.13's (2017: 7.1)
    construction and on the main point of the proof have no further formal content.

57. **Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9) and the discussion after it** *(pp. 387–390 (2017 pp. 279–281))*. `Diff_sc` is `MPolyfoldCat`
    (bundled M-polyfolds of one universe) with the sc-diffeomorphisms `ScDiffeo` (Part I's
    `IsScDiffeoOn` on `univ`, with an inverse). The category `C` with one object is `SingleObj G`
    for a group `G`, its automorphism group, and `D` a Mathlib `Groupoid`, both in `Type`; then `C
    ₛ×_f D = G × D` (`coveringMap`, `IsCoveringFunctor`, `GeometricLift`). The finiteness of
    Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9) ("finitely many objects and morphisms") is not part of `IsCoveringFunctor` and
    `GeometricLift`; it is carried as the instance arguments `[Fintype D] [∀ a b, Fintype (a ⟶ b)]
    [Fintype G]` of the results that use it (Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3), Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6)). `D = ∅` is allowed, as
    in the text (`isCoveringFunctor_of_isEmpty`; item 59). In the discussion after the definition,
    `U(x) = L_C(⋆)` is `GeometricLift.Ux`, `τ(y)` is `GeometricLift.τy`, `φ_{yy'}(ψ) = L_D(ψ)` is
    `GeometricLift.φ`, with `φ_{yy''}(ψ ∘ γ) = φ_{y'y''}(ψ) ∘ φ_{yy'}(γ)` (`GeometricLift.φ_comp`,
    `GeometricLift.φ_id`, `GeometricLift.φ_inv_φ`); the actions of `G_y` on `U(y)` and of `G_x` on
    `U(x)` (`GeometricLift.smul_def`, `GeometricLift.smul_def'`, `GeometricLift.isScSmoothMap_smul`)
    and the equivariance `τ(y)(h ∗ z) = f(h) ∗ τ(y)(z)` (`GeometricLift.τ_equivariant`) are proved.
    Functoriality is stated with Mathlib's `γ ≫ ψ` for the text's `ψ ∘ γ`; `G_y` is Mathlib's monoid
    `End y`, with `h * k = k ≫ h`, the text's `h ∘ k`; the action of `G_x = G` on `U(x)` is a left
    action through the composition of `SingleObj G`.

58. **Disjoint unions of M-polyfolds** *(p. 390 (2017 p. 281), proof of Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3))* *(book 2021: unchanged, proof of Proposition 8.5.7, p. 390)*. "`Y = ⊔ U(y)` possesses
    a natural M-polyfold structure" is not described in the text; it is read as the structure whose
    charts are those of the summands, transported along `Sigma.mk i` (`MChart.pushforward`,
    `MPolyfold.sigmaChart`, `MPolyfold.sigma`). Charts of different summands have disjoint domains,
    and Part I's compatibility of charts then asks for the sc-smoothness of maps between empty
    retracts, which holds (`MChart.compatible_of_disjoint`), so no condition is added. The index
    type is arbitrary; paracompactness is proved summand by summand, without metrizability
    (`paracompactSpace_sigma`). The transported chart is extended by `0` off its image, so no
    summand needs to be nonempty. Sc-smoothness, local sc-diffeomorphisms, the degeneracy index and
    tameness are summand-wise (`MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_sigma_iff`,
    `MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeo_sigma_iff`, `MPolyfold.degIndex_sigma`,
    `MPolyfold.isTame_sigma_iff`); products distribute over the union
    (`MPolyfold.isScDiffeoOn_sigmaProdDistrib`), and `G × X ≅ ⊔_G X` for discrete `G`
    (`isScDiffeoOn_prod_discrete_sigma`).

59. **Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3): `D` nonempty, and the other readings** *(Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3), pp. 390–392 (2017 pp. 281–283))* *(book 2021: unchanged, Definition 8.5.5, p. 388, and Proposition 8.5.7, pp. 390–391)*.
    Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9) allows `D = ∅`: the map `ψ ↦ (f(ψ), s(ψ))` is then a bijection of empty sets
    (`isCoveringFunctor_of_isEmpty`). Then `Y = ∅` while `U(x)` is arbitrary, and `F` is surjective
    on objects (Definition 8.5.1 (1) (2017: 8.8)) only if `U(x) = ∅` (`geometricLiftFunctor_surjective_iff`). The
    text does not say so; `proposition_8_5_7` assumes `[Nonempty D]`, used for the surjectivity only.
    The hypothesis holds in Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6), where `D` is on `F⁻¹(x)` (`EpFunctor.nonempty_fiberCat`).
    Further readings: the finiteness of Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9) enters as instance arguments (finitely many
    morphisms make `t : 𝐘 → Y` proper, finitely many objects make the fibres finite, a finite `G`
    makes `G ⋉ U(x)` an ep-groupoid); `X = G_x ⋉ U(x)` is Chapter 7's action ep-groupoid
    (`EpGroupoid.Examples.actionEpGroupoid`), `G` with a discrete topology (an instance argument,
    satisfiable by `⊥`) and lifted by `ULift` to the universe of `U(x)`, since the translation
    groupoid takes its group and its space in one universe; `mor(y, y') × U(y)` is modelled as `⊔_{ψ
    : y → y'} U(y)` (item 58); the composition of `Y` is total, `(ψ, z') ∘ (γ, z) = (ψ ∘ γ, z)`,
    with a junk value off composable pairs. The "one verifies" is carried out: the composition is
    sc-smooth in the sheet form, the summand index of `σ(t ψ)` being locally constant
    (`GeometricLift.isScSmoothCompSheet_y`), and properness holds with `V = Y`, `t` being proper
    (`GeometricLift.isProperMap_yTgt`); Definition 8.5.1 (2) (2017: 8.8) holds with `U(x)` the whole object space
    of `X`. The text deduces that (8.16) is an sc-diffeomorphism from "bijection and local
    sc-diffeomorphism"; the sc-smoothness of the inverse is proved directly
    (`GeometricLift.fibredInv`, `GeometricLift.isScSmoothMap_fibredInv`). The proof's "the map `F :
    X → Y`" is read as `F : Y → X` (possible misprint).
    (2026-11-09) For `D = ∅` and `U(x) = ℝ` the proposition does not hold as we read it
    (`CoveringExamples.not_proposition_8_5_7_empty`, item 130).

60. **Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6): readings and possible misprints** *(Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6) and its proof, pp. 391–396 (2017 pp. 283–285))* *(book 2021: Theorem 8.5.8, pp. 392–393: "exists exists" and `A(ψ, z) = (f(z), F(z))` corrected; `τ(t)` unchanged)*. The
    theorem is stated for ep-groupoids whose objects and morphisms are in `Type`, since Definition
    8.5.5 (2017: 8.9) is (item 2). `C`, the full subcategory on `x`, is `SingleObj G_x`; `D` is the full
    subcategory on `F⁻¹(x)` (`GroupoidStr.FullOb`, `EpFunctor.FiberCat`), its finiteness, from
    Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8), entering as local instances (`EpFunctor.fintypeFiberCat`) and `D ≠ ∅` coming
    from the surjectivity of `F`. "A sufficiently small `U(x)` as in Theorem 8.5" is any chart of
    Theorem 8.5.3 (2017: 8.5) (a `ProperCoveringChart`); charts exist inside every open `V ∋ x` (part (b) of
    `theorem_8_5_8`), and part (c) holds for every chart. "A geometric lift `A : K → L`" is read as a
    geometric lift together with the proper covering functor `A` that Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) associates
    with it (`ProperCoveringChart.geometricLift`). The morphisms of `D` are the morphisms `ψ₀`
    themselves, so "`ψ : y → y'` where `ψ ∈ 𝐔(ψ₀)`" is read as `ψ = ψ₀`: `L_D(ψ₀) = t ∘ (s|𝐔(ψ₀))⁻¹`
    and `Ψ(ψ₀, z) = (s|𝐔(ψ₀))⁻¹(z)`. Both "one verifies" are carried out through `F`: on the sheets
    `F(σ_ψ(z)) = Γ(f(ψ), F(z))` (Theorem 8.5.3 (1), (4) (2017: 8.5)), so `τ(y') ∘ L_D(ψ) = Φ(f(ψ)) ∘ τ(y)`, and
    the functoriality of `L_D` follows from that of `Φ` and the injectivity of `F` on each `U(y)`;
    that `Ψ` preserves compositions and units uses the unique lifting of Definition 8.5.1 (3) (2017: 8.8). "Fully
    faithful open embedding" is `EpFunctor.IsFullyFaithfulOpenEmbedding`: full and faithful on the
    underlying groupoids, and an injective local sc-diffeomorphism on objects and on morphisms; "the
    image is the full subcategory on `U(x)`" is `range Φ.obj = U(x)` and `range Φ.mor = {φ | s(φ),
    t(φ) ∈ U(x)}` (`ProperCoveringChart.range_Φ_obj`, `ProperCoveringChart.range_Φ_mor`), and
    likewise for `Ψ` and `F⁻¹(U(x))`. Possible misprints: "there exists exists" (2017 p. 283); "`τ(t) :
    L_D(y) → L_C ∘ f(y)`" for `τ(y)` (2017 p. 284); "`A(ψ, z) = (f(z), F(z))`" for `(f(ψ), F(z))` (p.
    284), as in Proposition 8.5.7's (2017: 8.3) `F(ψ, z) = (f(ψ), τ(y)(z))`.

Found while formalizing Definition 8.5.9 (2017: 8.10) and Appendix 8.6 (2017 8.5) (2026-11-07).

70. **Definition 8.5.9 (2017: 8.10)** *(2017 p. 285)*. `EpStrongBundle.IsProperStrongBundleCovering EW EV F A`. `A` is
    taken in the functorial picture, as a strong bundle functor covering `F` (Definition 8.3.3 (2017: 8.6);
    equivalently its object map is a strong bundle map of Definition 8.3.2 (2017: 8.5), item 34). "A local strong
    bundle isomorphism" is: every `y` has open `U ∋ y` and `U'` with `A : W|U → V|U'` a strong
    bundle isomorphism covering `F : U → U'`; "`A : W|U(y) → V|U(x)` is a strong bundle isomorphism"
    is `StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleIsoOn` (`F : U(y) → U(x)` an sc-diffeomorphism and `A : P⁻¹(U(y))
    → Q⁻¹(U(x))` an sc-diffeomorphism on `[0]` and on `[1]`; the inverse is then linear on the
    fibres, `IsStrongBundleIsoOn.fiberEquiv`). The finiteness of `F⁻¹(x)` in (2) is that of
    Definition 8.5.1 (2) (2017: 8.8) and is not repeated. In (3) the text does not say which strong bundle
    structure `𝐕 ₛ×_A W → 𝐗 ₛ×_F Y` carries; it is read as the pull-back of `P : W → Y` along `pr₂ :
    𝐗 ₛ×_F Y → Y` (`EpFunctor.fibredSnd`), on Part I's fibred-product sub-M-polyfold. Its points
    `((φ, y), w)` with `P(w) = y` correspond to the text's `((φ, v), w)` with `v = A(w)`
    (`EpStrongBundle.fibredBundleEquiv`); under this correspondence the map of (3) is
    `EpStrongBundle.fibredLift` and the projection is the text's `((φ, v), w) ↦ (φ, P(w))`
    (`pullbackProj_fibredBundleEquiv`). "Strong bundle isomorphism" is
    `StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleIso`. The closing sentence, "all structural statements about proper
    covering functors between ep-groupoids lift to the strong bundle situation", is not formalized
    beyond §8.6.2 (2017 §8.5.2) (items 75, 113).

71. **§8.6.1 (2017 §8.5.1): cardinalities, and the classes indexed by their images in `|Y|`** *(2017 pp. 285–286)*.
    `mor(F⁻¹(x))` is `Y.morOn (F⁻¹(x))`, and `#` is the cardinality of finite sets (`Set.ncard`,
    `Nat.card`): the fibres are finite (Definition 8.5.1 (2) (2017: 8.8)), the isotropy groups are (Proposition
    7.1.12 (2017: 7.4)), hence so is `mor(F⁻¹(x))` (`IsProperCovering.finite_morOn_fiber`). The bijection
    `mor(F⁻¹(x)) → G_x × F⁻¹(x)` comes from Definition 8.5.1 (3) (2017: 8.8)
    (`IsProperCovering.bijective_fibredMap`, `IsProperCovering.existsUnique_lift`,
    `IsProperCovering.morOnFiberEquiv`). The isomorphism classes `Θ_1, …, Θ_q` of `F⁻¹(x)` are
    indexed by their images in `|Y|`: `Θ_c = F⁻¹(x) ∩ π⁻¹(c)` (`fiberClass`, `fiberIndex`,
    `fiberClasses`); the statements about `Θ_c` hold for every `c`, with `Θ_c = ∅` for `c ∉
    π(F⁻¹(x))`. With this indexing, the correspondence `Θ_j ↔ Θ'_j` of Lemma 8.6.2 (2017: 8.10) is "the same
    index" (item 73).

72. **Lemma 8.6.1 (2017: 8.9)** *(pp. 396–398 (2017 pp. 286–287))* *(book 2021: unchanged, proof of Lemma 8.6.1, now (8.24), p. 397)*. The set `{ψ ∈ mor(F⁻¹(x)) | s(ψ), t(ψ) ∈ Θ_j}` is `mor(Θ_j)`
    (`morOn_fiberClass_eq`); restricting the bijection of item 71 to (8.17) uses that `t(ψ) ∈ Θ_j`
    is automatic for `s(ψ) ∈ Θ_j` and `t(ψ) ∈ F⁻¹(x)` (`IsProperCovering.morOnClassEquiv`). The
    third claim divides by `#Θ_j ≥ 1` (`IsProperCovering.lemma_8_6_1`). (8.17) writes "`ψ → (Fψ),
    s(ψ))`", with an unbalanced parenthesis, for `ψ ↦ (F(ψ), s(ψ))` (possible misprint).

73. **Lemmas 8.6.2 and 8.6.3 (2017: 8.10 and 8.11)** *(2017 p. 287)* *(book 2021: unchanged, Lemmas 8.6.2, 8.6.3, p. 398; the citation now reads Lemma 8.6.2 for Lemma 8.6.1)*. For isomorphic `x, x'` the index sets agree
    (`IsProperCovering.fiberIndex_eq`), by the lifting of a morphism `x → x'` to morphisms out of
    `F⁻¹(x)` (Definition 8.5.1 (3) (2017: 8.8), `IsProperCovering.exists_isomorphic_of_isomorphic`);
    `IsProperCovering.lemma_8_6_2` states the correspondence by index,
    `IsProperCovering.lemma_8_6_2_equiv` as a bijection between the sets of classes. Lemma 8.6.3 (2017: 8.11)
    divides by `#G_{y₀} ≥ 1` (`IsProperCovering.lemma_8_6_3`,
    `IsProperCovering.ncard_fiber_eq_of_isomorphic`). Possible misprints: after Lemma 8.6.2 (2017: 8.10), "Using
    the third claim of Lemma 8.10, we infer that `#Θ_j = #G_x / #G_{y₀}`": Lemma 8.6.2 (2017: 8.10) has no third
    claim, and the third claim of Lemma 8.6.1 (2017: 8.9), `#G_x = #G_{y₀} · #Θ_j`, is meant; in Lemma 8.6.3 (2017: 8.11),
    `#F⁻¹(x) = ∑_{i=1}^q #Θ_j = ∑_{i=1}^q #Θ'_j` sums over `i` with summands indexed by `j`.

74. **Proposition 8.6.4 (2017: 8.4)** *(2017 p. 288)*. Only the local constancy of `x ↦ #F⁻¹(x)` is used
    (`IsProperCovering.eventually_ncard_fiber_eq`, `IsProperCovering.isLocallyConstant_ncard_fiber`:
    by Definition 8.5.1 (2) (2017: 8.8), `y ↦ (F|U(y))⁻¹(x')` is a bijection `F⁻¹(x) → F⁻¹(x')` for `x' ∈ U(x)`),
    not the text's "the structure of isomorphism classes stays the same". The function descends to
    `|X|` by Lemma 8.6.3 (2017: 8.11) (`IsProperCovering.fiberCardOrbit`), is locally constant there in the
    quotient topology (`IsProperCovering.isLocallyConstant_fiberCardOrbit`), hence constant on
    connected components (`IsProperCovering.proposition_8_6_4`). The text's `ℕ = {1, 2, …}` is Lean's
    `ℕ`, as the trivial ep-groupoid of the discrete M-polyfold (`EpGroupoid.trivial`,
    `discretePolyfold`); the values are `≥ 1` (`IsProperCovering.one_le_ncard_fiber`). The functor
    sends a morphism `φ` to the identity of `#F⁻¹(s φ) = #F⁻¹(t φ)`
    (`IsProperCovering.fiberCardFunctor`).

75. **§8.6.2 (2017 §8.5.2)** *(2017 pp. 288–289)*. `A(φ, w) = (F(φ), A_{s(φ)}(w))` is
    `IsProperStrongBundleCovering.mor_val`, and the `A_y` are topological linear isomorphisms by
    Definition 8.5.9 (1) (2017: 8.10) (`IsProperStrongBundleCovering.fiberEquiv`). The natural transformation `μ_Y
    → μ_X ∘ F` of functors into `Ban` is stated as its naturality identity `μ_X(F(φ)) ∘ A_{s(φ)} =
    A_{t(φ)} ∘ μ_Y(φ)` (`EpStrongBundle.section_8_5_2`), the fibres `Q⁻¹(F(s φ))` and `Q⁻¹(s(F φ))`
    being identified through their values in `V`; the category `Ban` is not formalized. Only the
    strong bundle functor part of Definition 8.5.9 (2017: 8.10) enters the identity
    (`IsStrongBundleFunctor.μ_comm`).

Found while checking that the hypotheses can hold (`NonVacuity.lean`, `NonVacuityBundle.lean` and
the witnesses of the other files, 2026-11-07; not in the text).

100. **Covering functors** (`CoveringExamples.isCoveringFunctor_id`,
     `CoveringExamples.not_isCoveringFunctor_one`). The identity of `SingleObj G` is a covering
     functor for every group `G`; for nontrivial `G` the functor sending every morphism to `1` is
     not, so Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9) is not vacuous in either direction. The empty groupoid gives a covering
     functor (`isCoveringFunctor_of_isEmpty`; item 59).

101. **A geometric lift, and Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) applied** (`CoveringExamples.reflectionLift`,
     `CoveringExamples.isProperCovering_reflectionLift`). `ℤ/2 = ℤˣ` acting on `ℝ`
     (`CoveringExamples.rCat`) by `y ↦ ±y` (`CoveringExamples.reflectionDiffeo`,
     `CoveringExamples.reflectionHom`) is a geometric lift of the identity of `SingleObj ℤˣ`, with
     `L_D = L_C` and `τ = 1`; Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) makes it a proper covering functor onto the
     translation groupoid `ℤ/2 ⋉ ℝ`, with non-trivial isotropy at `0`. Its fibres `F⁻¹(x)` have one
     point.

102. **Identities and trivial strong bundles** (`NonVacuityBundle.lean`). The identity functor of
     every ep-groupoid is a proper covering functor (`EpFunctor.isProperCovering_id`, with
     `EpFunctor.isScDiffeoOn_fibredMap_id`). Every strong bundle over an M-polyfold is a strong
     bundle over the trivial ep-groupoid of the M-polyfold, with `μ(z, w) = w`
     (`EpStrongBundle.trivial`, Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4)); the identity is a strong bundle map and a strong
     bundle functor (`EpStrongBundle.isMap_id`, `EpStrongBundle.isStrongBundleFunctor_id`,
     Definitions 8.3.2, 8.3.3 (2017: 8.5, 8.6)), and the identity of every strong bundle over an ep-groupoid is a proper
     strong bundle covering functor (`EpStrongBundle.isProperStrongBundleCovering_id`, with
     `EpStrongBundle.isStrongBundleIso_fibredLift_id` for (3), on the reading of item 70). Over the
     trivial ep-groupoid every section is functorial (`EpStrongBundle.isFunctorialSection_trivial`),
     so `Γ`, `Γ⁺`, `Fred` are Part I's sc-smooth, sc⁺- and sc-Fredholm sections
     (`EpStrongBundle.mem_sectionFunctors_trivial`,
     `EpStrongBundle.mem_plusSectionFunctors_trivial`,
     `EpStrongBundle.mem_fredholmSectionFunctors_trivial`). The witnesses use that maps of
     pull-backs `(z, y) ↦ (g(z), Φ(y))` are strong bundle maps
     (`StrongBundle.isStrongBundleMap_pullbackMap`).

103. **A strong bundle over an ep-groupoid in `Type`** (`TrivialBundle.epBundle`). Part I's trivial
     strong bundle `ℝⁿ × ℝᵏ → ℝⁿ` over the trivial ep-groupoid of `ℝⁿ`: its functorial picture is an
     ep-groupoid (`TrivialBundle.epBundleEpGroupoid`), its identity is a proper strong bundle
     covering functor (`TrivialBundle.epBundle_isProperStrongBundleCovering`,
     `TrivialBundle.epBundle_isMap_id`), `0 ∈ Γ⁺`
     (`TrivialBundle.fiberZero_mem_plusSectionFunctors_epBundle`), and for a `C^∞` map `φ : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ`
     the graph section `x ↦ (x, φ(x))` lies in `Γ` and in `Fred`
     (`TrivialBundle.graphSection_mem_sectionFunctors_epBundle`,
     `TrivialBundle.graphSection_mem_fredholmSectionFunctors_epBundle`, from Part I's results on
     graph sections, germ reading).

104. **Tangent witnesses** (`TangentTame.lean`, `TangentOrbit.lean`). The tangent of the trivial
     ep-groupoid of `ℝⁿ` is tame (`EpGroupoid.isTame_tangentEpGroupoid_trivial_rn`, Lemma 8.1.9 (2017: 8.8)), and
     the tangent of the trivial ep-groupoid of any M-polyfold has a paracompact orbit space
     (`EpGroupoid.hasParacompactOrbitSpace_tangent_trivial`, Theorem 8.1.15 (2017: 8.4)).

105. **Hypotheses check: every hypothesis is satisfiable; what the witnesses do not exercise**
     *(2026-11-07)*. (1) Tameness (Theorems 8.1.1, 8.1.12 (2017: 8.1, 8.3), Lemma 8.1.9 (2017: 8.8), the degeneracy remark) is
     existential, a tame atlas, as in Chapter 7 (Chapter 7, item 106); witnesses
     `EpGroupoid.isTame_trivial_rn`, `EpGroupoid.isTame_tangentEpGroupoid_trivial_rn`; the tame `X`,
     `Y` of `IsProperCovering.degIndex_prod_fibredMap` are satisfiable by the identity of the
     trivial ep-groupoid of `ℝⁿ` (not stated as a lemma). (2) `HasParacompactOrbitSpace` (Theorem
     8.1.15 (2017: 8.4)): `EpGroupoid.hasParacompactOrbitSpace_trivial`, item 104. (3) "A sufficiently small `U(x)`
     with the natural `G_x`-action" (Theorems 8.5.3, 8.5.8 (2017: 8.5, 8.6)) is a `ProperCoveringChart` datum; charts
     exist inside every open `V ∋ x` (`theorem_8_5_3`), so part (c) of `theorem_8_5_8`, which quantifies
     over all charts at `x`, is not vacuous; no hypothesis "for every `U(x)`" is made elsewhere. (4)
     Proper covering functors (Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8); Propositions 8.5.2, 8.6.4 (2017: 8.2, 8.4), Theorems 8.5.3, 8.5.8 (2017: 8.5, 8.6), Lemmas
     8.6.1–8.6.3 (2017: 8.9–8.11)): items 101, 102. (5) A covering functor with a geometric lift and `D` nonempty
     (Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3)): item 101. (6) Strong bundles over ep-groupoids, section functors and proper
     strong bundle covering functors (Definitions 8.3.1–8.3.4, 8.5.9 (2017: 8.4–8.7, 8.10), §8.6.2 (2017 §8.5.2)): items 102, 103. No
     hypothesis of the form "for all compatible charts" is made in Chapter 8. Not exercised: every
     proper covering functor constructed has one-point fibres `F⁻¹(x)` (identities, and the functor
     of item 101, whose `D` has one object), so the even coverings of Definitions 8.5.1 (2), 8.5.9 (2) (2017: 8.8, 8.10)
     are met with one sheet and the counting of Appendix 8.6 (2017 8.5) only with `q = 1`, `#Θ_1 = 1`; no
     proper strong bundle covering functor other than identities is constructed; `Γ⁺` is witnessed
     by the zero section only.

Not formalized (2026-11-07).

110. **Definitions 8.2.1, 8.2.2 (2017: 8.2, 8.3): sc-differential forms on ep-groupoids and the sc-de Rham complex**
     *(§8.2, pp. 368–375 (2017 pp. 268–270))* *(book 2021: Definitions 8.2.1, 8.2.2, pp. 372–373; both possible misprints unchanged)*. Not formalized. They need the Whitney sums `⊕^k TX` as M-polyfolds, the
     linear structure of `T_xX` (gap G.7), linear maps `Tφ` (gap G.70, item 112), the M-polyfolds
     `X^i` for `i ≥ 2` (gap G.6, closed since: Chapter 2, item 77) and the sc-differential forms, the Lie bracket and the exterior
     derivative of Part I's §4.4, which are not formalized either (gaps G.37–G.39; G.38 is closed since, Chapter 4, item 161); Stokes's theorem
     (gap G.40) is not used in §8.2. New gap G.74. Like Part I's §4.4 in `ch04.md`, the two
     definitions have no V-item. Possible misprints: Definition 8.2.1 (2017: 8.2) writes "`Tφ : T_xX → T_yY`" for
     `T_yX` (2017 p. 269), as in Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1) (item 10); in the argument that `dω` is compatible with
     morphisms (2017 p. 269), "`x = s(φ) ∈ U(x₀) ∩ X₁` and `y = t(φ₀)`" has `t(φ₀)` for `t(φ)`, the
     target of the morphism `φ` whose tangent `Tφ : T_xX → T_yX` follows.
     (2026-11-12) Formalized: `EpGroupoid.epForms` (Definition 8.2.1), `EP.epFormsInfty`, `EP.epFormsInftyD`,
     `EP.epDeRhamComplex` (Definition 8.2.2) (rows V8.53, V8.54; gap G.74 closed; item 132). The two places above
     (`T_yY` for `T_yX`, and `t(φ₀)` for `t(φ)`) are reading points; the formal statements use `T_yX` and `t(φ)`.

111. **Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1) as printed** *(Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1), p. 359 (2017 p. 259); the proof of Lemma 8.1.7 (2017: 8.6), p. 362 (2017 p. 262))*. The
     identification `T(𝐗 ₛ×ₜ 𝐗) = T𝐗 _{Ts}×_{Tt} T𝐗` and `m_{T𝐗} = Tm` on it are not formalized (new
     gap G.75). The sheet form (item 5) is what the proofs of Lemmas 8.1.2, 8.1.3 and 8.1.7 (2017: 8.1, 8.2 and 8.6) use, and

     nothing in the chapter depends on the gap.
     (2026-11-12) Formalized as printed (item 131; row V8.4, same; gap G.75 closed).

112. **Gap G.70 in part: `Tφ` well defined and functorial** *(Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1), pp. 364 ff. (2017 pp. 264–265); Chapter 7,
     Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4))*. Chapter 7 left all properties of `tangentMor` unformalized (Chapter 7, item
     110; gap G.70). Now formalized: `Tφ` is well defined, `Tφ(Ts(h)) = Tt(h)` for every `h ∈ T_φ𝐗`
     (`tangentMor_tSrc`), and functorial, `T(ψ ∘ φ) = Tψ ∘ Tφ` for `φ ∈ 𝐗₁` (`tangentMor_comp`), and
     the pairs `(Tφ, a)` of Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1) describe `T𝐗` (item 10). Still not formalized: that `Tφ` is
     bijective and linear (the linearity needs gap G.7), that `Tφ = Tφ̂(s(φ))`, a bounded linear
     isomorphism on level `0` and an sc-operator for smooth `φ`. A dated sentence is added to G.70.
     (2026-11-09) Now also formalized: `Tφ` is a bijection with inverse `T(φ⁻¹)`, `Tφ = Tφ̂(s(φ))`, and a bounded linear
     isomorphism on level `0` in charts (Chapter 7, item 110). Still open: the linearity on `T_xX` itself and the
     sc-operator property (gaps G.7, G.70).
     (2026-11-09) Now also formalized: the linearity on `T_xX` itself and the sc-isomorphism for smooth `φ` (Chapter 7,
     item 154). Gaps G.7 and G.70 closed.

113. **Not formalized, without a gap** *(pp. 364–400 (2017 pp. 264–289))*. Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1): the M-polyfold structure

Found while formalizing the additions of the 2021 edition (2026-11-08). Items 115–124: Propositions 8.1.16, 8.1.17 and
Definition 8.4.2 (`Chapter8/TangentZhou.lean`), Definition 8.3.5, Proposition 8.4.1, Example 8.5.6, the 2021 form of
Definition 8.5.9 and Lemma 8.5.10 (`Chapter8/Book2021.lean`), Proposition 8.2.3, not formalized, and Proposition 8.1.17 (2)
for every `(TX)^i` (item 124, `Chapter8/TangentZhouLevels.lean`); comparison items V8.44–V8.52.

115. **Proposition 8.1.16: the step from the tangent of `k` to that of `g` is a hypothesis** *(Proposition 8.1.16, p. 369,
     new in the 2021 edition)*. An isotropy element `k` of a smooth point of `TX` lies over an isotropy element `g` of a smooth
     point of `X`. The proof passes from "the tangent of `k` is the identity" to `Tg = id` by differentiating (8.16) and using
     that `Tτ` is onto; this needs the second tangent bundle `T(TX)`, which is not formalized, and is the hypothesis
     `TangentZhouReflect`, satisfied by the trivial ep-groupoid (`tangentZhouReflect_trivial`) (gap G.88, which stays open for
     this step after item 124). The rest is proved:
     `g ∈ T_x` by (ZHOU) for `X`, so `s = t` near `g` and `Ts = Tt` near `k` (`mem_nonEffectivePart_tangent`,
     `proposition_8_1_16`, `Examples.proposition_8_1_16_point`). As in Chapter 7 (item 135), the tangent of an
     isotropy element is a map of sets, and no linear structure is used.
     (2026-11-09) `TangentZhouReflect` is proved for every ep-groupoid, through the vertical vectors of `T(TX)`
     (`tangentZhouReflect`, item 126; gap G.88 closed).

116. **Proposition 8.1.17: the hypotheses of Theorem 7.6.7; (2) only for `(TX)⁰`** *(Proposition 8.1.17, p. 371, new in the
     2021 edition)*. (1) is proved through `(T𝐗)^T = p⁻¹((𝐗¹)^T)` (`nonEffectivePart_tangent_eq`): `⊆` because `p : T𝐗 → 𝐗¹` is
     open, `⊇` through Theorem 7.6.7's `(𝐗¹)^T = (𝐗^T)¹` and the last step of Proposition 8.1.16; then `(T𝐗)^T` is closed and
     Proposition 7.2.21 gives LUC for `TX` (`proposition_8_1_17_one`). The proof uses, as Theorem 7.6.7 does (Chapter 7,
     item 131), that `U(x) ∩ X₁` is connected in `X¹` and dense in `U(x)` (`HasConnectedDenseLevelOneReps`; the density is gap
     G.73), and the openness of `p` (gap G.8); both are hypotheses, satisfied by the point
     (`isOpenMap_tangentProj_of_subsingleton`, `Examples.proposition_8_1_17_one_point`). (2), (SLUC) for `X` gives (SLUC)
     for `TX`, is proved for `(TX)⁰ = TX` (`proposition_8_1_17_two`); for `i ≥ 1` it needs `(TX)^i = T(X^i)`, which was
     not formalized in the first pass (gap G.88). Since `TangentZhouLevels.lean`, (2) is proved for every `i` (item 124; gap
     G.88 closed for (2)).
     (2026-11-09) Both hypotheses are theorems (Chapter 7, item 153; Chapter 2, item 86), so (1) and (2) hold with no
     added hypothesis (`proposition_8_1_17_one_of_isLUC`, `EP.proposition_8_1_17_two_of_isSLUC`). Status:
     **settled**.

117. **Definition 8.3.5: readings** *(Definition 8.3.5, p. 379, new in the 2021 edition)*. The first three conditions are
     Part I's auxiliary norm on the underlying strong bundle, so `N` lives on its level-one space `W_{0,1}`, and its values
     in `[0, ∞)` follow from (1). In the invariance (3), `h ∈ W_{0,1}` is given and `h = μ(φ, k)` is an equation in `W`; (3) is
     not vacuous, since `μ` maps `𝐗 ₛ×_P W_{0,1}` into `W_{0,1}` (`EpStrongBundle.IsAuxNorm`,
     `EpStrongBundle.exists_oneVal_eq_μ`). Over the trivial ep-groupoid every auxiliary norm of Part I is one, and the
     product bundle `ℝⁿ × ℝᵏ → ℝⁿ` has one (`EpStrongBundle.exists_isAuxNorm_trivial`, `TrivialBundle.exists_isAuxNorm_epBundle`).

118. **Proposition 8.4.1: (2) ⇒ (1) by metrizability; the other implications not formalized** *(Proposition 8.4.1, p. 380,
     new in the 2021 edition)*. The zero section is compatible with `μ` and induces a continuous map `|0| : |X| → |W[0]|` with
     left inverse `|P|`, a topological embedding (`EpStrongBundle.zeroOrbitMap`, `EpStrongBundle.isEmbedding_zeroOrbitMap`).
     The text concludes from the closedness of the image; the formalization from metrizability: a paracompact `|W[0]|` is
     metrizable (Theorem 7.3.1 and Smirnov's theorem), so its subspace `|X|` is metrizable and hence paracompact
     (`EpStrongBundle.proposition_8_4_1_two_imp_one`). (1) ⇒ (2), (3) needs `G_x`-equivariant bundle charts with
     invariant metrics, and `W[1]` as an ep-groupoid, which the project does not build (gap G.86).
     (2026-11-09) (1) ⇒ (2) is proved (`proposition_8_4_1_one_iff_two`, item 127); (3) remains open (gap G.86).
     (2026-11-12) (3) is proved as well (`proposition_8_4_1`, item 133; gap G.86 closed).

119. **Definition 8.4.2: "strong bundle isomorphism `B`"; Proposition 8.4.3 not formalized** *(Definition 8.4.2 and
     Proposition 8.4.3, p. 382, new in the 2021 edition)*. `G_x` acts on `W|U(x)` by the natural lift `g * w = μ(Γ(g, P(w)), w)`
     (`EpStrongBundle.natLift`). "Strong bundle isomorphism `B : W|U(x) → W|U(x)`" is read as a strong bundle map `W → W` that
     is a strong bundle isomorphism over `U(x)` in Part I's sense (`StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleIsoOn`), as for Definition
     8.5.9 (item 70), and `|B(w)| = |w|` as equality of orbits (`EpStrongBundle.IsLR`). Every strong bundle over a trivial
     ep-groupoid has the property (`EpStrongBundle.isLR_trivial`). Proposition 8.4.3, which gives the property to every strong
     bundle over an effective `X` with Chapter 7's (LR) (Definition 7.4.19), needs among other things the openness of
     `P : W → X`; it is not formalized (gap G.86).
     (2026-11-09) Proposition 8.4.3 is proved with the text's hypotheses (`EpStrongBundle.proposition_8_4_3`, item
     128).

120. **Example 8.5.6, as stated** *(the remark after Definition 8.5.5 and Example 8.5.6, p. 388, new in the 2021 edition)*.
     For a covering functor `f : D → C` the restriction `G_d → G_{f(d)}` is injective (`IsCoveringFunctor.injective_map_end`);
     the example shows that it need not be onto. Formalized with `D` the groupoid with two objects and one morphism between
     any two, `C` the group `ℤˣ = {1, ε}`, `ε = −1`, and `f` sending both non-identity morphisms to `ε`: `f` is a covering
     functor, the `G_d` are trivial and `G_x = ℤˣ` is not (`Example856D`, `example856Functor`, `example_8_5_6`).

121. **Definition 8.5.9, condition (0): contained in the reading of item 70** *(Definition 8.5.9, p. 394 (2017: 8.10, p. 285),
     condition (0) new in the 2021 edition)*. The 2021 text adds (0), `τ(F(ψ), A(w)) = A(μ(ψ, w))`, the strong bundle map
     property (Definition 8.3.2 (2017: 8.5)) of the object map `A`. Item 70 read the 2017 phrase "strong bundle map `A`" as a
     strong bundle functor, which contains (0); with (0) stated for the object map, the 2021 definition is equivalent to that
     reading (`EpStrongBundle.IsProperStrongBundleCovering2021`, `EpStrongBundle.isProperStrongBundleCovering2021_iff`), and
     the identity of a strong bundle satisfies it (`EpStrongBundle.isProperStrongBundleCovering2021_id`).

122. **Lemma 8.5.10: readings; `F*V` as a strong bundle over `Y` is not proved** *(Lemma 8.5.10, p. 395, new in the 2021
     edition)*. "Strong bundle isomorphism over the ep-groupoid `Y`" is read as a strong bundle isomorphism `B(w) = (P(w),
     A(w))` of `W` onto Part I's pull-back `F*V`, covering the identity, with (8.23) for `μ_{F*V}(φ, (y, v)) = (t(φ), μ_X(F(φ),
     v))` (`EpStrongBundle.pullbackμ`); (8.23) is condition (0) (item 121). On the fibre over `y`, `A` is the linear isomorphism
     of a local strong bundle isomorphism of Definition 8.5.9 (1), so `B` is bijective; near every point `B⁻¹(y, v) = Ψ(v)` for
     the inverse `Ψ` of such a local isomorphism, so `B⁻¹` is a strong bundle map
     (`EpStrongBundle.IsProperStrongBundleCovering2021.bijective_bundleB`,
     `EpStrongBundle.IsProperStrongBundleCovering2021.bundleBInv_eq_of`,
     `EpStrongBundle.IsProperStrongBundleCovering2021.lemma_8_5_10`). That `μ_{F*V}` makes `F*V` a strong bundle over the
     ep-groupoid `Y` is not proved; the lemma uses only its formula (gap G.89).
     (2026-11-09) `F*V` is a strong bundle over `Y`, and `B`, `B⁻¹` are maps over `Y` (`lemma_8_5_10_full`, item 129;
     gap G.89 closed).

123. **Proposition 8.2.3, the Poincaré lemma, is not formalized** *(Proposition 8.2.3, p. 373, new in the 2021 edition)*.
     Every object has saturated open neighbourhoods `V ⊆ U` such that every closed sc-differential form on `U` in the sense of
     §8.2 has a primitive on `V`; the proof adapts Part I's Lemma 4.4.8 (p. 199, new in the 2021 edition) on the object M-polyfold and averages
     the primitive over `G_x`. The forms of §8.2 are not formalized (gap G.74), so neither is the proposition (gap G.87).
     (2026-11-12) Formalized as printed, with no added hypothesis: `EP.proposition_8_2_3` (row V8.55; gap G.87 closed;
     item 132). Status: **settled**.
124. **Proposition 8.1.17 (2) for every `(TX)^i`: "naturally `(TX)^i = T(X^i)`" through source and target** *(Proposition
     8.1.17 (2), p. 371, new in the 2021 edition)*. The proof applies (1) to every `X^i`, which needs LUC for `(X^i)¹ = X^{i+1}`
     from (SLUC) and gives LUC for `T(X^i)` (`EP.isLUC_tangent_lift`), and then identifies `T(X^i)` with `(TX)^i`. The
     identification is read as an equivalence of ep-groupoids in a weak sense: sc-diffeomorphisms of the object and of the
     morphism M-polyfolds commuting with `s` and `t` (`EpGroupoid.EpEquiv`). It maps `𝐗^T` onto `𝐗'^T`
     (`EpEquiv.nonEffectivePart_eq`), so it carries LUC by Proposition 7.2.21 (`EpEquiv.isLUC`). Part I's Proposition 2.3.17 for
     `i = 1`, on objects and morphisms, gives `T(X¹) ≅ (TX)¹` (`tangentShiftEpEquiv`), and recursion with the index raises gives
     `T(X^i) ≅ (TX)^i` for every `i` (`EP.tangentLiftEpEquiv`), as `BundledMPolyfold.tangentLiftEquiv` does for M-polyfolds
     (Chapter 2). Hence `TX` has (SLUC) (`EP.proposition_8_1_17_two_all`) under the hypotheses of (1) on every `X^i`
     (item 116), which the point ep-groupoid and its lifts satisfy (`Examples.proposition_8_1_17_two_all_pointEP`). Not
     formalized: the compatibility of the equivalence with unit, inverse and composition, not needed for LUC, and its
     linearity on the fibres (gap G.7). Status: **settled**; gap G.88 closed for (2), open for Proposition 8.1.16 (item 115).
     (2026-11-09) The hypotheses of (1) on every `X^i` are theorems, so (SLUC) for `X` is the only hypothesis
     (`EP.proposition_8_1_17_two_all_of_isSLUC`; Chapter 7, item 153).
     (2026-11-09) `T_xX` now carries the linear structure of Definition 2.3.14, Banach through every chart and sc at
     smooth points (gap G.7 closed, Chapter 2, item 87); this statement is not restated with it.

Follow-ups (2026-11-09).

125. **Theorem 8.5.8 in every universe** *(Definition 8.5.5, p. 388, Proposition 8.5.7, p. 390, Theorem 8.5.8, p. 392
     (2017: Definition 8.9, Proposition 8.3, Theorem 8.6); items 2, 60; round-trip item V8.36)*. Definition 8.5.5
     (`IsCoveringFunctor`, `GeometricLift`, `Chapter8/Basic.lean`) now takes `D`, `G` and `Diff_sc` in one universe
     `u`, and Proposition 8.5.7 (`proposition_8_5_7`) and Theorem 8.5.8 (`EpFunctor.theorem_8_5_8`,
     `Chapter8/GeometricLift.lean`) hold for ep-groupoids `X`, `Y` whose objects and morphisms lie in any one
     universe; no proof changed. Witness in every universe: `CoveringExamples.theorem_8_5_8_id` (the identity functor of
     any ep-groupoid, `Chapter8/NonVacuity.lean`). `X` and `Y` share the universe because `L_D` and `L_C` take values
     in one category `Diff_sc`; different universes would need lifted carriers. Status: **settled** (the restriction
     of item 2 to `Type` is removed).

126. **Proposition 8.1.16 without the added hypothesis: `TangentZhouReflect` holds for every ep-groupoid (gap G.88
     closed)** *(Proposition 8.1.16, p. 369, new in the 2021 edition; items 115, 124)* (2026-11-09).
     `Polyfold/Chapter8/TangentVertical2021.lean`, `TangentZhouReflect2021.lean`. The vertical vectors of `T(TX)` are
     built in a chart of `TX` (`MPolyfold.vert`, `vertChart`); they are injective (`vert_injective`) and natural,
     `T(Tf)(vert_α w) = vert_{Tf(α)}(Tf(w))` (`tangentMap_tangentMap_vert`). The step of item 115 follows: for `v ∈
     T_xX` take `u` with `Ts(u) = v` and the vertical vector `V` at `k` over `u`; then `T(Ts)V` and `T(Tt)V` are the
     vertical vectors over `v` and over `Tt(u)`, and the tangent of `k` being the identity gives `Tt(u) = v`, that is
     `Tg(v) = v` (`tangentZhouReflect`). Only the vertical directions, on which the tangent of `k` acts as `Tg`, are
     used, and not the surjectivity of `Tτ` of the text's proof. `proposition_8_1_16_2021` takes (ZHOU) for `X` only.
     Status: **settled** (row V8.44, now "same"; gap G.88 closed).

127. **Proposition 8.4.1: (1) ⇔ (2) (gap G.86 narrowed to (3))** *(Proposition 8.4.1, p. 380, new in the 2021 edition;
     Theorem 8.1.15; Lemma 7.3.2; item 118)* (2026-11-09). `Polyfold/Chapter8/BundleOrbitParacompact2021.lean`. (1) ⇒
     (2) follows Theorem 8.1.15, as `TangentOrbit.lean` does for `TX`. `G_x` acts on `W|U(x)` by homeomorphisms through
     the natural lift `g * w = μ(Γ(g, P w), w)` (`bundleMulAction`); orbits in `W|U(x)` are `G_x`-orbits
     (`π_eq_π_iff_exists_smul`); and `G_x\W|U(x) → |W|` is an open embedding onto `|P|⁻¹(|U(x)|)`
     (`isOpenEmbedding_bundleOrbitQuotientMap`, `range_bundleOrbitQuotientMap`), metrizable by the quotient metric of
     Lemma 7.3.2 (`metrizableSpace_orbitRel_quotient_finite`). With `|X|` metrizable (Theorem 7.3.1), Smirnov's theorem
     pulled back along `|P| : |W| → |X|` makes `|W[0]|` metrizable (`metrizableSpace_orbitSpace`,
     `proposition_8_4_1_one_imp_two`, `proposition_8_4_1_one_iff_two`). The text's invariant metrics and closed covers
     are not needed, only the continuity of `μ`. (3) is not stated, since `W[1]` is not built as an ep-groupoid: that
     needs the level-one bundles and `μ` as a local sc-diffeomorphism at level one; once `W[1]` exists the same proof
     applies. Status: **settled** for (1) ⇔ (2); (3) open (row V8.47; gap G.86).
     (2026-11-12) (3) is proved, with `|W[1]|` an orbit space (item 133). Status: **settled** (row V8.47, restated;
     gap G.86 closed).

128. **Proposition 8.4.3 (row V8.48)** *(Definition 8.4.2 and Proposition 8.4.3, p. 382, new in the 2021 edition; item
     119)* (2026-11-09). `Polyfold/Chapter8/BundleLocalRegularity2021.lean`. `EpStrongBundle.proposition_8_4_3`: an
     effective `X` with (LR) gives (LR) for every strong bundle over `X`, with the text's hypotheses only. The proof
     uses the `U(x)` of (LR) for `X`. At a regular object a morphism is determined by its source and target
     (`EpGroupoid.eq_of_isRegular_src`), so over a regular `P(w)` the morphism underlying `w → Φ(w)` is `Γ(g, P(w))`
     and `Φ(w) = g * w` (`exists_mor_of_π_eq`). Regular points are dense (Proposition 7.2.4) and `P` is open
     (`StrongBundle.isOpenMap_proj`), so the closed set where `Φ = g * ·` is all of `W|U(x)`. The text's auxiliary
     `g_w` and the uniqueness of `g` are not needed; effectiveness enters only through the density of regular points.
     Status: **settled** (row V8.48).

129. **Lemma 8.5.10: `F*V` is a strong bundle over `Y` (gap G.89 closed)** *(Lemma 8.5.10, p. 395, new in the 2021
     edition; items 121, 122)* (2026-11-09). `Polyfold/Chapter8/PullbackStrongBundle2021.lean`.
     `EpStrongBundle.pullbackBundle2021`: `(F*Q, μ_{F*V})` satisfies Definition 8.3.1 for every sc-smooth `F`; it is
     Chapter 10's `EpStrongBundle.pullbackAlong`, with structure map `pullbackμ` (`pullbackBundle2021_μ`). `B` and
     `B⁻¹` are strong bundle maps over ep-groupoids in the sense of Definition 8.3.2, covering the identity functor of
     `Y` (`isMap_bundleB`, `isMap_bundleBInv`), and `lemma_8_5_10_full` collects them with the inverse laws and `A = Ā
     ∘ B`. Status: **settled** (row V8.51; gap G.89 closed).

130. **Proposition 8.5.7 for `D = ∅` does not hold as we read it** *(Definition 8.5.5, p. 388, and Proposition 8.5.7,
     p. 390 (2017: 8.9, 8.3); item 59)* (2026-11-09). `Polyfold/Chapter8/GeometricLiftEmpty2021.lean`. Definition 8.5.5
     does not exclude `D = ∅`; then the functor `F` has empty domain and is not surjective on objects when `U(x) ≠ ∅`.
     `CoveringExamples.not_proposition_8_5_7_empty` is a Lean counterexample with `D = ∅` and `U(x) = ℝ`. Item 59
     recorded "`D` nonempty" as a hidden hypothesis; the counterexample shows that the narrowing of row V8.35 is
     necessary. The hypothesis holds where the proposition is used (Theorem 8.5.8), so nothing later is affected.
     Status: **settled**; for `D = ∅` the proposition does not hold as we read it.
