131. **Lemma 8.1.2 as printed and the M-polyfold of pairs of Remark 8.1.10 (gap G.75 closed)** *(Lemma 8.1.2, p.
     359 (2017: 8.1, p. 259); Remark 8.1.10, pp. 364–365 (2017: 8.1); items 5, 10, 111, 113)* (2026-11-12). `𝐗 ₛ×ₜ 𝐗`
     is the sub-M-polyfold `compPolyfold` of Definition 7.1.3 (4). The identification `v ↦ (Tπ₁ v, Tπ₂ v)`
     (`tangentCompPairs`) is injective with range `{(k, h) | Ts(k) = Tt(h)}` and is an sc-diffeomorphism onto the
     sub-M-polyfold `T𝐗 _{Ts}×_{Tt} T𝐗` of `T𝐗 × T𝐗` (`isScDiffeoOn_tangentCompPairs`); `Tm(v) = Tπ₁(v) ∘ Tπ₂(v)`
     (`lemma_8_1_2_tangentMul`), `k ∘ h = Tm(v)` for the one `v` over `(k, h)` (`lemma_8_1_2_book`), and `m_{T𝐗} = Tm`
     (`lemma_8_1_2_compMul`). Reading point: the proof does not differentiate `s(m(F(φ'), φ')) = s(φ')` as the text
     does; it uses that `π₂ : 𝐗 ₛ×ₜ 𝐗 → 𝐗` is a local sc-diffeomorphism (`isLocalScDiffeo_compSnd`), so a tangent
     vector of the fibred product is determined by its base point and `Tπ₂` (`MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeo_of_comp_eq`).
     For Remark 8.1.10, the M-polyfold structure on the pairs is the natural one of the fibred product
     `𝐗¹ _{s}×_{p} TX` (Proposition 2.5.20; `tangentPairsPolyfold`), and `G` (`remarkGInto`) is an sc-diffeomorphism
     for it (`remark_8_1_10_scDiffeo`); the triples `(Ts h, φ, Tt h)` are injective with range
     `{(a, φ, b) | φ ∈ 𝐗₁, a ∈ T_{s(φ)}X, b = Tφ(a)}` and compatible with the compositions (`remark_8_1_10_triples`).
     The first entry of `G` stays labelled by `φ` (item 10). Status: **settled** (rows V8.4, same; V8.12, narrower for
     the bare-map reading).

132. **§8.2: forms on ep-groupoids, the sc-de Rham complex and the Poincaré lemma (gaps G.74, G.87 closed)**
     *(Definitions 8.2.1, 8.2.2, pp. 372–373 (2017: 8.2, 8.3, pp. 268–270); Proposition 8.2.3, pp. 373–374, new in the
     2021 edition; items 110, 123)* (2026-11-12). `Ωᵏ_ep(X)` is `EpGroupoid.epForms`: Part I's sc-differential forms
     of the object M-polyfold (Definition 4.4.1) with `(Tφ)^*ω_y = ω_x` for every `φ ∈ 𝐗₁`, `Tφ` the bounded linear
     isomorphism `tangentMorCLE` (`IsMorCompatible`), equivalently `s^*ω = t^*ω` (`isMorCompatible_iff_formPullback`).
     `Ω*_{ep,∞}(X)` is the direct limit over the index lifts (`EP.epFormsInfty`, `Module.DirectLimit`), with
     `d[ω] = [dω]`, `d ∘ d = 0` and the complex `EP.epDeRhamComplex`, a subcomplex of Part I's complex of the object
     M-polyfold (`epFormsInftyToObj`, injective). Proposition 8.2.3 is `EP.proposition_8_2_3`, as printed, with no
     added hypothesis. Reading points: (a) the Whitney sum `⊕ᵏ TX` is read, as in Part I's §4.4, as families of
     alternating maps on the tangent spaces of level-one points; (b) the compatibility of `dω` with morphisms is
     proved by the naturality of `d` for the global maps `s, t`, where the text uses `f = t ∘ (s|U(φ₀))⁻¹`; (c) in
     Proposition 8.2.3, `Ω_{ep,∞}(U)` is that of the restriction `X|U` (Proposition 7.1.22) as an object of `EP`
     (`EP.sub`), 'on `V`' is the pull-back by the inclusion functor `X|V → X|U` (`EP.subIncl`), the text's `k ≥ 1` is
     written `k + 1`, and the statement also holds inside any saturated open `U ∋ x` given in advance
     (`EP.proposition_8_2_3_of_isOpen`); (d) the text's extension `σ(y) = ψ^*τ'(x')` is the push-forward of §11.2
     along the equivalence `G_x ⋉ U(x) → X|π⁻¹(π(U(x)))` (`EP.isEquivalence_modelFunctor`), and the average over `G_x`
     is taken on the translation groupoid of a natural representation (`NaturalRep.exists_primitive_translation`), so
     the proof lives in `Chapter11/GapP2_B2_Poincare.lean`. Beyond the text of §8.2: the pull-back by sc-smooth
     functors commutes with `d` and is invariant under natural equivalence (`EP.epFormsInftyPullback`,
     `epFormsInftyPullback_eq_of_natTrans`). The wedge product makes `Ω*_{ep,∞}(X)` a differential graded subalgebra
     of Part I's `Ω*_∞(Ob X)` (`Chapter11/GapP2_B2_EpWedge.lean`); the graded-algebra instances on the type itself are
     not built (§8.2 does not use a product). Status: **settled** (rows V8.53–V8.55, same).

133. **Proposition 8.4.1 (3): `|W[1]|` as an orbit space (gap G.86 closed)** *(Proposition 8.4.1, p. 380, new in
     the 2021 edition; items 118, 127)* (2026-11-12). `EpStrongBundle.proposition_8_4_1`: `|X|`, `|W[0]|` and `|W[1]|`
     are paracompact together (`List.TFAE`), with no added hypothesis. Reading point: the project does not build
     `W[1]` as an ep-groupoid; `|W[1]|` is defined directly as the orbit space of the groupoid `(W[1], 𝐗 ₛ×_P W[1])`,
     the M-polyfold `W[1]` modulo `w ∼ μ(φ, w)`, with the quotient topology (`OrbitSpaceOne`, `πOne_eq_πOne_iff`),
     which is all the statement uses. (1) ⇒ (3) follows (1) ⇒ (2) (item 127): `G_x` acts on `W[1]|U(x)` by
     homeomorphisms, from the sc-smoothness of `μ` at level one (`continuous_bundleOneSmul`), `W[1] → |W[1]|` is open
     (`isOpenMap_πOne`), `G_x\W[1]|U(x) → |W[1]|` is an open embedding onto `|P[1]|⁻¹(|U(x)|)`, and Smirnov's theorem
     pulled back along `|P[1]|` gives metrizability (`metrizableSpace_orbitSpaceOne`). (3) ⇒ (1) is the text's:
     `|0| : |X| → |W[1]|` is a closed embedding (`isClosedEmbedding_zeroOrbitMapOne`). Status: **settled** (row V8.47,
     restated).

## Chapter 9 (Branched ep⁺-subgroupoids; Lean `Polyfold/Chapter9/`)

*Numbering.* The items of this section are numbered in blocks, one block per part of the chapter, so that agents
working at the same time do not collide; the gaps in the numbering are unused numbers, not deleted items. 1–19:
§9.1, Definition 9.1.2 to Proposition 9.1.12 (2017: Definition 9.1 to Proposition 9.2; `Chapter9/Basic.lean`,
`Symmetric.lean`, `Propositions.lean`); 20–39: §9.2 up to Definition 9.2.12 (2017: 9.6), good points, the
tangent section and the tangent (`GoodPoints.lean`, `Tangent.lean`, `TangentSlicesBasic.lean`,
`TangentSlicesRn.lean`, `TangentSlices.lean`); 40–49: §9.2 from Lemma 9.2.13 (2017: 9.9), the boundary
(`BoundaryPosition.lean`, `BoundaryPositionConverse.lean`, `Boundary.lean`); 50–69: §9.3, orientations
(`Orientation.lean` and the `Orientation*.lean` files); 70–79: §9.4, the geometry of branching
(`BranchingGeometryMeasure.lean`, `BranchingGeometryManifold.lean`, `BranchingGeometry.lean`); 80–89: §9.5,
measure zero, σ-algebras and isotropy factors (`Measure.lean`, `MeasureEffective.lean`); 90–99: Appendix §9.6.1
(`Appendix.lean`, `AppendixSlices.lean`); 100–109: witnesses and the hypotheses taken in general. Part II has no
2014 preprint: statement numbers and pages are those of the Springer edition (2021, pp. 401–458), with the 2017
text's in parentheses (2017 pp. 291–332); Part I results are cited by their 2021 numbers with the preprint's in
parentheses. The comparison items are `Exposition/verification/ch09.md` (V9.1–V9.62); the gaps are G.93–G.110.

Found while formalizing §9.1 (2026-11-08).

1. **Definition 9.1.2: functors to ℚ, paracompactness and properness** *(Definition 9.1.2, p. 402 (2017:
   Definition 9.1, p. 292))*. A functor `Θ : X → ℚ⁺` is a function on objects with `Θ(s φ) = Θ(t φ)`
   (`EpGroupoid.IsFunctorial`), with values in `ℚ` and `Θ ≥ 0` a field of `IsBranchedEpSubgroupoid`; `supp`,
   `orbitSupp`. "The topology induced on `|supp(Θ)|` is paracompact" is a `ParacompactSpace` instance on the
   subtype, and "the inclusion `Mᵢ → U(x)` is proper" is `IsProperMap` of the inclusion of subtypes, automatic
   for `Mᵢ` closed in `U(x)` (`isProperMap_inclusion_iff`). Witnesses: the zero functor
   (`isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_zero`) and the indicator of a smooth point of `ℝⁿ`
   (`rnPolyfold_isSmoothSubmanifold_singleton`, `localBranchingStructure_indicator`,
   `isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_indicator`). The 2017 text refers in (4) to "(ii) and (iii)" for (2) and (3)
   (possible misprint, corrected in 2021). Status: **settled**.

2. **The dimension of a submanifold, in a chart; Remark 9.1.1 as a hypothesis** *(Remark 9.1.1, p. 402 (2017:
   Remark 9.1, p. 291))*. `T_mM` is a set of tangent vectors (gap G.7), so the dimension is measured in a chart
   (`MPolyfold.HasDimAt`): it does not depend on the chart or the presentation (`finrank_span_tangentSpace_eq`,
   `finrank_tangentSpace_chart_change`, `HasDimAt.finrank_eq`), is unique (`HasDimAt.unique`), exists
   (`IsSmoothSubmanifold.exists_hasDimAt`), and is invariant under restriction to open sets and
   sc-diffeomorphisms (`hasDimAt_inter_isOpen_iff`, `hasDimAt_image_iff`). The local constancy stated in the
   remark needs level-0 calculus of Part I that the project lacks; it is the hypothesis
   `HasLocallyConstantDimAt`, proved on `ℝᵐ` (`hasLocallyConstantDimAt_rn`: `T_yM` is the range of the
   idempotent `Ds(y)`, whose rank is its trace, continuous and integer valued). Without it the dimensions of the
   sheets enter as labellings, unique when they exist, since all sheets pass through `x`
   (`LocalBranchingStructure.dim_unique`). Status: **settled** on `ℝᵐ`; in general open (gap G.93).
   (2026-11-09) Remark 9.1.1 holds on every M-polyfold: in a chart, `dim_y A` is the rank of `Dt` for the chart
   sc⁺-retraction `t` of `A` (`hasDimAt_finrank`), which is locally constant along the retract
   (`ScRetraction.eventually_finrank_eq`), so `HasLocallyConstantDimAt` holds everywhere
   (`MPolyfold.hasLocallyConstantDimAt`, `Polyfold/Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero.lean`; item 107). Status: **settled**; gap
   G.93 closed in part (the footnote, item 3, stays open).
   (2026-11-09) `T_xX` now carries the linear structure of Definition 2.3.14, Banach through every chart and sc at
   smooth points (gap G.7 closed, Chapter 2, item 87); this statement is not restated with it.

3. **"n-dimensional", the footnote, and "locally equidimensional"** *(Definition 9.1.2, last paragraph, p.
   402)*. The 2021 text says the sheets "can be taken" `n`-dimensional (2017: are `n`-dimensional);
   `IsNDimensional` asks for some local branching structure with only `n`-dimensional sheets at every point of
   the support (`LocalBranchingStructure.IsOfDim`). The zero functor is `n`-dimensional for every `n`
   (`isNDimensional_zero`). The footnote (new in 2021), that an `n`-dimensional `Θ ≠ 0` is not `m`-dimensional
   for `m ≠ n`, and the notion "locally equidimensional" are not formalized (gap G.93). Witnesses on `ℝⁿ` for
   the whole chapter: closed submanifolds as images of smooth idempotents
   (`rnPolyfold_isSmoothSubmanifold_range`, `rnPolyfold_hasDimAt_range`), graphs (`graph2`,
   `rnPolyfold_isSubmanifoldOfDim_graph2`), finite weighted sums and indicators
   (`isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_sum_rn`, `isNDimensional_sum_rn`, `isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_indicator_rn`,
   `paracompactSpace_orbitSupp_trivial_rn`). Status: **settled**; the footnote open (gap G.93).
   (2026-11-09) The local constancy of item 2 is proved in general; the footnote and "locally equidimensional" remain
   open (gap G.93).
   (2026-11-09) The footnote, for `Θ` with nonempty support, and "locally equidimensional" are formalized (item 112;
   gap G.93 closed).

4. **Remark 9.1.3 (b): the second structure is forced, and the sign conditions are satisfiable** *(Remark 9.1.3
   (b), p. 403 (2017: Remark 9.2 (b), p. 292))*. The sign conditions on `β₁`, `β₂` are the structure
   `Remark913Hyp`, satisfied by `β₁(s) = e(s)`, `β₂(s) = e(−s)` with Mathlib's `expNegInvGlue` `e`
   (`remark913Hyp_expNegInvGlue`); `Θ(p) = ♯{i | p ∈ Gᵢ}` is `thetaGraphs` (`thetaGraphs_eq`). For the graphs of
   `0` and `γ₂` to describe the same `Θ`, `γ₂ = β₁ + β₂` is forced (`Remark913Hyp.eq_add_of_thetaGraphs_eq`),
   positive off `0` (`Remark913Hyp.γ₂_pos`). "Not unique, even close to `x`" is read as: no sheet of one
   structure agrees with a sheet of the other on any neighbourhood of the origin (`Remark913Hyp.structureβ`,
   `Remark913Hyp.structureγ`, `remark_9_1_3_b`). Status: **settled**.

5. **Lemma 9.1.5 without the properness property; the restriction remark read at `x`** *(Lemma 9.1.5, p. 403
   (2017: Lemma 9.1, p. 293); the remark before Lemma 9.1.7, p. 404)*. Lemma 9.1.5 is proved from the saturation
   of the support (`preimage_π_orbitSupp`), its local closedness in `X` (`LocalBranchingStructure.isClosed_M`,
   `isLocallyClosed_supp`) and the openness of `π` (`lemma_9_1_5`); the text's neighbourhood with the properness
   property is not needed. Before Lemma 9.1.7 the text restricts a structure to `Nᵢ = Mᵢ ∩ V(x₀)`, some `Nᵢ`
   possibly empty. Definition 9.1.2 asks `x ∈ Mᵢ`, which the `Nᵢ` need not satisfy at `x₀`; the remark is
   formalized for an open `V ∋ x`, the case the symmetrization uses (`LocalBranchingStructure.restrict`,
   `IsSmoothSubmanifold.inter_isOpen`). This is a reading, not a misprint. Status: **settled**.

6. **Lemma 9.1.7: the images `g ∗ Mᵢ` are submanifolds** *(Lemma 9.1.7, p. 405 (2017: Lemma 9.2, p. 294))*. The
   construction `J = I × G_x`, `M_{(i,g)} = g ∗ Mᵢ`, `σ_{(i,g)} = σᵢ/♯G_x` is formalized
   (`LocalBranchingStructure.symmetrize`, `SymmetricBranchingStructure`, `lemma_9_1_7`), and inside every
   neighbourhood of `x` (`lemma_9_1_7'`). The text uses without saying so that `Φ(g)(Mᵢ ∩ U)` is a properly
   embedded submanifold through `x` (`IsSmoothSubmanifold.image_of_isScDiffeoOn`). The weight computation uses
   `IsFunctorial.apply_Φ` and `NaturalRep.mem_image_Φ_iff`, with `♯G_x` the `Nat.card` of the finite group; the
   action on `J` is `mulActionProdLeft`. Status: **settled**.

7. **Definitions 9.1.6 and 9.1.8; Remark 9.1.4, Proposition 9.1.9 and Remark 9.1.10 not formalized** *(pp.
   403–406 (2017: Remark 9.3, Definitions 9.2, 9.3, Proposition 9.1, pp. 293–296))*. `IsClosedBranched`,
   `IsCompactBranched`, `IsOrbifoldType`, `IsManifoldType`, with `isCompactBranched_indicator`,
   `isManifoldType_indicator`. Not formalized: Remark 9.1.4, the metrizability of a paracompact subset of `|X|`
   and the compactness criterion (gap G.94); Proposition 9.1.9 and Remark 9.1.10, the manifold and orbifold
   structures on `|supp(Θ)|` (gap G.95). Status: **settled** (2026-11-12, below and item 114; gaps G.94, G.95 closed;
   rows V9.63–V9.65).
   (2026-11-12) Remark 9.1.4 is `remark_9_1_4` with `remark_9_1_4_metrizable`, `remark_9_1_4_exists_nhds`,
   `isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_of_isComponentCompact` (`Polyfold/Chapter9/GapP2_CRemark914.lean`): the step from the
   paracompact neighbourhood to `K` goes through metrizability, since a subspace of a paracompact space need not be
   paracompact. Proposition 9.1.9 is `proposition_9_1_9_one` (with `proposition_9_1_9_one_unique`) and
   `proposition_9_1_9_two_text` (with `proposition_9_1_9_two_independent`), and Remark 9.1.10 is
   `remark_9_1_10_manifold`, `remark_9_1_10_orbifold`, `remark_9_1_10_orbifold_etale` for `n`-dimensional `Θ`; the
   readings are item 114.

8. **Proposition 9.1.11: the uniqueness of the dimensional decomposition does not hold as we read it**
   *(Proposition 9.1.11, pp. 407–408 (2017: Proposition 9.2, p. 297))*. The statement is `Proposition_9_1_11`
   (`IsDimDecomposition`, `IsLocallyFiniteFamily`). The local construction is verified:
   `LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart`, `dimPartStructure`, `dimPartStructure_isOfDim`, `eq_sum_dimPart`,
   `dimPart_eq_zero`, `dimPart_eq_of_isOfDim`, with `SymmetricBranchingStructure.dim_smul` and
   `SymmetricBranchingStructure.dimPart_Φ` for the `G_x`-invariance. Counterexample `not_proposition_9_1_11_rn`:
   on the trivial ep-groupoid of `ℝ²` let `L` be the `x`-axis (`axis2`) and `Θ = 1_L`; `decompA` (`Θ₀ = 1_{0}`,
   `Θ₁ = 1_{L∖0}`) and `decompB` (`Θ₀ = 0`, `Θ₁ = 1_L`) both satisfy (1) and (2) (`decompA_isDimDecomposition`,
   `decompB_isDimDecomposition`), since `L ∖ 0` is a `1`-dimensional submanifold properly embedded in the open
   set `ℝ² ∖ 0`, which is all Definition 9.1.2 asks at its points. The proof of the text constructs `decompB`. A
   possible repair: each `Θ_k` is represented near every point by a subfamily of a local branching structure of
   `Θ`. Not formalized: the repaired uniqueness and the global gluing of the local `Θ_k` across morphisms, with
   the paracompactness of `|supp(Θ_k)|` and the local finiteness (gap G.96). Status: **open** (gap G.96); the
   counterexample is settled.

9. **Proposition 9.1.12 (new in the 2021 edition)** *(Proposition 9.1.12, p. 408; proof in §9.6.1, pp.
   452–457)*. `Proposition_9_1_12` with the conclusion `LocalBranchingStructure.DimPartsAgreeNear`; "an open
   `G_x`-invariant `V(x)` with the usual properties" by shrinking to a natural representation
   (`DimPartsAgreeNear.exists_naturalRep`); the equidimensional case is immediate
   (`dimPartsAgreeNear_of_isOfDim`). The general case is proved in §9.6.1 (items 90–92):
   `proposition_9_1_12_of_topMultiplicity`, `proposition_9_1_12_of_hasGraphChartAt`, and without hypothesis on
   every ep-groupoid over `ℝᵐ` (`proposition_9_1_12_rn`). Status: **settled** over `ℝᵐ`; in general under the
   graph representation (gap G.97).
   (2026-11-09) Proposition 9.1.12 holds for every ep-groupoid (`proposition_9_1_12`,
   `Polyfold/Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries.lean`), through `TopMultiplicity` for every M-polyfold
   (`MPolyfold.topMultiplicity`), with the graph representation chosen per tangent space (item 107). Status:
   **settled**; gap G.97 closed.

Found while formalizing §9.2 up to Definition 9.2.12 (2026-11-08).

20. **`T_yM` as a set of vectors, linear in charts; the category `Gr(X)`** *(pp. 408–409 (2017 pp. 297–298))*.
    `T_yM` is the set of tangent vectors fixed by the tangent of a retraction presenting `M`
    (`MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent`; Part I's Remark 4.2.2 (preprint: 4.14)), independent of the retraction
    (`mem_submanifoldTangent_iff`), local (`submanifoldTangent_inter_isOpen`), and mapped by sc-diffeomorphisms
    (`submanifoldTangent_image`). In a chart it is a linear subspace of dimension `dim_y M` (`chartTangent`,
    `chartTangent_eq`, `exists_submodule_chartTangent`, `finrank_chartTangent`), and chart changes act by linear
    isomorphisms (`chartTangent_chart_change`, `exists_linearEquiv_chartTangent`); so the generators of `Gr(x)`
    are linear subspaces in every chart (`LocalBranchingStructure.exists_submodule_of_mem_support`), which is
    what the text's "finite-dimensional linear subspaces of `T_xX`" means. `Gr`, `grPush`, `grPush_comp`,
    `grPush_unit`, `GrObj`, `grProj`. Status: **settled** (gap G.7 stays).
    (2026-11-09) `T_xX` now carries the linear structure of Definition 2.3.14, Banach through every chart and sc at
    smooth points (gap G.7 closed, Chapter 2, item 87); this statement is not restated with it.

21. **Theorem 9.2.1: the independence of the structure is the core; unconditional on `ℝᵐ`** *(Theorem 9.2.1, p.
    409, proof pp. 412–418 (2017: Theorem 9.1, pp. 298–306))*. The section is `theorem_9_2_1` under
    `HasIndependentTangentSums` (`LocalBranchingStructure.tangentSum`, `tangentValue`,
    `LocalBranchingStructure.transport`, `grPush_tangentValue`, `tangentSection`). The independence is proved at
    good points without hypothesis (`tangentSum_eq_of_isGoodPoint`,
    `hasIndependentTangentSums_of_subset_goodSet`), for equidimensional structures by counting on slices
    (`hasIndependentTangentSums_of_isOfDim`), and in general from Proposition 9.1.12
    (`tangentSum_eq_of_dimPartsAgreeNear`, `hasIndependentTangentSums_of_dimPartsAgreeNear`) with the labellings
    supplied by `HasLocallyConstantDimAt` (`exists_restrict_labelled`,
    `hasIndependentTangentSums_of_hasGraphChartAt_of_hasLocallyConstantDimAt`). On every ep-groupoid over `ℝᵐ`
    it holds for every `Θ` (`hasIndependentTangentSums_rn`). In Remark 9.1.3 (b) the two structures have the
    same tangent sum at the bad origin (`Remark913Hyp.tangentSum_structureβ_eq_structureγ`). Status: **settled**
    over `ℝᵐ`; in general under gaps G.93, G.97.
    (2026-11-09) The independence holds for every `Θ` on every ep-groupoid (`hasIndependentTangentSums`; item 107).

22. **Possible misprints in §9.2** *(pp. 408–418 (2017 pp. 297–306))*. The introduction (p. 408) calls `TΘ` a
    "branched ep-subgroupoid", Definition 9.2.12 an ep⁺-subgroupoid; "it suffices to prove the proposition"
    (p. 410) refers to Theorem 9.2.1; Definition 9.2.6 cites "Remark 9.2.4 (c)" (p. 411), the remark having (a) and
    (b), and the descent to `|X|` uses Lemma 9.2.5; the proof closes with "This completes the proof of Theorem
    9.2.8" (p. 418), presumably Theorem 9.2.1; in `∑_{i∈I | y∈M_j} σᵢ T_yMᵢ` (p. 418) the index is presumably
    `i`. Status: **settled** (possible misprints).

23. **Good points: an intrinsic form, in every dimension** *(Definition 9.2.2, Lemma 9.2.3, Remark 9.2.4, Lemma
    9.2.5, Definition 9.2.6, pp. 410–411 (2017: Definition 9.4, Lemma 9.3, Remark 9.4, Lemma 9.4, Definition
    9.5, pp. 299–300))*. `LocalBranchingStructure.IsGoodPoint`, with the intrinsic form `isGoodPoint_iff`: `y`
    is good iff `y ∈ supp(Θ)` and `Θ` is constant on `supp(Θ)` near `y` (`nbhdAt`, `le_of_mem_nbhdAt`,
    `eq_iff_of_mem_nbhdAt`). Hence `lemma_9_2_3` for any two structures, at possibly different points; in its
    proof `Q(z) = V(y) ∩ W(y)` is presumably `Q(y)` (possible misprint). `remark_9_2_4_a`, `remark_9_2_4_b`
    (`restrictAt`), `lemma_9_2_5` through the sheet of a morphism (`Sheet.apply_hat`, `src_mem_goodSet_of_tgt`),
    `goodSet`, `badSet`, saturated (`preimage_π_image_goodSet`, `preimage_π_image_badSet`). The text states the
    definition for equidimensional `Θ`; no proof uses it. Status: **settled**.

24. **Lemma 9.2.7: density without (2), and (2) under invariance of domain** *(Lemma 9.2.7, p. 412 (2017: Lemma
    9.5, pp. 300–301))*. (1): openness is `lemma_9_2_7_1`; density (`lemma_9_2_7_1_dense`, `dense_goodSet`,
    `isNowhereDense_badSet`) is proved by shrinking an open set one sheet at a time
    (`exists_isOpen_subset_inter_eq_empty_or_subset`), with neither (2) nor a dimension hypothesis, while the
    text derives it from (2). (2): the point found is "clearly" good only if an `n`-dimensional submanifold
    contained near it in another one equals it there, invariance of domain, which Part I does not provide: the
    hypothesis `HasDomainInvarianceAt` (`lemma_9_2_7_2`), proved on `ℝᵐ` by the inverse function theorem
    (`hasDomainInvarianceAt_rn`, `lemma_9_2_7_2_rn`). (2) holds at every `x`, not only at bad points (reading).
    In Remark 9.1.3 (b) the origin is bad and approached by good points on each graph
    (`Remark913Hyp.zero_mem_badSet`, `Remark913Hyp.exists_seq_goodSet_structureβ`). Status: **settled** over
    `ℝᵐ`; in general open (gap G.98).
    (2026-11-09) Invariance of domain holds on every M-polyfold (`MPolyfold.hasDomainInvarianceAt`, from
    `ScRetraction.eq_of_range_eq`), so (2) holds for every ep-groupoid (`lemma_9_2_7_2_general`; item 107). Status:
    **settled**; gap G.98 closed.

25. **Proposition 9.2.8 and Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11: slices instead of sequences, a graph chart as a hypothesis**
    *(Proposition 9.2.8, p. 413, Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11, pp. 414–417 (2017: Proposition 9.3, Lemmas 9.6–9.8, pp.
    302–305))*. The proof of Theorem 9.2.1 uses Proposition 9.2.8 to count the weights of a class of sheets with
    one tangent space by values of `Θ`; what the count needs is one finite slice per class meeting each sheet of
    the class once and missing the others (`HasTangentSlicesAt`). It is produced from the graph representation
    (`IsGraphChartAt`, `HasGraphChartsAt`, `hasTangentSlicesAt_of_hasGraphChartsAt`): rays replace the cones of
    Lemma 9.2.10, with secants uniformly approximated by `T_xM` (`IsGraphChartAt.approx`). Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11
    need level-0 sc-calculus in partial quadrants (sc-complements, a mean value formula for sc⁺-retractions, an
    inverse function theorem on a cone), not in Part I, so the graph representation is a hypothesis on a general
    M-polyfold. On `ℝᵐ` it is proved at every point and in every dimension (`isGraphChartAt_rn`,
    `hasGraphChartsAt_rn`, `hasTangentSlicesAt_rn`, via `exists_mem_graph_of_hasStrictFDerivAt` and
    `rn_exists_retraction`). For sheets of several dimensions one chart for all of them is needed
    (`HasGraphChartAt`, `HasGraphChartAt.hasGraphChartsAt`, `hasGraphChartAt_rn`,
    `exists_slice_of_isGraphChartAt`, `exists_generic_slice`; item 91). Proposition 9.2.8 as printed, with the
    splitting `I¹ ⊔ ⋯ ⊔ I^p` and the sequences, is not formalized. Status: **settled** over `ℝᵐ`; in general
    open (gap G.97).
    (2026-11-09) Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11 are proved on every M-polyfold, with one admissible cone per tangent space
    (`hasClassGraphChartAt`), and the slices exist at every point (`hasTangentSlicesAt`; item 107); Proposition 9.2.8
    stays in slice form. Status: **settled**; gap G.97 closed.

26. **Definition 9.2.12: `TΘ` is well defined; that it is a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid needs more** *(Definition
    9.2.12, p. 418 (2017: Definition 9.6, p. 306))*. `tangentTheta` evaluates `T_Θ(p(h))` on the tangent sets
    containing `h` (`grEval`, `tangentSubmanifold`), so it needs no choice; the text's "the local definitions
    fit together" is `tangentTheta_eq`, from `sum_tangent_eq_sum_tangent`; `tangentTheta_nonneg`,
    `isFunctorial_tangentTheta`. The text says without discussion that `TΘ` is a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid; this
    needs `TangentBranchingHyp` (`isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta`, `tangentBranchingStructure`).
    Closedness of the `TMᵢ` is proved (`isClosed_tangentSubmanifold`), paracompactness follows from that of
    `|X|` (`paracompactSpace_orbitSupp_tangentTheta`), and `TMᵢ` is a sub-M-polyfold of `TX`, the image of `Ts`
    (`IsSmoothSubmanifold.isSubMPolyfold_tangent`, `LocalBranchingStructure.isSubMPolyfold_tangentSubmanifold`,
    `rnPolyfold_isSubMPolyfold_tangent_graph2`); that `Ts` is an sc⁺-retraction of `TX` is not formalized, also
    on `ℝᵐ` (`tangentBranchingHyp_of_isSmoothSubmanifold`, `isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta_rn`). The full
    hypothesis has the zero functor as witness (`tangentBranchingHyp_zero`). Status: **open** (gap G.99).
    (2026-11-09) `TA` is a smooth submanifold of `TX` for every smooth finite-dimensional submanifold `A`
    (`IsSmoothSubmanifold.isSmoothSubmanifold_tangent`), so `TΘ` is a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid whenever `|X|` is
    paracompact (`isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta_general`; item 109). Status now: **settled**; gap G.99 closed.

Found while formalizing §9.2 from Lemma 9.2.13: the boundary (2026-11-08).

40. **Reduced tangent position in a chart** *(before Lemma 9.2.13, p. 419 (2017 p. 307))*. `T_xM ⊆ T^R_xX` is
    the inclusion of the chart image of `T_xM` in the reduced tangent space `E_z` (`IsReducedTangentAt`,
    `isReducedTangentAt_iff_subset_reduced`), equivalently in the partial quadrant or the partial cone
    (`isReducedTangentAt_iff_subset_partialQuadrant`, `isReducedTangentAt_iff_subset_partialCone`; the 2017
    Remark 9.5's "not contained in `C_xX`" is equivalent); it does not depend on the chart
    (`isReducedTangentAt_chart_change`, `MPolyfold.IsTangentReducedAt`, `isTangentReducedAt_iff_forall`). `d_M`
    is `subDegIndex`, at most `d_X` (`subDegIndex_le`). Status: **settled**.

41. **Lemma 9.2.13 read at points of `∂X`; the converse proved without the complement `Y` and the map `F`**
    *(Lemma 9.2.13, p. 419 (2017: Lemma 9.9, p. 307))*. As printed, (2) ⇒ "(1) `x ∈ ∂X` and `d_M(x) = 0`" does
    not hold as we read it at interior points: a point of `ℝⁿ` is in reduced tangent position and not in `∂ℝⁿ`
    (`not_lemma_9_2_13_two_one`). The lemma is read with `x ∈ M ∩ ∂X` as the standing assumption, where the text
    uses it; this is a reading. (1) ⇒ (2): `lemma_9_2_13`, `lemma_9_2_13_chart` (Part I's theorem for the
    induced structure), and off `∂X` too (`lemma_9_2_13_of_not_mem_boundary`). (2) ⇒ (1):
    `lemma_9_2_13_two_one`, from `ScRetraction.IsScPlus.exists_flat` (the chart `χ = p(· − z)` on `M ∩ G`, with
    inverse `s ∘ (z + ·) ∘ Ψ⁻¹` by Mathlib's inverse function theorem, a model without boundary) and
    `ScRetraction.IsScPlus.exists_injOn_proj` (the step "the image is `M` near `0`", which the text does not
    spell out: `p` is injective on `M` near `z`, by a level-1 contraction with the mean value inequality);
    `subDegIndex_eq_zero_of_isTangentReducedAt`, `degIndex_eq_zero_of_isReducedTangentAt`. Together:
    `lemma_9_2_13_iff` at `x ∈ ∂X`, and `subDegIndex_eq_zero_iff`, `d_M(x) = 0 ⟺ T_xM ⊆ T^R_xX`, at every `x ∈
    M`. No fact of Part I is assumed. Not formalized: a witness at a boundary point, which needs a submanifold
    API for quadrants. Status: **settled**.

42. **Remark 9.2.14** *(Remark 9.2.14, p. 419 (2017: Remark 9.5, p. 307))*. `x ∈ ∂M ⟺ x ∈ ∂X ∧ T_xM ⊄ T^R_xX`
    (`remark_9_2_14_iff`), from `remark_9_2_14`, `remark_9_2_14_mem_boundary` (`∂M ⊆ ∂X`),
    `remark_9_2_14_not_isTangentReducedAt`, `remark_9_2_14_not_mem_boundary_iff` and
    `mem_boundary_subPolyfold_iff`. Status: **settled**.

43. **Proposition 9.2.15 with fewer hypotheses** *(Proposition 9.2.15, p. 420 (2017: Proposition 9.4, p. 308))*.
    The boundary weight is the part of `T_Θ(y)` on tangent sets not in reduced position
    (`MPolyfold.submanifoldBoundary`, `mem_submanifoldBoundary_iff`, `isReducedTangentSet_iff`, `boundaryPart`,
    `filter_tangentValue_eq`). (1) `proposition_9_2_15_1`, under the independence of Theorem 9.2.1; (2)
    `proposition_9_2_15_2`, without it; (3) `boundaryTheta`, `isFunctorial_boundaryTheta`, `boundaryTheta_eq`,
    `proposition_9_2_15_3`. (1) and (2) need neither `x ∈ supp(Θ) ∩ ∂X` nor that `Θ` be branched. Status:
    **settled**.

44. **Definition 9.2.16: the characterization of `∂Θ` is not unique as we read it** *(Definition 9.2.16, p. 421
    (2017: Definition 9.7, p. 309))*. (1) and (2) of the text are `IsBoundaryCharacterized`, satisfied by `∂Θ`
    (`isBoundaryCharacterized_boundaryTheta`). Since (2) is asked only on `supp(F)`, the zero functor satisfies
    (1) and (2) for every `Θ` (`isBoundaryCharacterized_zero`), and for `Θ = 1` on `[0, ∞)`, where `∂Θ(0) = 1`
    (`boundaryTheta_halfLine_one`), both `0` and `∂Θ` do (`not_unique_isBoundaryCharacterized_halfLine`). With
    (2) asked on `supp(Θ)` and `F = 0` off `supp(Θ)`, `F = ∂Θ` (`eq_boundaryTheta`). Status: **settled**
    (corrected reading).
    (2026-11-12) Read as "the solution of (1) and (2) with the largest support", the characterization is unique: among
    the `F ≥ 0` vanishing off `supp(Θ)` with (1) and (2), `∂Θ` is the one with the largest support
    (`definition_9_2_16_existsUnique`; `F = ∂Θ` iff `supp(∂Θ) ⊆ supp(F)`,
    `IsBoundaryCharacterized.eq_boundaryTheta_iff`), and every such `F` equals `∂Θ` on `U(x)` for `x ∈ supp(F)`
    (`IsBoundaryCharacterized.eq_boundaryTheta_on`, `Polyfold/Chapter9/GapP2_DBoundaryChar.lean`). Row V9.27.

45. **Possible misprints around Definition 9.2.16** *(pp. 420–421 (2017 p. 309))*. "In view of Proposition
    9.2.13" (2017: "Proposition 9.9", the 2017 number of Lemma 9.2.13) presumably refers to Proposition 9.2.15;
    Definition 9.2.16 writes "branched ep⁺-groupoid" for ep⁺-subgroupoid. Status: **settled** (possible
    misprints).

46. **Remark 9.2.17** *(Remark 9.2.17, p. 421 (2017: Remark 9.6, p. 310))*. `∂Θ ≤ Θ` (`boundaryTheta_le`); `∂Θ`
    is not `Θ` restricted to `∂X`: for the indicator of the corner of `[0, ∞)`, `Θ(0) = 1` and `∂Θ(0) = 0`
    (`boundaryTheta_halfLineCorner`), while for `Θ = 1` on `[0, ∞)`
    (`HasCornerStructure.isSmoothSubmanifold_univ`, `isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_one`) `∂Θ(0) = 1`
    (`boundaryTheta_one`); for the indicator of an interior point `∂Θ = 0` (`boundaryTheta_indicator_of_mem`).
    The witnesses satisfy the independence (`hasIndependentTangentSums_indicator_of_mem`). The remark's "In
    Section 9.5, Definition 9.3.6" (also in 2017) refers to §9.3 (possible misprint). Status: **settled**.

Found while formalizing §9.3 (2026-11-08).

50. **Orientations as sets of frames; `Ĝr(X)`; Remark 9.3.1** *(p. 422 (2017 p. 310); Remark 9.3.1 (2017:
    9.7))*. An orientation of a tangent set is a set of frames whose chart images (`MPolyfold.chartVec`,
    `chartVec_injOn`) are the positive bases of an orientation of the chart image (`MPolyfold.OrTangent`,
    `chartFrames`, `IsChartOrientation`, `MPolyfold.IsOrientedAt`); chart changes act linearly
    (`exists_clm_chartVec`), so this does not depend on the chart (`IsOrientedAt.isChartOrientation`,
    `isOrientedAt_iff_forall`); every tangent set has exactly two orientations (`exists_two_orientations`),
    pushed forward by sc-diffeomorphisms and morphisms (`OrTangent.push`, `IsOrientedAt.push_tangentMapOn`,
    `isOrientedAt_push_tangentMor`). `GrHat`, `grHatPush`, `GrHatObj`, `grHatProj`, `grForget`,
    `grForgetFunctor`, `grForgetFunctor_comp_grProj`, `grForget_single_add_single`. Remark 9.3.1 has no formal
    content. Status: **settled** (gap G.7 stays).
    (2026-11-09) `T_xX` now carries the linear structure of Definition 2.3.14, Banach through every chart and sc at
    smooth points (gap G.7 closed, Chapter 2, item 87); this statement is not restated with it.

51. **Definition 9.3.2 uses the independence of Theorem 9.2.1** *(Definition 9.3.2, p. 423 (2017: Definition
    9.8, p. 311))*. A continuous orientation of a submanifold is a locally constant choice of chart frames
    (`MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation`); `EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure`,
    `OrientedBranchingStructure.orientedSum`, `grForget_orientedSum`, `EpGroupoid.IsOrientation`,
    `orientedSection`. "Lifts `T_Θ`" uses `T_Θ`, hence the independence (`IsOrientation.mk'`), free on `ℝᵐ`
    (`isOrientation_sum_trivial_rn`, `isOrientationOfDim_sum_trivial_rn`). Witnesses: `isOrientation_zero`,
    `isOrientation_sum_rn`. Status: **settled**.

52. **Remark 9.3.3** *(Remark 9.3.3, p. 423 (2017: Remark 9.8, p. 311))*. For the indicator of a point, every `q
    ∈ (0, 1) ∩ ℚ` gives the orientation `q · (T_p{p}, +) + (1 − q) · (T_p{p}, −)`, and these are pairwise
    distinct (`remark_9_3_3`). Status: **settled**.

53. **Lemma 9.3.4 does not hold as we read it without equidimensionality; its proof needs good points serving
    both structures** *(Lemma 9.3.4, pp. 423–424 (2017: Lemma 9.10, pp. 311–312))*. Counterexample
    `lemma_9_3_4_mixed_dim`, `lemma_9_3_4_mixed_dim_rn`: on `ℝ²`, `Θ = 1_{ℝ×0} + 1_{(0,0)}` (`mixedTheta`,
    `mixedTheta_isBranched`); the origin is bad (`zero_not_mem_goodSet_mixed`), and two orientations orienting
    the line alike and the point oppositely agree at all good points. The lemma is formalized for
    `n`-dimensional `Θ` (`IsOrientationOfDim`, `lemma_9_3_4`). The text compares the structures along good-point
    sequences of the first structure only; as we read it, this needs Proposition 9.2.8 for both families
    together, an argument the text does not give: the hypothesis `HasOrientedGoodPointsAt`. It follows from the
    ball form of the graph representation (`HasGraphBallAt`; the ray form does not provide an open set of foot
    points for the shrinking of Lemma 9.2.7) and the level-1 continuity of frames (`HasContinuousLevelOneOn`),
    through which relative orientations are locally constant (`frameDet`, `orientation_eq_iff_frameDet`,
    `frames_eq_iff_frameDet`, `continuousOn_chartVec_of_continuousOn`,
    `SubmanifoldOrientation.exists_isOpen_tangent_eq_iff`): `hasOrientedGoodPointsAt_of_hasGraphBallAt`,
    `lemma_9_3_4_of_hasGraphBallAt`. On `ℝᵐ` both hold (`hasGraphBallAt_rn`, `hasContinuousLevelOneOn_rn`,
    `hasOrientedGoodPointsAt_rn`, `lemma_9_3_4_rn`). Status: **settled** over `ℝᵐ`; in general open (gaps G.97,
    G.100).
    (2026-11-09) The level-1 continuity holds along every smooth finite-dimensional submanifold
    (`MPolyfold.hasContinuousLevelOneOn`), and the ball graph representation at interior points
    (`hasGraphBallAt_of_mem_interior`); so Lemma 9.3.4 holds with no hypothesis when `supp(Θ)` has degeneracy index `0`
    (`lemma_9_3_4_of_degIndex_eq_zero`), and otherwise with `HasGraphBallAt` on `supp(Θ)` as the only hypothesis
    (`lemma_9_3_4_of_hasGraphBallAt'`) (item 107). Gap G.100 closed.
    (2026-11-09) Lemma 9.3.4 now holds for `n`-dimensional `Θ` with no hypothesis on the boundary: the good-point input
    holds at every point (`MPolyfold.hasOrientedGoodPointsAt`, `EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4_general`; item 109).

54. **Example 9.3.5: "otherwise different" and "four possibilities" do not hold as we read them** *(Example
    9.3.5, p. 425 (2017: Example 9.1, p. 313))*. `betaPP`, `betaMM`, `betaPM`, `betaMP`, `example_9_3_5_count`,
    `example935Theta`, `example935Theta_isBranched`, `graphOrientation`, `exampleT1`, `exampleT2`. Verified as
    stated: the orientations coincide at the origin (`example_9_3_5_eq_origin`), differ for `s > 0`
    (`example_9_3_5_ne_of_pos`), and no signs on the second structure reproduce `T̂¹` near `0`
    (`example_9_3_5_cannot_coincide`; `example_9_3_5`, `example_9_3_5_rn`). They also coincide where `x < 0`
    (`example_9_3_5_eq_of_neg`), and the four sign choices on the first structure give four different
    orientations (`orientedLift1_injective`), none of them `T̂²` (`exampleT2_ne_orientedLift1`); with the four of the
    second structure the sign choices give exactly six orientations with weights `1` (`ncard_signOrientations`,
    2026-11-12), and infinitely many with fractional weights (Remark 9.3.3; classified, item 115). The good points
    distinguish `T̂¹` from `T̂²` (`exists_goodSet_exampleT1_ne_exampleT2`). All orientations are classified
    (2026-11-12, item 115; gap G.101 closed). Status: **settled** (row V9.33).

55. **Definition 9.3.6: the corner structure of a tame `Mᵢ`** *(Definition 9.3.6, p. 425 (2017: Definition 9.10,
    p. 314))*. `TameBranchingStructure`, `IsTameBranched`, with witnesses `isTameBranched_zero` and
    `isTameBranched_indicator` (`hasTameInducedStructure_of_degIndex_eq_zero`). "In particular every `Mᵢ` has an
    equivalent structure of a manifold with boundary with corners" is not formalized: the project has no bridge
    from tame finite-dimensional M⁺-polyfolds to Mathlib manifolds with corners (gap G.102). Status: **open**
    (gap G.102).
    (2026-11-09) Formalized for sheets of one dimension `n` in Mathlib's language (`TameBranchingStructure.isManifold`;
    item 109). Status now: **settled**; gap G.102 closed.

56. **Lemma 9.3.7 (new in the 2021 edition) in a stronger form** *(Lemma 9.3.7, p. 426)*. `lemma_9_3_7`;
    `d_M(y)` is the codimension of the reduced part of the chart image of `T_yM`
    (`subDegIndex_eq_quotDim_of_hasTameInducedStructure`, Part I's Remark 2.5.9 in every chart), so equal
    tangent spaces give equal indices without "`Y` tame" or "of the same dimension"
    (`subDegIndex_eq_of_tangentSpace_eq`, `subDegIndex_eq_of_submanifoldTangent_eq`). "`T_0O ∩ C = T^R_0O`" (a
    cone against a subspace) is read through the linearity of the chart image of `T_0M`. Status: **settled**.

57. **Definition 9.3.8: `T_y∂M` and the outward vector are data** *(Definition 9.3.8, p. 427 (2017: Definition
    9.9, p. 313))*. The convention orients a hyperplane (`exists_boundary_orientation`,
    `exists_basis_orientation_iff_det_pos`, `det_cons_smul_add`); in a tangent set, `boundaryFrames` with
    `isOrientedAt_boundaryFrames` and `boundaryFrames_eq` (unchanged by `e ↦ ce + k`), both orientations
    occurring on a graph (`exists_boundaryFrames_graph`). That `T_y∂M = T^R_yM` and the outward half-space are
    determined by `M` through the cones `C_yM` is not formalized (gap G.103). Status: **open** (gap G.103).
    (2026-11-09) `T_y∂M` and the outward vectors are determined by `M`: `T_y∂M = T^R_yM`
    (`chartVec_image_boundaryCarrier`), outward means "in `T_yM`, not in `C_yM`" (`isOutward_iff_not_mem_partialCone`),
    and the boundary operation `boundaryOp` built from them does not depend on the outward vector (`boundaryOp_eq`)
    (`Polyfold/Chapter9/BoundaryOperation.lean`; item 108). Status: **settled** except the continuity of `o_{∂M}` (gap
    G.103); the continuity settled 2026-11-09 (item 110), the stratum as an oriented submanifold 2026-11-13 (item 119;
    gap G.103 closed).
    (2026-11-13) For a tame sheet the stratum `{d_M = 1}` is a smooth `(n−1)`-dimensional submanifold of `X` with
    tangent spaces `T^R_yM` (`isSubmanifoldOfDim_stratumOne`, `submanifoldTangent_stratumOne`), oriented by `o_{∂M}`
    in the sense of Definition 9.3.3 (`stratumOrientation`); in corner coordinates the convention is "outward normal
    `Tι(−eᵢ)` first" (`incFrame_mem_boundaryFramesAt_iff`). Item 119.

58. **(9.11), Proposition 9.3.9 (new in the 2021 edition), Definition 9.3.10 and Remark 9.3.11** *(pp. 427–429
    (2017: Definition 9.11, p. 314))*. The split by degree (`degreePart`, `degreePart_orientedSum`,
    `HasSubDegree`, `SubmanifoldOrientation.hasSubDegree_tangent_iff`) does not depend on the structure
    (`eq_9_11`), by Lemma 9.3.7; the boundary operation is a function `bd` of the oriented tangent set
    (`proposition_9_3_9`); `boundaryLift` is Definition 9.3.10, whose condition `y ∈ ∂Mᵢ` is implied by
    `d_{Mᵢ}(y) = 1`. The continuity of `o_∂M` along `∂M` and its extension to the faces (Figure 9.1) are not
    formalized (gap G.103); Remark 9.3.11 has no formal content. Status: **open** (gap G.103).
    (2026-11-09) Proposition 9.3.9 and (9.12) hold with the boundary operation built from the `Mᵢ`, with no data
    hypothesis (`proposition_9_3_9_boundaryOp`), and the intrinsic `T̂_{∂Θ}` (`boundaryOrientation`) agrees with it for
    oriented tame `Θ̂` (item 108). The continuity and Figure 9.1 stay open (gap G.103); settled since, the continuity
    on 2026-11-09 (item 110) and Figure 9.1 on 2026-11-13 (item 119; gap G.103 closed).
    (2026-11-13) For a face-structured tame sheet Part I's face orientation is `o_{∂M}` at the points with `d_M = 1`
    (`faceOrientation_eq_iff_mem_stratumOrientation`), and the orientation of the open face extends to exactly one
    continuous orientation of the closed face, Part I's `faceOrientation` (`figure_9_1_existsUnique_faceOrientation`).
    Not formalized: the orientations of the faces of the faces (the caption's last sentence). Item 119.

Found while formalizing §9.5 (2026-11-08).

80. **Definition 9.5.1: the null sets of the sheets as data** *(Definition 9.5.1, p. 437 (2017: Definition 9.15,
    p. 322))*. Measure zero in a sheet `Mᵢ` (Definition 9.4.5) is not available for submanifolds of an
    M-polyfold, so it is an abstract system on a class `S` of sheets, `SheetNullSets`: a σ-ideal in every sheet
    (`SheetNullSets.isNull_iUnion_countable`, `SheetNullSets.isNull_union`), local, induced alike by two sheets
    of `S` on their overlap (`isNull_transfer`), a nonempty sheet not null in itself; with the covering
    criterion `SheetNullSets.isNull_of_cover`. `MPolyfold.SheetMeasureGeometry` is a §9.4 `SheetGeometry` with
    these properties (`SheetMeasureGeometry.toSheetNullSets`,
    `LocalBranchingStructure.hasNullPreimages_iff_isNullIn`). Definition 9.5.1 is `IsMeasureZeroSupp`, "a
    suitable `U(x)`" being a `TameBranchingStructure` (Definition 9.3.6) with sheets in `S`
    (`LocalBranchingStructure.HasNullPreimages`), with the variants `IsMeasureZeroSuppAny`,
    `IsMeasureZeroSuppAll` and the standing assumption `HasTameSheetsIn` (on `ℝⁿ`:
    `exists_tameBranchingStructure_trivial_rn`, `hasTameSheetsIn_trivial_rn`). Compactness and orientation of
    `Θ` are not used. Not formalized: Lebesgue null sets in the sheets of a general M-polyfold (gap G.106).
    Status: **settled** as read, and in general (2026-11-12, below; gap G.106 closed).
    (2026-11-09) In the sheets of a tame branching structure of dimension `n` the null sets of Definition 9.4.5 are now
    Mathlib's (item 109; gap G.106 in part); the statement is not restated with them.
    (2026-11-12) The null sets are concrete (`IsHNull`, `sheetNullSets`, `Polyfold/Chapter9/GapP2_DSheetNull.lean`)
    and Definition 9.5.1 is restated with them (`IsMeasureZeroH`, `lebesgueSigmaH`; gap G.106 closed; item 116).

81. **Lemma 9.5.2 across dimensions does not hold as we read it** *(Lemma 9.5.2, p. 437 (2017: Lemma 9.16, p.
    322))*. The text cites the literature, without proof. The core is `isMeasureZeroSuppAll_of_any`: near a
    point of `M'_j ∩ π⁻¹(A)`, `M'_j` is covered by the finitely many sheets of a structure with null preimages,
    and the covering criterion applies; `isMeasureZeroSuppAny_of_isMeasureZeroSupp`, `lemma_9_5_2`; the sets of
    measure zero form a σ-ideal (`isSigmaIdeal_isMeasureZeroSuppAll`, `isSigmaIdeal_isMeasureZeroSupp`), and `S
    ≠ ∅` is not null (`not_isMeasureZeroSuppAny_orbitSupp`, `not_isMeasureZeroSupp_orbitSupp`). The proof rests
    on the transfer property, two sheets inducing the same null sets on their overlap, which does not hold
    across dimensions: the axis `ℝ × 0` has measure zero in the sheet `ℝ²` and not in itself
    (`isNull_transfer_mixed_dim`). So the lemma is proved for structures with sheets in one class, as for the
    `n`-dimensional structures of an `n`-dimensional `Θ`; for every structure of an `n`-dimensional `Θ` it would
    need Proposition 9.1.12 in general (gap G.97). Status: **settled** for one class, and (2026-11-12, below) for
    every structure of an `n`-dimensional `Θ` (gap G.106 closed).
    (2026-11-09) Proposition 9.1.12 now holds for every ep-groupoid (item 9); Lemma 9.5.2 for every structure of an
    `n`-dimensional `Θ` is not restated with it (gap G.106).
    (2026-11-09) In the sheets of a tame branching structure of dimension `n` the null sets of Definition 9.4.5 are now
    Mathlib's (item 109; gap G.106 in part); the statement is not restated with them.
    (2026-11-12) With the null sets `IsHNull`, Lemma 9.5.2 holds for every local branching structure of an
    `n`-dimensional `Θ` (`lemma_9_5_2_of_isNDimensional`, `lemma_9_5_2_tame`): every local branching structure of such
    a `Θ` has `n`-dimensional sheets (`isOfDim_of_isNDimensional`). Across dimensions the transfer still does not hold
    as we read it (`isHNull_mixed_dim`). Row V9.50 explicit; gap G.106 closed; item 116.

    *(Definition 9.5.3 and the remark after it, p. 438 (2017: Definition 9.16, p. 323))*. For a σ-ideal `𝒩` the
    σ-algebra generated by the Borel sets and `𝒩` is `{A | A ∆ B ∈ 𝒩 for a Borel B}` (`borelNullSigma`,

    `isSigmaIdeal_measureZeroSets`), and the remark that it is obtained by adding the sets of measure zero is
    read as `K ∈ L(S) ⟺ K ∆ B` null for a Borel `B` (`remark_9_5_3`,
    `measurableSet_lebesgueSigma_of_isMeasureZeroSupp`); the form `B ∪ N` would need Borel null hulls.
    Witnesses: for Example 9.3.5's `Θ` (`theta935`, `isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_theta935`,
    `hasTameSheetsIn_theta935`) the touching point is a nonempty set of measure zero and `S` is not null

    on `ℝ²` (`planeSheets`, `planeNull`, `thetaPlane`, `hasTameSheetsIn_thetaPlane`) some member of `L(S)` is
    not Borel, the `2^𝔠` subsets of the null axis against `𝔠` Borel sets
    (`exists_mem_lebesgueSigma_not_borel_thetaPlane`). Status: **settled**.

103. **`SheetGeometry` is not tied to the geometry of the sheets** *(§9.4; round-trip items V9.42, V9.45–V9.48)*.
     The fields of `MPolyfold.SheetGeometry` (item 72) say nothing about the M-polyfold structure near a sheet.
     On `discretePolyfold` of a set with extra tag points, one for each pair of sheets, "essential" and "null"
     defined combinatorially satisfy every field (`RoundTrip/Items/V9_46.lean`, `tG`). The §9.4 theorems stated
     for a `SheetGeometry` therefore follow from its fields alone. The blind statements of the audit use
     concrete notions (sheets as embedded Mathlib manifolds, null sets in charts), and those comparisons come out
     incomparable. The same holds for `SheetNullSets` in §9.5 (item 80; items V9.50–V9.52): Lemma 9.5.2 is its
     field `isNull_transfer`. For locally Hausdorff-null sets, the σ-ideal and "a sheet is not null in itself"
     need the sheets to be second countable and the `n`-dimensional sheets to have positive measure. The project
     proves neither. Status: **settled** for the M-polyfold sheets (2026-11-12, below; gap G.105 closed); the abstract
     forms are kept.
     (2026-11-12) For the `n`-dimensional submanifolds of an M-polyfold, `MPolyfold.sheetGeometry` and `sheetNullSets`
     are built from the geometry of the sheets (essential points in M-polyfold charts, `IsHNull`), with no hypothesis,
     and the σ-ideal and "a sheet is not null in itself" asked above hold (`isHNull_iUnion`,
     `not_isHNull_of_hasDimAt`); so `SheetGeometry` is tied to the geometry of the sheets for this instance (item
     116).

104. **Proposition 9.6.5 (1) read literally** *(Proposition 9.6.5, pp. 456–457; round-trip item V9.62)*. With
     the printed `I_k = I¹ ⊔ ⋯ ⊔ I^p` (item 92), each tangent class contributes `∑_{i ∈ I_k} σᵢ = Θ_k(x)`, and
     the formula becomes `Θ_k(x) = ♯(classes) · Θ_k(x)`. This does not hold as we read it once there are two
     tangent classes, e.g. for `Θ = 1_{y=0} + 1_{y=x}` on the trivial ep-groupoid over `ℝ²` at the origin
     (`RoundTrip/Items/V9_62.lean`, `not_B`). This supports reading the partition as one of `Ξ` (item 92).
     Status: **settled**.

Follow-up for the notes to the authors (2026-11-09).

105. **Proposition 9.1.11: uniqueness for the decomposition the proof constructs** *(Proposition 9.1.11,
     pp. 407–408 (2017: Proposition 9.2, p. 297); item 8)*. A dimensional decomposition `(Θ_k)` is *local*
     (`EpGroupoid.IsLocalDimDecomposition`, `Polyfold/Chapter9/DimDecompositionUnique.lean`) when near every
     point `x` of `supp(Θ)` some local branching structure `B` of `Θ` at `x`, with a labelling of its
     submanifolds by their dimensions, has `Θ_k = B.dimPart dim k` for every `k`; this is the form the proof
     of the text builds. Given Proposition 9.1.12, two local dimensional decompositions are equal
     (`isDimDecomposition_unique`; off `supp(Θ)` all `Θ_k` vanish,
     `IsDimDecomposition.eq_zero_of_not_mem_supp`), hence with no hypothesis over `ℝᵐ`
     (`proposition_9_1_11_unique_rn`) and under the graph representation in general
     (`proposition_9_1_11_unique_of_hasGraphChartAt`). In the counterexample of item 8, `Θ_1 = 1_L` is local
     (`decompB_isLocalDimDecomposition`, so the condition can be met) and `Θ_0 = 1_{0}`, `Θ_1 = 1_{L∖0}` is
     not (`decompA_not_isLocalDimDecomposition`). The uniqueness of Proposition 9.1.11 thus holds when
     "uniquely" is read among local decompositions. The global gluing of the local `Θ_k` stays gap G.96.
     Status: **settled** (uniqueness, in this reading). (2026-11-09: the gluing is done, over `ℝᵐ` with no hypothesis, item 106.)
     (2026-11-09) The uniqueness of the local decomposition holds for every ep-groupoid (`proposition_9_1_11_unique`;
     item 107).

106. **Proposition 9.1.11: existence, and the proposition for local decompositions (gap G.96 closed over `ℝᵐ`)**
     *(Proposition 9.1.11, pp. 407–408 (2017: Proposition 9.2, p. 297); items 8, 105; gap G.96)*.
     `Polyfold/Chapter9/DimDecompositionExists.lean`. `EpGroupoid.dimComponent Θ k y` is the `k`-dimensional part at
     `y` of a labelled local branching structure at `y` (`0` if there is none); by Proposition 9.1.12 it does not
     depend on the choice (`dimComponent_eq_self`) and equals `B.dimPart dim k` on all of `U(x)`
     (`dimComponent_eq_of_mem`). It is a functor (`isFunctorial_dimComponent`, by transport of the labelled structure
     along morphisms, `isSubmanifoldOfDim_transport`), and `|supp Θ_k|` is closed in `|supp Θ|`, hence paracompact
     (`isClosed_orbitSupp_dimComponent`, `paracompactSpace_orbitSupp_dimComponent`). Given Proposition 9.1.12 and the
     local constancy of dimension (Remark 9.1.1) along `supp Θ`, it is a local dimensional decomposition
     (`isDimDecomposition_dimComponent`, `isLocalDimDecomposition_dimComponent`), the only one
     (`existsUnique_localDimDecomposition`), and it is locally finite when the dimensions of submanifolds are bounded
     (`isLocallyFiniteFamily_dimComponent`). `EpGroupoid.Proposition_9_1_11_local` states Proposition 9.1.11 with
     "uniquely" read among local decompositions, plus local finiteness; it holds for every ep-groupoid with `X.PObj =
     rnPolyfold m` with no further hypothesis (`proposition_9_1_11_local_rn`, from `proposition_9_1_12_rn`,
     `hasLocallyConstantDimAt_rn` and `MPolyfold.rn_hasDimAt_le`), and in general under these three inputs
     (`proposition_9_1_11_local_of`). In the example of item 8 the construction gives `Θ_0 = 0`, `Θ_1 = 1_L`
     (`dimComponent_axis2`). Functoriality is proved by transport rather than through the symmetric structure of the
     text, and the paracompactness of `|supp Θ_k|`, not discussed in the proof, is derived. Left in general:
     Proposition 9.1.12 beyond the graph representation, Remark 9.1.1 beyond `ℝᵐ`, and local finiteness at points of
     `closure(supp Θ) ∖ supp Θ` without a dimension bound. Status: **settled** over `ℝᵐ`; in general, reduced to these
     three inputs.
     (2026-11-09) The proposition for local decompositions holds for every ep-groupoid: existence and uniqueness
     (`existsUnique_localDimDecomposition_general`), local finiteness at the points of `supp(Θ)`
     (`dimComponent_locallyFinite_of_mem_general`), and local finiteness everywhere under a bound on the dimensions
     (`proposition_9_1_11_local_of_le`, witness `rn_hasDimAt_le`) (item 107).

107. **The level-`0` facts on a general M-polyfold: Remark 9.1.1, Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11, invariance of domain, level-`1`
     continuity (gaps G.97, G.98, G.100 closed, G.93 in part)** *(Remark 9.1.1, p. 402; Lemma 9.2.7 (2), p. 412;
     Proposition 9.2.8 and Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11, pp. 413–417; Lemma 9.3.4, p. 423; Propositions 9.1.11, 9.1.12, Lemma
     9.6.4, Proposition 9.6.5; items 2, 9, 21, 24, 25, 53, 91, 100, 105, 106)* (2026-11-09).
     `Polyfold/Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero.lean`, `GeneralCorollaries.lean`. The text works at level `0` with "`B` is
     `C¹`" while the retraction is only sc-smooth; the estimates are proved on level `1` for the lift `1₀¹ ∘ r` of an
     sc⁺-retraction, which is `C¹` (`hasFDerivWithinAt_plusLift`), and brought down by the inclusion, the two norms
     being equivalent on the finite-dimensional tangent space. This gives Lemma 9.2.9 (`ScRetraction.exists_cone`),
     Lemmas 9.2.10 and 9.2.11 (`exists_graph_unif`, `exists_graph`, `exists_graph_ball`), invariance of domain for
     retracts with the same tangent space (`ScRetraction.eq_of_range_eq`) and the local constancy of the rank
     (`ScRetraction.eventually_finrank_eq`). In an M-polyfold: the dimension of a submanifold is locally constant
     (`hasLocallyConstantDimAt`, Remark 9.1.1), invariance of domain holds (`hasDomainInvarianceAt`), level-`1`
     coordinates are continuous along every smooth finite-dimensional submanifold (`hasContinuousLevelOneOn`), and every
     such submanifold through `x` is a graph over the admissible cone of its tangent space
     (`isGraphChartAt_goodDirections`, `hasClassGraphChartAt`). The project's earlier hypothesis `HasGraphChartAt`, one
     cone for all submanifolds through `x`, was stronger than the slice arguments need, which use the cone of one
     tangent space at a time; `HasGraphChartAt` and `HasGraphBallAt` are proved at interior points. Consequences, for
     every ep-groupoid: `TopMultiplicity` and the tangent slices at every point (`topMultiplicity`,
     `hasTangentSlicesAt`); Proposition 9.1.12 (`proposition_9_1_12`); Theorem 9.2.1 (1), the independence of `Σ σᵢ
     T_xMᵢ` (`hasIndependentTangentSums`); Lemma 9.2.7 (2) (`lemma_9_2_7_2_general`); Lemma 9.6.4 and Proposition 9.6.5
     (`lemma_9_6_4_general`, `proposition_9_6_5_general`); Proposition 9.1.11 for local decompositions, with local
     finiteness off `supp(Θ)` under a bound on the dimensions (`existsUnique_localDimDecomposition_general`,
     `proposition_9_1_11_local_of_le`); Lemma 9.3.4 with no hypothesis when `supp(Θ)` has degeneracy index `0`, and with
     the ball graph representation on `supp(Θ)` otherwise (`lemma_9_3_4_of_degIndex_eq_zero`,
     `lemma_9_3_4_of_hasGraphBallAt'`). The forms with the hypotheses are kept. Not formalized: the footnote to
     Definition 9.1.2 and "locally equidimensional" (gap G.93). Status: **settled** (rows V9.2, V9.9, V9.10, V9.14,
     V9.21, V9.22, V9.32, V9.61, V9.62).

108. **Definitions 9.3.8, 9.3.10 and Proposition 9.3.9 with the boundary operation built from `M` (gap G.103 in
     part)** *(Definition 9.3.8, p. 427 (2017: Definition 9.9); Proposition 9.3.9, p. 428; Definition
     9.3.10, p. 428 (2017: Definition 9.11); Lemma 9.3.7; items 57, 58; Chapter 11, item 45)* (2026-11-09).
     `Polyfold/Chapter9/BoundaryOperation.lean`. `T_yX` has no linear structure in Part I (gap G.7), so `T^R_yX` and the
     partial cone `C_yX` are read in a chart with a presentation of its partial quadrant (`PresentedChart`) and shown
     chart independent (`PresentedChart.exists_clm`, `isReducedVec_iff`, `isInwardVec_iff`). For tame `M`, `d_M(y)` is
     the reduced codimension `dim(T_yM / T_yM ∩ T^R_yX)` (`subDegIndex_eq_quotDim_span`, Lemma 9.3.7's proof). The
     partial cone spans `T_yM`, so at reduced codimension `1` outward vectors exist and any two differ by `e' = ce + k`,
     `c > 0`, `k ∈ T^R_yM` (`IsBoundaryAdmissible.exists_outward`, `IsBoundaryAdmissible.exists_pos`). `T_y∂M = T^R_yM`
     (`chartVec_image_boundaryCarrier`), "outward" is "in `T_yM`, not in `C_yM`" (`isOutward_iff_not_mem_partialCone`),
     and `boundaryOp` maps `T_y(M, o)` to `T^R_yM` with the frames positive after every outward vector, which is
     Definition 9.3.8 for any single one (`boundaryOp_eq`, `SubmanifoldOrientation.boundaryOp_tangent`). With it
     Proposition 9.3.9 needs no data hypothesis (`proposition_9_3_9_boundaryOp`), and the intrinsic `T̂_{∂Θ}`
     (`boundaryOrientation`, filtering by reduced codimension `1`) is (9.12) for every oriented structure and agrees
     with Chapter 9's `boundaryLift boundaryOp` for oriented tame `Θ̂` (`proposition_9_3_9_boundaryOrientation`,
     `boundaryLift_boundaryOp_eq_boundaryOrientation`). The situation occurs at the corner of `[0, ∞)`
     (`exists_isBoundaryAdmissible_halfLine`). Not formalized: that `o_{∂M}` fits continuously together along `∂M`,
     which needs the stratum `{d_M = 1}` as a smooth submanifold, the extension to the closed faces (Figure 9.1) and
     Remark 9.3.11. Status: **settled** except the continuity (gap G.103; rows V9.36–V9.38); the continuity settled
     2026-11-09 (item 110), the rest 2026-11-13 (item 119; gap G.103 closed).
     (2026-11-09) `T_xX` now carries the linear structure of Definition 2.3.14, Banach through every chart and sc at
     smooth points (gap G.7 closed, Chapter 2, item 87); this statement is not restated with it.
     (2026-11-09) The continuity of `o_{∂M}` is proved along the stratum of reduced codimension `1`, without tameness
     (item 110).

109. **Lemma 9.3.4 at boundary points; `TMᵢ` smooth in `TX`; tame sheets as Mathlib manifolds with corners and Lemma
     9.4.6 on them (gaps G.99, G.102 closed, G.105, G.106 in part)** *(Definition 9.2.12, p. 418; Lemma 9.3.4, p. 423;
     Definition 9.3.6, p. 425; Lemmas 9.4.4, 9.4.6, Definition 9.4.5, p. 431; Definition 9.5.1, Lemma 9.5.2, p. 437
     (2017: 9.6, 9.10, 9.13–9.16); items 26, 53, 55, 72, 80, 81, 107)* (2026-11-09).
     `Polyfold/Chapter9/GeneralBoundaryPoints.lean`, `TangentSubmanifoldSmooth.lean`, `MathlibManifoldBridge.lean`. (1)
     Lemma 9.3.4: the good-point input `HasOrientedGoodPointsAt` holds at every point of every M-polyfold, in every
     dimension, boundary points included (`MPolyfold.hasOrientedGoodPointsAt`): the direction off the other tangent
     spaces is taken near an admissible direction of the partial quadrant (`exists_small_cone`), and the sheets tangent
     to it are graphs over a small ball around it, uniformly in the direction (`exists_graph_unif_chart`). So two
     `n`-dimensional orientations that agree at the good points agree on `X_∞`, with no hypothesis on the boundary
     (`EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4_general`). The ball form `HasGraphBallAt`, the project's earlier hypothesis, is stronger
     than the argument needs; the forms with it are kept. Mixed dimensions: item 53. (2) Definition 9.2.12: for a smooth
     finite-dimensional submanifold `A`, `TA` is near each of its points the image of the sc⁺-retraction `Ts` of `TX`
     (`SubmanifoldData.isScPlusRetractionOn_tmap`), hence a smooth submanifold of `TX`
     (`IsSmoothSubmanifold.isSmoothSubmanifold_tangent`); with `|X|` paracompact, `TΘ` is a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of
     `TX` (`isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta_general`). The paracompactness of `|X|` is the hypothesis of
     Proposition 9.1.9 (p. 405); Definition 9.2.12 does not state it. (3) Definition 9.3.6: for a tame local branching
     structure whose sheets have dimension `n`, each `Mᵢ` with the charted space of its induced corner structure is
     `IsManifold (modelWithCornersEuclideanQuadrant n) ∞` (`TameBranchingStructure.isManifold`), the partial quadrants
     of the corner charts moved into `[0, ∞)ⁿ` (`cornerChartedSpace`). (4) On these sheets the null sets of Definition
     9.4.5 are Mathlib's, and `K ∖ K^e` is null for every `K ⊆ Mᵢ` (`TameBranchingStructure.lemma_9_4_6`,
     `lemma_9_4_6_sheet`). Not formalized: Lemma 9.4.4 for M-polyfold sheets (the field `ess_comm`), which needs the
     change of charts between the induced structures of two sheets, and Definition 9.5.1, Lemma 9.5.2 with Mathlib null
     sets. Status: **settled** for (1)–(3), and (2026-11-12, item 116) for Lemma 9.4.4 and Definition 9.5.1, Lemma
     9.5.2 on M-polyfold sheets (gaps G.105, G.106 closed) (rows V9.23, V9.32, V9.34, V9.42, V9.44).
     (2026-11-12) Lemma 9.4.4 for M-polyfold sheets and Definition 9.5.1, Lemma 9.5.2 with Lebesgue null sets are
     proved in the M-polyfold chart reading, which on a tame sheet agrees with (4) (`isHNull_iff_isMeasureZero_sheet`;
     item 116).

110. **The continuity of `o_{∂M}` along the reduced-codimension-`1` stratum, without tameness (gap G.103 in part)**
     *(Definition 9.3.8, p. 427 (2017: Definition 9.9); Definition 9.3.10, p. 428 (2017: Definition 9.11); items 57,
     58, 108)* (2026-11-09). `Polyfold/Chapter9/BoundaryOrientationContinuity2021.lean`. `boundaryStratum A` is the set
     of points where `T_yA` has reduced codimension `1` in every presented chart; for a tame induced structure it is
     `{d_A = 1}` (`boundaryStratum_eq_of_tame`). For an oriented submanifold `(A, o)` of dimension `m + 1`, `m > 0`,
     near every point of the stratum there is a frame field along it, positive for Definition 9.3.8's orientation at
     every point, with continuous chart vectors (`SubmanifoldOrientation.exists_continuous_boundaryFrames`). So
     `o_{∂A}` is an orientation along the stratum (`OrientationAlong`, `boundaryOrientation`,
     `boundaryOrientation_tame`), equal to `boundaryOp` pointwise (`boundaryOp_tangent_eq_boundaryOrientation`), and a
     `SubmanifoldOrientation` on any submanifold inside the stratum with tangent spaces `T^R_yA`
     (`OrientationAlong.toSubmanifoldOrientation`). Every sheet of dimension `m + 1` of an oriented branching structure
     carries it (`OrientedBranchingStructure.exists_boundaryOrientation`), which is the continuity used in (9.12). The
     text takes the continuity as immediate; it needs no tameness, only reduced codimension `1`. Not formalized: the
     stratum as a smooth submanifold of `∂M`, the extension to the closed faces (Figure 9.1) and Remark 9.3.11.
     Status: **settled** for the continuity (rows V9.36, V9.38; gap G.103 open in part; closed 2026-11-13, item 119).
     (2026-11-12) For a sheet with tame induced structure the stratum is open and dense in `∂M`
     (`exists_isOpen_boundaryStratum_eq`, `submanifoldBoundary_subset_closure_boundaryStratum`,
     `Polyfold/Chapter9/GapP2_DBoundaryStratum.lean`); it is not built as a submanifold of its own. Remark 9.3.11 is a
     comment, with nothing to formalize.
     (2026-11-13) The stratum is a smooth `(n−1)`-dimensional submanifold of `X`, oriented by `o_{∂M}`
     (`isSubmanifoldOfDim_stratumOne`, `stratumOrientation`, `Polyfold/Chapter9/GapP2_E6_StratumRetraction.lean`,
     `GapP2_E6_StratumTangent.lean`, `GapP2_E6_BoundaryOrientation.lean`). Item 119.

111. **Lemma 9.4.3 (gap G.104 closed)** *(Lemma 9.4.3, p. 430 (2017: Lemma 9.12, p. 316); item 71)* (2026-11-09).
     `Polyfold/Chapter9/PropertyTShrinking2021.lean`. `OrientedBranchingStructure.lemma_9_4_3`: every oriented
     branching structure has Property (T) after restriction to a smaller open `U'(x)` (`restrict`,
     `lemma_9_4_3_propertyT`), with no added hypothesis. The proof goes pair by pair
     (`SubmanifoldOrientation.exists_isOpen_pairT`): sheets of different dimensions never have equal tangent spaces
     (`HasDimAt.eq_of_submanifoldTangent_eq`); a `0`-dimensional point is isolated
     (`HasDimAt.exists_isOpen_eq_of_mem`); where the tangent spaces agree at `x` the relative orientation is locally
     constant (`exists_isOpen_tangent_eq_iff`); and tangent spaces that differ at `x` differ nearby
     (`exists_isOpen_submanifoldTangent_ne`, through continuous chart frames, `exists_chartTangent_field`). This is the
     text's argument along sequences in direct form. Status: **settled** (row V9.41; gap G.104 closed).

112. **The footnote to Definition 9.1.2 and "locally equidimensional" (gap G.93 closed)** *(Definition 9.1.2, last
     paragraph and footnote, p. 402; Remark 9.1.1; items 2, 3, 107)* (2026-11-09).
     `Polyfold/Chapter9/LocallyEquidimensional2021.lean`. At a point of `supp(Θ)` the sheets of any two local branching
     structures have the same tangent spaces and dimensions (`LocalBranchingStructure.exists_submanifoldTangent_eq`,
     `isOfDim_unique`), by the independence of the tangent sums (item 107). Hence the footnote for `Θ` with nonempty
     support: an `n`-dimensional `Θ` is not `m`-dimensional for `m ≠ n` (`definition_9_1_2_footnote`,
     `definition_9_1_2_footnote_of_ne_zero`). The footnote does not exclude `Θ = 0`, which is `n`-dimensional for every
     `n` (`isNDimensional_zero`); for it the footnote does not hold as we read it (`definition_9_1_2_footnote_zero`).
     "Locally equidimensional" is formalized as: at every point of the support some local branching structure has
     sheets of one dimension (`IsLocallyEquidimensional`); for branched `Θ` this is equivalent to the text's wording,
     every sufficiently small structure having sheets of that dimension (`isLocallyEquidimensional_iff`), and the
     dimension is locally constant on the support (`IsLocallyEquidimensional.exists_isOpen_isNDimensionalAt`). Status:
     **settled** (row V9.2; gap G.93 closed); for `Θ = 0` the footnote does not hold as we read it.

113. **Lemma 9.4.4 for M-polyfold sheets, read in M-polyfold charts (gap G.105 in part)** *(Definition 9.4.1, Lemma
     9.4.4, p. 431 (2017: Lemma 9.13, p. 317); Definition 9.4.7, p. 432; items 72, 109)* (2026-11-09).
     `Polyfold/Chapter9/SheetEssentialChart2021.lean`. Definition 9.4.1 is read in M-polyfold charts, as in the text's
     proof: `T^K_zM` is the span of the tangent cone of `ψ(K)` at `ψ(z)` (`chartRelTangent`), and the essential points
     of `K` in `M` are the limits of points of `K` where `T^K_zM = T_zM` in every chart (`chartEssentialSet`). For `K ⊆
     M`, `T^K_zM ⊆ T_zM` (`chartRelTangent_le`), and `T_zM ⊆ T^M_zM`
     (`ScRetraction.range_scDeriv_subset_span_tangentConeAt`), so every point of `M` is essential for `M ⊆ M`
     (`chartEssentialSet_self`). For `n`-dimensional `M`, `M'` the set `K = M ∩ M'` has the same essential points in
     both (`lemma_9_4_4_chart`), and at essential points `T_zM = T_zM'`
     (`submanifoldTangent_eq_of_mem_chartEssentialSet`, the note in Definition 9.4.7). Sheets of one dimension are
     needed (item 72, `lemma_9_4_4_mixed_dim`). Not formalized: Lemma 9.4.6 in this reading, which needs a null-set
     notion on M-polyfold sheets (positive measure of the image of a sheet under a tangent projection), and the
     comparison with the corner-chart reading of the bridge; so `SheetGeometry` for M-polyfold sheets is not yet built.
     Status: **settled** for Lemma 9.4.4 in the chart reading (rows V9.39, V9.42); gap G.105 closed (2026-11-12, below
     and item 116).
     (2026-11-12) Lemma 9.4.6 in this reading is `lemma_9_4_6_chart`, with the null sets `IsHNull` (item 116);
     `SheetGeometry` for M-polyfold sheets is `MPolyfold.sheetGeometry`, and on tame sheets the null sets agree with
     those of the corner-chart reading (`isHNull_iff_isMeasureZero_sheet`). The essential points of the two readings
     are not compared; no statement of §9.4–§9.5 needs it.

114. **Proposition 9.1.9 and Remark 9.1.10: readings (gaps G.94, G.95 closed)** *(Remark 9.1.4, p. 403; Proposition
     9.1.9, Remark 9.1.10, p. 405 (2017: Proposition 9.1, Remark 9.3, p. 294); items 7, 109)* (2026-11-12).
     `Polyfold/Chapter9/GapP2_CRemark914.lean`, `GapP2_CProp919.lean`, `GapP2_CDescentPolyfold.lean`,
     `GapP2_CProp919Manifold.lean`, `GapP2_C2Prop919Text.lean`, `GapP2_C2Remark9110.lean`,
     `GapP2_C2Remark9110Etale.lean`. (1) The hypothesis "`|X|` paracompact" of Proposition 9.1.9 is not used:
     Definition 9.1.2 (1) already makes `|supp(Θ)|` paracompact, hence metrizable (Remark 9.1.4,
     `remark_9_1_4_metrizable`), which Remark 9.1.10 itself observes. (2) "Natural" in (1) is read as uniqueness: any
     two M-polyfold structures on `Z = |supp(Θ)|` for which `supp(Θ) → Z` is a local sc-diffeomorphism agree
     (`proposition_9_1_9_one_unique`). (3) "Equivalent orbifold structure" in (2) is read as a generalized isomorphism
     of Chapter 10 over `Z`: two choices of local branching structures give `M_c ← M_{c,c'} → M_{c'}`, both legs
     equivalences, through the common refinement (`proposition_9_1_9_two_independent`); the text's groupoid with
     objects `⊔ M_x` is the refinement of Proposition 10.1.3 (`proposition_9_1_9_two_text`), stated for `supp(Θ) ≠ ∅`.
     (4) Remark 9.1.10 is stated for `Θ` `n`-dimensional, since a Mathlib manifold has one model space
     (`remark_9_1_10_manifold`: `IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞`). Mathlib has no notion of a classical orbifold; in case (2) the
     object and morphism spaces are Mathlib `n`-manifolds and source, target, unit and inverse are local
     diffeomorphisms (`remark_9_1_10_orbifold_etale`); the composition is sc-smooth, as for every ep-groupoid, and is
     not stated as Mathlib-smooth. No counterexample; nothing is found not to hold as we read it. Status: **settled**
     (rows V9.63 same, V9.64 restated, V9.65 narrower).

115. **Example 9.3.5: all orientations classified (gap G.101 closed)** *(Example 9.3.5, p. 425 (2017: Example 9.1, p.
     313); item 54)* (2026-11-12). `Polyfold/Chapter9/GapP2_DExample935.lean`, `GapP2_D2Example935Sheets.lean`,
     `GapP2_D2Example935Class.lean`. The orientations of `Θ` are exactly the `classOrient a`
     (`example_9_3_5_classification`): coefficients `a(s, b) ∈ [0, 1] ∩ ℚ` for the four open arcs, constant along each
     arc, with `a(+,↑) + a(+,↓) = a(−,↑) + a(−,↓)`, the weights at the origin being `A` on `(1, 0)` and `2 − A` on
     `(−1, 0)` for this common sum `A`. So there are infinitely many (`example_9_3_5_infinite`), a three-parameter
     family, and the six orientations given by signs on the two structures (four on each, the two with all signs equal
     in common, `orientedLift1_eq_orientedLift2_iff`, `ncard_signOrientations`) are those with integer weights
     (`example_9_3_5_integral`, `example_9_3_5_integral_ncard`). "Four different possibilities" holds for each
     structure separately; for `Θ` it does not hold as we read it. The rigidity at the origin comes from the
     one-dimensional submanifolds of `ℝ²` inside `supp(Θ)` through `0`: each has tangent line `ℝ(1, 0)` there and
     meets every vertical line near `0` (`Ex935.submanifoldTangent_eq_of_subset_Z`, `Ex935.exists_mem_fst_eq`).
     Status: **settled** (row V9.33, narrower).

116. **The sheets of an M-polyfold: chart changes, essential points, null sets (gaps G.105, G.106 closed)**

     the definition is independent of the chart of `M`; the proof of Lemma 9.4.4 reads `T^K_zM` in an M-polyfold chart

     continuous, so the independence of the M-polyfold chart is not immediate. It holds because the points of `ψ(M)`
     lie on level `1` with level-`1` distance bounded by the level-`0` distance (the chart retraction of `M` is sc⁺)
     and the transition is differentiable from level `1` to level `0` (`ScRetraction.exists_lift_lipschitz`,
     `ScRetraction.hasFDerivWithinAt_of_isSc1`, `exists_hasFDerivWithinAt_transition`); so
     `isRelTangentFull_of_chart`. The same fact makes Definition 9.4.5 chart independent: `IsHNull` (the

     hypothesis (`sheetGeometry`, `sheetNullSets`; a nonempty sheet is not null, `not_isHNull_of_hasDimAt`). (3) Every

     `proposition_9_4_9_of_isNDimensional` with Property (T), `proposition_9_4_10_of_isNDimensional`), and Lemma 9.5.2
     holds as stated (`lemma_9_5_2_of_isNDimensional`). On a tame sheet `IsHNull` is Lebesgue measure zero in the
     smooth charts of the manifold with corners (`isHNull_iff_isMeasureZero_sheet`). No counterexample; nothing is
     found not to hold as we read it. Status: **settled** (rows V9.42–V9.44, V9.46–V9.51; V9.50 explicit).
