120. **§9.5 completed: the boundary measures and Stokes' theorem with the text's hypotheses, `n = 1`, and Remark
     9.5.20 in part (gap G.109 closed, G.110 in part)** *(Theorems 9.5.15–9.5.18, pp. 449–451; Remark 9.5.20, pp.
     451–452)* (2026-11-13). `Polyfold/Chapter9/GapP3_K1_*.lean`, `GapP3_K2_*.lean`, `GapP3_K3_*.lean`. (1) *The class
     condition near the corners.* Item 119 (9) recorded that the text integrates over `∂₁Mᵢ` without saying that these
     integrals are finite near the corners of `Mᵢ`. This holds for every oriented tame structure, so the condition is
     a tacit step, not an added hypothesis. Near a sheet's own corners, Part I's chart forms of `ω ∈ Ωᵐ_{ep,∞}` are
     continuous up to the corners, and on a face set of a corner chart `|ev ω|` is `|det|` times the face pull-back,
     integrable on the preimage of a compact set (`FormEval.boundaryStratum_inter_mem_msheets`, `abs_ev_faceFrame`,
     `integrableOn_facePullback_of_isCompact`); a structure is shrunk into a closed neighbourhood, and `Mᵢ ∩ K` is
     compact because `Mᵢ → U` is proper (`exists_restrict_boundary_mem_msheets`, `isCompact_M_inter`). Toward the
     frontier of `U(x)`, `HasTameInducedStructure` does not give `d_{Mᵢ} = d_X`, and it is not needed, since `{d = 1}`
     depends only on the tangent space: at each point of `∂₁Mᵢ` a sheet of another structure has the same tangent
     space, by the null-set argument of Lemma 9.4.6 (`MPolyfold.k1_exists_tangent_eq`), so `∂₁Mᵢ` lies in finitely
     many boundary sheets of good structures (`EP.boundarySheet_mem_msheets_of_loc`). Hence Theorems 9.5.15–9.5.18
     hold for `n ≥ 2` with the text's hypotheses only, with the local formula for every structure
     (`EP.theorem_9_5_15`, …, `EP.theorem_9_5_18`). (2) *`n = 1`.* The boundary sheets are finite sets of points;
     `ω ∈ Ω⁰_{ep,∞}(X)` is read as a function on objects (`EP.zeroFormEval`), and `∫ ω|(∂₁Mᵢ, o)` over a finite set is
     the signed sum `Σ ±ω(p)`, the reading of the text's integral in dimension 0 (`EP.finZeroFormIntegration`); Part
     I's boundary integral of a 1-dimensional sheet is this value (`boundaryIntegral_eq_pointInteg`). Each `∂₁Mᵢ` is
     finite by the covering argument of (1) (`EP.boundarySheet_finite_of_loc`), and Theorems 9.5.15–9.5.18 hold for
     `n = 1` (`EP.theorem_9_5_15_dim1_all`, `EP.theorem_9_5_16_dim1_all`, `EP.theorem_9_5_17_dim1`,
     `EP.theorem_9_5_18_dim1_isLUC`). (3) *Witnesses.* The trivial ep-groupoid of the closed upper hemisphere has LUC
     (`E8W.e8w_isLUC`), so it witnesses Theorem 9.5.18 too (`E8W.k2_hemisphere_stokes_eff`); for `n = 1` the closed
     right half-circle in `[0, ∞) × ℝ`, a tame 1-dimensional sub-M-polyfold whose boundary is its two end points,
     satisfies every hypothesis with `supp ∂Θ ≠ ∅` (`K2Arc.k2_arc_hypotheses`, `K2Arc.k2_arc_stokes`,
     `K2Arc.k2_arc_stokes_eff`). Neither witness has corners, branching or nontrivial isotropy. (4) *Remark 9.5.20.*
     In finite dimensions the remark's phenomenon cannot occur: a finite group fixing a boundary point and acting
     trivially on the face acts trivially on the inward normal, so `X` must be infinite-dimensional at `(±1, 0)`. "One
     can equip `X` with an M-polyfold structure" is realized by our choice of one chart onto an sc-smooth retract of a
     partial quadrant in `ℝ² ⊕ c₀ ⊕ c₀` (the rank-one family of Remark 4.3 over the quarter circle); with it
     `∂X = {(±1, 0)}` (`K3.boundary_eq`, the lower bound by Theorem 2.4.12), `ℤ₃ ⋉ X` has LUC, `♯G^eff = 3` on `M`,
     and at a boundary point the isotropy group is `ℤ₃` read in `X` and in the sub-ep-groupoid `∂X`, with
     `♯G^eff_x = 3` in `X` and `1` in `∂X` (`K3.remark_9_5_20_effIsotropy`): these claims of the remark hold as we
     read them. Not formalized: `Θ`, `∮_Θ̂ df = ⅓(φ(1) − φ(−1))` and the two boundary integrals (estimate 2,340–3,790
     lines; the main risks are sc-smooth partitions of unity on a `c₀` scale, since Corollary 7.6.6 needs a Hilbert
     `E₀`, and the tameness of `M` at the infinite-dimensional ends), and that `∂X` is a smooth submanifold. No
     counterexample; nothing is found not to hold as we read it. Status: **settled** for Theorems 9.5.15–9.5.18 (rows
     V9.67, V9.68, restated; gap G.109 closed); Remark 9.5.20 **open** in part (gap G.110 in part).

## Chapter 10 (Equivalences and localization; Lean `Polyfold/Chapter10/`)

*Numbering.* The items of this section are numbered in blocks, one block per part of the chapter, so that agents
working at the same time do not collide; the gaps in the numbering are unused numbers, not deleted items. 1–19:
§10.1, equivalences and what they preserve (`Chapter10/Equivalence.lean`, `EquivalenceRefinement.lean`,
`EquivalenceReduced.lean`, `EquivalenceExamples.lean`, `EquivalenceZhou.lean`); 20–29: §10.2, the weak fibred
product (`WeakFibredProduct.lean`, `WeakFibredProductTheorem.lean`); 30–39: §10.3, localization at the equivalences
(`Localization.lean`, `LocalizationCategory.lean`, `LocalizationProperties.lean`); 40–49: §10.4, strong bundle
equivalences (`StrongBundleEquivalence.lean`, `StrongBundleEquivalenceNat.lean`,
`StrongBundleEquivalenceExamples.lean`); 50–59: reserved for §10.5; 60–69: Appendix §§10.6.1–10.6.2, the proofs of
Theorems 10.3.8 and 10.3.10; 70–79: witnesses and the hypotheses taken. Statement numbers and pages are those of
the Springer edition (2021, pp. 461–520), with the 2017 text's in parentheses (2017 pp. 333–374). The comparison
items are `Exposition/verification/ch10.md` (V10.1–V10.75); the gaps are G.111–G.127.

Found while formalizing §10.1 (2026-11-08).

1. **Definition 10.1.1 and Lemma 10.1.2: equivalences as a structure** *(Definition 10.1.1, p. 461 (2017:
   Definition 10.1, p. 333); Lemma 10.1.2, p. 462 (2017: Lemma 10.1, p. 334))*. `EpFunctor.IsEquivalence` has the
   four conditions as fields, full and faithful on the sets of morphisms `x → x'`; they agree with Mathlib's
   `Functor.Full`, `Functor.Faithful` of the underlying functor (`GroupoidFunctor.full_iff`, `faithful_iff`). Lemma
   10.1.2 is proved with its converse (`isEquivalence_iff`), the bijectivity of `|F|` coming from fullness and
   essential surjectivity (`bijective_orbitMap_of_isEquivalence`) and its openness from Proposition 7.1.8
   (`isOpenMap_orbitMap`). "Not invertible as a functor": the equivalence from the pair groupoid of `ℤ` to the
   point has no left inverse on objects (`not_exists_leftInverse_pairToPoint`). Status: **settled**.

2. **Proposition 10.1.3: the refinement `X_𝒰`** *(Proposition 10.1.3, p. 462 (2017: Proposition 10.1, p. 334))*.
   The covering is indexed by a type `ι` (`EpGroupoid.OpenCover`), objects and morphisms are open subsets of
   `ι × X` and `(ι × ι) × 𝐗` with `ι` discrete, and the open-subset M-polyfold structure of Part I needs a
   nonempty set: the object set is assumed nonempty (`[Nonempty Obj]`), the statement being trivial otherwise.
   Properness is proved with ultrafilters, with `V(x)` an open set whose closure lies in `U_i` and in a
   neighbourhood with the properness property of `X` (`exists_isProperMap`). The formula for the functor prints the
   morphism as `(U, φ, v)`; we read `(U, φ, V)` (possible misprint). Witness: the covering `{x > -1}`,
   `{x < 1}` of `ℤ/2 ⋉ ℝ`, whose functor is an equivalence not injective on objects
   (`isEquivalence_reflectionCover`, `not_injective_reflectionCover_obj`). Status: **settled**.

3. **Definition 10.1.4 is Definition 8.1.13** *(Definition 10.1.4, p. 463 (2017: Definition 10.2, p. 335))*.
   Natural transformations and `NaturallyEquivalent` are Chapter 8's; the claims after the definition (equivalence
   relation, compatibility with composition) are `naturallyEquivalent_equivalence`,
   `NaturallyEquivalent.comp_left`, `comp_right`, collected in `definition_10_1_4`. Status: **settled**.

4. **Proposition 10.1.5, quoted without proof, is proved** *(Proposition 10.1.5, p. 464 (2017: Proposition 10.2, p.
   336))*. `τ` is a local sc-diffeomorphism because `s ∘ τ = F` (`EpNatTrans.isLocalScDiffeo_app`), so
   `G = t ∘ τ` is one on objects, and the underlying functors are naturally isomorphic (`EpNatTrans.toNatIso`);
   Lemma 10.1.2 concludes (`proposition_10_1_5`). Status: **settled**.

5. **Proposition 10.1.6: the object step covers only the image of `F`** *(Proposition 10.1.6, p. 464 (2017:
   Proposition 10.3, p. 336))*. The text's argument shows that `Φ` is a local sc-diffeomorphism at the points
   `F(x)`. A point `y` of `Y` is reached by a morphism `F(x) → y`, and the property is transported along it: a
   functor that is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects at `s(σ)` is one at `t(σ)` (`isLocalScDiffeoAt_obj_tgt`).
   The proof also writes `|Φ| : |X| → |Y|` for `|Φ| : |Y| → |Z|` (possible misprint). Status: **settled**
   (a step supplied).

6. **Theorem 10.1.7: fullness and faithfulness of `TF`** *(Theorem 10.1.7, p. 465 (2017: Theorem 10.1, p. 337))*.
   Left to the reader in the text, they are proved from the facts that a tangent morphism is determined by its base
   morphism and its source vector (`tangent_ext`) and that `TF` is injective on, and onto, tangent fibres
   (`IsLocalScDiffeo.injOn_tangentFiber`, `tangentFiber_subset_image`) (`theorem_10_1_7`). Status: **settled**.

7. **Not formalized in §10.1: `EP_lreg`, Remark 10.1.8, Propositions 10.1.9 and 10.1.10** *(p. 461; Remark 10.1.8,
   p. 467; Proposition 10.1.9, p. 468; Proposition 10.1.10, p. 470 (2017: Proposition 10.4, p. 340))*. Remark
   10.1.8 and its example in Appendix §10.6.3 need the weighted Sobolev sc-structure and sc-retraction of the
   appendix (gap G.112). Proposition 10.1.9, new in 2021, transports a natural representation along `F` and a
   morphism `F(x) → y`; the Chapter 7 API of natural representations has no such transport (gap G.113), and with it
   the subcategory `EP_lreg` (gap G.111) and Proposition 10.1.10, which assumes (LR) and uses 10.1.9 (gap G.114),
   remain open. Formalized since: Propositions 10.1.9 and 10.1.10 (item 16); and since 2026-11-12 `EP_lreg`
   (`EP.lreg`, `EP.Lreg`, `GapP2_F_LReg.lean`; row V10.74) and Remark 10.1.8 with Appendix §10.6.3 as printed, on the
   appendix's scale `ℝ ⊕ H^{m,δ_m}(ℝ)` with its projections (`ZhouTenSix.remark_10_1_8`, `ZhouTenSix.not_isLR`,
   `GapP2_A2TenSix.lean`; row V10.75); a variant with the moving projections of Remark 4.1.3 is kept
   (`ZhouSigma.remark_10_1_8`, `GapP2_F_ZhouExample.lean`). Status: **settled** (gaps G.111–G.114 closed).

8. **Remark 10.1.11 in a stronger form** *(Remark 10.1.11, p. 470 (2017: Remark 10.1, p. 340))*. On `ℤ/2 ⋉ ℝ²`
   with `F = id`, `G = −id`, no family `α(z) : z → −z` with `α(0) = 1_0` is even continuous at `0`
   (`remark_10_1_11`), hence none is sc-smooth (`remark_10_1_11_scSmooth`); the family `α(z) = (−1, z)` is
   sc-smooth (`remark_10_1_11_family`), so the conclusion of Proposition 10.1.10 (1) holds in the example. Status:
   **settled**.

9. **Remark 10.1.12: `G_x → Y_y`** *(Remark 10.1.12, p. 472, new in the 2021 edition)*. The isomorphism of
   isotropy groups is printed with target `Y_y`; we read `G_y` (possible misprint). Proved: `g ∈ T_x` iff
   `F(g) ∈ T_{F(x)}` for a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects (`isotropyHom_mem_trivialSet_iff`), bijectivity for
   an equivalence, and the conjugation by `ψ : F(x) → y` (`remark_10_1_12`). Status: **settled** (possible
   misprint).

10. **Propositions 10.1.13 and 10.1.16: Theorem 7.2.22 and closures** *(Proposition 10.1.13, p. 472; Proposition
    10.1.16, p. 474; both new in the 2021 edition)*. Both proofs cite Theorem 7.2.22; the citation is to the
    theorem on p. 323 (the reduced morphism space is Hausdorff iff (LUC) iff `𝐗^T` is closed;
    `EpGroupoid.theorem_7_2_22`) and holds as cited. The closedness of `𝐗^T` passes from `X` to `Y` by
    conjugating with a local inverse of `t` at a morphism `F(x) → y`, with closures instead of the text's
    sequences (`IsEquivalence.isClosed_nonEffectivePart_iff`). Part (1) of Proposition 10.1.13 holds for every
    functor that is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects (`continuous_reducedMap`, `isOpenMap_reducedMap`). Status:
    **settled**.

11. **Proposition 10.1.14: one Hausdorff hypothesis suffices** *(Proposition 10.1.14, p. 473 (2017: Proposition
    10.5, p. 341))*. Both hypotheses `T2Space X.ReducedMor`, `T2Space Y.ReducedMor` are kept, as in the text
    (`proposition_10_1_14`); by Proposition 10.1.13 (2) either implies the other. Status: **settled**.

12. **Example 10.1.15 in a stronger form** *(Example 10.1.15, p. 474 (2017: Example 10.1, p. 341))*. No map of sets
    `f : 𝐗^R → 𝐘^R` satisfies `f([φ]) = [Φ(φ)]` (`example_10_1_15`); no topology and no Hausdorff hypothesis
    enter. Status: **settled**.

13. **Proposition 10.1.17: another route, and readings in (b)** *(Proposition 10.1.17, p. 475, new in the 2021
    edition)*. The proof uses the naturality `T(F(φ)) ∘ TF = TF ∘ Tφ` (`tangentMor_mor`), the composition
    rule for `T` and the bijectivity of `TF` on tangent fibres, instead of natural representations
    (`isZhou_of_isZhou`, `isZhou_of_isZhou_right`). In (b) the text writes `U(F(y))` and "`x ∈ U(x)`", read
    `U(F(x))` and `a ∈ U(x)`, and at the start calls the functor `Φ` where it is `F` (possible misprints). The
    `G'_y` of the text are the isotropy groups of `Y` (in the plain-text extraction the primes appear as `0`).
    Status: **settled** (possible misprints).

14. **Proposition 10.1.18: "Proposition 10.1.9"** *(Proposition 10.1.18, p. 476, new in the 2021 edition)*. The
    proof cites Proposition 10.1.9 for the step "(LUC) along `F^i`", which is Proposition 10.1.16 (possible
    misprint). The lifts `F^i` are built by iterating the level-1 restriction (`EpFunctor.liftOne`,
    `IsEquivalence.liftOne`, `EP.exists_isEquivalence_lift`). Status: **settled** (possible misprint).

15. **Proposition 10.1.19: only the reduction** *(Proposition 10.1.19, p. 477, new in the 2021 edition)*. The proof
    applies Proposition 10.1.9 to the lifts; this is a hypothesis of `EP.isSLR_iff_of_isLR_iff`, satisfied when the
    two sides agree (`EP.isLR_iff_lift_self`). The unconditional statement is gap G.115. Formalized since, with
    Proposition 10.1.9 for the lifts (`EP.proposition_10_1_19`; item 16). Status: **closed** (gap G.115, closed).

Found while closing the gaps of §§10.1, 10.3 and 10.5 (2026-11-08).

16. **Propositions 10.1.9, 10.1.10 and 10.1.19, formalized since; a reading on p. 469** *(Proposition 10.1.9, pp.
    468–470, and Proposition 10.1.19, p. 477, both new in the 2021 edition; Proposition 10.1.10, p. 470 (2017:
    Proposition 10.4, p. 340))*. Proposition 10.1.9 is proved as stated (`EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_9`). For
    `ψ : F(x) → y` the composite `Q = ψ̂ ∘ F`, `ψ̂ = t ∘ (s|𝐔(ψ))⁻¹`, is an sc-diffeomorphism of a neighbourhood of
    `x` onto one of `y` (`TransportChart`, `exists_transportChart`), `g ↦ ψ ∘ F(g) ∘ ψ⁻¹` is an isomorphism
    `G_x → G_y` (`TransportChart.conj`, `bijective_conj`), and `Q(g ∗ z) = (ψ ∘ F(g) ∘ ψ⁻¹) ∗ Q(z)` ((10.2)–(10.3);
    `TransportChart.Q_Φ`). The text takes `U(y) = Q(U(x))` "with the natural action"; that `Q(U(x))` carries a
    natural representation of `G_y` is proved by restricting an arbitrary one at `y` (Theorem 7.1.13), invariant by
    the equivariance (`exists_naturalRep_push`), and the converse direction restricts one at `x` to `Q⁻¹(U(y))`
    (`exists_naturalRep_pull`); no transport of `Γ` is needed. Reading (possible misprint): on p. 469 the
    isomorphism `σ ↦ ψ ∘ σ ∘ ψ⁻¹` is printed `G_{F(x)} → U(y)`; we read `G_{F(x)} → G_y`. Proposition 10.1.10 (1)
    is proved with (LR) for `X` only, which is all its proof uses, and with (LR) for `Y` only through Proposition
    10.1.9 (`proposition_10_1_10_one`, `proposition_10_1_10_one_of_isLR_right`); (2) is the equality of the orbit
    maps of the tangent functors (`proposition_10_1_10_two`). The families `α_z` of (1) are in general not natural
    (item 58). Proposition 10.1.19 follows from the reduction of item 15 (`EP.proposition_10_1_19`), and
    Proposition 10.3.16 and the (LR), (SLR) parts of Theorem 10.3.21 from that of item 38
    (`EPLoc.proposition_10_3_16`, `EPLoc.theorem_10_3_21_all`). The hypotheses hold on the point ep-groupoid
    (`nonempty_transportChart_pointEP`, `proposition_10_1_10_hypotheses`). Status: **settled** (possible misprint;
    gaps G.113, G.114, G.115 and G.118 closed).

17. **Theorem 10.3.19 for an effective target** *(Theorem 10.3.19, pp. 493–494 (2017: Theorem 10.7, p. 355))*. The
    strongest correct version we prove adds that `Y` is effective (`EPLoc.theorem_10_3_19_of_isEffective`). In an
    effective ep-groupoid a continuous family `v ↦ k(v) ∈ G_v` on an open set of objects is the family of units
    (`EpGroupoid.eqOn_unit_of_isEffective`), so over an effective target two continuous families
    `α_z, α'_z : H(z) → H'(z)` on an open set agree when `H` is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects
    (`EpFunctor.eqOn_of_isEffective`). The families of Proposition 10.1.10 (1) therefore glue on the whole source
    and are natural, since at a morphism `h` the family `z ↦ H'(σ(z))⁻¹ ∘ α(t(σ(z))) ∘ H(σ(z))`, with `σ` the local
    inverse of `s` through `h`, is another such family: equivalences `H, H'` with `|H| = |H'|`, (LR) on the source
    and an effective target are naturally equivalent (`naturallyEquivalent_of_isEffective`). For `e = f' ∘ f⁻¹`,
    represented by `Y ←F A →Φ Y` with `|Φ| = |F|`, this gives `F ≃ Φ`, so `e = 1_Y` and `f = f'`. The proof needs
    neither the weak fibred product nor the cover `A_𝒰` of the text. Without effectiveness the conclusion fails
    (item 58; `not_naturallyEquivalent_id_inv`). The hypotheses hold on the point
    (`theorem_10_3_19_of_isEffective_hypotheses`, `naturallyEquivalent_of_isEffective_hypotheses`). Status:
    **settled** (gap G.120, with item 58).

18. **The weak fibred product of strong bundles and the category `SEP(F⁻¹)`, formalized since** *(§10.5, p. 504
    (2017 p. 364), and Definition 10.5.1, p. 506 (2017: Definition 10.14, p. 366); Theorem 10.2.2, p. 477, Lemma
    10.3.4, p. 485, Theorem 10.3.8, p. 488 (2017: Theorem 10.2, Lemma 10.4, Theorem 10.3))*. Reading: the text
    introduces refinements and classes of diagrams of strong bundles "following our earlier construction" (p. 504)
    and calls the classes the morphisms of a category (Definition 10.5.1), but it gives no weak fibred product of
    strong bundles and no composition. We take the weak fibred product of a strong bundle equivalence `Φ : W → W'`
    and a strong bundle functor `Ψ : W'' → W'` to be the pull-back `π_Z*W''` over the weak fibred product
    `X ×_{X'} X''` of the bases (`SBWeakFibredProduct.wfpSEP`, built with `EpStrongBundle.pullbackAlong`), with
    `Π_Z` the projection and `Π_X((x, φ, z), w'') = Φ_x⁻¹(μ'(φ⁻¹, Ψ(w'')))`, a fibrewise inverse lift
    (`EpStrongBundle.invLiftFunctor`, `SEP.coneHom`). The strong bundle Theorem 10.2.2 holds: `Π_Z` is a strong
    bundle equivalence, `Φ ∘ Π_X ≃ Ψ ∘ Π_Z`, and `Π_X` is one when `Ψ` is (`theorem_10_2_2`,
    `theorem_10_2_2_right`); its claims on degeneracy indices, tameness and orbit spaces concern the bases (items
    21–24). With it the strong bundle Lemma 10.3.4 (`SDiagram.lemma_10_3_4`, `cls_eq_cls_iff`) and Theorem 10.3.8
    (`SDiagram.comp`, `IsRefinement.comp`, `Equiv.comp`, `equiv_assoc`, `equiv_comp_id`, `equiv_id_comp`) are
    proved as in §10.3 and Appendix §10.6.1; on the pull-back the squares in these proofs commute strictly, by the
    fibrewise injectivity of strong bundle equivalences. `SEP(F⁻¹)` is a category (`SEPLoc.category`) with a
    localization functor `SEP ⥤ SEP(F⁻¹)` which inverts the strong bundle equivalences (`localizationFunctor`,
    `isInvertedBy_localizationFunctor`). Witnesses over `−id`: `theorem_10_2_2_negSEPHom`, and `F ∘ F = 1` for
    `foldDiagram` (`homMk_foldDiagram_comp`, `nonempty_comp_foldDiagram`). Status: **settled** (a reading; gap G.123
    closed, with the converse of item 19).

19. **Remark 10.5.3 read as "generalized strong bundle isomorphisms are isomorphisms"** *(Remark 10.5.3, p. 506,
    new in the 2021 edition; Theorem 10.3.10, p. 489 (2017: Theorem 10.4, p. 353))*. The remark says that a result
    similar to Theorem 10.3.10 can be proved in the strong bundle case and that it is built into Definition 10.5.2.
    We read this as: a generalized strong bundle isomorphism is an isomorphism of `SEP(F⁻¹)`. That is proved: if
    `Ψ` is a strong bundle equivalence, `[W ←Φ W'' →Ψ W']` is an isomorphism and every inverse of it is
    `[W' ←Ψ W'' →Φ W]` (`SEPLoc.theorem_10_3_10`, `isIso_of_isGeneralizedIso`, `inv_homMk`, with `equiv_comp_symm`,
    `equiv_symm_comp`). Of the converse, that every isomorphism of `SEP(F⁻¹)` is represented with both legs strong
    bundle equivalences, only the base half is proved: `[D] ↦ [d]` is a functor `SEP(F⁻¹) ⥤ EP(E⁻¹)`
    (`SEPLoc.baseFunctor`), so for an isomorphism `[D]` the functor `ψ` covered by `Ψ` is an equivalence, by
    Theorem 10.3.10 (`isEquivalence_base_of_isIso`). For `Ψ` itself the converse is proved since 2026-11-12
    (`SEPLoc.equivalences_Ψ_of_isIso`, `GapP2_F2_SBConverse.lean`): from the inverse `[E]`, `[D] ∘ [E] = 1` gives the
    fibrewise injectivity of `Ψ` and `[E] ∘ [D] = 1` a strong bundle equivalence naturally equivalent to `Ψ ∘ G`;
    local right inverses at levels 0 and 1 then make `Ψ` a strong bundle equivalence
    (`SEP.equivalences_of_natEquiv_comp`). So the isomorphisms of `SEP(F⁻¹)` are exactly the generalized strong bundle
    isomorphisms (`SEPLoc.isIso_iff_isGeneralizedIso`), with this saturation argument in place of strong bundle
    versions of the claims (C1), (C2) of Appendix §10.6.2 (item 61). Witness: the class over `−id`
    (`isIso_homMk_negDiagram`). Status: **settled** (a reading; gap G.123 closed; row V10.71 same).

Found while formalizing §10.2 (2026-11-08).

20. **Definition 10.2.1: iterated fibred products, a total multiplication, `ι(h, ψ, k)`** *(Definition 10.2.1, p.
    477 (2017: Definition 10.3, p. 342))*. Objects are elements of `X ₓ×ₛ (𝐘 ₜ×_G Z)` and morphisms of the
    analogous set over `𝐗`, `𝐘`, `𝐙` (`WeakFibredProduct.Obj`, `Mor`); the multiplication is total, its value off
    composable pairs (the first argument) unused (`WeakFibredProduct.comp`). The inverse is printed
    `ι(h, ψ, k) = (h⁻¹, G(k) ∘ φ ∘ F(h)⁻¹, k⁻¹)`; we read `ψ = φ` (possible misprint). Status:
    **settled** (possible misprint).

21. **Theorem 10.2.2: the M-polyfold structures, and the admissibility** *(Theorem 10.2.2, pp. 477–481 (2017:
    Theorem 10.2, pp. 343–346))*. The text calls the sets sub-M-polyfolds of `X × 𝐘 × Z` and `𝐗 × 𝐘 × 𝐙`.
    The formal structures are the iterated sub-M-polyfold structures of Part I's fibred products with a local
    sc-diffeomorphism (Proposition 2.5.20; `PObj`, `PMor`); they agree with the structures induced directly from the
    triple products, which nothing below needs (`theorem_10_2_2_triple`, `GapP2_F_TripleProduct.lean`; gap G.116
    closed). The construction uses of `F` only that it is a
    local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, or the same of `G` (`WeakFibredProduct.Admissible`), which every
    equivalence supplies (`Admissible.of_isEquivalence_left`, `of_isEquivalence_right`). Status: **settled**; gap
    G.116 closed.

22. **Theorem 10.2.2: properness, read with the closure** *(Theorem 10.2.2, proof, p. 481 (2017 p. 346))*. The text
    shows "`t : s⁻¹(U) → X` proper"; Definition 7.1.3 (3) asks it on `s⁻¹(cl U)`, which is what is proved
    (`exists_isProperMap`), for any `F` and `G`, with the text's sequential argument. Status: **settled** (a
    reading).

23. **Theorem 10.2.2: the fullness composite** *(Theorem 10.2.2, proof, p. 482 (2017 p. 346))*. In the fullness of
    `π_Z` the text writes `φ' ∘ G(k) ∘ φ⁻¹`, which does not compose; we read
    `φ'⁻¹ ∘ G(k) ∘ φ : F(x) → F(x')` (possible misprint). Essential surjectivity is taken from that of `F`
    (`isEquivalence_projRight`). Status: **settled** (possible misprint).

24. **Theorem 10.2.2: the case of `G` an equivalence, and of both** *(Theorem 10.2.2, p. 478 (2017: Theorem 10.2,
    p. 343))*. For `G` an equivalence the text states that `π_X` is an equivalence and the degeneracy index; the
    natural equivalence `F ∘ π_X ≃ G ∘ π_Z` and the transfer of tameness and of a paracompact orbit space
    from `X` are added (`theorem_10_2_2_right`); for both, `d_X(x) = d(x, φ, z) = d_Z(z)`
    (`theorem_10_2_2_both`). An equivalence preserves the degeneracy index (`IsEquivalence.degIndex_obj`). Status:
    **settled**.

25. **Remark 10.2.3: two equivalences, and "smaller models"** *(Remark 10.2.3, pp. 482–483 (2017: Remark 10.2, p.
    347))*. Both projections are equivalences and `τ(x, φ, z) = φ` is natural (`remark_10_2_3`), with the
    witness `id`, `−id` on `ℤ/2 ⋉ ℝ²` (`remark_10_2_3_negFunctor`). The closing sentences on smaller models have
    no formal content. Status: **settled**.

Found while formalizing §10.3 (2026-11-08).

30. **Diagrams one universe up; the order of composition; (E1)** *(§10.3, pp. 483–484 (2017 pp. 347–348))*. A
    diagram `X ←F A →Φ Y` (`EPLocalization.Diagram`) contains its middle ep-groupoid as an object of `EP.{u}`,
    so it is a structure in `Type (u+1)` and its classes form a type of that universe, that of the objects of
    `EP`; no class-sized collection occurs. `d.comp e` is the text's `[e] ∘ [d]`, in Mathlib's order. (E1),
    every isomorphism of `EP` is an equivalence, is `isEquivalence_of_isIso`; (E2), (E3) are `IsEquivalence.comp`
    and `proposition_10_1_5`. Status: **settled**.

31. **Definitions 10.3.1, 10.3.3, 10.3.5 and Lemmas 10.3.2, 10.3.4 as stated** *(pp. 484–486 (2017: Definitions
    10.4–10.6, Lemmas 10.3, 10.4, pp. 348–350))*. Both examples after Definition 10.3.1 are proved
    (`isRefinement_precomp`, `isRefinement_of_naturallyEquivalent`); Lemma 10.3.4 uses the weak fibred product
    (10.11) of `H'` and `K` (`lemma_10_3_4`). Witness for Definition 10.3.5: two copies of the equivalence from the
    pair groupoid of `ℤ` to the point form a diagram equivalent to `1_pt` (`equiv_pairToPoint_id`). Status:
    **settled**.

32. **Lemma 10.3.6 and Definition 10.3.7 as stated** *(p. 488 (2017: Lemma 10.5, Definition 10.7, p. 351))*.
    `|d| = |Φ| ∘ |F|⁻¹` with `|F|⁻¹` the inverse of the homeomorphism of Definition 10.1.1 (2); naturally
    equivalent functors induce the same orbit map (`NaturallyEquivalent.orbitMap_eq`) and
    `|F ∘ H| = |F| ∘ |H|` (`EpFunctor.orbitMap_comp`). Status: **settled**.

33. **Theorem 10.3.8 as stated** *(Theorem 10.3.8, p. 488 (2017: Theorem 10.3, p. 352))*. Well-definedness,
    associativity and units (`Diagram.theorem_10_3_8`); the weak fibred product of `Φ` and `G` is admissible
    because `G` is an equivalence (`Diagram.admissible`). The proof is item 60. Status: **settled**.

34. **Definition 10.3.9 and Theorem 10.3.10 as stated** *(Definition 10.3.9, Theorem 10.3.10, p. 489 (2017:
    Definition 10.8, p. 352, Theorem 10.4, p. 353))*. Generalized isomorphisms are the isomorphisms of `EP(E⁻¹)`
    (`isGeneralizedIso_iff_isIso`). Part (2) of Theorem 10.3.10 is stated as "every inverse of `[a]` equals
    `[Y ←Φ A →F X]`" (`theorem_10_3_10`, `inv_homMk`). The proof is item 61. Status: **settled**.

35. **Proposition 10.3.11, Definition 10.3.12 and Theorem 10.3.15 as stated** *(pp. 490–492 (2017: Proposition
    10.6, Definition 10.9, Theorem 10.6, pp. 353–355))*. `EPLoc` is a one-field structure around `EP`, a large
    category with `Category.{u+1}`; `TOP` is `TopCat` (`orbitFunctor`, `theorem_10_3_15`); the metrizability of
    orbit spaces mentioned near Theorem 10.3.15 is not part of the statement. Status: **settled**.

36. **Theorem 10.3.14: the direction of a refinement; the universal property** *(Theorem 10.3.14, p. 491 (2017:
    Theorem 10.5, p. 354); p. 483)*. The proof calls `d_{Ψ∘Φ}` a refinement of (10.13) by
    `π_X : X ×_Y Y → X`. With Definition 10.3.1 as stated, the refining equivalence goes out of the
    refinement, so it is (10.13) that refines `d_{Ψ∘Φ}`; that is what is proved (`isRefinement_ofFunctor_comp`),
    and the equality of classes is unchanged. The functor `i` inverts `E` in Mathlib's sense
    (`isInvertedBy_localizationFunctor`); the universal property of the localization, mentioned on p. 483 and not a
    numbered statement, is proved since 2026-11-12 (`EPLoc.isLocalization`, `EPLoc.universal_property`,
    `GapP2_F_LocUniversal.lean`): a functor inverting `E` identifies naturally equivalent sc-smooth functors, with the
    weak fibred product `X ×_Y Y` as the cylinder (`map_eq_of_naturallyEquivalent`; gap G.117 closed). Witness:
    the equivalence from the pair groupoid of `ℤ` to the point is not an isomorphism of `EP` but its image is
    invertible (`isGeneralizedIso_pairToPoint`). Status: **settled** (a reading); gap G.117 closed.

37. **Remark 10.3.13: no formal content** *(Remark 10.3.13, p. 491, new in the 2021 edition)*. The view of `X` as
    an atlas on `|X|` is interpretive. Status: **settled**.

38. **Propositions 10.3.16, 10.3.17 and Theorem 10.3.21** *(pp. 492–495, new in the 2021 edition)*. A generalized
    isomorphism has a representative with both legs equivalences (`exists_diagram_of_isGeneralizedIso`), so a
    property invariant under equivalences is invariant under generalized isomorphisms (`iff_of_isGeneralizedIso`).
    This gives Proposition 10.3.17 and Theorem 10.3.21 for (LUC), (SLUC), (ZHOU) (`proposition_10_3_17`,
    `theorem_10_3_21`), stated as equivalences; the proof of Theorem 10.3.21 is left to the reader in the text.
    Proposition 10.3.16 and the (LR), (SLR) parts rest on Propositions 10.1.9 and 10.1.19 (gap G.118). Formalized
    since: Proposition 10.3.16 and all five parts of Theorem 10.3.21 (`proposition_10_3_16`, `theorem_10_3_21_all`;
    item 16). Status: **closed** (gap G.118, closed).

39. **Remark 10.3.18, Theorem 10.3.19 and Definition 10.3.20** *(pp. 492–494 (2017: Remark 10.3, Theorem 10.7, p.
    355))*. The equivalence of pairs `(X, β)` is an equivalence relation (`OrbitChart.Rel`, `OrbitChart.setoid`),
    with a witness (`rel_pairEP_pointEP`); the metrizability of `Z` plays no role in it and is not assumed. The
    claim that `f` is in general not unique is not formalized (gap G.119; the example behind Remark 10.1.8 is gap
    G.112). Theorem 10.3.19 rests on Propositions 10.1.10 and 10.3.16 (gap G.120). `EP_reg` and `EP_reg(E⁻¹)` are
    Mathlib full subcategories, with the point as a witness (`EPreg`, `EPLocReg`, `Examples.pointReg`). Formalized
    since: the non-uniqueness, by the example of Remark 10.5.5 (item 56); Theorem 10.3.19 does not hold as we read
    it, and holds for an effective target (items 17, 58). Status: **settled** (gap G.119 closed, gap G.120
    settled).

Found while formalizing §10.4 (2026-11-08).

40. **Definition 10.4.1: level `[1]`** *(Definition 10.4.1, p. 496 (2017: Definition 10.10, p. 357))*. `W[1]` is
    not built as an ep-groupoid in the project. Condition (1) at level `[1]` is read as
    "`|Φ| : |W[1]| → |W'[1]|` is a homeomorphism", `|W[1]|` the quotient of `W_{0,1}` with its level-1 topology
    by the orbit relation (`OneOrbitSpace`, `oneOrbitMap`); fullness and faithfulness at `[1]` are those at `[0]`
    restricted, and the local sc-diffeomorphism property at `[1]` follows from (2)
    (`IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isLocalScDiffeo_one`). Witness: the projection `(−id)*(ℝⁿ × ℝᵏ) → ℝⁿ × ℝᵏ`
    over `−id` (`isStrongBundleEquivalence_pullbackProj'`, not over the identity: `trivialNeg_obj_ne_id`). Status:
    **settled** (a reading).

41. **Pull-back and push-forward: total definitions, (10.22) and the sc-smoothness** *(pp. 496–498 (2017 pp.
    357–360))*. `Φ^*` and `Φ_*` are defined on all maps, by the zero of the fibre where the value is not in the
    right fibre (never for sections), and the push-forward with one choice of `x` and `σ : φ(x) → x'`
    (`pullback`, `pushforward`). (10.22), the independence of the choice for section functors, is proved by
    fullness of `φ` (`pushforward_eq`). The sc-smoothness of the push-forward, "easily verified" in the text, is
    proved through the local formula `Φ_*f = μ' ∘ (τ, Φ ∘ f ∘ g₁ ∘ s' ∘ τ)`
    (`exists_pushforward_local`, `isScSmoothSection_pushforward`). Status: **settled**.

42. **Proposition 10.4.2: "`f' : W' → X'`"; no sc-smoothness** *(Proposition 10.4.2, p. 497 (2017: Proposition
    10.7, p. 358))*. The section functor is printed `f' : W' → X'`; we read `f' : X' → W'` (possible
    misprint). The statement holds for all section functors, sc-smooth or not (`proposition_10_4_2`). Status:
    **settled** (possible misprint).

43. **Propositions 10.4.3 and 10.4.4 without sc-smoothness** *(Propositions 10.4.3, 10.4.4, p. 499 (2017:
    Propositions 10.8, 10.9, p. 360))*. Both hold for all section functors; the pull-back identity of 10.4.4 for
    all sections (`proposition_10_4_3`, `proposition_10_4_4`). Status: **settled**.

44. **Theorem 10.4.5: the `Γ⁺` display; the Fred part** *(Theorem 10.4.5, pp. 500–501 (2017: Theorem 10.8, p.
    362))*. The second display, about `Γ⁺`, has `Φ^* : Γ(P', μ') → Γ(P, μ)`; we read `Γ⁺` (possible
    misprint). Proved: mutually inverse bijections of sc-smooth section functors, equality for `|Φ| = |Ψ|`, and
    the preservation of sc⁺-section functors (`theorem_10_4_5`). The preservation of sc-Fredholm section functors
    needs the invariance of `StrongBundle.IsScFredholmSection` under local strong bundle isomorphisms, of which
    Part I has only chart-level germ statements (gap G.121). Status: **settled** (possible misprint); gap G.121
    open.
    (2026-11-09) The Fred part is proved (`EpStrongBundle.theorem_10_4_5_fred`,
    `Polyfold/Chapter10/FredholmEquivalence.lean`): a local strong bundle isomorphism carries sc-Fredholm germs to
    sc-Fredholm germs in the transported chart (`StrongBundle.LocalIso.isScFredholmGerm`, `transportChart`), so
    Definition 3.1.18 is local (`isScFredholmSection_of_forall`, `Polyfold/Chapter3/FredholmPullbackIso.lean`), and the
    action of a morphism is such an isomorphism (`exists_localIso_mor`). Status now: **settled**; gap G.121 closed (row
    V10.27).

45. **Propositions 10.4.6 and 10.4.7** *(pp. 501–502, new in the 2021 edition)*. The strong bundle versions of
    Propositions 10.1.9 and 10.1.10; the proof of 10.4.6 is left to the reader in the text. Not formalized, with
    their ep-groupoid versions (gap G.122). The ep-groupoid versions are formalized since (item 16); the strong
    bundle versions need the transport `H_ψ̂` as a strong bundle isomorphism at levels 0 and 1 and the inverse of a
    strong bundle isomorphism on an open set, which the strong bundle API (composition and restriction only) does not
    provide. Status: see the last line.
    (2026-11-09) Proposition 10.4.7 is formalized on the bases with `IsLRLocal`; what Proposition 10.4.6 needs is item
    74.
    (2026-11-12) Both formalized: `EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_6`, `EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_7`
    (`GapP2_GBundleLR.lean`, `GapP2_GBundleFamily.lean`), with `IsLRLocal` (item 72); the missing inverse of a local
    strong bundle isomorphism is `IsLocalIsoOn.exists_isLocalIso₂`, the transport
    `IsStrongBundleEquivalence.exists_transport`. Status: **settled** (gap G.122 closed; rows V10.72, V10.73).

46. **Definitions 10.4.8, 10.4.10 and Remark 10.4.9: `T` as data; `μ` for `μ'`** *(pp. 502–503 (2017: Definitions
    10.11, 10.12, Remark 10.4, pp. 362–363))*. `T` carries no smoothness in Definition 10.4.8, as in the text
    (`StrongBundleNatTrans`). The second line of (10.23) is printed with `μ`; we read `μ'` (possible misprint;
    `StrongBundleNatTrans.obj_eq`). The determination of `Ψ` as a functor by `Φ` and `τ`, and the direction
    Definition 10.4.10 ⇒ Definition 10.4.8, need `Ψ` (and `Φ`) to be strong bundle functors (`unique_functor`,
    `IsStrongBundleNatTransMap.toNatTrans`). Naturally equivalent strong bundle functors induce the same orbit map
    (`StrongBundleNatEquiv.orbitMap_eq`). Status: **settled** (possible misprint).

47. **Definition 10.4.11: morphisms of `SEP` are pairs** *(Definition 10.4.11, p. 503 (2017: Definition 10.13, p.
    364))*. A morphism carries both `φ` and `Φ` (`SEP.Hom`), since `Φ` determines `φ` only on the image of `P`; the
    strong bundle equivalences form a multiplicative class mapped into `E` (`SEP.equivalences`,
    `SEP.toEP_map_mem_equivalences`). Status: **settled**.

Found while formalizing §10.5 (2026-11-08). Its comparison items are V10.51–V10.61; its gaps are G.123–G.127.

50. **Diagrams of strong bundles, refinements and classes** *(§10.5, p. 504 (2017 p. 364))*. A diagram
    `W ←Φ W'' →Ψ W'` of strong bundles over ep-groupoids, with `Φ` a strong bundle equivalence, is a structure
    (`SDiagram`). Refinements are by strong bundle equivalences `H` with natural equivalences of strong bundle
    functors (`IsRefinement`, `precomp`, `isRefinement_of_natEquiv`), and refining is reflexive and transitive
    (`IsRefinement.refl`, `IsRefinement.trans`). The text defines the classes "following our earlier construction".
    The transitivity of having a common refinement, the strong bundle version of Lemma 10.3.4, needs a weak fibred
    product of strong bundles over ep-groupoids, which neither the text nor the project constructs. The classes are
    therefore taken in `Quot SDiagram.Equiv`, for the generated equivalence relation (`GenSBMap`,
    `cls_eq_cls_of_equiv`). They are the text's classes as soon as the relation is transitive, and every map
    defined on them below is well defined for the generated relation. Formalized since: the transitivity, with the
    weak fibred product of strong bundles, so that the generated relation is having a common refinement
    (`SDiagram.lemma_10_3_4`, `cls_eq_cls_iff`; item 18). Status: **closed** (gap G.123 closed, with the converse of
    item 19).

51. **`[d]`, `|[D]|` and the square `|D|`** *(§10.5, pp. 504–505 (2017: Remark 10.5, pp. 364–365))*. A diagram of
    strong bundles gives a diagram of the base ep-groupoids and one of the total spaces (`SDiagram.base`,
    `SDiagram.total`), compatible with refinement and equivalence (`IsRefinement.base`, `Equiv.base`,
    `Equiv.total`), hence the classes `[d]` and the total class (`GenSBMap.base`, `GenSBMap.total`). `|[D]|` is the
    orbit map of the total diagram (`orbitMap_eq_total`, `continuous_orbitMap`), and
    `|P'| ∘ |[D]| = |[d]| ∘ |P|` (`SDiagram.orbitMap_square`, `GenSBMap.orbitMap_square`). Reading (possible
    misprint): the bottom arrow `[d]` of (10.24) (p. 504) and `|[d]|` of the square `|D|` (p. 505) are printed
    `X → X` and `|X| → |X|`, as is the bottom arrow of the diagram after Remark 10.5.3 (p. 506), in both
    editions; we read `X'`. The symbolic diagram (10.24) has no formal content, and its version with generalized
    vertical maps, left to the reader, is not formalized. Status: **settled** (possible misprint; the diagram with
    generalized vertical maps is gap G.124).
    (2026-11-12) (10.24) with the generalized maps `i(P)`, `i(P')` as vertical arrows commutes in `EP(E⁻¹)`
    (`SDiagram.square_10_24`, `GenSBMap.square_10_24`, `GapP2_GDiagram.lean`); gap G.124 closed.

52. **The homomorphism `γ : G_x → G'_{x'}`** *(§10.5, p. 505 (2017 p. 365))*. Formalized for every diagram
    `X ←φ X'' →ψ X'` of ep-groupoids (`Diagram.isotropyHom`, `isotropyHom_spec`): for `x, x'` with
    `|[d]|(|x|) = |x'|` there are `x''`, `a : φ(x'') → x` and `b : ψ(x'') → x'` (`exists_isotropyData`),
    and `γ(g) = b ∘ ψ(k) ∘ b⁻¹` for the `k` with `φ(k) = a⁻¹ ∘ g ∘ a`. It is a group homomorphism, and
    a group isomorphism when `ψ` is an equivalence (`bijective_isotropyHom`; added). The 2021 text has the first
    step `g ↦ a⁻¹ ∘ g ∘ a`, the 2017 text `a ∘ g ∘ a⁻¹`; the 2021 form is used. The equivariant germ `q` and its lift
    `Q` of (10.25) depend on the representative, and the text uses no property of them; since 2026-11-12 they are
    formalized for each choice of data (`Diagram.exists_germ_q`, `SDiagram.exists_lift_Q`, `GapP2_GDiagram.lean`,
    `GapP2_GDiagramLift.lean`). Status: **settled** (gap G.124 closed).

53. **Definitions 10.5.1, 10.5.2 and Remark 10.5.3** *(p. 506 (2017: Definitions 10.14, 10.15, p. 366); Remark
    10.5.3 new in the 2021 edition)*. The objects of `SEP(F⁻¹)` are the strong bundles over ep-groupoids and its
    morphisms the generalized strong bundle maps (`SEPLoc`), with identities and the prefunctor from `SEP`
    (`SEPLoc.idHom`, `localizationPrefunctor`, `localizationPrefunctor_map_id`). The composition is not
    constructed, since it needs the weak fibred product of strong bundles, so `SEPLoc` is a quiver, not a category.
    Definition 10.5.2 is formalized as stated (`GenSBMap.IsGeneralizedIso`; `isGeneralizedIso_ofHom`,
    `isGeneralizedIso_symm`). The strong bundle version of Theorem 10.3.10, which Remark 10.5.3 says can be proved
    and builds into Definition 10.5.2, needs that composition and is not formalized; what is proved is its
    consequence for the base and the total spaces, through Theorem 10.3.10: `[d]` and the total class are
    generalized isomorphisms, and `|[D]|` is a homeomorphism (`remark_10_5_3`). Formalized since: the composition,
    so that `SEPLoc` is a category (`SEPLoc.category`; item 18), and Remark 10.5.3 in the reading of item 19
    (`SEPLoc.isIso_of_isGeneralizedIso`). Status: **closed** (gap G.123 closed, with the converse of item 19,
    `SEPLoc.isIso_iff_isGeneralizedIso`).

54. **The push-forward along a diagram does not depend on the representative** *(§10.5, p. 507 (2017 p. 367))*. For
    a diagram with both legs strong bundle equivalences, `D_*f = Ψ_*Φ^*f` and `D^*g = Φ_*Ψ^*g`
    (`SDiagram.pushforward`, `SDiagram.pullback`). The text's step, along a refinement through Propositions
    10.4.2–10.4.4, is proved as printed (`pushforward_eq_of_isRefinement`). Since the classes are those of the
    generated relation, the independence is proved through orbit spaces instead: a section functor `g` is
    determined by the orbits `|g(x')|` (`π_eq_π_of_isFunctorialSection`, `eq_of_forall_π_eq`), and
    `|(D_*f)(x')| = |[D]|(|f(x)|)` when `|[d]|(|x|) = |x'|` (`π_pushforward`), so two diagrams with the same
    `|D|` have the same push-forward and the same pull-back (`pushforward_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`,
    `pullback_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`). This is stronger than the text's step. Status: **settled**.

55. **Theorem 10.5.4 without the Fred part** *(Theorem 10.5.4, pp. 507–508 (2017: Theorem 10.9, p. 367))*. For a
    generalized strong bundle isomorphism `[D]`, with a representative chosen once (`GenSBMap.rep`), `[D]_*` and
    `[D]^*` agree with those of every representative with both legs strong bundle equivalences (`pushforward_eq`,
    `pullback_eq`). They are mutually inverse bijections of `Γ` and of `Γ⁺`, and `[D]^*` is the push-forward along
    the inverse diagram; `|[D]| = |[D']|` gives `[D]_* = [D']_*` and `[D]^* = [D']^*` (`theorem_10_5_4`,
    `invOn_pullback_pushforward`, `bijOn_pushforward`, `bijOn_pushforward_plus`). "Isomorphism" of the vector
    spaces `Γ` is read as mutually inverse bijections: `Γ(P, μ)` has no vector space structure in the project, so
    the linearity is not stated. The preservation of sc-Fredholm section functors is not formalized, as for Theorem
    10.4.5 (G.121). Status: **open** (gap G.125).
    (2026-11-09) The Fred part is proved (`SBLocalization.GenSBMap.theorem_10_5_4_fred`), from that of Theorem 10.4.5
    (item 44); gap G.125 closed. The linearity remains unstated (row V10.59).
    (2026-11-09) The linearity is proved: `GenSBMap.pushforwardEquiv` is a linear isomorphism (item 73).

56. **Remark 10.5.5: an example** *(Remark 10.5.5, p. 508, new in the 2021 edition)*. The text gives no example.
    The positive half, `|[D]| = |[D']|` giving `[D]_* = [D']_*`, is the last assertion of Theorem 10.5.4
    (`pushforward_inv_eq_pushforward_id` for the example below). For the negative half, `W = ℝ × ℝᵏ → ℝ` over
    `ℤ/3 × ℝ ⇉ ℝ` (trivial action, `μ((g, x), w) = w`; `z3EpBundle`) with the strong bundle equivalence
    `Inv` covering `(g, x) ↦ (g⁻¹, x)` (`z3InvHom`, `z3InvHom_mem_equivalences`) gives `|[Inv]| = |[1_W]|`
    and `[Inv] ≠ [1_W]` (`remark_10_5_5`, `orbitMap_ofHom_z3InvHom`). The classes are separated by a new
    invariant, `Diagram.IsotropyRel`, the union of the graphs of the homomorphisms `γ` over all choices
    (`isotropyRel_isotropyHom`), unchanged under refinement and equivalence (`IsRefinement.isotropyRel_iff`,
    `Equiv.isotropyRel_iff`): for `[1]` the generator of `G_0` is related to itself, for `[Inv]` only to its
    inverse (`isotropyRel_id`, `not_isotropyRel_inv`). Already the base classes differ, with the same orbit map
    (`base_orbitMap_ofHom_z3InvHom`); by Remark 10.5.3 they are two distinct generalized isomorphisms, the
    non-uniqueness claimed in Remark 10.3.18 (item 39). `[Inv] ≠ [1]` is proved for the generated relation, so it
    holds for the text's classes too. Status: **settled** (gap G.119 closed).

57. **Proposition 10.5.6: only the reduction** *(Proposition 10.5.6, p. 508, new in the 2021 edition)*. A property
    of strong bundles that is invariant under strong bundle equivalences is invariant under generalized strong
    bundle isomorphisms (`GenSBMap.iff_of_isGeneralizedIso`), which is the text's argument. For the local regularity
    property this needs Proposition 10.4.6, formalized since 2026-11-12 with Definition 8.4.2 read as `IsLRLocal`
    (`EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_6`, item 45), so Proposition 10.5.6 holds in that reading
    (`SBLocalization.proposition_10_5_6`; row V10.61 same). Readings (possible
    misprints): "see Proposition 10.4.7 for the appropriate modification" (p. 508) is read as Proposition 10.4.6,
    the statement used; in Proposition 10.4.6 (p. 501), "`Φ : W → W`" is read `Φ : V → W`. Status: **settled** (gap
    G.126 closed; the two readings above are reading points).

58. **Theorems 10.3.19 and 10.5.7 do not hold as we read them** *(Theorem 10.3.19, pp. 493–494 (2017: Theorem 10.7,
    p. 355); Theorem 10.5.7, p. 508 (2017: Theorem 10.10, p. 367))*. Both statements are formalized as propositions
    (`EPLoc.Theorem_10_3_19`, `SBLocalization.Theorem_10_5_7`), and their negations are proved
    (`not_theorem_10_3_19`, `not_theorem_10_5_7`). The example is that of Remark 10.5.5 (item 56).
    `X = ℤ/3 × ℝ ⇉ ℝ` with the trivial action has the local regularity property of Definition 7.4.19: its orbits
    are points, so every orbit-preserving `β` is the identity, the action of `1`
    (`EpGroupoid.Examples.isLR_trivialZ3`); the strong bundle `ℝ × ℝᵏ → ℝ` over it with the trivial `μ` has that of
    Definition 8.4.2 (`isLR_z3EpBundle`). `[X ←1 X →Inv X]` and `[1_X]` are generalized isomorphisms with the same
    orbit map that differ (`theorem_10_3_19_counterexample`), and so are the strong bundle classes
    (`remark_10_5_5`). The step of the proof that we cannot follow is on p. 494: Proposition 10.1.10 (1) gives
    families `α_z : H(z) → H'(z)` depending sc-smoothly on `z`, and the proof uses them as a natural transformation
    `H_𝒰 → H'_𝒰`. In the example `z ↦ 1_z : z → Inv(z)` is such a family, but there is no natural transformation
    `1 → Inv` (`not_naturallyEquivalent_id_inv`): naturality at a generator `g` of `G_z = ℤ/3` would give
    `g = g⁻¹`. The example is not effective (`not_isEffective_trivialZ3`); with an effective target Theorem 10.3.19
    holds (item 17). The proof of Theorem 10.5.7, "immediately from Proposition 10.4.7", meets the same step; a
    version for effective strong bundles is not formalized. The 2017 Theorems 10.7 and 10.10, which have no local
    regularity hypothesis, do not hold as we read them either. Status: **settled** (does not hold as we read it;
    gaps G.120 and G.127 settled).

59. **Witnesses; no hypothesis taken** *(§10.5)*. No hypothesis beyond the text is taken in §10.5. Every definition
    has a witness that is not an identity: `negDiagram`, a generalized strong bundle isomorphism between two
    different strong bundles over `−id` (`isGeneralizedIso_negDiagram`), with Theorem 10.5.4 for it
    (`bijOn_pushforward_negDiagram`); `foldDiagram`, which refines the identity (`isRefinement_foldDiagram`,
    `cls_foldDiagram`) and has the identity as push-forward (`pushforward_foldDiagram`); and the `ℤ/3` example of
    item 56 (`z3InvHom_mem_equivalences`, `remark_10_5_5`). Status: **settled** (every hypothesis satisfiable).

Found while formalizing Appendix §§10.6.1–10.6.2 (2026-11-08).

60. **The proof of Theorem 10.3.8** *(Appendix §10.6.1, pp. 509–515)*. The functor
    `L(a', φ, b') = (H(a'), τ_{B'}(b') ∘ φ ∘ τ_{A'}(a')⁻¹, K(b'))` of (10.28), (10.30) (`wfpMap`) is
    shown to be an equivalence by two out of three, from `π_A ∘ L = H ∘ π_{A'}` (`isEquivalence_wfpMap`,
    `IsEquivalence.of_comp_left`), where the text checks directly that `L` is full, faithful and a local
    sc-diffeomorphism; its sc-smoothness, asserted in the text, is proved entrywise. The two iterated weak fibred
    products of the associativity, "the same space" in the text, are different types; the reassociation functor is
    an equivalence and a refinement with identity natural transformations (`assocFunctor`, `isRefinement_assoc`).
    Readings (possible misprints): in the naturality of `τ_{B'}` the letter `τ_A` appears (p. 511);
    "`(Φ ∘ π_B) ∘ L ≃ Ψ' ∘ π_{B'}`" (pp. 513, 514) is read with `Ψ ∘ π_B`; the unit law is announced as
    `[1_X] ∘ [d] = [d]` for `d : X → Y` (p. 515), in the text's order `[d] ∘ [1_X] = [d]`;
    `τ(a, φ, a)` is read `τ(x, φ, a)` and "`ψ = φ`" as `ψ = ϕ` (p. 515). Status: **settled** (possible
    misprints).

61. **The proof of Theorem 10.3.10: (C1) and (C2)** *(Appendix §10.6.2, pp. 515–519)*. (C1): faithfulness is
    checked on morphisms `(h, φ, k)` with `k = 1_b`; in the injectivity argument `A ×_X B` is read
    `A ×_Y B` and `mor_Y(Ψ(a), Ψ(a'))` as `mor_X(Ψ(b), Ψ(b'))`, and in the essential surjectivity "between
    `Φ(a)` and `x`" as "and `y`" (possible misprints) (`isEquivalence_toFunctor_of_comp`). (C2): the map
    `Γ(b') = (b', (s|U)⁻¹(b'), …)` is read with `(s|U)⁻¹(Ψ(b'))` (possible misprint). The text then uses that
    `Γ'(b') = (F|W)⁻¹ ∘ t ∘ (s|U)⁻¹(Ψ(b'))` is a local sc-diffeomorphism; as we read it, this needs `Ψ` to be
    a local sc-diffeomorphism, which is the other half of (C2), so the step does not hold as we read it. The formal
    proof argues differently: a local inverse `κ` of the equivalence `Φ ∘ π_{A'}` at `(b, φ, a)` gives the
    local sc-smooth right inverse `π_{A'} ∘ κ` of `Φ` through `a`, and `Φ` is injective near `a` by a local
    section of `π_A : A ×_Y B → A` and the local injectivity of `Ψ ∘ π_B`, `s` and `G`
    (`isLocalScDiffeo_obj_of_comp`, `MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeoAt_of_injOn`). Status: **settled** (does not hold as
    we read it; another argument).

Witnesses and the hypotheses taken (2026-11-08).

    equivalence; the pair groupoid of `ℤ` over the point, `theorem_10_2_2_pairToPoint`; `±id` on `ℤ/2 ⋉ ℝ²`,

Follow-up for the notes to the authors (2026-11-09).

71. **Theorem 10.5.7 for an effective target** *(Theorem 10.5.7, p. 508 (2017: Theorem 10.10); item 58)*.
    `SBLocalization.theorem_10_5_7_of_isEffective` (`Polyfold/Chapter10/LocalizationLREffectiveBundle.lean`):
    generalized strong bundle isomorphisms `[D], [D']` with `|[D]| = |[D']|` are equal when the base of the
    target is effective and the base of the source or of the target has (LR) (Definition 7.4.19), the
    hypothesis of Theorem 10.3.19. The hypotheses of the text (Definition 8.4.2 for both bundles) are kept but
    not used: as formalized (`EpStrongBundle.IsLR`) they speak of strong bundle maps defined on all of `W` and
    do not give (LR) of the base. The proof refines `D` and `D'` by the weak fibred product of `Φ` and `Φ'`
    (Theorem 10.2.2); the key step `SEP.natEquiv_of_isEffective` gives `F ≃ G` (Definition 10.4.8) for strong
    bundle equivalences with `|F| = |G|`: the base transformation `τ` is that of
    `EpFunctor.naturallyEquivalent_of_isEffective`, and `G(w) = μ'(τ(P(w)), F(w))` holds over the regular
    points of the base, which are dense, hence everywhere (`P` is open, `StrongBundle.isOpenMap_proj`;
    `|Φ| = |Ψ|` gives `|ϕ| = |ψ|`, `SEP.orbitMap_base_eq`). Witness:
    `LocalizationLREffectiveBundleExamples.theorem_10_5_7_of_isEffective_hypotheses` (`ℝⁿ × ℝᵏ → ℝⁿ` over the
    trivial ep-groupoid). Whether the theorem holds for an effective target without (LR) of a base is not
    decided. Status: **settled** (effective target, base (LR)). (2026-11-09: with Definition 8.4.2 read for local isomorphisms, no (LR) of a base is needed, item 72.)

72. **Theorem 10.5.7 for an effective target, with the hypothesis of the text** *(Definition 8.4.2, p. 382, new in the
    2021 edition; Theorem 10.5.7, p. 508 (2017: Theorem 10.10); items 58, 71)*. The text's Definition 8.4.2 speaks of
    strong bundle isomorphisms of `W|U(x)`; the formal `EpStrongBundle.IsLR` speaks of strong bundle maps of all of
    `W`. `EpStrongBundle.IsLRLocal` (`Polyfold/Chapter10/LocalizationLRBundleBase.lean`) is the reading with local
    isomorphisms (`StrongBundle.IsLocalIsoOn`); it implies the earlier one (`EpStrongBundle.IsLRLocal.isLR`). With it,
    Theorem 10.5.7 holds when the base of the target is effective, assuming (LR) of the target bundle only and no (LR)
    of a base: `SBLocalization.theorem_10_5_7_of_isEffective_of_isLRLocal` (and `…_of_isLRLocal'`, with the hypotheses
    of the text on both bundles). The proof applies (LR) of the target to `γ = Q ∘ ϕ_F⁻¹` on `W'|U(ϕ_F(x))`, which
    lifts to the local strong bundle isomorphism `w ↦ μ'(ψ, G(F⁻¹ w))`; this gives the local families of Proposition
    10.4.7 on the bases (`SEP.exists_family_of_isLRLocal`), hence `F ≃ G`
    (`SEP.natEquiv_of_isEffective_of_isLRLocal`), without Proposition 10.4.6. Witnesses:
    `EpStrongBundle.isLRLocal_trivial`,
    `LocalizationLRBundleBaseExamples.theorem_10_5_7_of_isEffective_of_isLRLocal_hypotheses` (`ℝⁿ × ℝᵏ → ℝⁿ`).
    Effectiveness is still needed: the `ℤ/3` example of item 58 satisfies `IsLRLocal` (`isLRLocal_z3EpBundle`), and
    there the theorem does not hold as we read it (`not_theorem_10_5_7_of_isLRLocal`). Whether the formal
    `EpStrongBundle.IsLR` alone suffices is not decided. Status: **settled** (effective target; Definition 8.4.2 read
    for local isomorphisms).
    (2026-11-12) The same reading of Definition 8.4.2 gives Propositions 10.4.6, 10.4.7 and 10.5.6 (items 45, 57, 74;
    rows V10.72, V10.73, V10.61).

73. **Theorem 10.5.4: `[D]_*` is a linear isomorphism (row V10.59)** *(Theorem 10.5.4, pp. 507–508 (2017: Theorem 10.9,
    p. 367); Theorem 10.4.5; Definition 8.3.4; item 55)* (2026-11-09).
    `Polyfold/Chapter10/SectionFunctorLinear2021.lean`. `Γ(P, μ)`, a set of maps `X → W` in the project, is realised as
    a submodule of `Π_x W_x` with the vector space structure of Definition 8.3.4 (`EpStrongBundle.sectionSpace`, and
    `plusSectionSpace` for `Γ⁺`). Push-forward and pull-back along a strong bundle equivalence and along `[D]` preserve
    fibrewise sums and scalar multiples for all sections (`pushforward_sectionAdd`, `pushforward_sectionSmul`,
    `pullback_sectionAdd`, `pullback_sectionSmul`), and `GenSBMap.pushforwardEquiv` is a linear isomorphism `Γ(P, μ) ≅
    Γ(P', μ')` with inverse `[D]^*`, as is `plusPushforwardEquiv` on `Γ⁺`. On `Fred`, which is not a vector space, the
    statement is the bijection `theorem_10_5_4_fred` (item 55). Status: **settled** (rows V10.27, V10.59).

74. **Propositions 10.4.6 and 10.4.7: 10.4.7 on the bases, and what 10.4.6 needs (gap G.122, closed since)** *(Propositions
    10.4.6 and 10.4.7, pp. 501–502, new in the 2021 edition; Definition 8.4.2; items 45, 71, 72)* (2026-11-09).
    Proposition 10.4.7 is formalized on the bases, with the local reading `IsLRLocal` of Definition 8.4.2 for the
    target (`SEP.exists_family_of_isLRLocal`, `Chapter10/LocalizationLRBundleBase.lean`): it gives the sc-smooth `z ↦
    α_z : φ_F(z) → φ_G(z)`. The identity `μ'(α_z, Φ(v)) = Ψ(v)` on the bundles is not stated; it follows from the last
    step of that proof, where `B = g * ·` on `W'|U` and `α_z = ψ_z⁻¹ ∘ Γ(g, φ_F(z))`. Proposition 10.4.6 is not
    formalized. The formal `EpStrongBundle.IsLR` asks the conclusion only for strong bundle maps defined on all of `W`,
    while the text's transport `H⁻¹ΘH` lives on `V|U(x)` only, and the project has no extension of a local strong
    bundle isomorphism to a global map; so the proof does not go through for `IsLR` as stated. With `IsLRLocal` the
    text's proof should work: it needs a strong bundle transport chart (`H` as a local strong bundle isomorphism at
    levels `0` and `1`, equivariant on `natLift`) and the composition and inversion of local strong bundle
    isomorphisms; Proposition 10.5.6 for `IsLRLocal` would then follow from `GenSBMap.iff_of_isGeneralizedIso`.
    Status: **settled** (gaps G.122, G.126 closed; row V10.61 same).
    (2026-11-12) Proposition 10.4.6 is proved along these lines with `IsLRLocal` (`EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_6`:
    the transport `IsStrongBundleEquivalence.exists_transport`, equivariant on the natural lifts by `transport_Γ`;
    composition and inversion of local strong bundle isomorphisms, `StrongBundle.IsLocalIso₂`,
    `IsLocalIsoOn.exists_isLocalIso₂`), and the bundle identity `μ'(α_z, Φ(v)) = Ψ(v)` of Proposition 10.4.7 is
    stated, with (LR) of the target only (`proposition_10_4_7`). Whether the formal `IsLR` alone suffices is still not
    decided.

## Chapter 11 (Geometry up to equivalences; Lean `Polyfold/Chapter11/`)

*Numbering.* The items of this section are numbered in blocks, one block per part of the chapter, so that agents
working at the same time do not collide; the gaps in the numbering are unused numbers, not deleted items. 1–19: §11.1,
the tangent functor and faces (`Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry.lean`, `EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces.lean`); 20–29:
§11.2, sc-differential forms (`GapP2_B2_*.lean`, since 2026-11-12); 30–39: §11.3 up to Theorem 11.3.3, branched
ep⁺-subgroupoids (`BranchedEquivalence.lean`, `BranchedEquivalenceLocalization.lean`); 40–49: the rest of §11.3, Lemma
11.3.4 to Theorem 11.3.9 (`BranchedEquivalenceTangentSection.lean`, `BranchedEquivalenceTangent.lean`,
`BranchedEquivalenceTangentOrientation.lean`); 50–59: §11.4, integration (`GapP2_H4*.lean`, since 2026-11-13); 60–69:
§11.5, auxiliary norms and multisections (`StrongBundleUpToEquivalence.lean`); 70–79: §11.6, proper coverings up to
equivalence (`CoveringEquivalence.lean`, `CoveringEquivalenceTheorem.lean`, `CoveringEquivalenceDiagram.lean`); 80–89:
witnesses and the hypotheses taken. Statement numbers and pages are those of the Springer edition (2021, pp. 521–566),
with the 2017 text's in parentheses (2017 pp. 375–416). The comparison items are `Exposition/verification/ch11.md`
(V11.1–V11.43); the gaps are G.128–G.135.

Found while formalizing §11.1 (2026-11-08).

1. **Theorem 11.1.1: the tangent functor on `EP(E⁻¹)`, composition supplied** *(Theorem 11.1.1, pp. 521–522 (2017:
   Theorem 11.1, p. 375))*. The text proves that `T` respects refinements and leaves "the remaining argument" to
   the reader. Identities: `T` of the identity diagram refines the identity of `TX` (`isRefinement_tangent_id`).
   Composition: for functors `P : C → A`, `Q : C → B` and a natural transformation `Φ ∘ P → G ∘ Q`,
   `wfpLift` is the functor `C → A ×_Y B`, `c ↦ (P(c), τ(c), Q(c))`; for `C = T(A ×_Y B)` it is an
   equivalence `T(A ×_Y B) → TA ×_{TY} TB` by two out of three, and `T(e ∘ d)` refines `Te ∘ Td`
   (`isRefinement_tangent_comp`). `T` maps generalized isomorphisms to generalized isomorphisms
   (`isGeneralizedIso_tangent`) and commutes with the localization functor
   (`tangentFunctor_map_localizationFunctor`). `T` is defined on `EP.{max u 1}`, the universe of Chapter 8's
   tangent functor. Status: **settled**.

2. **Proposition 11.1.2: the degeneracy index under generalized isomorphisms** *(Proposition 11.1.2, pp. 522–523
   (2017: Proposition 11.1, p. 376))*. Proved as stated, through a representative with both legs equivalences and
   `IsEquivalence.degIndexOrbit_orbitMap` (`proposition_11_1_2`, `EPLoc.degIndexOrbit_orbitMap`). The proof refers
   to "Proposition 10.3.10" for that representative; we read Theorem 10.3.10 (possible misprint). Status:
   **settled** (possible misprint).

3. **Definition 11.1.3: faces recorded by their object sets** *(Definition 11.1.3, p. 523 (2017: Definition 11.1,
   p. 377))*. `IsOrbitFace θ` (a face of `|X|`), `faceObj θ = π⁻¹(θ)` (saturated, `isSaturated_faceObj`),
   `faceMor θ` (the morphisms with source in it, `faceMor_eq`), `IsEpFace`, `IsEpFaceStructured`,
   `IsWeaklyFaceStructured`. The faces of `|X|` are Chapter 2's faces for the index `d_{|X|}` on the open set `|X|`
   (`isOrbitFace_iff_isFaceIn`, `orbitFacesThrough_eq`, `isEpFaceStructured_iff`), so that every statement about
   faces becomes one about homeomorphisms of orbit spaces preserving an index. The number of faces through a point
   is counted in `ℕ∞`. The ep-groupoid structure of a face is part of Proposition 11.1.6 (item 6). Status:
   **settled**.
   (2026-11-12) The structure is built: `faceEpGroupoid` (`Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces.lean`; item 6).

4. **Example 11.1.4: the quadrant with the swap, for any `W`** *(Example 11.1.4, p. 523 (2017: Example 11.1, p.
   377))*. Proved for `C = [0, ∞)² ⊕ W` with any sc-Banach space `W` (`example_11_1_4`): with only identities
   `C` is face structured (`isFaceStructured_quadrant`); `ℤ/2 ⋉ C` with the swap (`swapEpGroupoid`) is weakly
   face structured and not face structured. The reason, not given in the text: `{d_{|X|} = 1}` is the image of
   one connected stratum (`setOf_degIndexOrbit_eq_one_swap`), so `|X|` has exactly one face
   (`isOrbitFace_swap_iff`), and the corner, of index 2, lies in one face (`not_isEpFaceStructured_swap`). Status:
   **settled** (stronger).

5. **Remark 11.1.5: the quoted result is proved** *(Remark 11.1.5, p. 524 (2017: Remark 11.1, p. 378))*. The remark
   quotes [56, Proposition 3.15]; its content for faces of open sets is proved: a homeomorphism preserving the
   index maps faces onto faces and preserves face-structuredness (`TameBoundary.isFaceIn_univ_image`,
   `exists_isFaceIn_univ_preimage`, `isFaceStructuredOpen_univ_iff`). For equivalences: the bijection of faces with
   `Φ_*(X_θ) = saturation(Φ(X_θ))`, `Φ^*(Y_θ') = Φ⁻¹(Y_θ')` (`IsEquivalence.bijOn_faces`,
   `saturation_image_faceObj`, `preimage_faceObj`); for generalized isomorphisms `faceMap`, `faceComap`, equal to
   `Ψ_* ∘ Φ^*` and `Φ_* ∘ Ψ^*` on a representative (`faceMap_homMk`, `faceComap_homMk`) (`remark_11_1_5`). The
   first paragraph, on ordered face structures, has no formal content. Status: **settled**; the ordered face
   structures have no formal content.

6. **Proposition 11.1.6: faces as ep-groupoids, `[d]_F`, and the intersection clause** *(Proposition 11.1.6, pp.
   524–525 (2017: Proposition 11.2, p. 378))*. Proved, for every generalized isomorphism and with no face structure
   assumed: `[d]_*` is a bijection of the faces of `|X|` onto those of `|Y|` with inverse `[d]^*`,
   `[d]_*(X_θ) = Y_{|[d]|(θ)}`, and `|[d]|` restricts to homeomorphisms `θ → [d]_*θ` (`proposition_11_1_6`).
   (2026-11-12, `Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces.lean`, `GapP2_HFaceIso.lean`.) For face structured `X`: the object M-polyfold
   is weakly face structured (`IsEpFaceStructured.isWeaklyFaceStructured`), the only extra input the proof needs; each
   `X_θ` agrees near each of its points with one face of the object M-polyfold (`exists_nhds_eq_face`), so it is a
   closed saturated sub-M-polyfold, and with the morphisms between its points a tame ep-groupoid with
   `d_X = d_{X_θ} + 1` (`faceEpGroupoid`, `proposition_11_1_6_faces`); restrictions of equivalences to saturated
   ep-subgroupoids are equivalences (`EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.restrictSub`), and `[d]_F : X_θ → Y_{[d]_*θ}`
   (`EPLoc.faceIso`) is a generalized isomorphism, independent of the representative, whose orbit map restricts
   `|[d]|` (`proposition_11_1_6_faceIso`). Only `X` is assumed face structured; `Y` then is (item 7). The clause that
   two faces meet in a face of each does not hold as we read it (item 9). Status: **settled** (gap G.128 closed; row
   V11.6 narrower by the verdict rule).

7. **Remark 11.1.7: tameness transfers forward along equivalences** *(Remark 11.1.7, p. 525 (2017: Remark 11.2, p.
   379))*. Chapter 10 had tameness from `Y` to `X` (`IsEquivalence.isTame_of_isTame`). The converse, needed here,
   goes through `X ×_Y Y` for `F` and `1_Y`: `π_X` is an equivalence, so `X ×_Y Y` is tame, and `π_Y` is a
   surjective local sc-diffeomorphism on objects (`isTame_of_isTame_left`, `isTame_iff`). With item 5, "tame and
   face structured" is invariant under generalized isomorphisms (`remark_11_1_7`). Status: **settled**.

8. **Proposition 11.1.8: the maps on faces** *(Proposition 11.1.8, p. 526 (2017: Proposition 11.3, p. 380))*.
   `f_* = g_*`, `f^* = g^*` on faces and `|f| = |g|` on every face (`proposition_11_1_8`). (2026-11-12) The text's
   maps `|F| → |f_*F|` come from the generalized isomorphisms `f_F` of (11.1), now constructed (`EPLoc.faceIso`, item
   6); `|f_F| = |g_F|` is `proposition_11_1_8_faceIso`, with only `X` assumed face structured. Status: **settled**
   (row V11.8 same; gap G.128 closed).

9. **Proposition 11.1.6, the intersection clause: does not hold as we read it** *(Proposition 11.1.6, p. 524 (2017:
   Proposition 11.2, p. 378))* (2026-11-12). `Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeet.lean`, `GapP2_H2FaceMeetUnion.lean`. The
   clause, that a nonempty intersection of two faces `F`, `G` is a face in `F` as well as in `G`, is stated for two
   distinct faces `X_θ ≠ X_θ'` in the face ep-groupoids `faceEpGroupoid` (`EpGroupoid.FacesMeetInFaces`).
   Counterexample: for any sc-Banach space `W`, the trivial ep-groupoid of `V = ([0,∞)³ ⊕ W) ∖ K`,
   `K = {p₀ + p₁ ≤ 1/4, 1 ≤ p₂ ≤ 2}`, an open subset of the tame quadrant, is tame and face structured
   (`FaceMeetExample.isEpFaceStructured_XV`); its faces through the planes `p₀ = 0` and `p₁ = 0` are distinct and meet
   in the edge `p₀ = p₁ = 0` with `p₂ ∈ [1, 2]` removed, two components; in `|X_θ₀|` every point of index 1 has
   `p₂ < 1` or `p₂ > 2` (`cF_lt_or_gt`), so the intersection is not the closure of one component
   (`not_isEpFace_inter`, `FaceMeetExample.not_facesMeetInFaces`). With `W = 0` it is a 3-manifold with boundary and
   corners. Corrected form, proved for every face structured `X`: for `θ ≠ θ'`, `X_θ ∩ X_θ'` is the union of the faces
   of `X_θ` it contains, and of the faces of `X_θ'` it contains (`IsEpFaceStructured.faceObj_inter_eq_sUnion`,
   `IsEpFaceStructured.facesMeetInUnions`); the M-polyfold step is that in a tame M-polyfold a point on two distinct
   faces is a limit of points of index 2 on both (`MPolyfold.mem_closure_inter_faces`, by a ray in a tame chart). The
   text's proof does not address the clause. For the notes to the authors (one line): whether the clause is meant as
   "a union of faces in `F` and in `G`", the form proved. Status: **settled** (row V11.6 narrower; gap G.128 closed).

Found while reading §11.2 (2026-11-08).

20. **§11.2: forms up to equivalence** *(Theorem 11.2.1 to Proposition 11.2.9, pp. 526–535 (2017: Theorem 11.2 to

21. **§11.2: two reading points** *(p. 528 and the proof of Lemma 11.2.6, p. 531)* (2026-11-12). (1) The sentence
    before Definition 11.2.3 writes `F_*ω ∈ Ω_{ep,∞}(X)` for an equivalence `F : X → Y`; we read `Ω_{ep,∞}(Y)`, as the
    definition itself has it (row V11.10). (2) The proof of Lemma 11.2.6 cites "Lemma 11.2.2 and Lemma 11.2.3" for the
    composition and natural-equivalence rules it uses; we read Lemmas 11.2.4 and 11.2.5 (row V11.11). Neither changes
    a statement. Status: **settled** (readings).

22. **§11.2: `F_*` as the inverse of `F^*`; the local families of Proposition 10.1.10** *(Lemma 11.2.2, Definition
    11.2.3, Proposition 11.2.8)* (2026-11-12). For an equivalence `F`, `F^* : Ω^k_ep(Y) → Ω^k_ep(X)` is a bijection
    (`IsEquivalence.bijective_formPullback`), proved by descent of forms along `π_Y : X ×_Y Y → Y` (the weak fibred
    product of `F` and `1_Y`, whose objects are the text's triples `(x, ψ, y)`), a full functor and a surjective local
    sc-diffeomorphism on objects (`MPolyfold.formDescend`, `formPullback_formDescend`; sc-smoothness by the text's
    (11.4), `MPolyfold.isScForm_of_formPullback`). `F_*` is defined as the inverse, and the text's defining formula
    and Lemma 11.2.2 become theorems; Lemmas 11.2.4–11.2.6 are then formal. In Proposition 11.2.8 the morphism
    `ψ : F(x) → G(x)` with `Tψ ∘ TF(x) = TG(x)` is taken from the local sc-smooth families of Proposition 10.1.10 (1)
    (`EpFunctor.HasLocalNatIso`), restricted to the index lifts `X^i`, so that no local regularity of the lifts is
    needed; the conclusions hold with the local regularity property of one of `X`, `Y` only
    (`EP.epFormsInftyPullback_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`, `EPLoc.formsPullback_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`). The push-forward is also
    what the Poincaré lemma on ep-groupoids, Proposition 8.2.3, needs (`EP.proposition_8_2_3`,
    `Chapter11/GapP2_B2_Poincare.lean`; Chapter 8). Not formalized: the wedge product as a graded-algebra instance on
    `Ω*_{ep,∞}(X)` itself; `Ω*_{ep,∞}(X)` is shown to be a differential graded subalgebra of Part I's `Ω*_∞(Ob X)`
    (`EP.formsInftyWedge_mem_epFormsRange`, `GapP2_B2_EpWedge.lean`). Status: **settled**.

Found while formalizing §11.3 up to Theorem 11.3.3 (2026-11-08).

30. **Definition 11.3.1: total push-forwards; the target of `F_*`** *(Definition 11.3.1, p. 535 (2017: Definition
    11.4, p. 389))*. `pullbackTheta` and `pushforwardTheta` are defined for every sc-smooth functor and every map
    on objects; `F_*Θ(y)` uses one chosen `x` and morphism `F(x) → y`, and is `0` if there is none
    (`pushforwardTheta_of_not_exists`). The push-forward is typed `X′ → ℚ⁺` in both editions; we read `Y → ℚ⁺`
    (possible misprint). Status: **settled** (possible misprint).

31. **Lemma 11.3.2 needs less than equivalences** *(Lemma 11.3.2, p. 536 (2017: Lemma 11.5, p. 389))*. (1) holds
    for full `F` (`pushforwardTheta_eq`, `isFunctorial_pushforwardTheta`, `pullbackTheta_pushforwardTheta`); (2)
    for essentially surjective `F` (`pushforwardTheta_pullbackTheta`); (3) for naturally equivalent full functors
    in the case of push-forwards and for any naturally equivalent functors in the case of pull-backs
    (`pushforwardTheta_eq_of_naturallyEquivalent`, `pullbackTheta_eq_of_naturallyEquivalent`). Added:
    `pullbackTheta_comp`, `pushforwardTheta_comp`, `pushforwardTheta_id`. Status: **settled** (stronger).

32. **Push-forward and pull-back along generalized maps** *(§11.3, pp. 536–537 (2017 pp. 389–390))*. On diagrams
    `d_* = Φ_*F^*`, `d^* = F_*Φ^*` (`Diagram.pushTheta`, `Diagram.pullTheta`), invariant under refinements
    (`pullTheta_eq_of_isRefinement`, and `pushTheta_eq_of_isRefinement` when `Φ` is an equivalence); on classes
    through a chosen representative (`EPLoc.rep`, `EPLoc.pushTheta`, `EPLoc.pullTheta`). `f^*` is well defined and
    contravariantly functorial for all generalized maps, not only generalized isomorphisms (`pullTheta_comp`). The
    composition rules, "easily verified" in the text, go through base change in the weak fibred product
    (`WeakFibredProduct.pushforwardTheta_projRight_pullbackTheta`, `pushforwardTheta_projLeft_pullbackTheta`),
    giving `pushTheta_comp`, `pushTheta_inv`, `pullTheta_pushTheta`, `pushTheta_pullTheta`. Theorem 10.3.19, which
    does not hold as we read it (Chapter 10, item 17), is not used. Status: **settled** (stronger).

33. **Theorem 11.3.3, the step for an equivalence: paracompactness, restricted sheets, one possible misprint**
    *(Theorem 11.3.3, proof, pp. 537–538 (2017: Theorem 11.3, pp. 390–391))*. 2021 Definition 9.1.2 (1) asks that
    `|supp(Θ)|` be paracompact; the proof does not mention it, and it is proved from `orbitSupp_pushforwardTheta`,
    `orbitSupp_pullbackTheta` and `|F|` a homeomorphism. A local branching structure is moved by an
    sc-diffeomorphism between open subsets of two object spaces (`LocalBranchingStructure.mapDiffeo`), the sheets
    first restricted to its domain, here that of Chapter 10's `TransportChart`; dimensions are invariant across
    M-polyfolds (`MPolyfold.hasDimAt_image_iff_of_isScDiffeoOn`, `IsSubmanifoldOfDim.image_isScDiffeoOn`). Manifold
    type is shown for two morphisms `y → y′` directly. In the manifold-type step
    `ψ ∘ φ′ ∘ ψ⁻¹ : F(x) → F(x)` (for `ψ : F(x) → y`, `φ′ : y → y`) is read `ψ⁻¹ ∘ φ′ ∘ ψ`
    (possible misprint). Status: **settled** (possible misprint).

34. **Theorem 11.3.3 (6): every dimensional decomposition** *(Theorem 11.3.3, p. 537 (2017: Theorem 11.3, p.
    390))*. (6) speaks of "the dimensional decomposition", relying on the uniqueness part of Proposition 9.1.11,
    which does not hold as we read it (Chapter 9, `not_proposition_9_1_11_rn`). It is read as "every dimensional
    decomposition `Θ = Σ_k Θ_k` is mapped to one", which is what the proof gives (`theorem_11_3_3_six`,
    `isDimDecomposition_pushforwardTheta`); `n`-dimensionality is added (`isNDimensional_pushTheta`,
    `isNDimensional_pullTheta`). All six parts are proved (`theorem_11_3_3_one` … `theorem_11_3_3_six`), with `X`
    and `Y` in one universe. Status: **settled** in this reading.

35. **Witnesses for §11.3** *(not in the book)*. `Θ₀ = 1_{0}` on `ℤ/2 ⋉ ℝ` is a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid
    (`isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_reflectionTheta`); its pull-back along `reflectionCover`, an equivalence not

    `F_*F^*Θ₀ = Θ₀`; for the generalized isomorphism `[ℤ/2 ⋉ ℝ ← X_𝒰 → X_𝒰]`, `f_*Θ₀ = F^*Θ₀`
    (`pushTheta_reflectionCoverDiagram`). Status: **settled**.

40. **Lemma 11.3.4: section functors of `Ĝr`, (11.8) and (11.9)** *(Lemma 11.3.4, p. 539, with (11.8), p. 538, and
    (11.9), p. 539 (2017: Lemma 11.6, p. 392))*. `Γ(π̂)` is the set of section functors of `π̂ : Ĝr(X) → X_∞`,
    with no continuity required (`IsGrHatSection`, `GrHatSections`): `h(x)` is a finite formal sum of oriented
    tangent sets at `x ∈ X_∞`, natural along morphisms, recorded on all objects and `0` off `X_∞`; every
    orientation of Chapter 9 is one (`IsOrientation.isGrHatSection`). Along an equivalence, `F_*h` of (11.8) moves
    `h(x)` by `Tψ ∘ TF(x)` for a chosen `ψ : F(x) → y`, the formal sums by the image of carriers and frames
    (`OrTangent.map`, `pushSection`), and the value does not depend on the choice (`pushSection_eq`), as the text
    says; `F^*h′` of (11.9) uses the inverse of `TF` on `T_xX` (`fibreInv`, `pullSection`). Proved: `F_*` and `F^*`
    preserve section functors, are mutually inverse, are unchanged under natural equivalence, compose, and satisfy
    base change in the weak fibred product (`pushSection_projRight_pullSection`); on diagrams and classes they are
    well defined (`Diagram.pushSection`, `EPLoc.pushSection`, `pushSection_homMk`, `pushSection_inv`), with the
    composition laws for generalized isomorphisms, as in the text (`lemma_11_3_4`). Status: **settled**.

41. **Theorem 11.3.5: Chapter 9 across two M-polyfolds; the independence of the tangent sums carried along**
    *(Theorem 11.3.5, p. 539, proof pp. 539–540 (2017: Theorem 11.4, p. 393))*. Chapter 9 moves submanifolds,
    tangent sets and orientations by sc-diffeomorphisms of one M-polyfold; the proof moves an oriented branching
    structure at `x` by `ψ̂ ∘ F`, between open subsets of two. This is supplied: oriented tangent sets
    (`IsOrientedAt.map_tangentMapOn`), orientations of submanifolds with their frames moved by the tangent map
    (`SubmanifoldOrientation.mapDiffeo`), oriented branching structures (`OrientedBranchingStructure.mapDiffeo`,
    `orientedSum_mapDiffeo`), and `Tψ ∘ TF = TQ` on `T_uX` for a transport chart `Q = ψ̂ ∘ F`
    (`TransportChart.tangentMor_ψ_tangent_obj`). The theorem then follows as in the text, for equivalences
    (`isOrientation_pushSection`, `isOrientation_pullSection`) and for generalized isomorphisms
    (`theorem_11_3_5_push`, `theorem_11_3_5_pull`). Chapter 9's orientations assume the independence of the tangent
    sums of Theorem 9.2.1 (`HasIndependentTangentSums`), a hypothesis there, which holds on `ℝⁿ`
    (`hasIndependentTangentSums_rn`); it is assumed for `Θ` and proved for `F_*Θ`, `F^*Θ′`, `f_*Θ` and `f^*Θ′`
    (`hasIndependentTangentSums_pushforwardTheta`, `hasIndependentTangentSums_pullbackTheta`,
    `hasIndependentTangentSums_pushTheta`, `hasIndependentTangentSums_pullTheta`). Status: **settled** (hypothesis
    made explicit).

42. **Definition 11.3.6 and (11.10): the independence as a field** *(Definition 11.3.6 and (11.10), p. 541 (2017:
    Definition 11.5, p. 394))*. `OrientedBranched` records `Θ`, `T̂_Θ` and the independence of the tangent sums;
    `push` and `pull` along generalized isomorphisms give oriented branched ep⁺-subgroupoids by Theorems 11.3.3 and
    11.3.5, and (11.10) is `push_comp`, `pull_comp`, from Lemma 11.3.4 and item 32. Of the two inverse laws of

    its two components (`EPLoc.pushTheta_pullTheta`, `EPLoc.pushSection_pullSection`). Status: **settled**.

43. **Theorem 11.3.7: the proof left to the reader** *(Theorem 11.3.7, p. 541 (2017: Theorem 11.5, p. 395))*.
    Proved for generalized isomorphisms and branched ep⁺-subgroupoids with independent tangent sums
    (`theorem_11_3_7_push`, `theorem_11_3_7_pull`). The steps: `T_{f(a)}f(A) = Tf(T_aA)` for an sc-diffeomorphism
    `f` between open subsets of two M-polyfolds (`submanifoldTangent_image_of_isScDiffeoOn`); the tangent sums of a

    11.3.1 along the equivalence `TF` (`tangentTheta_pushforwardTheta`), and dually for `F^*`; and `Tf` is `[Td]`
    for the chosen representative `d` (`tangentFunctor_map_eq`, Theorem 11.1.1). Status: **settled** (hypothesis
    made explicit, as in item 41).

44. **Theorem 11.3.8: the boundary read through `∂M`** *(Theorem 11.3.8, pp. 541–542 (2017: Theorem 11.6, p.
    395))*. The sketch of the proof says that `d_M` is preserved; this is read as the invariance of the boundary

    (`boundaryTheta_pushforwardTheta`, `boundaryTheta_pullbackTheta`) and for generalized isomorphisms
