45. **Theorem 11.3.9 for a representative, under a boundary-transfer hypothesis** *(Theorem 11.3.9, p. 542 (2017:
    Theorem 11.7, p. 395))*. Chapter 9's boundary orientation `T̂_{∂Θ}` is the boundary lift of `T̂_Θ` by a
    boundary operation `bd` on oriented tangent sets, which Chapter 9 takes as data, since the partial cones of
    submanifolds are not formalized. A linear map `T_xX → T_yY` transfers `bd` to `bd′` if it preserves degree
    `1` and commutes with them there (`IsBoundaryTransfer`, pointwise, for the given map and operations); the
    identity transfers every boundary operation to itself (`isBoundaryTransfer_id`). For a representative
    `X ← A → Y` with `Φ` an equivalence and boundary operations on `X`, `A`, `Y` transferred by `TF(a)⁻¹` and
    by `Tψ ∘ TΦ(a)`: `d_*(∂Θ) = ∂(d_*Θ)` and `d_*T̂_{∂Θ} = T̂_{∂(d_*Θ)}`, and likewise for `d^*`
    (`pushSection_boundaryLift`, `pullSection_boundaryLift`, `theorem_11_3_9_push`, `theorem_11_3_9_pull`). Not
    formalized: that the boundary operations of Definition 9.3.8 satisfy the hypothesis along equivalences, which
    needs sc-diffeomorphisms between different M-polyfolds to preserve the tame induced structures, `d_M` and
    outward vectors; hence a form of the theorem independent of the representative. Status: **open** (gap G.130).
    (2026-11-09) For the intrinsic boundary orientation (Chapter 9, item 108) the theorem holds for the generalized
    isomorphism itself, with no transfer hypothesis: sc-diffeomorphisms preserve `T^R_xX`, `C_xX`, the reduced
    codimension and the boundary operation (`boundaryOp_map_tangentMapOn`), and so do equivalences
    (`EpFunctor.isReducedBoundaryTransfer_tangentMor`), which gives `EPLoc.theorem_11_3_9_push_boundaryOrientation` and
    `EPLoc.theorem_11_3_9_pull_boundaryOrientation` (`Polyfold/Chapter11/BoundaryOrientationEquiv.lean`). For
    `boundaryLift boundaryOp` the tameness of `f_*Θ̂` remains a hypothesis (`EPLoc.theorem_11_3_9_push_boundaryOp`), and
    so does `CarriesTameTangents` for `IsBoundaryTransfer`, since the restriction of sc-diffeomorphisms to tame
    sub-M-polyfolds is not formalized; `∂Θ̂` as an oriented branched ep⁺-subgroupoid is not formalized, so the theorem
    is stated componentwise. Status: **settled** for the intrinsic boundary orientation; gap G.130 closed.

72. **Definition 11.6.4 (2): the fibre condition is redundant** *(Definition 11.6.4, p. 553 (2017: Definition 11.6,
    p. 404))*. If `F`, `F′` are proper covering functors and `Ψ`, `Φ` are equivalences, `Ψ` maps each `F⁻¹(x)`
    bijectively onto `F′⁻¹(Φ(x))`: injectivity from the fullness of `Ψ`, the faithfulness of `Φ` and unique lifting
    along `F`; surjectivity from the essential surjectivity of `Ψ`, the fullness of `Φ` and unique lifting along
    `F′` (`isFiberBijective_of_isEquivalence`, `isEquivalence_iff`). The text's remark after the definition treats
    the fibre bijection as singling out a subclass of the functors of (1); within (2) it is automatic. Witness:
    `pairToPointCovering`, an equivalence with no inverse functor (`isEquivalence_pairToPointCovering`). Status:
    **settled**; the hypothesis is redundant.

75. **The category `PC`, Definition 11.6.7 and Proposition 11.6.8: the last step of the chain** *(Definition
    11.6.7, p. 561 (2017: Definition 11.8, p. 410); Proposition 11.6.8, p. 562 (2017: Proposition 11.8, p. 411))*.
    `PC` is a category with composition associative on the nose (`ProperCoveringHom.comp_assoc`) and the
    multiplicative class `PC.equivalences`; all proper coverings are taken in one universe, so that the weak fibred
    product `PC.fibred` stays in `PC`. In the proof of Proposition 11.6.8 the displayed chain for the `ε`'s ends at
    `ε′ ∘ K ∘ π_{B″}`; the last step to `ε″ ∘ K′ ∘ π_{B″}` uses the assumption `ε′ ∘ K ≃ ε″ ∘ K′` and
    is added (`proposition_11_6_8`); with it, having a common refinement is an equivalence relation
    (`hasCommonRefinement_equivalence`). Witnesses: `PC.Examples.diagram`, `diagram'`,
    `hasCommonRefinement_diagram_diagram`. Status: **settled**.

    (2026-11-12). The text defines neither a class of equivalences of proper strong bundle coverings nor natural

    (`SEP.isProperStrongBundleCovering2021_pullbackCovering_of_isEquivalence`); in the project the weak fibred product
    of strong bundles is a pull-back. (3) The composition of `PC(E⁻¹)` is well defined with the common refinement of
    Definition 11.6.7 directly: maps of weak fibred products built from natural transformations (`PC.fibredLift`) are
    equivalences by two out of three (`PC.IsEquivalence.of_comp_left`), with no separate check of the fibre condition,
    which is automatic for proper coverings (item 72). Nothing is found not to hold as we read it. Status:
    **settled**.

Witnesses and the hypotheses taken (2026-11-08).

81. **Proposition 11.5.1 with conditions (1) and (2) of Definition 8.3.5 (gap G.132 closed)** *(Proposition 11.5.1, p.

    continuity of `μ[1]` (`SDiagram.tendsto_zeroOne_pullNorm`, `tendsto_zeroOne_of_tendsto_obj`,

    (`SDiagram.isAuxNorm_pushNorm`). No hypothesis is added. Status: **settled** (row V11.30; gap G.132 closed).

82. **Definition 13.2.1, Lemma 11.5.2 and Proposition 11.5.3 for sc⁺-multisections (gap G.133 closed)** *(Lemma 11.5.2,
    p. 548 (2017: Lemma 11.7, p. 400); Proposition 11.5.3, p. 548 (2017: Proposition 11.7, p. 401); Definition 13.2.1;
    item 61)* (2026-11-09). `Polyfold/Chapter11/MultisectionLocalStructure2021.lean`. Definition 13.2.1 is formalized:
    an sc⁺-multisection is a multisection functor with local section structures, whose local sections are sc⁺-sections
    on an open set in the form of `isScPlusSection_iff` (`IsScPlusMultisection`, `HasLocalSectionStructure`,
    `IsLocalRepOn`, `IsScPlusSectionOn`); the multisection of the zero section is one
    (`isScPlusMultisection_zeroMultisection`). Along a strong bundle equivalence the local section structures go both
    ways by the text's construction: the local sections of `Φ_*Λ` are `μ'(σ', Φ(s_i(x)))`, extended by a local inverse
    of `t'` (`exists_isLocalRepOn_pushMult`, `exists_isLocalRepOn_pullMult`). A local representation on any open
    neighbourhood is shrunk to the domain of a natural representation by Theorem 7.1.13, so the strong bundle transport
    of natural representations that item 61 expected is not needed. `lemma_11_5_2_book` and
    `GenSBMap.proposition_11_5_3_book` state Lemma 11.5.2 and Proposition 11.5.3 for sc⁺-multisections, with no added
    hypothesis; the last clause of Proposition 11.5.3 is read for generalized strong bundle isomorphisms, as in item
    61. Status: **settled** (rows V11.31, V11.32; gap G.133 closed).

## Chapter 12 (Fredholm theory in ep-groupoids; Lean `Polyfold/Chapter12/`)

*Numbering.* The items of this section are numbered in order of the text; later waves continue from the last number.
Statement numbers and pages are those of the Springer edition (2021, pp. 569–598), with the 2017 text's numbers in
parentheses. The comparison items are `Exposition/verification/ch12.md` (V12.1–V12.46); the gaps are G.136–G.140, G.147,
G.158 (G.136, G.137 closed in wave 2, G.147 in wave 3, G.138, G.139 in wave 5).

Found while formalizing §§12.1–12.5 in Part III wave 1 (2026-11-13; files `Chapter12/P3N_*`, `P3S_*`, `P3B_*`, `P3O_*`).

1. **The remark after Definition 12.1.1: f(φ) as a section of the pull-back bundle** *(Definition 12.1.1 and the remark
   after it, p. 569 (2017: Definition 12.1))* (2026-11-13). `Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp.lean`. The regularizing
   property on morphisms is read for the induced section of the pull-back bundle `𝐗 ₛ×_P W → 𝐗`, `φ ↦ (φ, f(s φ))`; it
   follows through the pull-back projection, a strong bundle map (`remark_12_1_1_regularizing_mor`; row V12.2). Status:
   **settled**.

2. **Theorem 12.2.7: the local step taken as a hypothesis** *(Theorem 12.2.7, pp. 574–576 (2017: Theorem 12.3); gap
   G.136)* (2026-11-13). `Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormExtension.lean`. The global part of the proof is formalized: the
   extension property survives the `G_x`-average because `N` is invariant, the transport to the saturation, natural
   representations inside `X ∖ ∂X` carrying a Part I norm, and the gluing (each nonzero term is `β_x N`). The local
   coordinate step near `x₀ ∈ ∂X` in a tame strong bundle chart (the map `r ∘ q` into `∂O` and the norm
   `N(rq(u), A(rq(u))w) + ‖w − A(rq(u))w‖`) is the hypothesis `HasLocalExtensions X B N` of `theorem_12_2_7_hyp`, with
   witness `theorem_12_2_7_hyp_witness`; every restriction of a global auxiliary norm satisfies it
   (`hasLocalExtensions_of_isAuxNorm`). It needs tame strong bundle charts around boundary points, not available in the
   project (row V12.9). Status: **settled in Part III wave 2 (item 12; gap G.136 closed)**.

3. **Definition 12.3.1 and Part I's Definition 5.3.1: two readings of "bump function"** *(Definition 12.3.1, Theorem
   12.3.2, p. 579, Theorem 12.3.3, p. 581 (2017: Definition 12.7, Theorems 12.6, 12.7); Chapter 5, items 41, 160–163)*
   (2026-11-13). `Chapter12/P3S_BumpEp.lean`, `P3S_ScPlusSectionFunctor.lean`. Definition 12.3.1 asks for `f` not
   identically 0; the project reads Part I's Definition 5.3.1 pointwise (`f(x) ≠ 0`). Theorem 12.3.2 (1) is proved in
   each consistent pairing (`theorem_12_3_2_1` pointwise on both sides, `theorem_12_3_2_1_weak` with "not identically 0"
   on both sides); the mixed pairing of the printed text would, in direction (⇒), be Part I's open question whether the
   weak reading gives a bump function non-zero at a given point (Chapter 5, item 163). Theorem 12.3.2 (2) and Theorem
   12.3.3 are proved with the pointwise reading (`AdmitsBumpFunctionsPointwise`, witness
   `admitsBumpFunctionsPointwise_trivial_rn`); rows V12.10–V12.13. Status: **in part (the weak-to-pointwise question of
   Part I is open)**.

4. **Theorem 12.2.2: the transport needs only invariance under G_x** *(Theorem 12.2.2, pp. 570, 572–574 (2017: Theorem
   12.1))* (2026-11-13). `Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp.lean`, `P3N_GoodNeighborhood.lean`. The local norm is a Part I
   auxiliary norm (Proposition 5.1.3) averaged over `G_x`; its transport through a chosen morphism to the saturation
   does not depend on the choice because of the `G_x`-invariance (`transNorm_μ`), so property (5) of Theorem 12.2.6 is
   not needed. The completeness of the glued fibre norms, asserted in the text, follows from a general fact: a
   continuous fibrewise seminorm with property (2) of Definition 5.1.1 is squeezed near each point between multiples of
   the chart norm (`StrongBundle.isAuxNorm_of_tendsto`; rows V12.4, V12.27). Status: **settled**.

   (2026-11-13). The proof averages a bump function `f` over `G_x`; the average of a function that takes both signs can
   vanish at `x`. Averaging `f²` keeps `f(x) ≠ 0`, presumably what is intended, since the functions of Proposition 5.5.3
   are `≥ 0` (`exists_natAverage`; row V12.11). A reading point. Status: **settled**.

    sentence of Theorem 12.5.3 and `proposition_12_5_6_mpr_hyp` is (⇐) with continuity, both with Part I's hypotheses
    only (gap G.140). Readings: "continuous local section" is Part I's `IsContOrOn` over an open set, whose section $y
    \mapsto (y, o_y)$ is continuous for Part I's topology; $\hat\Phi$ is the local isomorphism of the sheet of $\sigma$
    (`E.morIso σ`). Two tools Part I lacked are proved: continuity of an orientation is a local property (V12.45), and
    the orientation map of a local isomorphism depends only on its germ (V12.46) (rows V12.24, V12.26). Status:
    **settled (gaps G.138, G.139 closed; gap G.140 remains)**.

22. **Theorem 12.5.7 (2): the continuity for one representative** *(Theorem 12.5.7, pp. 595–597 (2017: Theorem 12.12);
    item 17; gap G.158)* (2026-11-13). `Chapter12/P3W5OR_EquivCont.lean`. `theorem_12_5_7_two_hyp`: the orientation $o'$
    carried along a generalized strong bundle isomorphism is continuous when $o$ is, with continuity read as Part I's
    `IsContOrOn` over all of $X$ for input and output; the book's `Continuous (orSec o)` follows from it. Still open:
    the converse of that implication, the homeomorphism of (1), the independence of the representative and functoriality
    (gap G.158, now 650–1,050 lines; there is no Lean notion yet of equivalent representatives) (row V12.39). Status:
    **in part (gap G.158 open)**.

23. **Every hypothesis taken in Part III wave 5 for Chapter 12 is satisfiable** *(§12.5)* (2026-11-13). No hypothesis
    beyond Part I's standing ones was added: tameness, bump functions and the tame germ data (G.140) with the witnesses
    of `theorem_12_5_3_hyp`; the standing `hsec` of §12.5 (`MPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctions.hasScPlusSectionsThrough`);
    "$\hat\Phi$ maps $f$ to $f'$", discharged for morphisms (`eqOn_morIso_of_functor`) and for equivalences; Part I's
    paracompactness instances, discharged inside the main theorems. No hypothesis quantifies over all charts. Status:
    **settled**.

## Chapter 13 (sc⁺-multisections; Lean `Polyfold/Chapter13/`)

*Numbering.* The items of this section are numbered in order of the text; later waves continue from the last number.
Statement numbers and pages are those of the Springer edition (2021, pp. 599–640), with the 2017 text's numbers in
parentheses. The comparison items are `Exposition/verification/ch13.md` (V13.1–V13.59); the gaps are G.141–G.143, G.148,
G.149, G.163 (G.141–G.143 closed in wave 2, G.148, G.149 in wave 3, G.163 in wave 5).

Found while formalizing §§13.1–13.2 in Part III wave 1 (2026-11-13; files `Chapter13/P3G_*`, `P3M_*`).

1. **"U(x) equipped with the natural G_x-action" read as a natural neighbourhood** *(Lemma 13.1.1, p. 599, Definition
   13.1.2, Proposition 13.1.3, p. 600 (2017: Lemma 13.1, Definition 13.1, Proposition 13.1))* (2026-11-13).
   `Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem.lean`. `NatNbhd x`: an open subset of the domain of a natural representation at `x`,
   invariant under its `Φ_g`; it need not be connected. With this reading Proposition 13.1.3 holds as printed; with "the
   domain of a natural representation", which is connected, an invariant open shrinking could fail to be one. Components
   of `𝒰(x,x')` are indexed by a point in them; for open components condition (3) is injectivity of `s` and `t`
   (`isDiffeoComponent_iff_injOn`). Chapter 11's reading of Definition 13.2.1 and Definition 13.2.5 keeps the connected
   domain (item 8) (rows V13.1–V13.6). Status: **settled**.

2. **Lemma 13.1.1: the invariance of V is not used** *(Lemma 13.1.1, p. 599 (2017: Lemma 13.1))* (2026-11-13). (⇒) uses
   only properness (Proposition 7.1.10); (⇐) only the natural action, by a pigeonhole argument over the finite `G_x`
   (`lemma_13_1_1`; the form with the invariance hypothesis is `lemma_13_1_1_book`; row V13.1). Status: **settled**.

3. **Theorem 13.1.7: properness relative to Q** *(Theorem 13.1.7, p. 602 (2017: Theorem 13.1); gap G.141)* (2026-11-13).
   `Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystemExistence.lean`. The hypothesis is a good system of the full sub-ep-groupoid on `Q`, whose
   condition (1) is properness inside `Q`. The formalization asks it in `X` (`IsGoodOn N Q`, witness
   `GoodSystem.isGoodOn`), and is otherwise stronger: `Q` need not be open, and the given `U(q)` are kept. That
   properness in `Q` implies properness in `X` when `|Q| = |X|` is presumably true and is not formalized. The proof uses
   transports carrying `U(y)` into `U(q_y)`, not the text's smallness condition on the closures (row V13.7). Status:
   **settled in Part III wave 2 (item 10; gap G.141 closed)**.

4. **Theorem 13.1.8: "for all ∈ X" read as "for all x ∈ X"** *(Theorem 13.1.8, p. 604 (2017: Theorem 13.2))*
   (2026-11-13). The variable is missing in the printed quantifier. The proof uses the paracompactness of `|X|` through
   a precise refinement and the shrinking lemma; metrizability is not used (`theorem_13_1_8`; row V13.8). A reading
   point. Status: **settled**.

5. **Proposition 13.1.9: uniqueness among all maps** *(Proposition 13.1.9 and the discussion before it, pp. 606–607
   (2017: Proposition 13.2))* (2026-11-13). `Chapter13/P3G_BiAction.lean`. The isomorphism `g ↦ g'(g)` of stabilisers is
   unique among all maps with the intertwining property, not only among homomorphisms; the proof goes through Lemma
   13.1.6 and the bi-action laws (`GoodSystem.proposition_13_1_9`, `proposition_13_1_9_D`; row V13.9). The bi-action of
   Definition 13.1.5 is given by the formula used in the book's proofs (`biact`; row V13.5). Status: **settled**.

6. **§13.2: the algebra at functor level; decorations and inverses not formalized** *(Definitions 13.2.7–13.2.10, Lemmas
   13.2.11, 13.2.13, pp. 610–612 (2017: Definitions 13.9–13.12, Lemmas 13.4, 13.5); gaps G.142, G.143)* (2026-11-13).
   `Chapter13/P3M_*.lean`. Sums, scalar multiples, products with sc-smooth functors and locally finite sums of
   sc⁺-multisection functors are sc⁺-multisections, with their local representations
   (`multisectionAdd_eq_sum_of_isLocalRepOn`, `multisectionSmul_eq_sum_of_isLocalRepOn`, `isLocalRepOn_conv`). Decorated
   sc⁺-multisections (systems of symmetric structures over a good system, their equivalence) and the decorated
   conclusions are gap G.142; the remark that inverses do not exist in general is gap G.143 (rows V13.15–V13.19).
   Status: **settled in Part III wave 2 (item 11; gaps G.142, G.143 closed)**.

7. **Lemma 13.2.13: the sum over an infinite index set** *(Lemma 13.2.13, p. 612 (2017: Lemma 13.5))* (2026-11-13). The
   text does not write out `⊕_j Λ_j` for infinite `J`. It is read through finitely supported families:
   `lfSum Λ w = ∑ᶠ v, [∑ v = w] ∏ᶠ_j Λ_j(v_j)`, where the indices off `J_x` contribute the zero vector with weight 1; it
   agrees with Definition 13.2.9 (1) for finite `J` (`lfSum_eq_conv`) and near `x` with the finite convolution over
   `J_x` (`lfSum_eq_conv_of_mem`; row V13.19). Status: **settled**.

8. **Definition 13.2.5: the reading of the symmetric structure** *(Definition 13.2.5, Lemma 13.2.6, p. 610 (2017:
   Definition 13.8, Lemma 13.3))* (2026-11-13). "`G_x`-invariant with the natural action" is read as "`U(x)` is the
   domain of a natural representation", Chapter 11's reading of Definition 13.2.1, which includes connectedness;
   properness is the existing `HasPropernessProperty`; the weights are in `ℚ≥0`. Lemma 13.2.6 is the text's construction
   before Definition 13.2.5, with the sections extended by 0 off `U` before transporting (`SymmetricStructure`,
   `lemma_13_2_6`; rows V13.13, V13.14). Status: **settled**.

9. **Every hypothesis taken in Chapter 13 is satisfiable** *(§§13.1–13.2)* (2026-11-13). One hypothesis: properness in
   `X` in Theorem 13.1.7 (`GoodSystem.isGoodOn`). Every M-polyfold as a trivial ep-groupoid has a good system
   (`nonempty_goodSystem_trivial`), and natural neighbourhoods with proper closure exist inside every open set
   (`exists_natNbhd_isProperSubset`). §13.2 adds no hypothesis. Status: **settled**.

Found while formalizing §§13.1–13.3 and §13.5 in Part III wave 2 (2026-11-13; files `Chapter13/P3E_*`, `P3D_*`,
`P3A_*`).

10. **Theorem 13.1.7 as printed: Q-properness forces cl_X U(q) ⊆ Q** *(Theorem 13.1.7, p. 602 (2017: Theorem 13.1); gap
    G.141, closed)* (2026-11-13). `Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative.lean`. The printed hypothesis, a good system of the
    full subcategory on the open `Q` (`IsGoodIn`, properness inside `Q`), is formalized without a sub-ep-groupoid
    structure, through the morphism set and the source and target maps on `Q` (`subSrc`, `subTgt`). When `|Q| = |X|` and
    `Q` is open, `Q`-properness of `cl_Q U(q)` forces `cl_X U(q) ⊆ Q` and gives properness in `X`
    (`isProperSubset_of_isProperSubsetIn`, by ultrafilters and local sections of `s`), so the printed theorem
    (`theorem_13_1_7_book`) follows from the project's stronger form (item 3; row V13.7). Status: **settled (gap G.141
    closed)**.

11. **Definitions 13.2.9 and 13.2.13: the intersection U′(x) ∩ U″(x)** *(Definitions 13.2.7–13.2.10, Lemmas 13.2.11,
    13.2.13, pp. 610–612 (2017: Definitions 13.9–13.12, Lemmas 13.4, 13.5); gaps G.142, G.143, closed)* (2026-11-13).
    `Chapter13/P3D_SymmetricOn.lean`, `P3D_Decorated.lean`, `P3D_NoInverse.lean`. The decorated sc⁺-multisections and
    their sums, multiples and locally finite sums are formalized (item 6). For the sum the text takes
    `U(x) = U′(x) ∩ U″(x)`; the intersection need not carry one natural action for which both structures are symmetric.
    It is read as an open neighbourhood of `x` inside the intersection with the natural action of `U′(x)`, on which the
    two actions agree (`NatNbhd.exists_le_of_finite`); the class does not depend on the choice, since Definition 13.2.8
    allows shrinking. For a locally finite sum with no non-trivial `Λ_j` near `x` the natural action is taken from a
    given good system. The remark that inverses do not exist is `remark_13_2_9_no_inverse` (rows V13.15–V13.17, V13.19,
    V13.22–V13.24). Status: **settled (gaps G.142, G.143 closed)**.

12. **§13.3: Definition 13.3.8, Remark 13.3.13, and condition (3) for the new τ′** *(Definition 13.3.8, Remark 13.3.13,
    the construction before Proposition 13.3.15, pp. 616–619 (2017: Definition 13.18, Remark 13.4, before Proposition

    the positive half is formalized; the negative half is about an equality of types, which has no Lean statement. For

    V13.39). Status: **in part (gap G.148 open)**.

## Chapter 14 (Extension of sc⁺-multisections; Lean `Polyfold/Chapter14/`)

*Numbering.* The items of this section are numbered in order of the text; later waves continue from the last number.
Statement numbers and pages are those of the Springer edition (2021, pp. 637–682), with the 2017 text's numbers in
parentheses. The comparison items are `Exposition/verification/ch14.md` (V14.1–V14.44); the gaps are G.164, G.165,

1. **The standing assumptions of Chapter 14: tame, |X| paracompact** *(§14.1, p. 638, Theorem 14.1.6, p. 643 (2017:
   §14.1, Theorem 14.1))* (2026-11-13). The chapter opens with "$X$ is a tame ep-groupoid with paracompact orbit space
   $|X|$ admitting sc-smooth partitions of unity". Theorem 14.1.6 as printed asks only that $|\partial X|$ be
   paracompact; its proof uses Proposition 14.1.1, which needs tameness, and Definition 14.1.2 is stated for tame $X$.
   The formalization reads it with the standing assumptions (`theorem_14_1_6_hyp`:
   `X.IsTame ∧ X.HasParacompactOrbitSpace`), witness the tame trivial ep-groupoid (`trivial_quadrant_witness`,
   `hasParacompactOrbitSpace_trivial`); the printed version without tameness was not attempted (row V14.6). The other
   results take tameness, the standing assumption Proposition 14.1.1 needs. In Proposition 14.1.4 the readings of the
   standing assumptions are `hB` (tame strong bundle charts) and `hpu` (partitions of unity), witness
   `proposition_14_1_4_hypotheses_rn` (row V14.4). Status: **narrower for Theorem 14.1.6 (standing assumptions read
   in)**.

2. **§§14.1–14.2: four reading points** *(Definitions 14.1.2, 14.1.7, Proposition 14.1.4, Lemma 14.2.2, pp. 641–650
   (2017: Definitions 14.1, 14.4, Remark 14.2, Lemma 14.1); gap G.165)* (2026-11-13). (a) $\bar\theta_j$ is the closure
   of the face in $V(x)$; that it is a tame M-polyfold is gap G.165. (b) Lemma 14.2.2 is read with
   $t(\varphi) \in U(x')$. (c) Proposition 14.1.4 says "sc⁺-multisections $\bar s_i$" for sc⁺-sections. (d) The
   equivalence in Definition 14.1.7, "similar to the $X$-case", is formalized in two equivalent forms; condition (4) is
   read pointwise on $\mathcal U(x, x')$ (rows V14.2, V14.4, V14.7, V14.11). Reading points. Status: **settled; (a) open
   (gap G.165)**.

3. **§14.3: the neighbourhoods (P5), (P6) and the symmetric extension of the correspondences** *(Lemmas 14.3.1, 14.3.6,
   14.3.7, Propositions 14.3.4, 14.3.8, pp. 650–658 (2017: Lemmas 14.2, 14.4, 14.5, Propositions 14.3, 14.4); gap
   G.169)* (2026-11-13). (P5) is read with the natural action on $\tilde U'(x)$ that of the good system, and (P6) with
   $\tilde U(x)$ carrying the restricted action and $\tilde U(x) \subseteq \tilde U'(x)$; this is what the text's

   Witnesses `P5Nbhds.ofGood`, `P6Nbhds.exists_`. Not in the text, but proved: the sets $\tilde O$ of Lemma 14.3.1, and
   hence $\hat O$ and $\hat\tau$, are symmetric under inversion (row V14.13, stronger); the diagonal property of
   $\hat\tau$ in Proposition 14.3.4 has its proof supplied (row V14.16). The properties (1), (2) of Definition 13.3.6
   for $\hat\tau$, which §14.4 uses implicitly, are the named fields `diag`, `swap` of `ZSetup` (witness
   `ZSetup.trivialSetup`); the instance from the objects of §14.3 is gap G.169 (rows V14.13–V14.24). Status: **settled;
   the instance open (gap G.169)**.

4. **§14.4: z-loops, Θ and the coherent neighbourhood systems** *(Definitions 14.4.8, 14.4.11, Proposition 14.4.6,
   Lemmas 14.4.9, 14.4.13, pp. 659–669 (2017: Definitions 14.8, 14.9, Proposition 14.5, Lemmas 14.8, 14.9); gap G.168)*

## Chapter 15 (Transversality and invariants; Lean `Polyfold/Chapter15/`)

*Numbering.* The items of this section are numbered in order of the text; later waves continue from the last number.
Statement numbers and pages are those of the Springer edition (2021, pp. 683–703), with the 2017 text's numbers in
parentheses. The comparison items are `Exposition/verification/ch15.md` (V15.1–V15.43); the gaps are G.144, G.145,
G.150–G.152, G.159–G.162, G.177–G.183 (G.145 closed in wave 2, G.144, G.161 in wave 3, G.151 in wave 4,
G.150, G.152, G.177, G.183 in wave 5).

Found while formalizing §15.1 in Part III wave 1 (2026-11-13; files `Chapter15/P3T_*`).

1. **Theorem 15.1.1, reading (a): the topology of the separation argument** *(Theorem 15.1.1, proof, pp. 684–687 (2017:
   Theorem 15.1))* (2026-11-13). `Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationModel.lean`, `P3T_SeparationLemmas.lean`. The separation
   argument (Proposition 15.1.3, Lemmas 15.1.4, 15.1.5) is run in the level-1 topology, and the "weak topology" in which
   the derivatives converge is read as pointwise convergence on `E₀`: the derivatives `D(g ∘ r)` of an sc¹ map are
   continuous only from level 1 (`continuousOn_scDeriv_coe`; row V15.2). A reading point. Status: **settled**.

2. **Theorem 15.1.1, reading (b): the index set of the final display** *(Theorem 15.1.1, proof, p. 687 (2017: Theorem
   15.1))* (2026-11-13). In the final display, presumably the sum runs over `{i : f(0) = s_i(0)}`, since `f(0) = s_i(0)`
   need not hold for all `i`. The proof compares the formal sums of the pairs `(s_i(r(y)), D((f − s_i) ∘ r)(y))`
   (`wsum_pair_eq_of_isLocal`, `wsum_model_eq`; row V15.2). A reading point. Status: **settled**.

3. **Proposition 15.1.3 at an isolated point** *(Proposition 15.1.3, p. 684 (2017: Proposition 15.1))* (2026-11-13). The
   proposition asks for `x_k → 0` with `x_k ≠ 0`. At an isolated point of the local model, for instance when `X` is
   zero-dimensional near `x`, no such sequence exists, so the proposition does not hold as we read it there
   (`not_proposition_15_1_3_of_isolated`, `not_proposition_15_1_3_point`). It is proved for `x₀` not isolated
   (`proposition_15_1_3_hyp`, witness `proposition_15_1_3_hyp_witness`), in a topological form with no sc-structure.
   Theorem 15.1.1 is unaffected: its core lemma handles isolated points through locality. A degenerate case and a
   reading point, not a question for the authors (row V15.4). Status: **settled**.

4. **Theorem 15.1.1: the functor property and the Fredholm summands** *(Theorem 15.1.1, pp. 683–684 (2017: §15.1,
   Theorem 15.1); gaps G.144, G.145)* (2026-11-13). `Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationIntrinsic.lean`. The value
   `T(f, Λ)(x) ∈ GrF(x)` is defined and proved independent of the local section structure and the chart at every level-1
   point, for `Λ` not necessarily a functor (`theorem_15_1_1_intrinsic`, `linearization_eq`). Not formalized: the action
   `φ_*` on `GrF` and the functor property `T(f, Λ)(tφ) = φ_* T(f, Λ)(sφ)` (gap G.144), and that the summands are
   sc-Fredholm (gap G.145); `GrF(x)` allows all linear maps (rows V15.1, V15.2, V15.8). Status: **open (gap G.144; G.145
   closed in Part III wave 2, item 5)**.

Found while formalizing §15.1 (2), §15.2 and part of §15.3 in Part III wave 2 (2026-11-13; files `Chapter15/P3L_*`,
`P3P_*`).

5. **Theorem 15.1.1 (2): the summands are sc-Fredholm, in the chart reading** *(Theorem 15.1.1 (2), pp. 683–684 (2017:
   Theorem 15.1); gap G.145, closed)* (2026-11-13). `Chapter15/P3L_FredholmSummands.lean`. For `f` with Part I's tame
   germ data (item 6) and `s_i` sc⁺ on `O` with `f(x) = s_i(x)`, the chart operator `D((f̂ − ŝ_i) ∘ r)(z)` restricts to
   an sc-Fredholm operator `T_zO → K_z` (`subDeriv_isScFredholm`), and every operator in the support of `T(f, Λ)(x)` is
   of this form (`linearization_summand_isScFredholm`). `T_xX` and `W_x` carry no sc-structure in the project, so
   "sc-Fredholm" is read in the chart; `GrF` is not cut down to a subtype (rows V15.1, V15.2, V15.9). The functor
   property is still gap G.144 (item 4). Status: **settled (gap G.145 closed; G.144 open)**.

6. **§15.2: the tame germ data are inherited from Part I** *(§15.2, Theorems 15.2.2, 15.2.5, Remark 15.2.3, pp. 688–690
   (2017: Theorems 15.2, 15.3, Remark 15.2))* (2026-11-13). `Chapter15/P3L_*.lean`. Theorems 15.2.2 and 15.2.5 rest on
   the implicit function theorem (Theorem 3.6.8) for `f − s_i`, which Part I proves for tame germ data (rows V3.94,
   V3.103, V3.105); with the 2021 untamed notion Theorem 3.6.8 does not hold as we read it (row V3.130, Chapter 3).
   §15.2 says only "a strong bundle over an ep-groupoid, `f` an sc-Fredholm section functor", so the statements carry
   `hft : IsScFredholmSectionTame f` and the rows are narrower; witness `theorem_15_2_2_hyp_witness` (the graph section
   of 0 over `ℝⁿ × ℝ⁰ → ℝⁿ` with `Λ₀`). The same hypothesis appears in Chapter 12 (gap G.140) and for `[0, 1] × X` (row
   V15.18) (rows V15.9, V15.12, V15.13, V15.15). Status: **narrower (inherited from Part I)**.

7. **§15.2: four reading points** *(Definitions 15.2.1, 15.2.4, Theorem 15.2.2 and its proof, pp. 688–689 (2017:
   Definitions 15.2, 15.3, Theorem 15.2))* (2026-11-13). (a) In Definition 15.2.1, "nonzero" and "sc-Fredholm" are
   automatic (`linearization_ne_zero`, item 5), so only the surjectivity of the support is asked. (b) In the proof of

   (2017: Remark 15.2, Theorem 15.3); gaps G.150–G.152)* (2026-11-13). The remark is local to `U(x)`. Its global form,

   pp. 691–699 (2017: Definitions 15.4, 15.6, Corollary 15.1); gaps G.160–G.162)* (2026-11-13). `Chapter15/P3P_*.lean`.

   Theorems 15.3.7, 15.3.9 are gaps G.161, G.162 (rows V15.17–V15.26). Status: **in part (gaps G.160–G.162 open)**.

13. **Theorems 15.3.7 and 15.3.9: the reductions, and a good system in Theorem 15.3.7** *(Theorem 15.3.7, Remark 15.3.8,
    Theorem 15.3.9, pp. 694–699 (2017: Theorems 15.4, 15.5); gaps G.162, G.177–G.179)* (2026-11-13).
    `Chapter15/P3W4GP_*.lean`, `P3W4TX_*.lean`. Theorem 15.3.7 is `theorem_15_3_7_of_hyp`, from the two analytic steps
    of the proof stated as Props: local families at the points of $S_f$ (`HasLocalGPFamilies`) and parametric general
    position (`HasParametricGeneralPosition`, gap G.162). The latter quantifies over all linear families with the listed
    properties; on $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^0 \to \mathbb R^n$ every pair is in general position, so it holds there
    for every family, and `theorem_15_3_7_statement_epSEP_zero_of_hyp` derives the theorem with all hypotheses
    discharged. The example has zero fibres, so it shows that the hypotheses are consistent, not more. "Structurable" in
    Theorem 15.3.7 presupposes a good system (Definition 13.3.6), and Remark 15.3.8 drops paracompactness, which is how
    good systems are obtained (Theorem 13.1.8): as we read it the theorem needs a good system in addition
    (`Nonempty A.X.GoodSystem`, necessary; Chapter 13, item 17). "Compact" in the theorem uses only $N(\Lambda) \le 1$,
    $\text{dom-supp} \subseteq U$ and the control of compactness. Theorem 15.3.9 is reduced to Theorem 14.1.9 (Chapter
    14, item 6) and two steps of its proof (gaps G.177, G.178); "surjective with respect to intersections of local
    faces" is read as onto $T^R_xX$ for every sc⁺ extension (gap G.179), "a saturated subset" as open and saturated, and

16. **Theorem 15.3.7: the parametric step and the groupoid part of the local constructions are proved** *(Theorem
    15.3.7, pp. 693–698 (2017: Theorem 15.4); item 12; gap G.162)* (2026-11-13). `Chapter15/P3W5GA_*.lean`,
    `P3W5GB_*.lean`. `hasParametricGeneralPosition` proves "achieving global transversality" with exactly the hypotheses
    of the theorem. The local constructions are proved from two Props on the object M-polyfold: (15.1) at one point with
    small vectors (`HasPointwiseParamOnto`) and its openness along $S_f$ (`HasParamOntoOpen`);
    `theorem_15_3_7_of_paramOnto` is the theorem from these two and a good system. Reading: the text's (15.1) uses
    $T^R_xX$, Part I's proof of Theorem 5.3.10 uses the properties (i)–(ii) with the full tangent space; the two are
    equivalent by elementary linear algebra, and the text presumably relies on this when it cites the implicit function
    theorem for the openness of (15.1). What remains is the bridge between the two in a chart (gap G.162, 530–950
    lines). The passage from $V(x)$ to its saturation "by equivariance" is the morphism invariance of general position

## Chapter 16 (Polyfolds; Lean `Polyfold/Chapter16/`)

*Numbering.* The items of this section are numbered in order of the text; later waves continue from the last number.
Statement numbers and pages are those of the Springer edition (2021, pp. 705–740), with the 2017 text's numbers in
parentheses. The comparison items are `Exposition/verification/ch16.md` (V16.1–V16.79); the gaps are G.146, G.153–G.157,
G.166, G.167, G.174–G.176 (G.146 closed in wave 2, G.154 in wave 3, G.156 in wave 4,
G.155, G.157, G.174 in wave 5).

Found while formalizing §16.1 in Part III wave 1 (2026-11-13; files `Chapter16/P3Z_*`).

1. **The uniqueness sentence after Definition 16.1.2 does not hold as we read it** *(Definition 16.1.2 and the sentence
   after it, p. 707 (2017: Definition 16.2); Chapter 10, item 58)* (2026-11-13).
   `Chapter16/P3Z_ZhouUniquenessCheck.lean`, `P3Z_PolyfoldStructure.lean`. The sentence says that the generalized
   isomorphism `f` with `α = β ∘ |f|` is unique, as a consequence of (ZHOU). The trivial `ℤ/3`-ep-groupoid on `ℝ`
   satisfies (ZHOU) (`isZhou_trivialZ3`: every element of `G_x` acts trivially), and its orbit space is homeomorphic to
   `ℝ`, hence paracompact, so `(ℤ/3 × ℝ ⇉ ℝ, π⁻¹)` is a polyfold structure on `ℝ` in the exact sense of Definition
   16.1.1 (`z3PolyfoldStructure`). The identity and the generalized isomorphism through the inversion functor both
   satisfy `α = α ∘ |f|` and differ (`uniqueness_16_1_2_counterexample`, `not_uniqueness_16_1_2`); this is the pair
   behind `not_theorem_10_3_19` (Chapter 10, item 58). Uniqueness holds when the target is effective: (ZHOU) gives the
   local regularity property, and Theorem 10.3.19 holds for effective ep-groupoids (`uniqueness_16_1_2_of_isEffective`).
   In 2017, Definition 16.2 says that `f` is necessarily unique, citing Theorem 10.7 (2021: 10.3.19); the 2021 text adds
   "as a consequence of (ZHOU)". Definitions 16.1.2, 16.1.3 and the rest of wave 1 do not use the uniqueness; Lemma
   16.2.1 and the isomorphisms of polyfold structures in Definitions 16.1.6–16.1.11 rest on it and will carry either
   effectiveness or the generalized isomorphism as data. Candidate for the notes to the authors (rows V16.2, V16.3).
   Status: **does not hold as we read it; the effective form is proved**.

2. **Remark 16.1.7 and the sentence on pp. 709–710 do not hold as we read them** *(Remark 16.1.7, p. 711, and pp.
   709–710 (2017: Remark 16.1))* (2026-11-13). Remark 16.1.7 says that over a homeomorphism `h : Z → W` there is at most
   one generalized isomorphism `f` with `h ∘ α = β ∘ |f|`; the sentence on pp. 709–710 says that for an isomorphism of
   polyfold structures the generalized isomorphism is determined by the map, as a consequence of Theorem 10.3.19. With
   `h = id`, the pair of item 1 contradicts both (`not_remark_16_1_7`). Both hold for an effective target
   (`remark_16_1_7_of_isEffective`). Part of the same candidate for the notes to the authors as item 1 (row V16.7).
   Status: **does not hold as we read it; the effective form is proved**.

3. **The metrizability remark after Definition 16.1.1** *(the remark after Definition 16.1.1, p. 706 (2017: Proposition
   16.1); gap G.146)* (2026-11-13). The text remarks that `Z` is metrizable when `|X|` is paracompact (in 2017 the
   numbered Proposition 16.1). The ingredients exist: local metrizability of `|X|` (`lemma_7_3_2_naturalRep`),
   regularity and the Hausdorff property (Lemmas 7.3.4, 7.3.5); the Smirnov metrization theorem is not in Mathlib
   (estimate 600–1,500 lines; row V16.1). Status: **settled in Part III wave 2 (item 7; gap G.146 closed)**.

4. **Proposition 16.1.4 (1): bump functions on the object M-polyfold** *(Proposition 16.1.4, p. 708 (2017: Proposition
   16.2))* (2026-11-13). `Chapter16/P3Z_PolyfoldBump.lean`, `P3Z_PolyfoldPartitions.lean`. (1) is read for the object
   M-polyfold (Definition 5.3.1, `f(x) ≠ 0`), as the proof uses it; Definition 12.3.1's notion is equivalent to it by
   Theorem 12.3.2 (1) in the pointwise reading (Chapter 12, item 3). The proof differs from the text's: local inverses
   for (1), partitions of unity descended to `|X|` for (2) (`proposition_16_1_4`; row V16.5). Status: **settled**.

5. **Definition 16.1.1 in 2017 and 2021** *(Definition 16.1.1, p. 705 (2017: Definition 16.1))* (2026-11-13). The 2021
   definition adds (ZHOU) and the paracompactness of `|X|`, which the 2017 definition does not have; `Z` lives in the
   universe of the object and morphism sets of `X` (`PolyfoldStructure`; row V16.1). Every definition of §16.1 has a
   witness: the polyfold `ℝ` with the trivial `ℤ/3`-action (`z3Polyfold` and the `z3Polyfold_*` declarations; row
   V16.13). Status: **settled**.

Found while formalizing §16.2 and §16.4 in Part III wave 2 (2026-11-13; files `Chapter16/P3H_*`).

6. **Lemma 16.2.1 does not hold as we read it** *(Lemma 16.2.1, p. 716 (2017: Lemma 16.3); items 1, 2)* (2026-11-13).
   `Chapter16/P3H_TangentLemma.lean`. The lemma says that two isomorphisms `(f, 𝔣)`, `(g, 𝔤)` of polyfold structures
   with `f = g` have `𝔣 = 𝔤` and `T𝔣 = T𝔤`; the proof uses `|𝔣| = |𝔤|` and Theorem 10.3.19. The pair of item 1 (the
   trivial `ℤ/3`-action on `ℝ`, `f = g = id`, `𝔣` through the inversion functor, `𝔤 = 1`) satisfies the printed
   hypotheses and has `𝔣 ≠ 𝔤` (`not_lemma_16_2_1`). What holds: the orbit form `|𝔣| = |𝔤|`, `|T𝔣| = |T𝔤|` under the
   printed hypotheses (`lemma_16_2_1_orbit`), and the full statement for an effective target
   (`lemma_16_2_1_of_isEffective`, witness `lemma_16_2_1_of_isEffective_hypotheses`). Every later use in §16.2 needs
   only `|T𝔣|` (rows V16.16, V16.18), and the tangent polyfold is built with it. Whether `T𝔣 ≠ T𝔤` in the example is not
   decided. Part of the same candidate for the notes to the authors as items 1 and 2: is the orbit form what §16.2 uses
   (row V16.15)? Status: **does not hold as we read it; the orbit form and the effective form are proved**.

7. **The metrizability remark is proved** *(the remark after Definition 16.1.1, p. 706 (2017: Proposition 16.1); gap
   G.146, closed)* (2026-11-13). `PolyfoldStructure.metrizableSpace` (`Chapter16/P3H_TangentPolyfold.lean`), from
   Theorem 7.3.1's `theorem_7_3_1_metrizable` and `β`. The metrization step is Part I's `metrizableSpace_of_locally`
   (Chapter 2), so the Smirnov theorem asked for in item 3 is not needed (rows V16.1, V16.14). Status: **settled (gap
   G.146 closed)**.

8. **Theorem 16.4.6: partitions of unity** *(Theorem 16.4.6, p. 732 (2017: Theorem 16.5); gap G.153)* (2026-11-13).
   `Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold.lean`. The text derives Stokes on polyfolds from the ep-groupoid level ("On the
   ep-groupoid level Stokes' Theorem holds"); Theorems 9.5.17 and 9.5.18 there assume sc-smooth partitions of unity.
   Theorem 16.4.6 does not state them, and the standing assumption of Chapter 16 is only (ZHOU) (p. 705). The
   formalization adds `hPU : c.AdmitsScPartitionsOfUnity` (Definition 16.1.5; by Definition 16.1.5 (2) every
   representative then has them), witness `theorem_16_4_6_hyp_witness`; without it is gap G.153 (rows V16.27, V16.28).
   Candidate for the notes to the authors: is the existence of sc-smooth partitions of unity meant as an assumption of
   Theorem 16.4.6? Status: **open (gap G.153)**.

9. **§16.4: tameness invariance and the integrals on representatives** *(p. 729, Definition 16.4.2, Proposition 16.4.3,
   the integrals on p. 732 (2017: Definition 16.30, Proposition 16.6); gaps G.154, G.155)* (2026-11-13). The text says
   before Definition 16.4.1 that the properties of `Θ` are preserved by `f_*`, `f^*`. This is proved for closed,
   compact, manifold-type, orbifold-type and dimension (`hasRepProperty_iff`, from Theorem 11.3.3), not for tameness
   (gap G.154), so "tame" means "some representative is tame", the integrals are defined on tame compact
   representatives, and their independence is proved among those (`integral_eq_of_rel`, Theorems 11.4.1, 11.4.2). The
   structure on `supp θ` is proved for every representative; that two representatives give diffeomorphic structures is
   gap G.155. In Definition 16.4.4 the orientation `T̂` is normalized to vanish off `X_∞`, where the text's `T̂_Θ` lives
   (rows V16.22–V16.27). Status: **open (gaps G.154, G.155)**.

10. **§16.2: the tangent polyfold from a base point** *(§16.2, pp. 715–721 (2017: §16.2); gaps G.156, G.157)*
    (2026-11-13). `Chapter16/P3H_TangentPolyfold.lean`, `P3H_PolyfoldForms.lean`. `T(Z, c)` is `|TX₀|` for the base
    point `c.out`, and `Tα` does not depend on the choice of `𝔣` (`tangentMap_eq`, through
    `EPLoc.orbitMap_tangentHom_eq`: (LR), from (ZHOU)); Lemma 16.2.2, Definition 16.2.3, Definition 16.2.5 and the
    complex of Theorem 16.2.6 are as stated. The projection `τ_Z`, the raised polyfolds (gap G.156), the tangent functor
    and the pull-back of forms, which need the morphisms of Definitions 16.1.6–16.1.11 (gap G.157), are not formalized
    (rows V16.16–V16.21). Status: **in part (gaps G.156, G.157 open)**.

Found while formalizing §§16.1–16.6 in Part III waves 3–4 (2026-11-13; files `Chapter16/P3W3V_*`, `P3W3Y_*`, `P3W4SM_*`,
`P3W4PB_*`, `P3W4FN_*`).

11. **The uniqueness of f and F after Definition 16.3.3 does not hold as we read it** *(Definition 16.3.3 and the
    sentence after it, p. 723 (2017: Definition 16.17); items 1, 2, 6, 12)* (2026-11-13).
    `Chapter16/P3W3V_UniquenessCheck.lean`. After Definition 16.3.3 the text states that $f$ and $F$ are uniquely
    determined by $\gamma'\circ|f| = \gamma$, $\Gamma'\circ|F| = \Gamma$. As we read it this needs the target base to be
    effective, as do Theorem 10.3.19 and Proposition 10.4.7 it relies on: on
    $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R$ over $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ with
    trivial actions ((ZHOU), paracompact, locally regular), $[1_W]$ and the class through the inversion functor both
    satisfy the conditions and differ already on the bases (`not_uniqueness_16_3_3`). With an effective target base both
    are unique (`uniqueness_16_3_3_of_isEffective`). Nothing later in §16.3 uses the uniqueness. The cause is that of
    items 1, 2, 6 and 12: a non-effective isotropy acting trivially. Part of the same candidate for the notes to the
    authors (row V16.40). Status: **does not hold as we read it; the effective form is proved**.

12. **Definition 16.1.10: the composite does not depend on the choices, as we read it, only for effective polyfolds**
    *(Definitions 16.1.6, 16.1.10, 16.1.11, pp. 709–711 (2017: Definitions 16.5, 16.7, 16.8); items 1, 2, 6, 11)*
    (2026-11-13). `Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps.lean`, `P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample.lean`. As we read Definition
    16.1.6, the isomorphism $(k, \mathrm{Id}_W)$ is any generalized isomorphism over $\mathrm{Id}_W$. The composite of
    Definition 16.1.10 then depends on the representative of $\hat f$ when the middle structure has a non-effective
    isotropy (`not_definition_16_1_10`, `not_exists_comp`, on a $(\mathbb Z/3)^2$-structure on $\mathbb R$ with the
    trivial action, `k2Structure`). For an effective middle polyfold it holds (`PSHom.Equiv.comp_of_isEffective`), and
    the polyfold category of Definition 16.1.11 is formalized as the category of effective polyfolds (`EffPolyfold`,
    witness `EffPolyfold.point`). Presumably the text intends effective polyfolds, or a choice of $\mathfrak f$ carried
    as data. The same mechanism as items 1, 2, 6 and 11; part of the same candidate for the notes to the authors (rows
    V16.32, V16.33). Status: **does not hold as we read it; the effective form is proved**.

13. **§16.2: the raised polyfolds, the tangent projection and the tangent functor** *(§16.2, pp. 715–719, Theorem
    16.2.4, p. 719 (2017: §16.2, Theorem 16.1); item 10; gaps G.156 (closed), G.157)* (2026-11-13).
    `Chapter16/P3W3Y_TangentFunctor.lean`, `P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold.lean`. The raised polyfolds $(Z, c)^i$ and the
    projection $\tau_Z$ are formalized, $(Z, c)^1$ with its own topology (gap G.156 closed). $T$ is a functor on the
    category PS of polyfold structures (`PSCat.tangentFunctor`) and is well defined on sc-smooth maps
    (`theorem_16_2_4`). $T(\hat g \circ \hat f) = T\hat g \circ T\hat f$ is proved under the effectiveness of $d$ and of
    $Td$ (`tangent_comp`); the second hypothesis has no witness, since that the tangent of an effective polyfold is
    effective is not formalized (gap G.157, retitled). The pull-back of forms is proved on every class (rows V16.21,
    V16.34–V16.36). Status: **in part (gap G.156 closed; gap G.157 open)**.

14. **§16.4: tameness is invariant; the integrals on classes** *(p. 729, Definition 16.4.2, the integrals on p. 732
    (2017: Definition 16.30); item 9; gap G.154, closed)* (2026-11-13). `Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame.lean`,
    `P3W4SM_SuppNaturality.lean`. Tameness of branched suborbifolds is invariant under equivalence, so "tame" in
    Definition 16.4.2 (5) is as stated and the integrals are defined on classes; their independence of the
    representative at the boundary still uses sc-smooth partitions of unity (item 8, gap G.153). The structure on

    (rows V16.23, V16.24, V16.27). Status: **in part (gap G.154 closed; gaps G.153, G.155 open)**.

    16.3.16, Theorem 16.3.17, pp. 721–729 (2017: Definitions 16.16–16.28, Propositions 16.4, 16.5, Theorems 16.3, 16.4);

    function $n : Y \to \mathbb R$ for $n : Y_{0,1} \to [0, \infty)$. (b) Definition 16.3.5 (2), (3) is read through one

16. **§§16.5–16.6: reductions to the ep-groupoid level, and four reading points** *(§16.5, §16.6, pp. 733–740 (2017:
    §§16.5, 16.6); gaps G.174–G.176)* (2026-11-13). `Chapter16/P3W4PB_*.lean`, `P3W4FN_StructurablePullback.lean`. The
    relations of Definitions 16.5.1 and 16.5.5 do not depend on the non-unique $\bar f$ (`rel_iff`, checked on the

    $\gamma$ for $\Gamma$; in Definition 16.5.4 $\lambda : Y \to \mathbb Q^+$; in Theorem 16.6.6 $n$ on $Y_{0,1}$
    (printed $Z_{0,1}$); "controlled by $(n, U)$" is $n(\lambda) \le 1$ and $\text{dom-supp} \subseteq U$ (rows

17. **Every hypothesis taken in Part III waves 3–4 for Chapter 16 is satisfiable, except one** *(§§16.1–16.6)*

18. **Theorem 16.2.4: $T$ preserves effectiveness; the tangent functor on effective polyfolds** *(Theorem 16.2.4, p. 719
    (2017: Theorem 16.1); items 13, 17; gap G.157, closed)* (2026-11-13). `Chapter16/P3W5PC_TangentEffective.lean`. The
    tangent of an effective polyfold is effective (`PolyfoldClass.IsEffective.tangent`), and
    `EffPolyfold.tangentFunctor` is a Mathlib functor on effective polyfolds with no hypothesis beyond the text's. The
    proof goes through a smooth point and uses (ZHOU), Definition 16.1.1 (2): effectiveness is a level-0 statement,
    while open sets of $T\mathbf X$ see only level 1. The hypothesis of `tangent_comp` now holds for every effective
    target (row V16.34). Status: **settled (gap G.157 closed); item 17's exception settled**.

    Proposition 16.6, §16.5); items 14, 16; gaps G.155, G.174, closed)* (2026-11-13).
    `Chapter16/P3W5PC_SuppNaturality.lean`, `P3W5PC_NormLamContinuous.lean`. The transition between the structures on
    $\mathrm{supp}\,\theta$ of two representatives is an sc-diffeomorphism for any induced structures of Proposition

    V16.67, now same). Status: **settled (gaps G.155, G.174 closed)**.

    (row V16.71). Status: **in part (gaps G.166, G.176 open)**.
